author: chandanaroyals
body:
Builds the deadline mechanism T7.11 queued.

## The defect

The correlate wait was `CORRELATE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 900` of wall clock. But the question the wait
is asking is *has the world had enough chances to alert* — and a chance is a scrape, not a second.
The two quantities are the same only while the host is running. When it suspends, seconds keep
passing and chances do not, and a clock cannot tell the difference.

T7.11 measured the cost: a sixteen-minute telemetry gap inside the 900s deadline discarded
`frauddetection-memory-squeeze` as a fault that does not page. It pages at T+390s.

## The derivation

`CORRELATE_SCRAPES = 180`, from the catalog rather than from a guess:

| input | value | source |
|---|---|---|
| recorded onsets, 12 current bundles | 166–390s | the bundles |
| recorded onsets, every recording archived | 165–469s (n=20) | archive |
| longest `for:` clause | 3m (`ServiceHighLatency`, `ServiceNoTraffic`) | `alert-rules.yml` |
| scrape interval | 5s | `prometheus-config.yaml`, pinned by test |
| onset decomposition, measured | condition true at T+201s → fired at T+381s | T7.11 |

180 scrapes × 5s = **900s of world time** — 1.9× the longest onset ever recorded, 2.3× the
longest in the current catalog. Deliberately the same coverage the old deadline intended:
**the value was never the problem, the unit was.** On a healthy world the wait still ends at
exactly 900s, and a test pins that equivalence.

Scrapes are counted as `max(count_over_time(up[Ns]))` — `up` is synthetic, present per target, and
appended once per scrape. Measured at 12/minute against the 5s interval. Not
`prometheus_tsdb_head_samples_appended_total`: this deployment does not scrape Prometheus itself,
so that counter is absent here.

## A gap does not end the wait — it fails to advance it

This is the part that actually recovers T7.11's scenario. Sixteen minutes of silence now costs
zero of the 180 scrapes, so the world resumes, and the alert lands inside the budget.

Two bounds remain: `CORRELATE_CEILING_SECONDS = 1800` (wall clock, for a world that never
returns — after a 16-minute gap 840s remains, short of the full allowance but longer than any
onset ever recorded) and `CORRELATE_GAP_SECONDS = 60` (twelve intervals; jitter loses one or two).

## Two discards, not one

`WorldStoppedReportingError` → `metrics-gap`. `NoAlertError` → `no-alert`. The reason travels on
the exception and the manifest records it. These are different findings — only `no-alert` says
anything about a scenario — and they shared one message until now, which is how T7.11's discard
came to be recorded under the wrong meaning.

## The stamp does not move

`1b0e7cbb4c47`, unchanged. The stamp hashes role prompts and contract schemas
(`faultline.agents.stamp`); no part of `evalharness` reaches it. Runs either side of T7.12 stay
comparable. Same precedent as T4.7, which excluded budget bounds for the same reason. Pinned by
`test_the_correlate_budget_is_not_a_stamp_input`.

## Tests

Both paths, on a virtual clock so a sixteen-minute outage is arithmetic rather than sixteen
minutes:

- **the T7.11 shape** — silent from t=60 to t=1020, alert at t=1100: returns the incident having
  spent 29 of 180 scrapes. The old 900s deadline died at t=900, mid-gap.
- **world never returns** — `metrics-gap` at the 1800s ceiling, 12 scrapes.
- **reporting world, no alert** — `no-alert` at exactly t=900, 181 scrapes.
- the two reasons are distinct in the written manifest; the scrape interval is pinned against
  `prometheus-config.yaml`; the budget covers the longest onset ever seen.

`make check`: 464 passed, 1 skipped.

## Not re-run

`frauddetection-memory-squeeze`'s S6 discard stands as recorded (T7.11's position). This changes
how the next sweep behaves, not what the last one measured.

author: firedmosquito831
body:
**What was broken.** NVIDIA NIM requests silently lost their reasoning
instruction. On the user's live data `nvidia_nim/moonshotai/kimi-k3` produced
thinking on 2 of 111 requests, while `nvidia_nim/minimaxai/minimax-m3`, which
was not 400ing, produced thinking on 7 of 10.

**Mechanism.** NIM's reasoning instruction lives entirely in
`extra_body.chat_template_kwargs` (`thinking` / `enable_thinking`, plus
`reasoning_budget`). The chat-template rung of `_get_retry_request_body` decided
whether to strip that field by testing `"chat_template" in error_text`, where
`error_text` was `str(error)` concatenated with `json.dumps(error.body)`. Both
halves can contain the *echoed request*: a pydantic-style validation 400 carries
the objection in `msg`/`loc`/`type` and the entire submitted body under `input`,
and the OpenAI SDK's `str()` renders the whole response payload. So a rejection
about something else entirely — kimi-k3's was
`Validation: top_p is immutable for this model and must be 0.95, got 1` — could
match on the request's own `chat_template_kwargs` and retry without it. The
retry then succeeded, so the user saw an answer, just never a thinking block.
The same substring test made the rung fire on any 400 whose text happened to
contain the token, with no requirement that the provider was complaining about
it.

**Fix.** Split evidence from surgery in `providers/nvidia_nim/retry.py`,
following the shape of `providers/openai_chat/output_cap.py`, which already
parses a named cap out of a 400 rather than guessing.

`upstream_complaint()` builds the evidence string from the structured error body
only, walking message-bearing keys (`message`, `detail`, `msg`, `loc`, `param`,
`type`, ...) and skipping request-echo keys (`input`, `body`, `request`,
`payload`, `ctx`, `value`, ...) outright. It falls back to `str(error)` only when
the body yields nothing readable. Word-boundary matchers then report *which*
field the provider named: `chat_template_evidence`, `reasoning_content_evidence`,
`reasoning_budget_evidence`, `sampling_parameter_evidence`.

The ladder in `nvidia_nim/client.py` now reads, in order:

1. `reasoning_budget` — narrowest removal, and the only rung that keeps the
   thinking flags themselves; still the only rung that accepts a 500.
2. `chat_template` / `chat_template_kwargs` — fires only when the complaint names
   the field. Ordered ahead of the sampling guard on purpose: naming the field is
   direct evidence, whereas a sampling name is only a negative signal, so a
   complaint naming both still strips. This keeps the load-bearing recovery for
   models that reject the field outright.
3. sampling-parameter guard — a 400 naming `top_p`, `top_k`, `min_p`,
   `temperature`, `seed` or a penalty, and *not* naming the chat template,
   returns `None`. Removing the reasoning instruction cannot fix a sampling
   complaint; it only trades a visible failure for an invisible loss of thinking.
4. `reasoning_content` — fires only when named.
5. anything unrecognised — `None`. Re-sending an unchanged body is pointless and
   re-sending a degraded one is worse than failing, so an unreadable 400 now
   surfaces instead of costing the request its reasoning.

Every rung logs which rung fired and the matched token plus a bounded excerpt of
the provider's own words, so "why did my thinking disappear" is answerable from
the log. The no-retry paths log too.

`reasoning_emitted` on `request_attempts` needs no change: `record_wire_request`
is called inside `_create_stream`'s retry loop and `WireTrace.record` recomputes
`reasoning_was_emitted(body)` per attempt, last-write-wins, so a stripped retry
already records `reasoning_emitted=0` for that attempt.

**Verification.**

    $ uv run python demo.py
    'Validation: top_p is immutable for this model and must be 0.95, got 1'
      sampling='top_p' chat_template=None
    'chat_template_kwargs is not supported for Mistral tokenizers.'
      sampling=None chat_template='chat_template_kwargs'
    'Internal validation failure'
      sampling=None chat_template=None

    $ uv run ruff format --check . && uv run ruff check . && uv run ty check
    976 files already formatted
    All checks passed!
    All checks passed!

    $ uv run pytest -q --tb=line
    14 failed, 5684 passed, 38 skipped in 197.29s (0:03:17)

All 14 are the documented pre-existing baseline: 8 websearch tests that read the
real `~/.fcc/.env`, 6 PowerShell installer tests. None are in the files this
commit touches; `tests/providers/test_nvidia_nim.py` and
`tests/providers/test_nim_request_clone.py` are 39 passed, 0 failed.

New tests: the real kimi-k3 `top_p` string retries nothing and leaves
`chat_template_kwargs` intact on the wire; a pydantic 400 whose `input` echoes
`chat_template_kwargs` while `loc` names `top_p` does not strip; an unrecognised
400 strips neither `chat_template_kwargs` nor `reasoning_content`; a named
`chat_template_kwargs` 400 still strips exactly as before; a complaint naming
both still strips; a named `reasoning_content` 400 still strips. The existing
`test_stream_response_retries_without_chat_template` and
`..._chat_template_kwargs_issue_993` pin the preserved behaviour and are
unchanged.

**Not done.** `_apply_context_headroom` has no floor; the ~22 `NoReasoning`
provider profiles are unaudited. Both separately queued. Mistral's
`is_mistral_reasoning_rejection` and DeepSeek's
`is_deepseek_tool_choice_rejection` flatten body + response text the same way and
are echo-susceptible in principle, but both additionally require a rejection
*phrase* rather than a bare field name, so neither is fixed here.

**Residual risks.**

- The evidence walk trusts key *names*. A provider that reports its objection
  under a key not in the complaint list, and nothing else readable in the body,
  falls back to `str(error)` — which still carries the echoed payload. That
  fallback is strictly no worse than the old behaviour, and it only applies when
  the structured body yields nothing.
- A NIM deployment that rejects `chat_template_kwargs` without ever naming it
  (a bare "invalid request") no longer recovers; it fails visibly instead. That
  is the deliberate trade in rung 5 — a visible failure beats a silent downgrade
  — but it is a behaviour change for any such deployment.
- The sampling guard's parameter list is fixed. A provider complaining about a
  sampling knob not on the list falls into the unrecognised bucket, which is
  also no-strip, so it fails safe.

**CI note.** The local run is `14 failed, 5684 passed, 38 skipped` — exactly the
documented pre-existing baseline (8 websearch tests that read the real
`~/.fcc/.env`, 6 PowerShell installer tests). None are in the files this PR
touches.

Retires the remote cache server from CI: every job now uses mbx's GitHub Actions cache backend. Removes the backend-selection expression, the `mbx-backend` workflow plumbing, the fork-PR cache mirror, and the server-warming workflow — all of which existed to route trusted builds at cache.mise.jdx.dev. mbx itself stays.

`id-token: write` grants are left in place where they may serve Pages deploys or attestations; they can be tightened separately.

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Workflow-only simplification of Rust cache plumbing; build behavior may shift (slower warm caches, no shared remote cache) but no application or security logic changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> CI no longer routes **mbx** through `cache.mise.jdx.dev` or picks a backend per trust level. The composite **`.github/actions/mbx`** action always sets `backend: github` and drops the `backend` / `mirror-github-cache` inputs, the conditional backend expression, remote server settings (`server-url`, `namespace`, `oidc-audience`), and the main-branch step that mirrored cache for fork PRs.

> **`ci-impl.yml`** stops accepting `mbx-backend`; every job invokes mbx with defaults only (no `mirror-github-cache` on build/Windows jobs). **`ci.yml`** no longer passes `mbx-backend: server` vs `github` into trusted vs untrusted runs. author: danfiedler-msft
body:
## Summary

This PR pins GitHub Actions to full-length commit SHAs for improved security and reproducibility and adds a 7 day cooldown to Dependabot configuration for GitHub Actions. This work is described in more detail at https://aka.ms/action-pinning.

## Why?

Pinning actions to commit SHAs prevents supply-chain attacks where a tag could be moved to point to malicious code. This is a recommended security best practice per the [GitHub Actions security hardening guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions).

This change mitigates the risk of tag retargeting to malicious code as seen in incidents like the [tj-actions/changed-files action compromise](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/harden-runner-detection-tj-actions-changed-files-action-is-compromised) or [codfish/semantic-release-action compromise](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/supply-chain-compromise-codfish-semantic-release-action) and improves the integrity and reproducibility of the CI/CD pipeline.

## What changed?

**Action pinning:** Third-party action references in `.github/workflows/` that used mutable tag-based references (e.g., `actions/checkout@v4`) have been updated to full-length commit SHAs with a version comment (e.g., `actions/checkout@<sha> # v4`) using the [pinact](https://github.com/suzuki-shunsuke/pinact) tool. References that were already pinned to a SHA, or that used immutable release tags, were left unchanged.

**Dependabot configuration:** `.github/dependabot.yml` has been updated to ensure a `github-actions` package-ecosystem section is present with a `cooldown` configuration (`default-days: 7`). If the file did not exist, it was created. If a `github-actions` section already existed, only the `cooldown` block was added or its `default-days` value was increased to 7 if it was lower. The 7-day cooldown provides a window for the community to detect and report compromised releases before they are automatically proposed as updates, reducing exposure to supply-chain attacks via newly published malicious versions.

## Is this safe to merge?

Yes. The pinned SHAs correspond to the same commits that the existing tags pointed to. No behavioral changes in action execution are introduced. You can verify the pinned SHA value using the GitHub REST API (e.g., the commit hash for `actions/checkout@v7` can be found in the `sha` property in the JSON response for `GET https://api.github.com/repos/actions/checkout/commits/v7`).

## Additional Information

For more information, please see https://aka.ms/action-pinning

author: jav359003
body:
## Summary

On real hardware there is no success oracle, so an attended run's ground truth is the string a human types. The vocabulary that decides which strings count lived in a private `scorer._OPERATOR_SUCCESS`, so KitchenBench copied it (`kitchenbench/scoring.py:17`) and guards the copy with a test that imports the private symbol across repos (`kitchenbench/tests/test_world.py:50`).

That guard is insufficient in two ways:

1. It pins a private symbol from another repo. Per `tests/test_api_snapshot.py`, private names carry no stability guarantee and the snapshot fence does not cover them, so renaming `_OPERATOR_SUCCESS` breaks KitchenBench after release rather than during review.
2. It compares the vocabulary but not the comparison. Both sites also do `verdict.strip().lower() in <set>` plus a `None` check. The two frozensets can stay equal while that normalization drifts, and the assertion stays green.

This promotes the contract to public API so there is one owner for both halves.

## Changes

- Add `is_affirmative_verdict(verdict: str | None) -> bool` to `inspect_robots.scorer`: the vocabulary *and* the comparison rules (case-insensitive, whitespace-tolerant, `None` is not affirmative).
- `_OperatorScorer` now calls it instead of restating the comparison, so the repo holds exactly one implementation.
- Export from `inspect_robots.__all__` and add to the API-snapshot `EXPECTED` set.
- `_OPERATOR_SUCCESS` is unchanged and stays private as backing data.
- Tests: the full vocabulary, case/whitespace variants, rejections (including `"yes please"`, which contains an affirmative word but is not one), `None`, and a consistency test asserting the scorer's value *is* the predicate's, so a second copy cannot be reintroduced silently.
- CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased.

No behavior change. The existing `test_operator_scorer_reads_recorded_verdict` passes unchanged, which is the evidence.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

KitchenBench drops `_AFFIRMATIVE` and the private-symbol guard in favor of importing this. It is blocked on a release, since KitchenBench resolves `inspect-robots` from PyPI. Happy to open it as soon as a version ships.

## Open question

I chose a predicate over exporting the frozenset because it also owns the normalization that the current cross-repo guard cannot check. If you would rather expose `OPERATOR_SUCCESS_VERDICTS` as data and leave normalization to callers, say the word and I will switch.

## Checklist

- [x] `pre-commit install` done; hooks pass (commit and push stages)
- [x] Tests added/updated
- [x] Coverage stays at **100%** (`pytest --cov`: 1639 passed, 100.00%)
- [x] `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on the touched files
- [x] `mypy` passes (strict), 86 source files clean
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` updated under "Unreleased"
- [x] Public API changes reflected in `inspect_robots.__all__` and the API-snapshot test
- [x] Core stays NumPy-only (no new dependencies)

## Related

Closes #414

author: sbtheg17-market
body:
## Pilot finding M-1 — Activation Hub next action vs. verification gate

**Root cause.** deriveActivationNextAction branched on applicationStatus alone; every setup destination it emits sits behind requireApprovedProvider (application AND verification approved). In the window "application approved, verification under_review" the hub pointed the primary CTA at routes answering 403.

**Fix (server source of truth, no schema/contract change).** The approved branch now gates on the C1 approved milestone: pre-gate it emits wait_for_review (decision pending) or review_update_needed (verification rejected — resubmission is accessible). Web renders the same server truth: checklist deep links key on milestones.approved, pre-gate hero titles added, and the review_update_needed anchor target exists in both producing states. requireApprovedProvider untouched; no route opened to unapproved providers; no client-side lifecycle recomputation.

**Invariant now regression-tested (table-driven, live routes):** every server-derived provider nextAction resolves to a destination the provider is authorized to use in the same lifecycle state.

**Validation (local disposable PostgreSQL):** typecheck/build/build:deploy PASS; API unit 132/132; web 242/242 (+2 hub tests incl. axe); a11y + tz PASS; targeted suites all PASS (activation-status 13, return-path-drift 11, route-read-drift 19, provider-status 9, onboarding 23, verification 13, registration 15, authorization 7, provider-readiness 14, provider-application 8, provider-dashboard 17, booking-page 17, service-area 30, role-state 2); independent E2E verification 33/33 live checks. Managed DB NOT accessed; production NOT deployed.

Closes pilot finding M-1 (docs/pilot/provider-client-journey-validation.md addendum). L-1/L-2 remain deferred (LOW).

body:
## 何を変えたか

「この地点について言えること」と「この周辺について、公式資料から言えること」を分けた（ADR 0062）。

```
いまの地形から     ここは、かつて水面で、その後陸地にされた土地   この地点
明治期の地図から   河川・湖沼・海面 でした                        この地点
空中写真から       1936–42 の写真が残っています                   この地点
─────────────────────────────────────
この周辺について、公式資料から                                    別の箱
  東京港一帯には、1974年に「13号地外貿定期船ふ頭完成」という記録があります。
  ※この地点に関する記録ではありません。この場所がいつ陸になったかは、この資料からは分かりません。
  出典：東京都港湾局「東京港の歴史」
```

## なぜ 1 件だけか

原典に座標も丁目も無く、現在地の住所も持っていないので、記録と地点を結びつけられない。

はじめは 3 件並べた。豊洲で「要綱の施行」「13号地」「品川」が並んだ（実測 2026-08-29）。
古い順にすると「隅田川口改良工事」「日の出ふ頭完成」「開港」になる。どちらもこの場所の話ではない。
なぜその 3 件なのかを説明できないので、並べること自体をやめた。

代表は地域ごとに手で選び、JSON に理由と一緒に置いた（`representative` / `representative_note`）。
地点ごとに選び分けない。選び分けると、選ばれた理由が「この場所に近いから」と読まれる。

- 東京港の 1974 年は Owner が選んだ
- 浦安の 1975 年はこちらが仮に選んだもので、Owner の確認を取っていない

## 利用者テスト（実在の利用者ではない）

利用者役 3 名。375×667・明るい色み。5 秒だけ見せて、伏せてから聞いた。
問い:「これを見て、この土地がいつ〇〇になったと思いましたか？」

| 見込み | 結果 |
|---|---|
| 「※」を添えれば誤認しない | **反証された。3 名中 1 名が、豊洲・浦安の両方で年を地点のものとして読んだ** |
| 幅（1970 年代）としては伝わる | 反証されなかった。3 名中 2 名が地域の話として受け取った |

反証した 1 名（30 秒見せ直したあと）:
「※の行を読んだら、たしかに違うと書いてある。でも 5 秒では太字の 1974 年しか見ていない」

新しく出たこと: **箱が出ないことが「変わっていない」と読まれうる**（春日部で 2 名）。
掟 §1 の「取得できなかった ≠ 存在しなかった」の裏返し。まだ手当てしていない。

## 確かめたこと

- `npm run check` 緑（263 件・既存の警告 2 件のみ）
- 豊洲（35.6553,139.7967）→ 箱が出る／浦安（35.6540,139.9020）→ 別の資料で出る／春日部（35.9756,139.7523）→ 箱が出ない
- `public/` は変更していない

## Owner 判断が要ること

- 年の太字をやめるか（誤認した 1 名は、そこしか見ていない）
- ※ を先に置くか（いまは記録が先、断りが後）
- 箱が出ない場所で、何か言うか（言うと「無い」を言うことになる）
- 浦安の代表 1 件を、これでよいか

---

## 追記（2026-08-29）── 直して、もう一度測った

2 か所を動かして 2×2 で比べた（375px・明暗）。

| 案 | 年を地点のものとして読んだ | 出た言葉 |
|---|---|---|
| いま（太字・記録が先） | 3 名中 1 名 | 「5 秒では太字の 1974 年しか見ていない」 |
| 案A（太字なし・記録が先） | 3 名中 1 名 | 「数字はどのみち 1 つしかないので、そこを読む」 |
| **案B（太字あり・断りが先）** | **0 名** | 「※を先に読んだので、この場所の話ではないと分かった」 |
| 案C（太字なし・断りが先） | 0 名 | 「情報として弱くなった。何のために出ているのか分からない」 |

効いたのは位置。太字の有無は単独では効かなかった。

**案B を採った**（Owner が絵で確かめて決定）。

```
この周辺について、公式資料から
※この地点に関する記録ではありません。この場所がいつ陸になったかは、この資料からは分かりません。
東京港一帯には、1974年に「13号地外貿定期船ふ頭完成」という記録があります。
出典：東京都港湾局「東京港の歴史」
```

掟 §4-1（できないことから書き始めない）に反する向きだが、§1（誤認させない）が上位。
箱の見出しが先にあるので、箱の 1 行目ではない。

## 合わせて直した

出典のリンクが 154×16px で、44×44 を割っていた（このPRで足した要素）。
字を大きくすると出典が主役になるので、当たり判定だけを広げた（実測 154×45px）。
同じ測り方を 44px と分かっている現在地ボタンに当てて 44 と出ることを確かめてある
（測り方のずれではないことを、別の道で確かめる）。

明暗どちらも撮って確かめた。`npm run check` 緑（263 件・既存の警告 2 件のみ）。

## Owner 判断が残っていること

- 箱が出ない場所で、何か言うか（言うと「無い」を言うことになる）
- 浦安の代表 1 件を、これでよいか（こちらが仮に選んだ）

author: willem445
body:
Closes #1601 — every bullet on that issue (0.1-0.4, the performance.md model update, and committing the plan) ships here.

**Part of #1600**, which stays OPEN: this is Phase 0 of five, and the phases that BOUND anything (single-flight polls, a bounded acquisition, isolating the pty write path, consolidating the lock surface) are 1 through 4. Nothing here bounds, refuses, or changes behaviour.

## Why

Three betas in a row shipped a responsiveness fix derived from *reading* code, and each one relocated the symptom instead of removing it. The reason a reading was the best evidence available is the plan's §2.3: **a hang produces no artifact at all.** `obs` writes a crash log when the process dies, and a process wedged on a mutex does not die — so the total evidence for #1592, #1595 and the beta6 field report was a human saying "it froze".

This PR is the missing artifact, and nothing else. It bounds nothing, refuses nothing, and changes no user-visible behaviour. It exists so the next remedy is chosen against evidence rather than against a story that fits.

The plan states the specification as a sentence:

> One breadcrumb reading *"`mq_state_lock` held 340 s by `queue_merge_with`, 87 waiters, pool in-flight 512"* would have collapsed beta4, beta5 and beta6 into a single diagnosis.

## What changed

**0.1 — `TrackedMutex<T>`** (`crates/loomux-engine/src/lockwatch.rs`). Same poison-tolerant `lock_safe()` signature the call sites already use, so **446 of the 448** in `orchestration/mod.rs` are byte-identical and the migration is a change of field type. (The two that moved are `AUDIT_LOCK.lock_safe()`, forced because a `static` cannot hold a lock that registers itself — measured in *Validation* below.) On acquire it records the thread id, the `#[track_caller]` call site and the acquisition time; the guard clears them on drop; waiters register **before** they block. It returns its own `TrackedGuard` newtype and never exposes `std::sync::MutexGuard`, so Phase 2.1 can swap the inner primitive invisibly.

**0.2 — the self-watchdog** (`crates/loomux-engine/src/selfwatch.rs`). One thread, 1 s cadence, off every hot path, taking no tracked lock and no registry lock. It breadcrumbs a hold past 5 s with the holder's call site, the duration and the waiter count.

**0.3 — blocking-pool depth.** `blocking::spawn_counted` is now the **one door** onto the pool and the only `tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking` call in `src-tauri/src`; all eight hand-off sites route through it. Breadcrumbed at 64 / 128 / 256.

**0.4 — the liveness heartbeat.** The watchdog stamps per tick with its own scheduling lag; the webview stamps through the transport seam (`src/liveness.ts` → `liveness_stamp`) with its timer lag and how late a frame was serviced. Divergence separates GUI-stuck from backend-stuck.

**Docs.** `performance.md` §1.1 names the three scarce resources the model omitted (the shared pool, the MCP threads, acquisition time) and gains §4 X7; `doc/plans/responsiveness-root-cause.md` is committed; `doc/design/self-observability.md` is the mechanism and the decisions worth arguing.

## The scope correction

The plan says `OrchRegistry` carries **17** `Mutex` fields. Measured, it carries **82** — 66 plain and 16 behind an `Arc`. Both columns are measured, not derived (recipe and full table in the committed plan's §6):

| §1.2 says | at blob `b280c2f8` (the plan's own tree) | at blob `005d2e5d` (`main`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 47,035 lines | 47,035 — exact | 54,784 |
| 407 `lock_safe()` sites | 407 — exact | 448 |
| 90 mutexes in the module | 92 | 99 |
| **17** registry `Mutex` fields | **75** — never 17 | **82** |
| zero `try_lock` | 0 — exact | 0 |

Three of the five went stale by a rebase. The fourth was never right, and it is the one that decided scope: 17 is close to the count of `Arc<Mutex<..>>` fields alone (16 today), and taking it at face value would have migrated a fifth of the registry — leaving 65 locks invisible, which is **exactly** the blindness §1.2 blames for the previous audit missing this class ("a long hold on any of the other 15 registry mutexes"). So all 82 are migrated, plus `AUDIT_LOCK`, the per-pane delivery lock, the per-group usage-memo cell, and the engine-side `QueueMap` / `DrainerRegistry` / gh-capture-backlog locks.

The plan file is committed **verbatim** with only its Status line changed; the numbers are corrected in an appended, dated §6 rather than rewritten in place, because rewriting an accepted argument is how a document stops being checkable.

## What acquiring and releasing cost

This is the app's hottest shared path, so the cost is stated rather than asserted. On top of the `Mutex::lock` that was already there — **per acquisition**: two relaxed read-modify-writes on the waiter count, three relaxed stores, one release read-modify-write on the generation, and one monotonic clock read. **Per release**: one clock read, four relaxed loads, four relaxed stores and two release read-modify-writes.

No allocation, no formatting, no global lock, no syscall, and nothing that can block, **on either path**. The global registry is touched at **construction** only, and every byte of every report is composed on the watchdog thread with no tracked lock held — see *Review round 2 / B1*, which is where that last clause came from.

The clock read is the only item above a few nanoseconds. A cheaper design was available and rejected: stamping holds against the watchdog's 1 Hz tick would cost one atomic load and would **floor every reported duration at a second** — on the one instrument whose entire job is to say how long something took.

## Decisions a reviewer should push on

**Two reporters, and they are not redundant.** The guard's `Drop` reports a hold that ended, with the exact total; the watchdog reports one still in flight. `Drop` cannot report a hold that never ends — the beta6 case. The watchdog cannot report one that began and ended between two looks. Together every hold past the threshold is reported by one of the two, and neither depends on the other being wired.

**The observer never takes the lock it observes.** An instrument that waited on the lock it is reporting would be the first casualty of the hang it exists to describe. The holder's fields are therefore published behind a generation counter in the seqlock shape (even = free, odd = held), and the mutex itself serialises the writers, so there is one writer per generation and no CAS loop.

**One door rather than eight wrapped sites.** A depth reading means something only if it is complete: `in-flight 480` is a diagnosis, `in-flight 480 plus however many sites nobody wrapped` is not. Eight wrapped sites is a convention somebody has to remember; one door is a property a scan pins. The ticket is taken **before** the hand-off so the count includes work still *queued* — a counter incremented inside the closure would read 512 at saturation and go no higher, hiding the queue behind it, which is the number the mechanism actually turns on.

**`liveness_stamp` must not delegate.** The pool is one of the two things it measures; delegated, it would stop running exactly when the pool is exhausted and would report the webview stuck on the one occasion it is the only healthy half left. It is `exception`, not `cheap`, because the synchrony is a *requirement* and a future sweep that mechanically converts the `cheap` rows must not take it.

**A hidden window is "no evidence", not "stuck".** The platform throttles a hidden window's timers, so `GuiHidden` is a distinct verdict that writes no breadcrumb. Calling it `GuiStuck` would fire the alarm on every minimize, which is how an instrument stops being read. The residual is stated at the variant: a GUI genuinely wedged while hidden reads as `GuiHidden`, bounded by the human's next interaction un-hiding the window.

**One `unsafe` block**, in `lockwatch::site_of`. The only value ever stored in `holder_site` comes from `Location::caller()` — a reference to a con

Supersedes the two per-package Dependabot PRs OpenSaasAU/stack#1027 and OpenSaasAU/stack#1026, and stops the same split from recurring.

## What changed

- `@opensaas/stack-storage-s3`: bumped `@aws-sdk/client-s3` and `@aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner` from `^3.1084.0` to `^3.1121.0` — both in one change, so the lockfile resolves a single consistent set of `@aws-sdk/*` and `@smithy/*` internals.
- `.github/dependabot.yml`: added an `aws-sdk` group to the npm ecosystem matching `@aws-sdk/*` and `@smithy/*`, so future SDK updates arrive as one PR instead of per-package bumps.
- Changeset: patch for `@opensaas/stack-storage-s3`.

## Why

The AWS SDK v3 packages are released in lockstep and depend on shared `@aws-sdk/*` / `@smithy/*` packages. Bumping `client-s3` and `s3-request-presigner` in separate PRs leaves each branch's lockfile with one package at the new release and the other pinning older shared internals. Grouping them is the durable fix; the version bump here is the one-off catch-up.

## Verification

Run locally on this branch:

- `pnpm exec turbo run test --filter='./packages/*'` — 19/19 tasks pass
- `packages/storage-s3`: `pnpm build` (tsc) clean, `pnpm test` 43/43 pass
- `pnpm manypkg check`, `pnpm lint` (0 errors), `pnpm format:check` all pass

Example app builds were not run here — they fetch Prisma engine binaries, which this sandbox's proxy blocks with a TLS error unrelated to the diff. CI covers them.

author: levidaloca
body:
The payoff the PWA programme was built toward: task pings on the phones committee members installed the app on. Merges dormant like the rest of the push layer, and lights up the moment the VAPID secrets are provisioned.

## The policy: mirror the email, exactly

Any time the task pipeline emails a member, `mirrorTaskEmailToPush` sends the same fact to whatever devices that member has enabled. Having enabled notifications on a device is the opt-in, as native apps behave. That single decision buys three properties for free:

- **No new preference modelling.** `notifications.ts` warns that `channels` means email-address routing, not transport; mirroring sidesteps the trap entirely, and per-category push preferences stay possible later as a sibling field.
- **The config/task-emails kill switch covers push**, because all five routes early-return before their sends when it is off (verified in each route).
- **Volume is bounded by the existing email budget** rather than a new one.

## Wiring

All five send sites, each immediately after its `sendEmail`: added-to-task (batch and single), comments and mentions (the push body carries the comment preview), review requests, review outcomes. After-the-email placement means a failed email pushes nothing; the helper swallows its own failures so a push problem can never mark an email as failed; a recipient with no devices costs one Firestore query; awaited rather than fire-and-forget so Cloud Run cannot reap the sends after the response. Deep links go to the same board URL the email button uses.

## Also here

Two lint escapes fixed (earlier checks piped exit codes through `tail` and lied): PushSettings no longer sets state synchronously in its init effect, and Dropdown's `handleKeyDown` gains the `closeMenu` dependency it acquired in the dismiss rewiring.

## Verification

Build clean, 291 tests pass, lint back to zero errors. The delivery pipeline beneath these call sites was proven end to end earlier tonight in Chromium: a real FCM subscription minted with the dev VAPID key, the declarative envelope sent through `web-push`, and the service worker rendering the notification with the correct icon and click target. The remaining untested leg is these call sites firing on a real task action, which the first task assignment after provisioning demonstrates.

body:
## Summary
- The Rig board's cell-cost tag (icon + number) was hardcoded at font size 14 across both phone and standard modes, rendering at 5.1pt on phone and 9.6pt on iPad mini — both under the project's 11pt legibility floor, and the reason Lee couldn't read the number or its glyph in the 29 Aug playtest.
- Adds `CostFontSize`/`CostFontSizePhone` (20/36) and `CostIconSize`/`CostIconSizePhone` (22/40) to `RigBoardLayout`'s font ladder, wired through `WeaponsScreen` the same way every other node label already is.
- Adds `RigBoardLayout.LabelOffsetYPhone` (ability nodes only, phone mode only) pushing the label down 30 ref-px so the enlarged tag fits the pill-to-label collar (was 22 ref-px, needed ~52+).
- Cost tag box/offset geometry now derives from the font-ladder sizes instead of literals, with icon/text boxes sized so they can never overlap regardless of font size.

## Not implemented (flagged, not silently dropped)
Ticket item 4 / AC7 — swapping the cost-tag glyph back to the PowerCell icon for both owned and unowned states — is **not** implemented. `WeaponHudIcons.PowerCell` caches its sprite under a single fixed key regardless of the requested size, so both states would resolve to the exact same `Sprite` reference. That directly breaks `MV520RigCostAlwaysVisibleTests`'s own guarded assertion that the unlock/upgrade glyphs "must be two distinct sprites, distinguishable without reading the number" (marked sole-guard/do-not-cull). Per this ticket's own AC8 instruction — "if one genuinely conflicts with this change, stop and comment rather than editing it" — the glyph assignment at `WeaponsScreen.cs`'s cost-tag call site is left unchanged. Flagging for Lee's call on which regression should win.

## Evidence
- `CostFontSizePhone` (36) → 36 * (393/1080) = **13.1pt** at real-iPhone scale (matches `CategoryLabelFontSizePhone`).
- `CostFontSize` (20) → 20 * (744/1080) = **13.8pt** at iPad mini scale.
- `CostIconSizePhone` (40) → 40 * (393/1080) = 14.6pt; `CostIconSize` (22) → 22 * (744/1080) = 15.2pt.
- Phone-mode pill-to-label collar: was 22 ref-px, tag now needs ~43px (max of icon 40 / text box 43.2), label pushed down 30 ref-px → new collar 52 ref-px, ~4.4px margin each side (confirmed by the new EditMode test's AC6 assertions).
- Owned/unowned glyphs confirmed unchanged: still `WeaponHudIcons.UpgradeGlyph()` / `UnlockGlyph()` (see "Not implemented" above).
- Full EditMode run: **1655/1655 passed**, 0 failed.
- Visually reviewed `rig-phone.png`, `rig-ipad-mini.png`, `rig-16x9.png` (fresh from this run) — cost numbers/glyphs are now clearly legible on all three, correctly sandwiched between each node's level pill and its ability-name label, no visible overlap or clipping.

## Test plan
- [x] `cc-verify.bat` green (compile, EditMode 1655/1655, Windows standalone build, frame-time gate, UI conformance gate)
- [x] New sole-guard EditMode test `MV620RigCostTagLegibilityTests` covering AC1-6 (rendered-pt floor, parity, font routing, no clipping, no overlap)
- [x] Regression `MV520RigCostAlwaysVisibleTests` still passes unmodified (AC8)
- [x] Opened and visually compared `rig-contact-sheet.png` / `rig-phone.png` / `rig-ipad-mini.png` / `rig-16x9.png` against expected layout

body:
## Historical commit reference `6d0cf96f6f56e214a7d6724920d91e5166beef63` — *"feat(ui): establish accessible design system foundation"*, authored 2026-08-25, parent `5d66dea`. It has **never been released** (lived only on `homolog/meta-consent-hardening`). author: sucheet2000
body:
## Please read this first

**The notebook has not been run against the live API.** The transcription and projection cells have not executed; every cell output is empty. The matcher itself — canonicaliser, folding rules, ranking bands, renames handling — is plain standard library with **177 tests that run and pass today**.

## The problem

A caller says *Nagar*. The roster says *Ahilyanagar*. The transcript is in Devanagari, the database is in Latin script, the same village romanizes six ways (oo/u, ee/i, v/w, -pur/-pura), and some districts have been renamed outright. Matching spoken place names against a canonical roster is where kisan call centres, delivery routing and field surveys quietly go wrong — and a wrong district is misdirected help.

## The design decision that matters most

**Under confidence, it asks — it never guesses.** Candidates rank into three bands (`MATCH` / `ASK` / `NO_MATCH`, named constants). In the middle band the output is a clarifying question naming the top candidates. A silent wrong match is the failure mode this exists to prevent.

## Both scripts come from the speech API itself

The speech endpoint's `mode` Literal includes `transcribe` (native script) and `translit` (the same utterance in Latin script) — verified by live introspection and pinned by a standalone test. So one clip transcribed twice gives both projections directly; no post-hoc transliteration step to introduce its own errors. The roster side is projected with the transliterate endpoint once and cached.

## Folding that respects minimal pairs

Indian romanization variants fold (`Balrampur`/`Balrampura`, `Kanpur`/`Cawnpore`-era spellings, oo/u, ee/i, v/w) — but the canonicaliser is tested in **both directions**: what must fold, and what must never merge. Dropping a single folding rule fails 3–5 tests; the minimal pairs the spec names stay distinct under every rule.

## Facts, stated as facts

- The **renames table** carries only verified official renames with their years (Prayagraj 2018, Ahilyanagar 2024, and peers). Anything uncertain was dropped rather than guessed.
- The **roster** is forty real district and tehsil names across four states in native script and Latin — public facts, no licensing question, and the README says plainly it is a demonstrative sample, not a gazetteer.

## Tests

**177 tests**, written first and watched failing, including 19 standalone guard traps (the mode Literal by live introspection, difflib determinism). Mutation testing:

```
MATCH_THRESHOLD 0.9 -> 0.70    CAUGHT (2 failed)
MATCH_THRESHOLD 0.9 -> 0.99    CAUGHT (4 failed)
ASK_THRESHOLD 0.6 -> 0.40      CAUGHT (2 failed)
ASK_THRESHOLD 0.6 -> 0.80      CAUGHT (3 failed)
drop oo->u fold                CAUGHT (3 failed)
drop ee->i fold                CAUGHT (5 failed)
```

6 of 6 caught, 0 holes — both thresholds armoured in both directions.

One test defect found and fixed during verification, in the open: a recipe-wide scan read the `__pycache__` its own import had created and crashed on non-UTF-8 bytes; the walk now skips compiled artifacts, which never ship.

## Checks

```
python3 -m pytest tests/ -q                                            259 passed
python3 scripts/validate_recipe.py examples/kisan-village-matcher --strict   PASS, 0 errors
python3 scripts/ci_validate.py --base-ref main                         PASS, 0 errors (committed diff)
```

The matcher module imports only stdlib (`difflib`, `re`, `unicodedata`, `dataclasses`). The API layer lives in a separate small module whose `build_client()` reads the key at call time and passes it explicitly — the SDK evaluates `os.getenv` at import as a default argument, so the import-then-load_dotenv pattern silently fails. Plain UTF-8, no BOM, no emoji, empty outputs.

## Overlap

No open PR or issue covers place-name matching. #150 owns romanized *input* round-trips (chat); this is roster matching with confidence bands, a different mechanism for a different failure. The Travel Planner example uses transliterate for display, not matching.

author: vsharlay
body:
## Summary

Backend service for a third-party "Receipts" module — scans a photo/PDF receipt with a vision model (Gemini or Claude, admin supplies the key once), the household reviews/corrects the extraction, then tracks spend by category, item, and merchant over time.

This is the companion-service half described in [MODULES.md](../blob/main/MODULES.md)'s "Modules With A Backend Service" section. The module's client UI half is intentionally **not** in this PR — `modules/*` is already gitignored by this repo, since third-party module UIs aren't meant to live in core.

No core file is touched (nothing under `server/` or `public/` changed). The service owns its own SQLite database and image storage; it never opens `yuvomi.db`. It verifies every request by forwarding the caller's Yuvomi session cookie to the real `GET /api/v1/auth/me` and trusts only that response for identity/role.

## Changes

- `services/receipt-tracker/src/index.js` + `routes/`: settings (vision provider/model/key, admin-only writes), scan (upload → vision extraction, held for review before persisting), receipts (search/CRUD, per-item edit/delete), stats (category/item/merchant/time breakdowns), merchant-groups (roll up e.g. "ShopRite of Bayonne" + "ShopRite of Metro Plaza" under one name for reporting), export (CSV)
- `src/auth.js`: session verification against Yuvomi's own `/api/v1/auth/me`, never a client-supplied user id
- `src/csrf.js`: independent double-submit CSRF (Yuvomi's own CSRF token protects Yuvomi's endpoints, not a module's)
- `src/providers/`: Gemini and Claude behind one interface (`extract`, `listModels`, `classifyItems`, `classifyMerchants`)
- `dev-proxy.js`: local stand-in for the reverse-proxy rule a real deployment needs (routes `/api/extensions/receipt-tracker/*` here, everything else to Yuvomi) — dev tooling only, not part of the running service

## Deployment

Runs as a sibling container in `docker-compose.yml` next to the existing `yuvomi` service, plus one added reverse-proxy rule for `/api/extensions/receipt-tracker/*`. Yuvomi's own image and upgrade path are unaffected either way.

## Checklist

- [ ] `npm test` passes — not run against this change; it's additive and touches no file the suite covers, and the suite doesn't exercise anything under `services/`
- [x] Follows CONTRIBUTING.md conventions
- [x] No new frontend dependencies (Yuvomi's own `public/` frontend is untouched; this is a separate backend service with its own dependency tree, per MODULES.md's guidance for backend-service modules)
- [ ] UI strings use `t('key')` — N/A, this PR is backend-only (no UI strings)
- [ ] CHANGELOG.md updated — not updated; core's shipped behavior doesn't change

author: adammarquette
body:
Closes #87

## What changed and why

SignalR automatic reconnect mints a new connection id, so server-side hub subscriptions are gone. Both hub `Reconnected` handlers only logged and published `Connected`, which left the client reporting healthy while delivering nothing — silent, plausible, and permanent. The client now records each successful `SubscribeTo*`, re-invokes the set against the new connection *before* publishing `Connected`, and raises `MessageSendFailed` / `Failed` if restore does not succeed. `MarketSubscriptions` and `UserSubscriptions` expose the recorded sets so a consumer can verify recovery.

## How it was verified

- Wrote the failing unit suite first in `HubReconnectResubscribeTests`: a `FakeHubConnection` raises the SignalR `Reconnected` callback (no socket). The tests failed on the empty handler (one invoke, not two; no `MessageSendFailed`; empty snapshot).
- After the registry + restore, the same tests are green: recorded subscribes are re-invoked, `Connected` is not published until restore has run, a failed restore raises `MessageSendFailed` and reports `Failed`, unsubscribed and failed-original subscribes are not replayed.
- `dotnet test MarqSpec.Client.ProjectX.Tests -c Release`: 202 passed on net8.0 and net10.0 (plus the new reconnect facts).
- `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` clean; `dotnet build -c Release` clean on both target frameworks, 0 warnings.

- [x] `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` clean
- [x] `dotnet build -c Release` clean on **both** target frameworks, warnings-as-errors on
- [x] Unit tests green
- [ ] Integration tests green against the fake gateway (no credentials required) — QA owns this tier; see the note on #87

## Checklist

- [x] **Test-first** — the new test failed before the implementation; a bug fix reproduces the bug first
- [x] **Docs in lockstep** — R-5.3, the architecture Real-time paragraph, and the library README reconnect / property sections
- [x] **No secrets** — nothing logged, nothing tracked, no credential-shaped value in a committed file

author: srikat
body:
Fixes #2.

`X_CLASS` was the literal `chrome-x.com__-Default` and both lookups compared it with `.class==$c`. Omarchy derives a webapp window class from the browser binary, the host and path, and the profile directory, so that string is correct only for a Chrome user on the default profile. Under Brave the window is `brave-x.com__-Default`; a secondary profile gives `...-Profile_2`.

The failure mode is worse than a no-op: `find_x` returns empty, `resolve` reports no window, and every toggle falls through to `launch_or_reuse`, which spawns a fresh X window and polls 40 times at 0.3s for a class that never appears. That is a 12-second hang, `failed to launch X window`, exit 1, and one orphaned browser window per keypress.

This switches to an anchored regex over the Chromium family with any profile suffix, and uses `test($c)` in both `find_x` and the pid-based branch of `resolve`. The `// ""` guard keeps a window with no class from erroring the jq filter.

## Verification

Match behaviour against real classes from this machine:

```
brave-x.com__-Default            -> true
chrome-x.com__-Default           -> true
brave-x.com__-Profile_2          -> true
brave-web.whatsapp.com__-Default -> false
chromium                         -> false
```

End to end on Brave, the window is now found and reused rather than relaunched:

```
$ omarchy-x-panel toggle     # launches, adopts
class=brave-x.com__-Default  ws=Main floating=true pinned=true
$ omarchy-x-panel hide
ws=special:sidepanelX pinned=false
$ omarchy-x-panel toggle     # same window comes back, session intact
ws=Main floating=true pinned=true
```

author: tlapik123
body:
Fixes #65 

- `chattr +C` on `LIMA_HOME` right after its `mkdir`, before `limactl create` — NOCOW is inherited at file creation, so the disk image gets it from birth.
- Linux-only, `check=False`: on ext4/xfs chattr just fails silently.
- Only helps new VMs — existing images must be migrated by hand:

```bash
locki vm stop
chattr +C ~/.local/state/locki/lima ~/.local/state/locki/lima/locki
cd ~/.local/state/locki/lima/locki
cp --reflink=never --sparse=always disk disk.nocow
mv disk disk.old && mv disk.nocow disk
# boot the VM, verify, then: rm disk.old

- Note: btrfs snapshots re-CoW NOCOW files once per snapshot — if you snapshot ~/.local/state, put the lima dir on its own subvolume.

body:
## What

**T-0296 — the rest of the scene month.** The four Chicago Democrats printed *after* the
scene date — **1835-07-08 (Vol. II No. 12, PARTIAL), 07-15 (No. 13), 07-22 (No. 14) and
07-29 (No. 15)** — read end to end through the T-0257 schema. Piece 2 of 4 of T-0260.

**60 claims**, one extraction file per issue, plus a declared coverage range for
1835-07-08 to 1835-07-29 so the gate asserts the range rather than counting files.

## Acceptance, stated before working and not weakened

| clause | result |
|---|---|
| all four issues have an extraction file, coverage asserted by the gate | ✅ `59 issue(s) inside 13 declared coverage range(s), none missing` |
| letter lists in full where legible, post office on the claim, hand count in the PR | ✅ five lists, all out-of-county, all recorded, none minted — counts below |
| every claim passes the T-0257 gate, quotes reassembled character for character | ✅ `773 quote(s) reassembled from the transcription and identical` |
| the gazetteer recompiles green; new merges carry `merge_rule` | ✅ rebuilt; **no** new `identity.json` merges were needed |
| the PR states counts | below |

## Counts

**Claims: 60** — 07-08: 20 · 07-15: 7 · 22: 15 · 29: 18.
By kind: business 28, notice 9, infrastructure 7, person 5 (the letter lists), building 4,
shipping 3, price 2, event 2.

**Persons: 35 touched, 21 of them new to the corpus** — A. B. Field, Chas. L. Bristol,
Cooley and Halsman, D. S. Dewey, E. D. Taylor, George Hall, George W. Dole, H. B. Clarke,
H. Crocker, James Whitlock, Joseph Duncan, Joseph Lafrombois, L. G. Curtiss, O. I. Thompson,
Peter Pruyne, Rev. Mr. Blackwell, Robert Dixon, Russell E. Heacock, Stephen E. Dow,
William Jones, Wm. Hogue. **letter-list-only: 0** — see below.

**Businesses: 15 touched.** Placement classes across the 30 claims that carry a `business`
(the 28 of kind `business`, plus the two dissolution notices):
`relative` 7, `corner` 1, `street_only` 6, `none` 16.

Placed storefronts, best first:

- **Russell E. Heacock**, counsellor and attorney at law — *`corner`* — "Office in the 2d
  story, opposite the Exchange, corner of Lake and Franklin-sts."
- **Cooley and Halsman**, tailors — *`relative`* — a shop on Dearborn Street, "nearly
  opposite the Eagle Coffee House". Announces an opening, so **not** a shop standing on 1 July.
- **W. Montgomery**, auction and commission — *`relative`* — David Carver's old stand,
  South Water Street; corroborated on 07-22 by "received at Montgomery's Auction Room,
  South Water Street".
- **L. G. Curtiss**, deputy surveyor of Cook County — *`relative`* — orders left at the
  Mansion House. The second witness reads a different house; the disagreement is recorded.
- **John Dean Caton**, attorney — *`street_only`*, Dearborn Street.
- **Samuel Lewis**, music school and piano tuning — *`street_only`*, a room on south Water street.
- **the Dearborn Street auction and commission rooms** — *`street_only`* — "rented the New
  Store on Dearborn Street", 27 July. Announces an opening; the proprietor's signature is
  too far gone to name and `entities` is therefore empty.

**Ruling 3's only veto in the range:** the dissolution of **Wm. Hogue & Co.**, advertised in
both 07-22 and 07-29 over three signatures. Both claims carry `contradicts: true` and the
compiler now reports the house `built_at_scene_date: false` — computed, not asserted.

## The letter lists — hand counts, and why nothing is minted

**No Chicago post-office letter list stands anywhere in the four issues.** Swept all four
for every form the Democrat uses — *list of letters*, *letters remaining*, *remaining in the
post office*, *uncalled for*, a signature ending *P. M.* — for **five hits, every one an
out-of-county return of the quarter day 1 July 1835**:

| list | printed | reprinted | postmaster | hand count |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hennepin, Putnam co. | 07-08 | 07-15, 07-22 | Thos. Galaher, jr. | **38** complete entries in the right alphabetical column; left column's surnames sheared by the crop; printed list ~80 |
| Plainfield | 07-08 | 07-15, 07-22 | L. F. Arnold | **22** complete, same shear |
| Du Page | 07-08 | 07-15, 07-22 | J. H. Giddings | **8** complete, same shear |
| Juliet | 07-22 | 07-29 | A. W. Bowen | **91** counted by hand, 46 left column + 45 right — **legible whole** |

All five are recorded with their verbatim text and their post office on the claim, and
**none of them mints a person.** Two reasons, both on the record: under ruling 1 a
letter-list name mints a resident candidate for *the town whose office printed the list*,
and none of these is Chicago's — which is the treatment T-0292 gave the out-of-county lists
of October 1834; and under T-0299 a list printed three times is one cohort, not three.

A finding worth keeping: for the Hennepin/Plainfield/Du Page block the **two witnesses are
complementary and neither is sufficient**. The 07-08 deposit printing is clean but the
segmenter sheared the left alphabetical column's surnames off; the 07-15 rebuild carries
both columns whole but at the weakest name-level quality in the corpus. That is written into
c018 and c007 so the next pass does not rediscover it.

## What the reading adds to the town

- **The Eagle Coffee House** is corroborated twice over — the Democratic citizens of Chicago
  Precinct meet there on Friday 24 July, and a tailor's shop stands nearly opposite it on
  Dearborn Street.
- **A reading room proposed for the Public Square**: the board of the Chicago Reading Room
  resolved to seek a joint stock company that would appropriate about **$2,000** for a
  building on the square, containing the reading room and usable as a meeting or lecture
  room. **Proposed, not standing** — the claim says so in as many words and nothing in the
  model may stand on it.
- **A Baptist meeting house** in Chicago, holding a school-district election on the evening
  of Saturday 11 July.
- **A large dwelling house lately erected** and standing empty (E. K. Hubbard letting it,
  street cut away at the crop and *not* supplied), and **a good store to let** in John T.
  Temple's gift.
- The land office's hour on 3 August, on which the three witnesses **disagree** (nine in the
  best text, ten in the other two) and which is left disagreeing rather than tidied.

## Provenance discipline in this PR

- Every claim carries `reading: transcription_mediated`. Quotes are **assembled from the
  transcription by tooling**, never typed, which is why 773 of 773 reassemble identically.
- 07-08 is read from the reconciled **deposit** `.txt`; the other three from the committed
  derived text. All four resolve on `dev` since the T-0275 back-merge, so every quote is
  machine-checked *here* rather than only on `main`.
- **07-08 is PARTIAL** — issue page 4 is absent from the source PDF. The extraction file and
  the coverage note both say so; the issue is declared read because every page that exists
  was read.
- **No person is minted from a crop-edge name.** The Chicago Reading Room's committee and
  secretary, the second auctioneer's signature, the note-repudiating "HENR:", the millwright
  advertiser and the settling agent of Wm. Hogue & Co. are all left unminted, with the
  reason on each claim. Uncertain readings stay inside `[uncertain: …]`; `[…]` marks absence
  and never supplies.
- `data/datum.json` untouched. No GLB touched — this is a data-and-text unit and
  `needs_bake` is false.

                                       773 quote(s) reassembled and identical
                                       1972 person(s), 177 business(es), compile deterministic

author: lawrenceli0228
body:
Reported as "the site looks washed out next to my local player". It is not a
rendering bug in the player and it is not the file: Chrome composites
`<video>` — and only `<video>` — through a transfer conversion that lifts the
midtones while pinning black and white.

## What is actually happening

Measured against ffmpeg's decode with a 16-step greyscale wedge, on a file
carrying no colour signalling at all (no `colr` atom, VUI unspecified — the
normal shape of a Baha / ANi WEB-DL):

| source | ffmpeg | Chrome | | source | ffmpeg | Chrome |
|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 0 | 0 | | 136 | 136 | 147 |
| 17 | 17 | 16 | | 170 | 170 | 179 |
| 51 | 51 | 58 | | 204 | 203 | 210 |
| 102 | 102 | 114 | | 255 | 255 | 255 |

Mean absolute error 7 levels, peaking at +12. The ends are nailed down and the
middle is flattened, which is exactly what reads as grey. mpv, IINA and VLC do
not apply the conversion, so the same file is more contrasty there.

**The player itself was innocent.** A colour-band clip rendered through
`/player` and through a bare `<video>` came out byte-identical on all six
patches, the video's computed style is `filter:none / opacity:1 /
mixBlendMode:normal`, and the only element stacked over it (`.art-bottom`) is
`opacity: 0` during playback.

## Why this hid so well

The decode is correct — reading the frame back with
`canvas.drawImage(video)` matches ffmpeg to within 2 levels. Only the
composited output is shifted, so **every way of inspecting the pixels from
JavaScript says the picture is fine**. It has to be caught with a screenshot,
against a CSS swatch of the same nominal colour as a control — the swatch
comes out exact, which is what proves the shift is video-specific rather than
an artefact of the capture path.

Two fixes that sound right and are not:

- **Tagging the file.** The same bitstream stream-copied into untagged /
  BT.709 / sRGB-TRC variants renders identically. Chrome does not listen to
  the tags here.
- **The display colour profile.** `--force-color-profile=srgb` is identical to
  the default; `--force-color-profile=display-p3-d65` shifts video *and* CSS
  together, while the defect is video shifting and CSS not.

## The correction: measured, not derived

The analytic BT.709 → sRGB model predicts a large shadow lift Chrome does not
actually apply — it predicts 17 → 32, Chrome leaves it at 16. Fitting a single
`feFunc type="gamma"` exponent to the midtones therefore over-darkens the
bottom end; 1.136 is the best power fit and it still crushed code 17 to 10.

The committed table is the inverse of the *measured* curve. Put back through
Chrome:

| | mean abs error vs ffmpeg | code 17 |
|---|---:|---:|
| uncorrected | 7.00 | 16 |
| best gamma fit (1.136) | 1.44 | 10 |
| **this table** | **0.31** | **16** |

End to end on the reported file, same frame, same geometry, only the filter
changing (`.art-bottom` hidden so the control gradient does not pollute the
statistics):

| | mean R/G/B | saturation |
|---|---|---|
| ffmpeg reference | 122.8 / 108.9 / 85.4 | 37.5% |
| before | 133.7 / 118.4 / 92.6 | 36.8% |
| after | 124.4 / 109.2 / 84.5 | 37.9% |

`contrast()` / `saturate()` cannot do this — contrast pivots on mid-grey and
measured 140, unmoved. CSS `filter` has no gamma or table primitive; only SVG
filters do.

## Cost

None measurable. Six alternating 20s runs at 1920x1080 with 4000 danmaku and
the ASS overlay up: **zero dropped frames in every run**, filter or not. The
late-frame counts climb monotonically with run order regardless of the filter
(an unfiltered run scored worse than a filtered one), so that drift is machine
load rather than the correction. A single run had suggested otherwise.

## Two details that are load-bearing

- **The fullscreen rule now names both filters.** `filter` is a single
  property, so leaving it as `opacity(0.999)` alone would silently drop the
  correction in fullscreen only — the hardest case to notice and the one
  people actually watch in. `opacity()` is kept rather than assumed redundant:
  it is what blocks hardware-overlay promotion and so what fixes the subtitle
  flicker (#24), and that has not been re-verified against a `url()` filter
  alone.
- **`color-interpolation-filters="sRGB"`.** The SVG default is linearRGB,
  which would apply the table in the wrong space entirely.

The filter is scoped to the `<video>` element. The jassub subtitle canvas and
the danmaku layer are drawn by us in sRGB and never went through Chrome's
video path, so correcting them would introduce the error this removes.

Chrome-only by decision, not feature-detected: Safari and Firefox handle the
video transfer differently and were not measured.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test` — 1761 pass, 0 fail
- [x] `bunx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `node scripts/ci/eslint-ratchet.mjs` — OK
- [x] `node scripts/ci/assert-isr.mjs` — PASS
- [x] `next build --webpack` — succeeds
- [x] Verified in a production build of `/player`, real Chrome, real file:
      computed filter is `url("#animego-video-transfer")`, the definition is
      present with `sRGB` interpolation and three `table` functions, and the
      colour bands move 139 → 127 at 50% grey
- [x] Playback cost measured (above)
- [ ] Eyeball check against a desktop player — the numbers say the picture is
      back at the reference, but "does it look right" is not something a
      histogram answers

`videoTransferFilter.test.ts` pins the id across the two files, the presence of
both filters in the fullscreen rule, and the shape of the table. A
`filter: url(#id)` whose target is missing renders the video uncorrected
without any error — verified, Chrome does not hide the element — so a rename on
either side would otherwise be completely silent.

author: theaggressive
body:
The contract, from the template, the way P3 through P10 were. **No implementation** — the document says so.

P10 already defined `viewable` and placed it after `served`. Nothing writes it. This phase is the client measurement, the beacon that carries it, and the server rule that it may only follow a real fill.

## Three things the contract settles that the roadmap line does not

**Viewability is client-attested, and the document says so plainly.** The browser is the only thing that knows what was on screen, so the number is not trustworthy against an adversary — pretending otherwise would be worse than useless.

What the server *does* control is stated instead: a `viewable` must carry a signed token bound to a real fill, that token must already have recorded a `served`, and it can be spent exactly once. A dishonest client can inflate viewability only as far as it could already inflate fills. **No new leverage.**

**The same beacon route, not a second one.** It carries the same token, needs the same per-client bound, and a separate endpoint is another thing to authorize and forget to rate limit. Sending no event type still records `served`, so a cached page running the previous script keeps reporting.

**Historical rows are not backfilled, deliberately.** A day before this shipped has no viewability data, and projecting zero would be indistinguishable from "nothing was seen". Reporting must say *not measured* — an exit criterion, not a nicety.

## Scope boundary

Viewability stays **out of the decision engine**. A vCPM goal is P6 vocabulary and a later decision; no stage may read this without amending that contract. Same split that stopped P3 swallowing five phases.

Also out: conversions and view-through (P12), the analytics schema (P13), and cross-domain/in-iframe measurement — native fill paints into the host page, which is why this is measurable at all.

## Why the evidence section looks different

This is the first phase whose correctness lives in the browser, so the Playwright lane is named authoritative alongside the Docker ones. The suite that found five inert stages this session **cannot see an observer that never fires** — and "the client called the beacon" is not evidence the event was recorded. The contract says to assert the row.

Docs only. `qa:fast` clean.

author: drdmytrush90
body:
Closes #65. Pairs with `gitops-flux` PR pinning `keyrenewperiod: "0"`.

## What this changes

| Section | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| §4 `Refresh` | Monthly, and after any controller key renewal | Once, then immediately after any deliberate key rotation |
| §5 rotation row | Every 30 days — automatic; back up afterwards | Not on a schedule — deliberate rotation only; back up immediately afterwards |

Plus a paragraph under §5 recording why, and what should now trigger a rotation
given nothing does automatically.

## Why the old wording was right and still wrong

§5 was **accurate**. The chart leaves `keyrenewperiod` empty, and empty is not
"off" — the controller reads it as its own 30-day default:

```
helm show values sealed-secrets --repo https://bitnami.github.io/sealed-secrets --version 2.19.1
# keyrenewperiod: ""   ## Default 30 days. To disable use "0", with quotes!
```

So the unset field was already a policy of monthly renewal, and §5 described it
correctly.

It is the wrong policy. Automatic renewal is safe only when every renewal is
followed by a backup: the controller retains superseded keys in etcd, but the
Secrets Manager copy is point-in-time. Miss one month and the newest active key
is back to existing in exactly one place — the precise failure §4 exists to
prevent. Given the backup has never been taken once (`gitops-flux#16`), a
recurring manual obligation was never a real control.

## Draft, and why

**Do not merge this alone.** It must land with the `gitops-flux` HelmRelease
change, or this document asserts something untrue in one direction or the other.
That change is itself gated on the key backup being taken and the restore
tested, because it triggers a Helm upgrade and a controller restart.

Order: backup → restore test → both PRs together.

## Follow-up

`runbooks/sealed-secrets-key-backup-and-restore.md` (PR #63, not yet merged)
Prevention step 0 says the decision is open and to assume monthly. That is
accurate today and becomes stale the moment the pin lands — it gets corrected
once #63 merges, rather than churning a PR that is under review.

author: teinhonglo
body:
### Motivation

- Implement scheduled generated-ASR loss weighting during finetuning so models can gradually incorporate model-generated transcripts as training targets for MAC-SLU.
- Provide data-preparation tooling to generate Qwen3-ASR transcripts and embed them into MAC-SLU JSONL records for scheduled-prefix training.
- Support LoRA/QLoRA finetuning workflows and make checkpoints inferable with saved processor/tokenizer/generation artifacts and prompt.

### Description

- Add `finetuning/qwen3_asr_sft_scheduled_asr_prefix.py` which implements a `ScheduledASRPrefixTrainer` that linearly schedules the weight of a generated-ASR loss term, custom data collators `DataCollatorForQwen3ASRScheduledPrefix` and `DataCollatorForQwen3ASRFinetuning`, LoRA/QLoRA handling, checkpoint handling, and helpers to make every checkpoint inferable and save the best checkpoint.
- Add `local/prepare_macslu_scheduled_asr_prefix.py` which loads a Qwen3-ASR model to transcribe batches of MAC-SLU audio, writes `generated_asr_text` and replaces the `asr_text` field in the canonical JSON payload stored in `text` to produce `text_asr` in the output JSONL.
- Add `run_macslu_scheduled_asr_prefix.sh` to orchestrate dataset prep, ASR generation, scheduled-prefix finetuning, inference and evaluation stages for MAC-SLU experiments.
- Add `conf/macslu_qwen3_asr_17b_ep20_lora_woemblmhead_scheduled_asr_prefix.json` containing a sample training + model configuration including LoRA settings and `scheduled_asr_prefix` schedule parameters.

### Testing

- No automated tests were executed as part of this PR; CI should validate imports, linting and run any repository test suite after merge.

author: agustin-y2k
body:
## Qué trae

**RF-08.17 — salida a reparación.** Un equipo en mantenimiento o fuera de servicio ya no sale del laboratorio en una entrega común: rebota diciendo por qué. Para sacarlo está su propio panel, que exige decir a dónde va. Lo dado de baja no sale ni así. Y `FUERA_DE_SERVICIO` deja de ser terminal: una máquina que se arregla vuelve a circular.

Lo demás salió de probar el sistema **contra el inventario real de la escuela** —91 equipos en tres carros— donde aparecen cosas que con ocho equipos de prueba no se ven:

- **Los avisos decían «PC 4» a secas.** El identificador es el número del zócalo, así que «PC 4» existe una vez por carro. Ahora dicen «PC 4 del Carro 1», y cuando son varias del mismo carro se dice una sola vez al final.
- **El motivo repetía el nombre del equipo** y gritaba el valor del enum. Ahora: «el equipo quedó en mantenimiento».
- **Un pedido de materia no decía qué materia era ni quién la pedía**, y su fecha se corría un día por tomar el día en UTC.
- **«Ver contraseña» contestaba 500 «error interno»** cuando lo guardado no se descifra con la `CUENTAS_SECRET` que corre. Ahora es 409 con la explicación que el servicio ya armaba.
- **El perfil listaba materias que no dictás.**
- **Elegir equipos era tildar de a uno**: 60 casillas en una reserva, 85 en un bloqueo. Ahora hay buscador y «marcar el carro entero» en las tres listas.
- **Se aprobaba una cuenta a ciegas** desde Usuarios, sin ver qué pidió dictar y sin ofrecer «Rechazar».
- **En un teléfono la lista de equipos escondía sus acciones** detrás de un gesto lateral. Abajo de 640px son tarjetas.
- **El panel de «Cómo entrar» se abría al final de la lista**, treinta filas más abajo del equipo del que salía.
- **El calendario no decía de qué equipo era** y su salida era el botón menos visible de la pantalla.
- **`PATCH /equipos/{id}` aceptaba `estado` y lo descartaba en silencio.**

## Documentación

Las dos guías tenían texto que había dejado de ser cierto. Se actualizaron y se regeneraron las 46 capturas de las guías y las 12 del README contra una base recreada con datos neutros. Los datos de demostración crean ahora un pedido de materia sin resolver: ese capítulo venía ilustrado con una pantalla vacía desde que existe.

## Despliegue

**Sin cambios de esquema ni de `.env`.** Se espera `no migrations to run. current version: 2`.

| ドメイン | `errors.New` 24件 → `NewDomainErrorCode(<センチネル>, "napoleonssquare.err*", nil)`（同じ文面は1キーを共有し17キーに整理）。フェーズ違いだけ `ErrWrongPhase`、盤の状態による拒否は `ErrInvalidPlay` |
| バックエンド locale | `internal/i18n/locales/{ja,en}/napoleonssquare.json` に17キー |
| **フロントエンド locale** | `frontend/src/i18n/locales/{ja,en}/common.json` の `messageCode` に同じ文言で登録。Web は messageCode を**クライアント側で解決**するので、ここに無いと生のキーが画面に出ます |
| **Web presenter** | `Error()` を message に入れていたのを、コードがあれば `messageCode` として渡す形に (#5553) |
| テスト | ドメイン / CUI / Web の3面 |

## テスト

- **ドメイン**: 公開の入口ごとに拒否がキーを名乗ること。**文言ではなくコード**を見ています
- **CUI**: ja で日本語・en で英語が出て、**反対の言語が漏れていない**こと
- **Web**: コード付きは `messageCode` に、**コード無しは今までどおり `message` に**（否定コントロール）

**否定コントロールを3件とも実施し、1件が空振りだったので直しました。** Web と CUI は一発で落ちましたが、ドメインのテストは代表6経路しか踏んでおらず、`MoveWasteToTableau` / `MoveWasteToFoundation` の拒否を**一度も通っていませんでした**（そこを `errors.New` に戻しても緑のまま）。2ケース追加して、同じ変異で3本落ちることを確認しています。

`go test -tags test ./internal/...` 全パッケージ ok / `bun run check` 通過（ja/en 差分ゼロ、17キーすべてフロントに登録済み・文言一致）/ `golangci-lint` 0 issues。

body:
## Goal
Make BuildNumbers feel like a clear construction-planning product instead of a wall of calculators.

### Homepage product story
- first screen now explains what BuildNumbers is, who it is for, and what users can produce

### Calculator Library

- filters for Concrete & foundations, Interiors & finishes, and Masonry & landscape

### Scale architecture
- central `lib/calculator-catalog.ts` registry for calculator identity, routes, guides, groups, descriptions, and search vocabulary
- homepage no longer renders the full 13-tool directory; the scalable library owns discovery
- desktop/mobile navigation routes to `/calculators`
- footer and sitemap expose the library

### QA
- product-led homepage tests protect definition, audience, how-to-use flow, starting paths, Project Mode, and readable responsive design
- catalog integrity tests enforce 13 unique tool IDs/routes/guides and expected grouping
- calculator library SSR/navigation regressions
- full typecheck/lint/unit/rendered/build/dependency gate

author: s4k10503
body:
`Given_ExplicitResourceKey_When_InlineLambdaFactoryReRenders_Then_DoesNotWarn` carried no assertion,
and the comment standing in for one — "No LogAssert.Expect — any leaked warning fails the test" —
described a mechanism the test framework does not have for a warning.

It is worse than an absent assertion, and this is the part the issue did not have: the case arranged
none of what it is named for either. `ExplicitResourceKeyFactoryRender`'s factory read only static
fields, so the C# compiler caches the lambda in a static field and it has **one identity for the life
of the process**. Measured: deleting `resourceKey: "stable-key"` from that component leaves the whole
fixture green and logs no additional warning, because the factory identity the warning is gated on
never changed. The sibling that does warn,
`Given_NoResourceKey_When_InlineLambdaFactoryReRenders_Then_WarnsOnSecondRender`, captures the
render-local `tick`, which is what makes its lambda fresh.

The factory now captures `tick` too, so it is a new delegate each render and only the key can name
the same resource. Three cases stand where the empty one did:

- `Given_AnExplicitKeyBesideAFreshLambdaEachRender_When_ReRendered_Then_TheFactoryRunsOnce` — what the
  hatch delivers. The mount run rides along in the tuple, because a count of one after the re-render
  alone also holds for a resource that never started at mount and started there.
- `Given_AnExplicitKey_When_TheFactoryIdentityChanges_Then_NoWarningIsLogged` — the same arrangement,
  read from the console rather than from the factory. The key matches, so the resource is reused and
  the branch the warning lives in is not entered.
- `Given_AnExplicitKeyThatChangesEachRender_When_ReRendered_Then_NoWarningIsLogged` — the warning's own
  `!resourceKeyExplicit` gate, which nothing reached. A matching explicit key takes the key-equal
  branch and never gets there; reaching it needs an explicit key that *differs* across renders, so the
  resource is rebuilt and the caller chose the key. Measured: deleting `!resourceKeyExplicit &&` from
  `UseCore` leaves all 4189 cases green without this one, and fails only this one with it.

The first two go red when `resourceKey` is removed from that component, where the case they replace
stayed green — measured, and the warning count over the fixture goes from one to three at the same
time. `LogAssert.NoUnexpectedReceived()` does catch the leaked warning; what does not is the implicit
failing-log path the deleted comment appealed to.

`s_explicitKeyFactoryRender` goes with them: it counted component renders, nothing read it, and the
count the hatch is about is of factory runs.

No `Documentation~` guide changes: the escape hatch's behaviour is unchanged, only what the suite
says about it.

Closes #767

author: jburns3141
body:
From the 0.2.0 project review, non-security finding **P3**.

## Problem

`[workspace.package] rust-version = "1.85"` declares the MSRV, and the `test` / `bench` / `live-activemq` jobs each hardcode `1.85.0`, so the floor is only checked as a side effect. Nothing asserts it — a `1.86`-only API could land unnoticed and `rust-version` would silently become wrong.

## Change

New `msrv` job in `ci.yml`:

- reads the version from `Cargo.toml` (`grep -m1 '^rust-version' | sed ...`) so it can't drift from the declared value,
- `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` at that version,
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked`.

Runs in parallel with `test`; it's a check, not a gate on the others.

## Verification

- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked` passes locally on `rustc 1.85.0` (the `rust-toolchain.toml` pin).
- `ci.yml` parses; new job wired as `jobs.msrv`.

Closes #38.

author: dotcoocoo
body:
## Summary

A detached CMS signature can now be produced and verified over a streamed content. Pass the content to `pki.cms.sign` as an async iterable of byte chunks, such as an async generator, together with `detached: true`, and the payload is hashed incrementally to build the message-digest attribute rather than buffered whole. A single pass serves every signer, so signers may use different digest algorithms. `pki.cms.verify` accepts the same async-iterable form for its `content` option. The message-digest is computed over the same content bytes as the buffered form, so a streamed signature verifies wherever a buffered one would and the two are interchangeable. A `Buffer` content is unchanged, so no existing call needs to change.

The app began speaking Tibetan in #580 — every button and message. author: mattiashognas
body:
## Summary
- Adds `buildSub`/`buildRetVoid` (`LLVMBuildSub`/`LLVMBuildRetVoid`) to `AshesCompiler.Backend.Llvm` - the two remaining primitives an RC retain/release pair needs that nothing earlier in this arc happened to require.
- `selfhost/tests/backend` gets a real RC cell using the exact 16-byte `{i64 reference_count, i64 allocation_size}` header from `architecture.md`'s "RC allocation and layout" section, with the public value pointer addressing the payload past it, not the header.
- `defineRcAllocFunction` mallocs `16 + payloadSize` bytes and writes `count = 1`; `defineRcRetainFunction`/`defineRcReleaseFunction` walk a value pointer back to its header with a NEGATIVE `buildGEP` offset (mirroring `rcAlloc`'s forward one - no new API surface for that, just a different element type/index sign than every earlier struct/array GEP use) and increment/decrement the count, freeing the ORIGINAL header pointer only once the count reaches zero.
- `buildRcCellLifecycleModule` proves the full sequence: allocate, retain, release once (not zero yet), read the payload while still alive, release again (now zero, actually freed), return the value read before the free.
- A leaf payload with no owned children is deliberately the only case handled - the type-directed child-drop path a real ADT needs, multi-field payloads, and atomicity are all out of scope for this slice.

## Test plan
- [x] `dotnet run --project src/Ashes.Cli -- compile --project selfhost/packages/backend/ashes.json` and `.../selfhost/tests/backend/ashes.json` build clean
- [x] Compiled test binary (vendored `libLLVM` alongside it) runs and prints `all self-hosted backend tests passed`, exit 0
- [x] Independently dumped the emitted x86-64 assembly from a standalone scratch program: `rcAlloc` stores `count=1` and the requested size into the malloc'd header then returns `header+16`; `rcRetain`/`rcRelease` both correctly address the header via a folded `-16(%reg)` addressing mode; `rcRelease` only calls `free` on the header pointer when the decremented count truly reaches zero; the lifecycle function reads the payload before the release that actually frees it
