author: lucasquiles
body:
## Summary

Diagnosability fix for the pre-dispatch admission-wedge class (#3374 / #3295 family), driven by the 2026-08-29 q DM-scope incident: the owner's DM chat was wedged for two hours — every DM journaled, then rejected before dispatch (`pre_dispatch_error`, "automatic replay unavailable"), while group scopes and public health stayed green. The journal carried only `err:{"errorClass":"Error"}` for every rejection: the log sanitizer drops message/stack by design, **every admission gate threw a bare `Error`**, and the recovering restart destroyed the in-memory state that would have named the gate. Live forensics falsified the supervisor-block hypothesis (`turnFinalizationDegradedScopes` was 0 during the wedge) and the durable-recovery hypothesis (arm-2 of `hasOutstandingTurnRecoveryForScope` provably empty), but the actual throw site is unprovable post-restart. That is the defect this PR removes: **the class is now self-identifying on first occurrence.**

- `src/runtimes/agent/turn-admission-errors.ts` (new) — `ScopeBlockedByDurableRecoveryError`, `ScopeBlockedByFinalizationRecoveryError`, `PerChatTurnFifoOwnerConflictError`. The sanitizer already logs `constructor.name`, so each gate discriminates in the existing `turn processor error — finalizing before queue advance` line with zero sanitizer changes (same pattern as `TurnDeferredToObligationError` on this seam).
- `runtime-turn-coordinator.ts` — both `beginRuntimeTurnEvidence` gates throw the typed classes; `finalizeUndispatchedRuntimeTurnAndWait` now logs one structured record (`pre-dispatch turn rejection — finalizing failed with no replay`) for **every** pre-dispatch rejection — per-chat AND shared/singleton scopes: `rejectionClass` + `scope`/`inboundSeq`/`logicalTurnId`, plus `fifoHeadTurnId` for per-chat scopes (explicit `'none'` for an empty FIFO — the stale-head-vs-empty discriminator the incident forensics lacked; omitted for shared scopes, where no per-chat FIFO exists).
- `runtime.ts` — the per-chat FIFO owner conflict throws its typed class.
- `runtime-turn-supervisor.ts` — `block()` now takes a `cause` (`degraded` | `retain_non_advancing` | `retry_failed` | `retry_exhausted`) and logs a structured warn on each turn's first block and on the retry-exhaustion transition (`scopeKey`, `logicalTurnId`, `blockedInScope`, `cause`); `unblock()` logs when a scope's block set empties. A blocked scope rejects every subsequent turn at admission, yet these mutations were previously silent. `cause: 'degraded'` exposes the `markDegraded` one-way door: a block with no retained record that `runRetries` can never release (restart-only).

## Deliberately out of scope (owner decisions, surfaced not implemented)

1. **`markDegraded` permanence** — blocking a scope forever on an invariant break is plausibly intended fail-closed behavior; making it sweep-recoverable is a semantic change. It is now visible (log + existing `degradedScopes` health counter) and characterized by a test. Note: `grep markDegraded tests/` matched nothing before this PR.
2. **#3295 deferral scope** — the deferral seam deliberately excludes the supervisor gate ("Every other rejection class … keeps the terminal path bit-for-bit"). Extending it so admission-blocked DMs defer instead of terminally failing (what cost the owner 4 lost DMs) is a scope decision on #3295.
3. **Turn-queue log message** — unchanged (`runtime-edge-coverage` pins the exact string).

## Evidence

- Red-first: `tests/runtimes/agent/turn-admission-errors.test.ts` (7 — typed classes survive the sanitizer; both coordinator gates throw typed; structured-fields contract incl. the `'none'` FIFO case and the omitted-FIFO shared-scope case) and `tests/runtimes/agent/runtime-turn-supervisor-block-visibility.test.ts` (3 — block warn with `cause: 'degraded'`, no re-log storm, and a characterization test documenting that `retryAll` never releases a `markDegraded` block).
- Regression: turn-admission-errors, supervisor-block-visibility, turn-recovery-supervisor, runtime-turn-supervisor, runtime-terminal-coordinator-integration, scheduled-turn-lifecycle, deferred-turn-admission — 7 files, 111 passed | 5 expected-fail (pre-existing matrix probes); `tsc --noEmit` clean; full 52-step push battery green.
- Incident receipts: BOT ERRORS ledger entries `fb4161b7…` (diagnosis + granted restart) and `5598c16b…` (fire 71).

## Review pass (2026-08-29)

A five-reviewer pass (four cleanup lenses + a delivery gap analyst) ran over the first push. Applied: the rejection log moved from the per-chat-only branch into `finalizeUndispatchedRuntimeTurnAndWait` so shared/singleton rejections are covered identically; supervisor block logging gained the `cause` vocabulary plus an unblock line; the FIFO-head lookup was hoisted to a single expression; test files switched to the shared `hoistedLoggerMock` helper and a typed `IOutboundQueue` stub; `turn-recovery-supervisor.test.ts` now constructs the real `ScopeBlockedByDurableRecoveryError` instead of fabricating its message string.

Named follow-ups (deliberately not in this diff):
1. **Durable `AdmissionRejectClass` taxonomy members** for the typed rejections (with the reply-guarantee breach ternary widened to match) — a semantic change to durable column values, outside diagnosability-only scope.
2. **Typed-error class-home consolidation** — other admission-adjacent error classes live beside their throw sites; unifying them in `turn-admission-errors.ts` touches code outside this diff.
3. **Context-fixture extraction** — six test files hand-roll near-identical `createRuntimeTurnContext` fixtures; a shared helper is a separate cleanup.

## Owner decisions (2026-08-29, resolving the two surfaced questions — recorded in the BOT ERRORS ledger)

1. **`markDegraded` blocks stay non-sweep-recoverable.** They represent integrity-proof failures (FIFO drift, unproven terminal post-effects); time-based clearing could manufacture false green. Any future recovery must be an invariant-specific, generation-fenced reconciliation that durably owns the block and clears it only after proof.
2. **#3295 deferral is NOT extended to every supervisor rejection.** A later narrow extension is approved only when ALL hold: the blocker is an explicit retained, recoverable same-scope finalization owner; the follower is replay-safe and pre-dispatch; the durable deferral + fenced drain path is available; and the feature stays default-off with kill-switch semantics. `recoverable:false` blocks, FIFO-owner conflicts, unknown rejection classes, and closed/full supervisor states remain non-deferrable and operator-visible.

**Scope statement: this PR is diagnosability-only. It does NOT fix the wedge root cause or the outage class** — it makes the next occurrence self-identifying so that fix can be built on evidence.

author: brittanyrey
body:
`set()` and `set.update()` already presize their underlying containers when they can infer the expected container size from another `set` or `dict`, but they fall back to incremental growth for all other iterables. 

Since we can also retrieve the size of lists and tuples, we can extend the same logic to sized iterables to reduce container resizing overhead. Iterables that have no clear size (i.e. generators) will remain unaffected. 

For this PR, I first refactored the two existing explicit presize calls into a helper function to be shared for the sized iterables as well. 

  | Benchmark | main | PR |
  |---|---|---|
  | set(list[str]) 10k | 158 us | 119 us: 1.32x faster |
  | set(list[str]) 1M | 88.2 ms | 68.7 ms: 1.28x faster |
  | set(tuple[str]) 1M | 85.6 ms | 66.9 ms: 1.28x faster |
  | set(list[int]) 10k | 117 us | 95.3 us: 1.23x faster |
  | set(list[int]) 1M | 24.9 ms | 20.6 ms: 1.21x faster |
  | set(tuple[int]) 1M | 23.8 ms | 19.9 ms: 1.20x faster |
  | set.update(list) 1M | 24.2 ms | 20.5 ms: 1.18x faster |
  | frozenset(list) 1M | 26.6 ms | 22.6 ms: 1.18x faster |
  | set(genexpr) 1M [no hint] | 59.4 ms | 60.3 ms: 1.02x slower |

**Note:** In the no hint case, theres about a ~8ns fixed overhead to call `PyObject_LengthHint` and discard the output.

<details>
<summary>Benchmark script</summary>

```python
"""set/frozenset built from a sized iterable (Objects/setobject.c)."""
import pyperf

def mkset(s): 
  set(s)

def mkfrozen(s): 
  frozenset(s)

def upd(s): 
  d = set(); d.update(s)

def gen(n): 
  set(x for x in range(n))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    r = pyperf.Runner()
    ints = list(range(1000000)); strs = [str(i) for i in ints]
    r.bench_func("set(list[int]) 1M", mkset, ints)
    r.bench_func("set(list[str]) 1M", mkset, strs)
    r.bench_func("frozenset(list) 1M", mkfrozen, ints)
    r.bench_func("set.update(list) 1M", upd, ints)
    r.bench_func("set(list) 10k", mkset, list(range(10000)))
    r.bench_func("set(genexpr) 1M [no hint]", gen, 1000000)
```
</details>

author: dpri0017
body:
# E1-US2-AC1–AC5: Add offline pack provenance and source handling

> **STACKED DRAFT — DO NOT MERGE YET**

This branch is stacked on `feature/e1-us1-ac9-pack-size-download` so review
shows only US2. After AC9 is accepted into the Epic branch, update this branch,
retarget this PR to `epic/epic-1-prepared-local-pack`, rerun every gate, and
only then request merge review.

## Scope

- Open a complete saved pack from Home and list each available stored layer,
  destination, manifest-verified recovery reference and attributed basemap.
- Group each item name with `Published by <publisher> · Saved <date>` and its
  device-calculated age, using full Australian month names and no leading zero.
- Label items from day 31 as `Not recently verified` without hiding, dimming or
  disabling their content or source controls.
- Remove a layer, destination or recovery item missing publisher or saved date
  before offer calculation and storage, then show the mandated omission reason.
- Reject other incomplete or unreviewed provenance, including non-HTTPS or
  non-allow-listed source URLs and missing licence values.
- Open pack detail from local complete-pack reads only. Recovery rows render
  only when the current local snapshot exactly matches the pack manifest.
- Intercept an original-source link while offline, keep the pack open behind
  the explanation, and repeat the locally stored publisher and saved date.

## Decisions

- `Source.retrievedAt` is the item saved-date field. Age does not use a
  publisher date, `Pack.createdAt`, or the current network.
- Device-clock dates in the future clamp to `Saved today`; the app does not
  display a negative age or claim that the device clock is correct.
- The day-30 refresh window is inclusive. `Not recently verified` begins on
  day 31 and is informational only.
- AC3's authoritative requirement that online and offline pack content be
  identical controls this surface. Opening PackDetail adds no network-dependent
  content or connectivity banner.
- Pack-detail recovery rows are not inferred from global storage: their count
  and canonical SHA-256 must match the pack manifest or they are withheld with
  an explicit integrity state.
- Original source links accept HTTPS subdomains of the reviewed source-domain
  register only. Link activation is an explicit user action; PackDetail itself
  contains no fetch path.

## Security and privacy

- Stored: no new record type or field. Valid layers, destinations, recovery
  rows and packs retain their existing shapes. Missing-publisher/date items are
  absent from IndexedDB, confirmed by integration and browser inspection.
- Not stored: omission details remain in the transient offer only. No search
  history, rejected address candidate, position, needs selection, device
  identifier, document content or polygon geometry was added.
- Leaves the device: opening a pack and every offline source interaction send
  zero requests. An online source link can navigate only to the selected
  validated HTTPS source URL.
- Queued: no job is created or changed.
- Permissions: none requested.
- Integrity: building packs remain inaccessible; recovery manifests are
  checked before rows render; malformed display provenance is omitted before
  offer size/hash calculation; other incomplete provenance fails the build.

## Resumen

Se actualizaron los horarios de la librería y se agregó un suite de tests para prevenir desincronización entre las múltiples ubicaciones donde aparecen en el HTML.

## Cambios principales

- **Horarios actualizados**: De "Lunes a sábado, 9:00 a 20:30" a "Lun a vie 9:00–13:00 y 16:30–20:30 · Sáb 9:00–14:00 · Dom cerrado" (reflejando cambio a horario de dos turnos)

- **Nuevo test suite** (`test/horarios.test.mjs`): 269 líneas que validan:
  - Sincronización de horarios entre tabla, cartel de "abierto ahora" y footer
  - Consistencia de colores en modo oscuro (verificando que bordes y fondos estén definidos)
  - Comportamiento correcto del sistema de horarios congelando el reloj en momentos específicos
- **Actualización de documentación**: `docs/concepto-landing.md` y `CLAUDE.md` reflejan los nuevos horarios y la existencia del nuevo test

## Detalles de implementación

El test suite resuelve dos problemas estructurales que causaban roturas recurrentes:

1. **Desincronización de horarios**: El horario estaba escrito a mano en tres lugares (tabla HTML, badge de "abierto ahora", footer). El test extrae el `<script>` de `index.html`, lo evalúa en un `vm` con un reloj congelado, y verifica que todas las ubicaciones muestren el mismo horario.

2. **Colores en modo oscuro**: Los estilos CSS se definían de forma incompleta, dejando algunos bordes con valores del modo claro. El test parsea la paleta de colores y verifica consistencia.

El test corre con `node --test test/` sin dependencias externas, siguiendo el patrón ya establecido en `test/mercadito.test.mjs`.

## Summary
Fourth of the 6-PR OAuth series (see #84, #85, #86 — **based on #86's branch**, not `main`).

## This PR's changes
- `POST /api/mcp/oauth/token` — `authorization_code` grant (validates the code against `oauth_authorization_codes`: unused, unexpired, matching `client_id`/`redirect_uri`, then verifies the PKCE `code_verifier` against the stored `code_challenge` from PR 3's authorize step) and `refresh_token` grant (rotates: the old refresh token is revoked and linked via `replaced_by` to the new one, per PR 1's schema). Both issue a fresh access+refresh token pair scoped to whatever the user approved on the consent screen.
- `POST /api/mcp/oauth/revoke` (RFC 7009) — always returns 200 even for an unknown/already-revoked token, per the RFC, so this endpoint can't be used to probe which tokens are valid.

Public client only throughout — no `client_secret` is checked anywhere in this flow, matching PR 2's dynamic client registration.

author: o-yutaka
body:
## Purpose

Phase C of #89: training Experience may propose a route preference, but BLACK may call it VERIFIED only after disjoint held-out evaluation shows a measurable positive delta.

## Training candidate

- one exact task fingerprint
- caller fixes the baseline route before proposal
- at least two routes with bounded minimum samples
- deterministic route metrics: Mission success, verified success, and complete-only resource averages
- training produces `requires_held_out_evaluation=true`
- structurally non-sovereign: adoption/execution false

## Held-out gate

- training/held-out Experience identity overlap fails closed
- held-out set must match the exact task fingerprint
- baseline and preferred routes must both be represented
- minimum held-out sample count required
- preferred verified success must beat baseline by configured minimum
- Mission success regression is bounded
- optional cost/token/duration regression thresholds use only complete measured truth
- if a required resource threshold lacks complete truth => BLOCKED, never fabricated PASS

Verdicts: VERIFIED / REJECTED / BLOCKED. Even VERIFIED does not authorize adoption or execution.

## Regression

- true held-out improvement => VERIFIED
- training winner that does not improve held-out => REJECTED
- incomplete required resource truth => BLOCKED
- training/held-out leakage => fail closed
- mixed task fingerprints => fail closed

## Stack

Based on Phase B #92. Parent phases must pass exact-head verification before promotion to master.

No Core / Contracts / Constitution changes. Tracks #89.

author: giltik123
body:
Clean replacement for research Draft #222, rebuilt directly from current `main@5c5edab2c7ac26d77a1aba40ecc17bf25ada72e1` after #225 merged.

## Problem
A deterministic FINAL can be prepared from canonical source A while another tab/process moves the Project cursor to B via Undo/Redo/Restore before Accept. A browser mutex cannot serialize those authorities.

## Selected authority
Project Accept remains server-owned. `PostgresProjectStore.acceptFinal()` already executes under the Project row `FOR UPDATE` lock. This PR makes source-lineaged FINAL admission compare durable `canonical_image_artifacts.source_image_storage_id` against the locked `canonical_projects.current_image_storage_id` before appending history.

- already-accepted FINAL replay remains idempotent and is checked first;
- a new source-bound FINAL whose source no longer matches the locked cursor fails `409 final_source_conflict`;
- rejected Accept does not mutate Project/history;
- returning the Project explicitly to the exact durable source permits the still-unaccepted FINAL again;
- no browser/client source claim is trusted.

## PostgreSQL acceptance
Adds an exact-head PostgreSQL workflow and a real lock-order regression. The test manually holds the Project row lock, queues navigation first and stale Accept second, observes both waiters through `pg_stat_activity`, then proves navigation wins and the queued stale Accept sees the new cursor and fails closed.

## Scope
Exactly three files relative to current main:
- `.github/workflows/project-accept-source-lineage.yml` +44
- `server/core/projects/postgresProjectStore.ts` +9/-1
- `tests/project-accept-source-lineage-postgres.test.ts` +164

This PR does not add browser locking, change provider/Billing semantics, add cloud FINAL provenance (#224), or implement Editor conflict recovery (#226). Those remain separate follow-ups.

author: kimjh96
body:
## Why

A swipe-back inside a `history="memory"` Router animated the screen away and then left the stack exactly where it was. The dismissed screen kept `data-flemo-active="true"`, parked one full width off-stage, and stayed on top of the screen it should have returned to — so every tap after the gesture landed on an invisible surface and did nothing. The app's own back control popped the same stack correctly, which is what made it look like a gesture bug rather than a routing one.

Nobody was listening to the driver. `HistoryListener` mounts `ensureScopeHistorySync`, whose `driver.subscribe` handler turns a traversal into the store pop, and `Router.tsx` rendered it under `{!useMemory && <HistoryListener />}`. So a memory Router had no subscriber at all: `createMemoryHistoryDriver.back()` decremented its index, emitted to an empty listener set, and that was the whole commit.

Reproduced on the built package, chromium, the playground's 346x706 nested stage, cupertino, touch drag from the stage's left edge across 85% of its width:

```
                  list           detail
before            active=false   active=true   tx 0
after release     active=false   active=true   tx 346
```

`elementFromPoint` at the middle of the stage returns the detail's own content after the gesture has finished. With the fix the detail unmounts, the list comes back active, and a tap on a card pushes again (4 flight elements to 7).

## What changed

Every scope mounts the sync now, memory included. That is the smaller change and the truer one: the sync is driver-agnostic — it subscribes to `stores.driver`, not to `window` — and `driver.back()` is what the swipe controller commits with, synchronously, because the code right after it depends on the landing flight already existing:

```
// After `back()`, so the landing flight has already re-held these
// elements under the engine's owner
```

Two places inside the sync do read the browser's live entry, and a memory scope stays out of both. `recordTraversal` pushes `{raw: window.history.state, pathname}` into module-level state shared by every browser Router on the page; a memory Router's pathnames belong to a stack the document knows nothing about and have no business there. The zone replay built on those records reads the live entry the same way. `FlemoStores.memory` is what gates them.

A memory scope also gets a real self-pop guard instead of the no-op one. With a sync mounted, the navigation controller's own `driver.back()` comes back as an event, and an unbalanced guard would let it pop a second time.

## What this replaced

The first version of this fix routed a memory commit through the navigation controller's `pop` instead, behind a new `commitScopeBack` seam. That works — the stack pops — but it makes the commit a queued navigation task, and the swipe controller is written against a synchronous one. It also left the two backends committing by different routes for no reason a caller could see. Both the seam and its test are gone.

## Tests

`createRouterScope.test.ts` pins the guard: a memory scope's mark is consumed exactly once, where it previously asserted the opposite.

author: lefouzebreizh
body:
Trouvé par la compétence `/video-de-reference` de #388, en la testant sur les exports d'Amorce eux-mêmes : **les fichiers que le studio produit écrêtent.**

## Mesuré

| export | vrai pic avant | après |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6 rushes | **+0,3 dBFS** | **−0,3 dBFS** |
| 28 rushes | **+0,5 dBFS** | **−0,5 dBFS** |

Au-dessus de zéro, donc en distorsion — alors que le seuil du limiteur est à −6 dB.

## La cause n'est pas un réglage

`DynamicsCompressorNode` n'a **aucune anticipation** : une crête sèche est déjà passée quand il commence à réagir. Ce n'est pas un limiteur, et aucun réglage ne le rendra tel.

Éprouvé avant de conclure : resserrer l'attaque de 3 ms à 1 ms rend **0,2 dBFS** et ne franchit pas zéro. Le paramètre n'était pas le problème.

## Un écrêteur doux en bout de chaîne

La courbe laisse tout passer **intact sous −3 dBFS** — la couleur du mixage ne change pas — et ne se referme que sur les crêtes, vers −1 dBFS. Un `WaveShaper` borne son domaine à [−1, 1], si bien qu'un dépassement franc reçoit le bout de courbe : le plafond tient même sur une pointe brutale, ce qui est exactement le cas visé.

**Coût : 0,2 dB de sonie.** L'alternative — baisser le niveau général — coûterait sur *chaque seconde* ce qu'on ne paie ici que sur quelques millisecondes, et le format court se joue précisément sur ce niveau (`/master-telephone`).

## Vérification

- `npm test` — 206/206
- `npm run verify` — 92/92 dans un vrai Chromium
- deux exports régénérés et remesurés, `tsc` et `eslint` verts

Aucun conflit avec #371, qui n'a touché que `montage-auto/` et `lecons.md`.

author: tschm
body:
The material was written against rhiza `v1.3.3` and rhiza-claude `v0.8.2`. Four template minors and five plugin minors later, the largest claim in it was false: that `core` syncs a make layer into every consumer.

## What actually changed upstream

Template **v1.4.0** ([ADR-0011](https://github.com/Jebel-Quant/rhiza/blob/main/docs/adr/0011-replace-the-synced-make-layer-with-a-pinned-cli.md)) replaced the synced `.rhiza/rhiza.mk` and `make.d/` — ~1,500 lines copied into every repo — with the pinned [`rhiza-task`](https://github.com/Jebel-Quant/rhiza-task) CLI, provisioned per invocation by `uvx`. **v1.3.4** did the same for `.rhiza/tests/` with the [`pytest-rhiza`](https://github.com/Jebel-Quant/pytest-rhiza) plugin. What `core` still ships is a 71-line shim that pins `RHIZA_TASK` and forwards to it.

The curriculum now teaches that split — *a template distributes configuration; a package manager distributes code* — and everything else follows from it.

## Lesson by lesson

| File | What changed |
|------|-------------|
| **L5, L7** | Bundle model rebuilt from the live manifest: 26 bundles, and `tests` / `marimo` / `paper` are no longer names the template accepts. All five profile expansions were wrong; corrected against the source. |
| **L10** | Rewritten. `custom-task.mk` and `custom-env.mk` are gone; the extension points are `local.mk`, `[tool.rhiza-task]`, the new `local-setup.sh` (v1.7.0) and `.rhiza/.env`. Every settings key and the six-layer precedence order verified against rhiza-task's `Config`. |
| **L11** | New sections for `rhiza-task` and `pytest-rhiza`; skills 8 → 10 (`/rhiza:remote`, `/rhiza:completions`); ecosystem diagram redrawn. |
| **L9** | The second Renovate custom manager, for the `pytest-rhiza` pin — including that it silently died when `make.d/` retired, which is the failure mode worth teaching. |
| **L8** | What crossing v1.4.0 costs, since that update is not routine. |
| **L1–L3, A1** | `make`-layer wording, bundle attributions, and the project-layout tree. |
| **A2** | All five downstream configs refetched. |
| **A3** | Contribution counts refreshed from the API (tschm 1,910 → 2,338, across two new repos). |

## Two claims that had become false

- **rhiza-claude is not a rhiza-managed repo.** It has no `.rhiza/template.yml` — it adopted the shim `Makefile` and `RHIZA_TASK` pin in v0.12.0 without being synced by the template. A2 said the opposite; it now uses this as the instructive partial case.
- **rhiza-task keeps its contributor guide at the root**, not under `.rhiza/`. L12's link was dead.

## The A2 refresh is worth a look

Three of the five real-world configs moved on in ways that teach something:

- **jquantstats** dropped an exclusion for a fuzzing workflow the template retired in v1.5.0.
- **chebpy** dropped `book/marimo/notebooks/rhiza.py`, an exclusion that had been there since v1.2.5 and **never matched anything**.
- **loman** is still at `v0.10.3` and names two bundles (`marimo`, `tests`) that v1.7.1 would reject — a sharper counter-example than it was a year ago.

Mutation testing, fuzzing, marimushka and `rhiza-cli` references are dropped throughout; all retired upstream.

## Verification

- 42 code-block tests pass (every YAML and TOML snippet parses).
- All 100 external links resolve, bar one VS Code marketplace URL that rejects `HEAD` — pre-existing and untouched.
- All local links resolve.
- `mkdocs build --strict` reports the same **7** warnings as before this branch; confirmed by stashing and rebuilding. CI builds non-strict.
- Both Marp decks rebuilt, so the committed HTML matches its source.

author: onemorepereira
body:
## Summary
Fixes silent session death and an unbounded refresh loop.

**Problem:** Outside the mount-time `checkAuth()`, nothing handled 401s. Once the Cognito ID token expired (~1h TTL), every mutating action (`guitarService`, `documentService`, `shareService`, `provenanceService`) threw a generic error with no refresh and no re-login prompt.

## Changes
- **`authService.authFetch(url, opts)`**: attaches the JWT; on a 401 it refreshes the token once and retries once; on definitive failure it clears the session, dispatches an `auth:logout` window event, and throws.
- **`AuthContext`** listens for `auth:logout` and clears the user → `ProtectedRoute` redirects to `/login`.
- Migrated all four services from `authenticatedRequest(url, getToken(), opts)` to `authService.authFetch`; removed the now-dead per-service `getToken` helpers.
- **`getCurrentUser`**: now refreshes only on a 401 and is capped to a single retry. Previously it recursed unconditionally whenever `/user/profile` was not-ok while `/auth/refresh` kept succeeding — an unbounded loop that hung the app on the spinner (and OOM'd the test worker until the cap was added).

## Tests
Adds the **frontend's first tests** (vitest + jsdom, `npm test`): 401→refresh→retry success, logout on failed refresh, no-more-than-one-retry, and the recursion cap. `tsc --noEmit`, `vitest run`, and `vite build` all pass; ESLint problem count is unchanged vs main (pre-existing `any`/unused-arg warnings only).

## Note
Redirect-on-expiry relies on the `auth:logout` event + ProtectedRoute; worth a manual smoke test (let a session expire, attempt a save, confirm redirect to /login).

author: chmoses98
body:
## ⚠️ DO NOT MERGE — results PR, presented for review

**RESEARCH ONLY. No production change. Zero parameters fitted.**

## The algebra, corrected first

An earlier session guessed that wide bid/ask spreads mechanically produce large declared edges. **That is backwards.** Decomposing about the vig-free midpoint:

```
declaredEdge = (model − fairMid) − (executablePrice − fairMid)
             =  MODEL_SIGNAL     −  EXECUTION_PENALTY
```

A *larger* execution penalty **reduces** declared edge. So the mechanism was measured, not preregistered as the answer.

## What production actually computes (traced from main)

`lib/research/hitter_pricing.py::price_hitter_contract` → `edge = model_prob − executable_yes_price`. Fee-blind, YES-only, no spread/confidence/threshold/staleness term.

`lib/research/hitter_board_builder.py::_executable_yes_price` → **mid** → `(bid+ask)/2` → ask → bid. It prefers the **midpoint**.

### The decomposition collapses — verified, not assumed

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `executionPenalty == 0` | **100.0000%** of rows, max abs difference **0.00e+00** |
| `declaredEdge` reproduced from source fields | **100.0000%** |

**`declaredEdge == MODEL_SIGNAL` exactly.** Execution cost cannot explain the inversion — it is not present in the quantity that inverts. **Mechanism: `CASE_A_MODEL_SIGNAL_INVERSION`.**

## What the inversion actually is

The preregistered descriptive OLS hit a **rank deficiency** — the execution-penalty column has zero variance, which is the finding restated as linear algebra. The clearly-labelled refit without that degenerate term gives:

**`modelSignal` coefficient = +0.2334**

The model's disagreement points toward the outcome, but only ~a quarter of it is real. A claimed 10pp edge is worth roughly **2.3pp**; the unearned remainder grows with the claim. That is the inversion.

## Hypotheses cleanly refuted

| | Finding |
|---|---|
| **H3 staleness** | Median quote age **0.0 min**; older quotes score *better* (−0.008 at 180min+). Inversion **False**. |
| **H4 liquidity** | High-signal rows have **narrower** mean spread (1.45c vs 1.77c) and similar capture counts. Not a thin-market phenomenon. |
| **H7 tails** | Across **953 ladders**, deeper rungs carry *smaller* mean signal (0.014 → −0.004), not larger. |

## Two caveats that weaken the claim

- The inversion appears in **DEVELOPMENT but not VALIDATION**.
- By family, signal inversion is **True only for `hitter_hits`**, and **no family is FDR-significant**.

With 261 playerGameKeys over 36 games and 7 dates this is a **mechanism hypothesis, not a confirmed law**.

**H5 refines it:** conditioning on probability band, the inversion disappears in `[0,0.10)`, `[0.10,0.25)` and `[0.25,0.50)` and survives only in `[0.50,0.75)` — so part of the marginal inversion is composition, not a uniform defect.

## A separate genuine defect

Because production differences against the mid, its declared edge and `expectedValuePerDollar` **omit the half-spread a taker pays** (median 0.005, mean 0.0088).

| Entry convention | Net ROI |
|---|---:|
| Honest executable ask | **−6.6%** |
| Production's own mid | −3.07% |

RSCH-0028's economics inherited that optimism and are corrected here.

## No filter simulated

Under `CASE_A` a spread/staleness filter has no mechanism to act on; simulating one anyway would be post-hoc fishing. **Disposition `LEVEL_0_MEASUREMENT_ONLY`; no shadow candidate justified.**

## Test plan

- [x] 38 focused tests: the identity and its sign convention, that a wider penalty *reduces* declared edge, that inversion needs three qualifying buckets, that a below-floor bucket cannot create a trend, that scoring never reads the ask while economics do, that paying the ask costs more than the mid, that quote age is never fabricated, that liquidity reads only archived fields, that filters are not simulated under CASE_A, and that rank deficiency is reported rather than hidden.
- [x] Full suite: **8,343 passed, 7 skipped**.
- [x] Artifact byte-identical before and after syncing main.

author: t-rav
body:
## Why

PR #11754 gave **"Council"** to the agent governance layer (`agents/council/` — the Council, with chambers, per the 2026-08-25 house standard). But `src/adr_reviewer.py` had long been using the same word for something else entirely: the multi-model ensemble that votes on proposed ADRs.

Under [ADR-0053](docs/adr/0053-ubiquitous-language-as-living-artifact.md) the ubiquitous language is single-valued — a term anchors to one live surface. Two meanings for "Council" is a vocabulary collision, not cosmetics. The governance layer keeps the name; **the ADR reviewer becomes a review panel.**

## What changed

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `ADRCouncilReviewer` | `ADRReviewPanel` |
| `ADRCouncilResult` | `ADRReviewPanelResult` |
| `CouncilVote` / `CouncilVerdict` | `PanelVote` / `PanelVerdict` |
| `_run_council_session` / `_parse_council_result` / `_build_council_summary` | `_run_panel_session` / `_parse_panel_result` / `_build_panel_summary` |
| `COUNCIL_RESULT:` (prompt + transcript marker) | `PANEL_RESULT:` |
| `## Council Amendment Notes` | `## Review Panel Amendment Notes` |
| `docs/wiki/terms/adr-council-reviewer.md` | `docs/wiki/terms/adr-review-panel.md` |

The term file **keeps its ULID**, so the inbound `depends_on` edges from `adr-reviewer-loop.md` and `dedup-store.md` still resolve. Its aliases drop `"council reviewer"` rather than re-registering the retired sense. `make quality` runs `lint-ul` first: 0 uniqueness failures, 0 unresolved anchors, 0 paraphrase warnings.

## The two pre-rename keys this PR still READS

A blanket rename would have broken both of these silently — no exception, no red test, just wrong behaviour on a later cycle.

1. **`## Council Amendment Notes`** — the clerk's amendment block is written *into the ADR file*. `docs/adr/0007-dashboard-api-multi-repo-scoping.md:86` carries one on disk right now. `_AMENDMENT_BLOCK_RE` matches `(?:Review Panel|Council)` so a stale block is **replaced in place**; match only the new heading and a re-review appends a second block beside the first.
2. **`COUNCIL_RESULT:`** — the orchestrator transcript header. A stale or cached prompt still elicits it; reading only `PANEL_RESULT` would discard a real verdict as `NO_CONSENSUS`.

ADR-0007's existing block is left as written — it's a record, not a live surface.

## Ratchets

`disturbance/baselines/mass.yaml`'s key is renamed `src/adr_reviewer.py:ADRCouncilReviewer` → `:ADRReviewPanel` with `loc: 833` / `methods: 29` **unchanged**. That is a key rename, not a raise — without it the class reads as a brand-new god class and trips `new_god_classes`. Verified: `new_god_classes` and `grown` both return empty against `src/`.

## Deliberately untouched

- **`PlanCouncil`, `DecompositionCouncil`, `DiscoveryCouncil`, `ShapeExpertCouncil`** — a separate family (the adversarial pipeline, ADR-0064/0105), not in scope here. See the note below.
- **`agents/council/`** — the governance layer; it keeps the name.
- **`repo_wiki/`** (31 files) — dated rows the factory wrote about work done under the old name.
- **`docs/wiki/terms/adr-reviewer-loop.md` and `adr-pre-validator.md`** — fenced off to avoid colliding with the concurrent #11747 term-file work. Their prose still cites `ADRCouncilReviewer`, which propagates into the generated glossary. Not a CI failure (the drift check resolves `code_anchor`, not prose), but it is a stale citation — a two-line follow-up.

## Verification

- Full `make quality`: **exit code 0** — `29360 passed, 1 skipped, 112 xfailed, 2 xpassed`. All stages green (lint, host-exclusive, gateway-coverage, typecheck, security, serial, scenario-loops, tests). UI vitest took its sanctioned skip path (`src/ui` untouched vs `origin/staging`); CI's Dashboard Build still runs it.
- The reviewer is exercised, not merely compiled: its loop tests, `tests/test_adr_reviewer.py` (237 sites), the gateway-canary MockWorld scenario, the eval's `_run_panel_session` call, and the prompt fixture (`tests/fixtures/prompts/adr_reviewer.json` resolves `adr_reviewer.ADRReviewPanel._build_orchestrator_prompt`; the rendered snapshot was regenerated through the real builder).
- Both new compat pins are **mutation-checked**: dropping `COUNCIL_RESULT` from the parser regex reddens `test_legacy_header_parses_to_a_decision` only; dropping `Council` from `_AMENDMENT_BLOCK_RE` reddens `test_legacy_block_is_replaced_in_place` only.
- Generated artifacts regenerated via `make arch-regen` (`coverage_matrix.md`, both ubiquitous-language views, `.meta.json`).

## Out of scope, for the record

"Council" still has a **third** meaning in this repo: the adversarial-review ensembles (`PlanCouncil`, `DecompositionCouncil`, `DiscoveryCouncil`, `ShapeExpertCouncil`, `src/plan_council.py`, `src/decomposition_council.py`). Renaming the ADR reviewer removes the collision the operator named, but does not make the word single-valued repo-wide. That family is larger and was not scoped into this change.

author: mlurz92
body:
## Gestaffeltes BD-Ziel für Hr. Safari

Hr. Safari soll nicht ab dem ersten Monat die volle Dienstlast tragen. Sein BD-Monatsziel ist jetzt gestaffelt:

| Monat | Ziel | Obergrenze |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Monat — November 2026 | **0** (reine Einarbeitung) | hart 0, auch manuell nicht überschreibbar |
| 2. Monat — Dezember 2026 | **3** | 3 |
| ab 3. Monat — Januar 2027 | **4** (AA-Standard) | keine |

## Umsetzung

Die Staffelung ist deklarativ als `SPECIAL_RULES.bdTargetSchedule` hinterlegt — eine Liste von Stufen, die jeweils **ab** einem Monat bis zum Beginn der nächsten gelten; eine Stufe ohne `target`/`min`/`max` beendet die Staffel und gibt an die statischen Regeln zurück. Sie hat Vorrang vor `reducedBdTarget`, `maxBdTarget` und `minBdTarget`.

Dafür nehmen `getReducedBdTarget`, `getMaxBdTarget` und `getMinBdTarget` den Planmonat entgegen. Der Kontext ist durch **alle** Zieleingänge gezogen: Auto-Plan-Konfigurationsdialog (Vorbelegung und Reglergrenzen), Solver-Zielermittlung und harte Obergrenzen-Constraints, Mehrmonats-/Jahresplanung (`computeCrossMonthBDTargets` — das kumulierte Soll wird je bereits geplantem Monat mit dessen eigenem Ziel gebildet), Konfliktmarkierung importierter Pläne, manuelle Zellbearbeitung, Drag-and-Drop von Dienst-Badges sowie beide Fairness-Berichte (`js/model.js` und `js/analytics/engine.js`).

Beide Fairness-Berichte summieren das BD-Soll jetzt **pro aktivem Monat**, statt ein Monatsziel mit der Monatszahl zu multiplizieren. Für ein konstantes Ziel ist das arithmetisch identisch, für ein gestaffeltes das einzig richtige Ergebnis (Nov + Dez 2026 ergibt für Hr. Safari 3, nicht 8).

## Schutz gegen einen stillen Fehler

Ein Aufruf dieser Getter **ohne** `(y, m)` fällt still auf die statischen Regeln zurück — er würde eine Person in ihrem Einarbeitungsmonat mit dem vollen Standardziel verplanen, ohne dass irgendein Laufzeitfehler auftritt. Genau das war beim ersten Durchgang in `js/analytics/engine.js` passiert (der Zeitraum-Fairness-Bericht hätte 12 statt 7 Dienste als Soll ausgewiesen und damit dem Abteilungsbericht widersprochen). `test/bd-target-context.test.js` prüft deshalb statisch, dass unterhalb von `js/` — rekursiv, inklusive `js/analytics/` — kein einarmiger Aufruf existiert; der Wächter enthält eine Selbstprüfung, damit ein fehlerhaftes Suchmuster nicht stillschweigend nie etwas findet.

## Tests

`npm run verify` grün: **198 Tests, 0 Fehler**, Lint und Typecheck sauber.

Neu:
- Staffelstufen, Verhalten vor dem Eintritt und Nichteinmischung in andere Personen (`test/constants.test.js`)
- Soll-Summierung in beiden Fairness-Berichten (`test/model.test.js`, `test/analytics-engine.test.js`)
- Vollständige Solverläufe für November 2026, Dezember 2026 und Januar 2027, die je Stufe die AA-Invarianten und die Obergrenze prüfen (`test/autoplan-rules.test.js`)
- Der Call-Site-Wächter selbst, gegen ein absichtlich zurückgebautes Call-Site verifiziert

## Dokumentation

Neuer Abschnitt **5.5 Gestaffelte BD-Ziele zur Einarbeitung** im README (inkl. des Hinweises zum Monatskontext), aktualisierter Safari-Hinweis in Abschnitt 5, ergänzte Regelbeschreibung in `algorithm_rules.md` §2.4. Nebenbei: der `reducedBdTarget`-Eintrag in README 5.4 listete Dr. Hellmann noch nicht.

author: ttoanhb24
body:
Gom các thay đổi **thêm khả năng mới** cho luồng đăng bài. Phần sửa lỗi nằm ở PR riêng, lấy nhánh này làm base.

---

## 1. Hạ tầng nhận diện và đo media dùng chung

`media-url.util.ts` — gom việc nhận diện URL video về một chỗ. Trước đây mỗi publisher tự viết một biểu thức và chúng lệch nhau: Facebook chỉ bắt đuôi `.mp4`, Instagram/Threads bắt thêm dạng `?filename=x.mp4`. Cùng một URL đi qua Facebook bị coi là ảnh và đẩy nhầm vào `/photos`.

`media-probe.util.ts` — đọc thông tin kỹ thuật của media, **thấy được cả luồng audio** (bản `isVideoCompliant` cũ dùng `-select_streams v:0` nên chỉ nhìn luồng video). Kèm giới hạn thời lượng theo docs Meta: Facebook Reels 3–90 giây, Instagram Reels 3 giây–15 phút.

Bổ sung fallback `@ffprobe-installer` / `@ffmpeg-installer`. Hai gói này đã nằm trong `dependencies` và `videos.service.ts` đang dùng, nhưng social-publishing thì không — nên trên máy không có `/usr/bin/ffprobe` (macOS dev, image Docker gọn) phần probe tự tắt im lặng.

## 2. Facebook đăng Reels qua `/video_reels`

Mọi video trước đây đi vào `/{page-id}/videos` — endpoint tạo **video thường**, chỉ phân phối tới người đã follow Page. Reels feed, tức nguồn hiển thị cho người chưa follow, đi qua `/video_reels`. Bài không bao giờ vào được nhánh phân phối đó.

Video **3–90 giây** giờ đăng qua Reels API 3 pha:

1. `POST /{page-id}/video_reels?upload_phase=start` → `video_id` + `upload_url`
2. `POST rupload.facebook.com/video-upload/{video_id}` — nạp bytes hoặc header `file_url`
3. `POST /{page-id}/video_reels?upload_phase=finish&video_state=PUBLISHED`

Pha 2 khác hẳn luồng `/videos`: nằm trên host `rupload`, xác thực bằng header `Authorization: OAuth <token>` chứ không phải query param. Ưu tiên nạp bytes khi có file local — server Facebook từng tải URL Railway thất bại lúc nhiều bài đăng đồng thời, đúng lý do đã ghi trong nhánh carousel ảnh.

Ngoài khoảng 3–90 giây hoặc không đọc được thời lượng thì giữ nguyên `/videos`.

## 3. YouTube: tiêu đề, tag và upload tiếp tục được

**`tags` luôn là mảng rỗng** — bỏ trống hoàn toàn một trường mà người dùng đã tự điền sẵn dưới dạng hashtag trong caption. Giờ rút hashtag thành tag (bỏ dấu `#`, khử trùng lặp không phân biệt hoa thường, tối đa 15).

**Tiêu đề là 100 ký tự đầu của caption** — cắt cụt giữa từ và kéo theo cả chuỗi hashtag. Tiêu đề là tín hiệu xếp hạng mạnh của Shorts. Giờ lấy dòng đầu, bỏ hashtag, cắt ở ranh giới từ.

**`Content-Length` đo bằng một request, tải bằng một request khác** — `HEAD` lấy kích thước rồi mở `GET` stream mới để tải. Hai request có thể trả kích thước khác nhau (Drive redirect, CDN đổi bản) khiến số byte khai với YouTube lệch với số byte thực gửi, upload hỏng hoặc cụt. Giờ lấy từ chính luồng đang tải, chỉ quay lại `HEAD` khi nguồn không khai.

**Mở phiên `uploadType=resumable` nhưng PUT một phát toàn bộ stream** — đứt giữa chừng là mất trắng. Giờ hỏi mốc đã nhận bằng `Content-Range: bytes */<total>` (chấp nhận 308 Resume Incomplete) rồi mở lại nguồn từ đúng mốc đó. Nguồn không trả 206 thì dừng, không nối nhầm dữ liệu.

---

## Kiểm chứng

body:
Stacked on #17 (`fix/0832-cyclone-funnel`), per the FIFO merge-queue rule — not on `main`.

Docs only. Two issues filed for gaps measured while fixing #17; neither is fixed here.

**#0880 — `just format` is build-state dependent.** `examples/workspaces/launch`'s two Rust leaves are members of a workspace root that `nros build` generates and `.gitignore` hides, so the recipe is green on a tree that built that workspace and red on one that did not. `example_shape.rs` already records this fact and reads the tracked `.colcon_workspace` marker; nothing else does.

Swept the class, not the site — nearest enclosing `[workspace]`, root `members` globs expanded, `exclude` honoured, each candidate cross-checked against `cargo metadata`. Exactly two leaves, both under `launch`. Third occurrence of the shape issue 0359 named, second distinct cause.

The detail that makes it a design question rather than two `exclude` lines: `mixed` is equally unbuilt and equally migrated, and formats fine only because its one leaf carries its own `[workspace]` while `launch`'s two do not. Two leaf shapes coexist in one workspace class, and the gate that could forbid that currently does neither.

**#0881 — the funnel-ON cyclone path has no fast-line lane.** The switch only exists on the self-provision branch, so: standalone backend project has no platform to funnel into; native host resolves `find_package` from the SDK store; only a cross build lands on source-with-platform. Before #17 the standalone project was what caught the missing link dependency — after it, that lane no longer compiles the funnel, so the next regression of this shape surfaces in tier 2. Issue carries three candidate fixes and the ~4 min by-hand check that stands in meanwhile.

`just check-fast`: green.

author: zacxdev
body:
Adds the **sixth worktree surface** to `claude/RULES.md`, plus a paired clause on
"find the WRITER". Both come from a measured case closed this session
(devrc#1005 documents the investigation; this lands the rule).

## The gap
The five existing surfaces are all about the working tree, the session or the
checkout. **None mentions the config file** — and `git remote add`,
`git config --local` and `core.hooksPath` all write the **common** config, so a
worktree does not scope them at all.

Measured: a hook-verification session **in a different repo** ran
`git -C /tmp/wt-hookcheck remote add localverify …` inside what was a worktree
*of devrc*. Its cleanup removed the worktree, the branch and the remote's target
directory — **but not the remote**. The shared base clone then carried a remote
pointing at a deleted path for five days, inside every `fetch --all`.

## The paired clause: an mtime cannot NAME a writer
Two sessions read `.git/config`'s mtime moving and concluded the remote "is
written repeatedly, not a one-off" — promoting a five-day-old leftover into a live
writer worth hunting. That file holds **442 `[branch]` sections** and ~40 agent
worktrees append to it constantly.

A content-diffing watcher caught the rival mechanism two minutes after removal:
file changed, `localverify` still absent, the diff being another session's
`[branch]` entry. This is `empty-result` in the time axis — "the file changed" is
the observable the most causes share, so it identifies none of them.

The same case also identifies the writer of devrc's repo-local `core.hooksPath`,
which `CLAUDE.md` records as arriving from "something else" with no known writer.
Scoped in the archive to exactly what it proves: the `githooks/` sighting only,
**not** the 08-20 `.git/hooks` ones, and the value stayed volatile.

## Ceiling: 41,400 → 42,450
Floor-relative slack going in was **4 B**, so this had to pay ceiling — which is
precisely what the previous ledger entry predicted ("the next NEW rule pays
ceiling, exactly as the entries above insist").

**Eviction was re-run, not assumed exhausted**, by that entry's identical
documented method and now against the new prose as well: 80 lines scanned, 24
blocks matched, largest still the 107 B sops-retraction sentence that *is* the
rule, every other match imperative/scope/failure-shape text the playbook keeps.
**Yield: 0 B** — third consecutive empty run.

Slack held at the same **429 B floor-relative** precedent rather than widened, so
the next rule pays ceiling too and this does not become a habit of buying room in
advance. No rule lost scope; nothing was narrowed to buy bytes.

## The instrument was validated, not assumed
| mutant | expected | observed |
|---|---|---|
| `+500 B` | headroom floor | `test_rules_md_keeps_working_headroom` |
| `+1500 B` | hard ceiling | `test_rules_md_under_hard_ceiling` ("OVER BY") |
| rename the new anchor | pointer test | `test_every_archive_pointer_resolves`, naming `worktree-config` |

The first two **discriminate** (floor fires without the ceiling), so neither is
passing by an earlier check always winning. Both files restored byte-identical
after the battery.

author: johnbn1970
cliffhall
body:
Closes #2163

`AGENTS.md` was a single 1,223-line contract loaded in full on every turn — the issue/board workflow, the priority rubric, the release procedure, the Mantine conventions — whether the task was a one-line CSS fix or a release cut. This splits it along the line the issue drew: **rules stay resident in `AGENTS.md`; procedures move to `.claude/skills/`.**

Nothing is duplicated. Every recipe that moved was removed from where it was.

## The skills

Ten, under `.claude/skills/`. Seven are `disable-model-invocation: true` — procedures with side effects, invoked by name — so there is no trigger question for them at all and their descriptions never enter the listing budget.

| Skill | Covers | Invocation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `issue-create` | The five-step create flow | `/issue-create` |
| `issue-triage` | The two-pass sweep, the priority rubric, the board audit | `/issue-triage` |
| `board-ops` | `gh project` recipes + the field/option IDs for #28 and #11, the option-deletion hazard | `/board-ops` |
| `pr-flow` | Branch naming, DCO, screenshots, Copilot review, closing out | `/pr-flow` |
| `pre-push-gate` | Running `local:gate` and diagnosing a failing stage | `/pre-push-gate` |
| `release` | Cutting a release | `/release` |
| `test-servers` | Picking and running a showcase server | `/test-servers` |
| `local-dev` | Install/run + dependency placement reasoning | model-invoked |
| `testing` | Where a test goes, which command runs it, clearing the gate | model-invoked |
| `project-structure` | Where things live | model-invoked, `user-invocable: false` |

## What shrank

| File | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AGENTS.md` | 1,223 | 380 |
| `README.md` | 811 | 105 |

`README.md` is split into `docs/{architecture,quality-gate,test-servers,publishing,docker}.md` and is **no longer auto-loaded** by `CLAUDE.md`. The project tree in `AGENTS.md` is one line per entry — the thirty-line commentary on `app-origin-controller.ts` and friends is gone, with a note that those files carry their own header comments and the source is the place to read them.

`.github/copilot-instructions.md` and the rule to mirror review-relevant changes into it are deleted. Copilot reads `AGENTS.md`.

## Reliability

The issue's central concern: `AGENTS.md` is unconditional, a skill is not, and a skill that stops firing loses behavior **silently**. Four things address that.

**`npm run verify:skills`** runs inside `validate`, so it is in `local:gate` **and** in GitHub CI. It parses each `SKILL.md` the way Claude Code does and fails on anything that would strip the metadata — the whole-class failure being malformed frontmatter YAML, which loads the body with an *empty* description, so `/skill-name` still works and a manual spot check passes while the skill can never auto-fire again. It also requires an explicit invocation mode on every skill, requires eval cases (positives **and** negatives) for model-invoked ones, and budgets the listing. It runs `claude plugin validate` too when that CLI is on PATH — but the check does not *depend* on it, because the CLI is absent in CI and a guard that skips itself wherever it actually runs is worse than one that reimplements the check. Its pure parsers are unit-tested via `test:scripts` (13 cases).

That guard earned its keep during this PR: tuning the `testing` description introduced `description: Testing procedures for this repo: which npm command…`, and the unquoted colon was caught immediately.

**Listing budget: 1,173 / 4,000 characters**, printed on every run and failed when exceeded. I used a computed measure rather than a `/doctor` reading because it is enforceable and regresses visibly when a skill is added; the acceptance criterion asked for the number to be recorded, and it is now recorded somewhere that checks itself.

**`npm run skills:eval`** runs the committed trigger cases headless (`claude -p … --output-format stream-json`), N samples per case, asserting on a `Skill` tool_use. It is deliberately **not** in the gate — it needs the CLI and real model calls.

## Two measured findings, both recorded in AGENTS.md

**`paths` is not a free win.** The issue recommended it for `testing` as "far closer to deterministic than description matching". It does gate loading to matching files — but measured against that skill's own cases, adding it roughly **halved** the rate at which the same skill fired from a conversational prompt (0–50% with `paths`, 33–100% without). It also cannot be measured at all: a prompt-only eval can never exercise a path trigger, so shipping it means shipping an untestable claim. I dropped it and wrote down why, so it does not get helpfully re-added.

**A case whose answer is already in `AGENTS.md` is not a trigger case.** Two early `local-dev` cases sat at 0% because the model answered them correctly and directly from the resident rules — which is the design working, not a miss. Likewise a prompt naming a concrete file ("how does the `@inspector/core` alias resolve?") invites a `Read`, which is a better answer than a skill. Good cases are "how do I / where does this go" procedure questions.

Current hit rates at `RUNS=3`: `project-structure` 5/5, `local-dev` 5/6, `testing` 3/5, negatives 100% across the board. The two below threshold are borderline-by-nature rather than broken, and are committed as-is so the next tuning pass has them.

## Gate

`npm run local:gate` passes end to end (`GATE_EXIT=0`), including the Firefox engine pass and Storybook. `npm run test:scripts` is 305/305. All relative Markdown links across the repo were verified to resolve.

## Deliberate calls worth reviewing

- **`.gitignore` now un-ignores `.claude/skills/`** (`.claude/*` + `!.claude/skills/`), so the skills ship with the checkout while Claude Code's local state stays out.
- **The dependency-placement *rules* are back in `AGENTS.md`** as six bullets, with the reasoning in `local-dev`. The issue's table assigned them to the skill, but they are exactly what a reviewer cites against a diff, and the issue's own constraint says rules stay resident. The skill carries the war stories.
- **The authoritative validator runs in both tiers, and fetches a pinned CLI if it has to.** `npm run verify:skills:cli` is a step in `local:gate` **and** in CI. It uses an installed `claude` only when it matches `PINNED_CLI_VERSION` exactly, and otherwise runs `npx -y @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.250` — so **the gate can reach the network**, and CI installs that package on every push. That is a deliberate supply-chain trade for making "authoritative validation runs in CI" true rather than aspirational; the pin is what bounds it, and the version is a one-line change. `verify:skills` (inside `validate`) stays offline and best-effort, so the fast inner loop needs no CLI and no network.

author: keirsalterego
body:
Three things `fixtures/README.md` asserted that the files do not support. All
found by reading the files rather than the notes.

**1. The pip fixture is not poisoned `reqs-s`.**
`reqs-s` has 23 lines, every one exactly pinned. `poisoned.requirements.txt` has 6,
written from scratch, sharing exactly one name (`numpy` — and there it carries no
constraint at all). Poisoning `reqs-s` would have put 23 clean lines around 2 bad
ones, which is a worse demo and a slower test.

**2. `npm-m` has 3 workspace members, or 6.**
Both numbers are real and they count different things. npm writes a monorepo member
twice — the directory (`apps/admin`) and a `link: true` entry under `node_modules`
pointing at it. Three of each, so `grep -c '"link": true'` is 3 and the report
header says `6 workspace`. The file quoted one and the tool prints the other.
`npm-xl` is 7 and 14 by the same arithmetic.

**3. The pip table listed 4 of 6 lines.**
Missing the pinned control line (`requests==2.31.0`) and one of the three unpinned
ones (`flask~=3.0`) — so it did not add up to the 2 hallucination + 3 unpinned
findings the fixture actually produces.

## Verification

```console
$ wc -l < fixtures/reqs-s.requirements.txt          # 23
$ wc -l < fixtures/poisoned.requirements.txt        # 6
$ grep -c '"link": true' fixtures/npm-m.package-lock.json   # 3
$ ./target/release/stranger scan fixtures/npm-m.package-lock.json | head -1
  npm-m.package-lock.json  576 packages   (20 direct · 556 transitive · 6 workspace)
```

Data files only — no code touched.

author: liusuzeng
body:
## Why

The exact-main CI for #24 failed twice in the same new E2E test because its fixture assigned fake-Pi scenarios by worker-process startup order. An extra/replacement worker can consume a slot, causing an intended long-running session to receive the provider-error scenario instead.

This is a test-fixture sequencing problem, not a production count-rendering failure: format, typecheck, 651 unit tests, build, site validation, and the rest of the Electron E2E suite passed.

## Fix

- Remove `createSequencedFakePiBinary` and its worker-start counter.
- Add a test-only fake-RPC option, `--prompt-error-prefix`.
- The #24 E2E now deterministically makes prompts beginning `count consistency failed` emit the fake provider error, while the two `count consistency running` prompts remain long-running regardless of worker startup order.
- No production/runtime behavior changes unless the test-only flag is explicitly supplied.

## Validation

A staging run passed formatting, typecheck, all unit tests, build, and site validation on the resulting tree. The normal PR CI should now provide the macOS Electron E2E gate, including the previously failing #24 test.

Refs #24

author: goospel
body:
## 무엇을 / 왜

「여백에 글 남기기」를 **전체 화면에서 하단 슬라이드업 바텀시트로** 바꿨다.

한 줄 끄적이러 들어가는데 화면이 통째로 갈아치워지는 값이 컸다 — 밑 화면이 언마운트됐다 다시 마운트되며 스크롤·탭 자리가 날아갔고, 쓰기가 읽던 자리와 이어지지 않는 별개의 여행처럼 느껴졌다. 시트는 덮을 뿐이라 취소하면 하던 자리가 그대로 남는다.

> 시안은 사용자 승인이 끝난 상태로 받았다(전체 화면 → 시트 · 애니메이션을 `Sheet` 공용 껍데기에 붙여 네 시트에 일괄 적용 · 출구 이중화). **설계는 Fable, 구현은 opus**가 맡았고, 그 뒤 **독립 리뷰(reviewer)를 한 번 돌려 커밋 2개로** 정리했다.

### 셋으로 나뉜다

1. **`Sheet`에 올라오는 움직임** — 딤 `opacity 0→1` 0.25s ease, 패널 `translateY(102%)→0` 0.28s `cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.3,1)`. 태깅·서재 관리·좋아요 명단·여백 쓰기 **네 시트가 함께** 부드러워진다(일관성, 승인 사항).
   - ⚠️ **일회성 마운트 애니메이션 · 움직이는 속성은 `transform`·`opacity`뿐** — T-176(발광 `box-shadow` 무한 반복이 실기기를 무너뜨린 자리)의 규율이다. `ui.test.tsx`가 keyframes의 **속성 집합**을 `{transform, opacity}`로 잠근다.
   - 인라인 style이 아니라 클래스인 이유는 `prefers-reduced-motion`이 인라인 선언을 이길 수 없어서다.
2. **`StoryComposer`를 시트 안으로** — 필드·팔레트·체크·문구는 그대로, 출구가 ✕ 하나 늘었다.
3. **셸을 교체에서 겹침으로** — `underCompose`(= `composeBook`을 걷어낸 `marginScreen`)가 밑 화면을 판정하고, `withCompose`가 **도달 가능한 밑 화면 둘**(사람축 여백 상세 · 탭 화면)에 시트를 얹는다. 시트 zIndex 200/201이 탭바(100)를 딤으로 덮으므로 억제 코드는 없다.

## 겹침이 삼킨 것 셋 — 하나는 구현 중, 둘은 리뷰가 잡았다

전체 화면 교체를 겹침으로 바꾸면 **밑 화면이 살아남는다**. 얻는 것이 크지만, 「언마운트가 대신 해 주던 일」이 조용히 사라진다. 이 PR에서 그게 세 번 나왔다.

| # | 언마운트가 해 주던 일 | 증상 | 발견 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 여백 상세의 재조회 | 저장해도 글 목록이 3편 그대로 | 구현 중(스펙이 지목) |
| 2 | **서재 인라인 여백 박스의 재조회** | 저장해도 「여백 3」 그대로 | **구현 중 발견**(계획에 없던 자리) |
| 3 | **`slot.destroy()`로 배너 끄기** | 배너가 딤 뒤에서 계속 갱신 = 무효 트래픽 | **리뷰가 발견**(수익 경로) |

1·2는 글을 남긴 뒤에만 `composeEpoch`를 올려 remount로 되돌렸다(취소는 안 올린다 — 바뀐 게 없다). 2는 plan.md의 「응답 캐시 ⏸ 보류」가 기대던 **바로 그 리마운트**여서 그 줄에 갱신 주석을 달았다.

3은 **수익 경로라 보수적으로** `adSuppressed`로 지면을 접어 main과 같은 동작으로 되돌렸다 — 조건부 렌더가 곧 언마운트라 destroy가 그대로 돌고, 시트를 닫으면 부착이 1회 돈다. `toss.ts`가 접힌 슬롯을 되살리며 **스스로 금지한** 「사용자는 못 보는 노출만 집계」가 딤 뒤에서 재현되는 것이었다.

## 리뷰 반영 (커밋 2 · `b3ae0e1`)

판정 「수정 필요」(Critical 0 · Important 4 · Minor 6). 위 3번 외에:

- **I-1 딤 탭이 확인 없이 원고를 버렸다.** main의 출구는 「취소」·뒤로가기뿐이라 둘 다 **의도적**이었는데, 딤은 이 PR이 새로 연 **우발적** 출구다 — 시트 밖은 스치기만 해도 눌리고, 인용 200 + 본문 500자가 저장 전에 날아간다. 확인 시트를 새로 세우는 대신 **딤만 막았다**(`dimClosable` — 빈 시트일 때만 딤이 닫는다). ✕·취소는 그대로라 갇히지 않는다.
  `Sheet`에 `onDimClose`(기본값 = `onClose`)를 두어 딤과 ✕를 갈랐다 — **한 핸들러로 묶으면 딤을 막는 순간 ✕까지 잠긴다.** 다른 세 시트는 기본값을 타므로 무변화.
- **M-1 도달 불가 `withCompose` 2곳 제거**(책축·남의 책방). 책축 뷰는 `onCompose` 프롭 자체가 없고, 남의 책방은 `setMargin(null)`을 거쳐야 열려 작성과 공존할 수 없다. 감싸 두면 「이 조합이 가능하다」는 거짓말이 코드에 남는다.
- **M-5 `withCompose`가 무엇에 기대는지 경고를 남겼다.** 밑 화면이 remount되지 않는 것은 React가 **key 없는 최상위 Fragment를 언랩**하는 덕이다 — Fragment에 key를 달거나 `{composer}{under}` 순서를 뒤집으면 밑 화면이 **조용히** remount된다.
- **M-2·M-3·M-4 사실과 어긋난 서술 정정.** 특히 **「remount로 잃는 상태가 없다」는 틀렸다** — 축하 배너·태깅 시트 상태와 스크롤, 여백 상세의 탭·펼친 글은 버려진다. 다만 **회귀는 아니다**: 저장 경로는 전체 화면 시절과 똑같이 전부 새로 마운트되던 자리이고, 취소 경로는 오히려 개선됐다(예전엔 취소해도 날아갔다).
- **I-4 보고 숫자 정정** — 아래 「테스트」 절.
- **하지 않은 것**: M-6(trailer)은 하네스 규정이라 그대로. I-3(실기기 키보드)은 코드로 닫지 않고 ABANDON으로 남긴다.

## 미검증 가정 원장 — 6/6 충족 + ABANDON 3

- [x] **CHECK**: 홈의 여백 문 탭 → **EXPECT**: 시트가 아래에서 올라오고 딤 뒤에 홈 마크업이 DOM에 그대로 남음
  **EVIDENCE**: `.sheet-panel` = `role="dialog"` · `aria-label="여백에 글 남기기"`. 애니메이션 실측 `sheet-panel-in / 280ms / iterations 1 / cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.3, 1)`, `sheet-dim-in / 250ms / 1`. 정착값 `transform: none` · 딤 `opacity 1` · 패널 `bottom = 812`(뷰포트 바닥) · `height 633 = 78vh`. **밑 화면 생존**: 홈 마크업(`함께 읽는 사람`·`책 뉴스`) 잔존, `nav` 1개. 컴포저 내용물 = textarea 2 · 인용 라벨 · 공개 체크 · 팔레트 전부 존재.
- [x] **CHECK**: ✕ / 취소로 닫힘 → **EXPECT**: 시트 제거 후 홈이 그대로
  **EVIDENCE**: 두 출구 각각 `.sheet-panel` 0 · `.sheet-dim` 0 · 홈 마크업 잔존 · 탭바 1 · 여백 문 재사용 가능.
- [x] **CHECK**(리뷰 추가): **빈 시트**에서 딤 탭 → **EXPECT**: 닫힌다(버릴 원고가 없다)
  **EVIDENCE**: 딤 클릭 후 `.sheet-panel` 0.
- [x] **CHECK**(리뷰 추가): **원고가 있는** 시트에서 딤 탭 → **EXPECT**: 무시되고 원고가 남으며, 그 상태에서 ✕는 여전히 닫힌다(갇힘 방지)
  **EVIDENCE**: 딤 클릭 후 `.sheet-panel` **1**(그대로) · textarea 값 `"원고 보호 확인"` 보존. 이어서 ✕ 클릭 → `.sheet-panel` **0** · 홈 잔존.
- [x] **CHECK**: 여백 상세에서 compose 열고 글 저장 → **EXPECT**: 시트 닫힌 뒤 밑 여백 상세에 방금 글이 보임
  **EVIDENCE**: 시트 열린 동안 밑 상세 3편 생존. 저장 후 헤더 「내가 쓴 여백 **4**」 + 새 글 최상단. **서재 직행 경로도 「여백 **4**」 + 새 글 최상단, 서재 탭 유지.** 리뷰 배치 후 재확인까지 동일.
- [x] **CHECK**: 진입 직후(`localStorage.clear()` 후 첫 로드) 자동으로 뜨는 시트·딤 0개 → **EXPECT**: T-183 위반 없음
  **EVIDENCE**: `position:fixed && zIndex>=99` 요소 = **`NAV[z=100]` 하나뿐**(상시 탭바). `[role="dialog"]` 0 · `.sheet-dim` 0.

**ABANDON: 실기기 키보드 확인 — 배포 전 사용자 확인 필요.** 시트 안에서 소프트 키보드가 올라올 때의 스크롤·입력·`78vh` 상한 거동은 데스크톱 목 모드가 원리상 못 잡는 클래스다(T-176 계열).

**ABANDON: 배너 접기(F-2)는 브라우저로 관측 불가.** 목 모드에서는 지면 자격이 **원리상 꺼져 있다** — 그룹 ID가 `import.meta.env` 값이라 dev 빌드에선 빈 값이고, 실측해도 `[data-ad-group]`이 0개다(억제 전에도 0). 정적 테스트(`adSuppressed` true→부재 / false→존재)와 돌연변이로 대신 잠갔다.

**ABANDON: 스크린샷 없음.** Browser 패널이 표시되지 않아 그 탭이 프레임을 합성하지 않았고(`not compositing frames`), `chrome-devtools` MCP는 이전 세션의 크롬이 프로필을 점유해 붙지 못했다. 사용자 크롬을 죽이는 대신 **판정을 수치로 마감**했다(위 EVIDENCE 전부 DOM 실측 — 레포 규칙의 「수치 선행·스크린샷 후행」 그대로).

## 테스트 (보고 직전 재측정)

- `npm --prefix miniapp test` → **26개 파일 · 1164건 전원 통과**. `npx tsc --noEmit` 클린.
- **이 PR의 신규 테스트는 15건**이다(`it`/`test` 블록 실측 **1145 → 1160**). ⚠️ 커밋 1의 changelog·PR body에 적었던 **「신규 12건」은 틀린 숫자**였고 리뷰가 잡았다 — 기억으로 적은 값이었다. 지금 값은 재측정이다.
- **Red를 눈으로 확인하고 구현했다** — 커밋 1에서 10건 실패 → Green, 리뷰 배치에서 다시 6건 실패 → Green.
- **돌연변이 8종 전부 사살**:

| 돌연변이 | 결과 |
|---|---|
| `underCompose` → `marginScreen(margin)` | app.test 3건 실패 |
| `className="sheet-panel"` 제거 | ui.test + story.test 2건 실패 |
| keyframes에 `box-shadow` 추가 | T-176 속성 가드 1건 실패 |
| `prefers-reduced-motion` 블록 제거 | 1건 실패 |
| 한 분기에서 `withCompose` 누락 | 겹침 카운트 1건 실패 |
| **`key={composeEpoch}` 제거** | **브라우저 실측 — 저장한 글이 실제로 안 나타남** |
| `adSuppressed` 무시(배너 항상 렌더) | 1건 실패 |
| `dimClosable` 항상 `true` | 2건 실패 |

## 변경 규모

| 구분 | 줄 수 (vs `origin/main`) |
|---|---|
| 구현 코드 (`App.tsx`·`ui.tsx`·`Story.tsx`·`global.css`) | **+217 / −34** |
| 테스트 3파일 | +186 / −12 |
| 문서(plan.md·changelog) | +48 / 0 |
| **합계 (9파일)** | **+451 / −46** |

밝은선 ④(코드 ±150줄)에 해당해 **독립 리뷰를 이미 돌렸다**(이 PR의 커밋 2가 그 반영분). ①②는 비해당. ③(수익 경로)은 **리뷰 결과 해당으로 판명** — 배너를 직접 고치진 않았지만 겹침이 배너 수명주기를 바꿔 무효 트래픽을 만들고 있었다(I-2). 지금은 main과 같은 동작이고, 「한 화면에 배너 1개」도 유지된다(컴포저 시트에는 배너가 없다).

body:
Workstream: #601

## What & why

After a successful monthly → annual switch, the Membership card kept showing **Monthly**, at the **monthly price**, with **"Switch to Annual" still offered** on a plan the user had just paid to leave. Found live during PR #600's pre-merge UAT, step 4.

Sibling of #600 — same class, different site. #600 was the *absent*-mirror case at the render gate; this is the *stale*-mirror case at the price derivation.

**Review budget:** `sensitive` tier, 5 rounds — payments surface. Receipt: `.agents/receipts/loop-budget-602.json`.

**UAT:** [`docs/tests/UAT/PR602_BILLING_CYCLE_FROM_APP_DB_UAT.md`](docs/tests/UAT/PR602_BILLING_CYCLE_FROM_APP_DB_UAT.md) — 4 steps + 3 regression checks. This PR also **unblocks PR #600's script**, whose steps 4–6 were held behind this bug; those notes are removed here because merging this makes them false.

## Approved-plan oracle

**Fix tier:** B — Q1 fired (payments), and Q2.2 (it changes a render predicate: `isMonthly` decides whether the switch button exists). Tier C ruled out on every ground: no behavior change — the intended behavior is what the code's own comment already stated — no schema/migration/backfill, no design flaw, no new abstraction, no vendor.

**Reported symptom:** David, during PR #600's subset UAT, immediately after confirming the switch: "It paused for a moment while processing then the dialog closed. However the screen still looks the same as it did before I performed the upgrade." The card continued to read *Monthly subscription*, *$3.99/month*, with **Switch to Annual — save 48%** still offered. No error banner and no amber stale-records notice.

**Intended correct behavior:** stated by the code itself, at the comment this PR replaces — *"avoid showing 'Switch to Annual' immediately after an upgrade (before webhook fires)"*. After a successful switch the card should report the plan the user is actually on.

**Must not change:**
- A genuine monthly subscriber still sees "Switch to Annual" and their `$3.99/month`.
- Legendary for Life still shows no recurring controls; non-members still get the Free Plan block.
- A subscription cancelling at period end still hides the controls and offers Reactivate.
- #600's behavior is preserved exactly: controls still appear while the mirror row is entirely **absent**.
- Where the app DB has nothing to say, the mirror is still used — this inverts precedence, it does not drop the mirror.

**Root cause:** The precedence was inverted, on a false premise in its own comment:

> `// Live Stripe price data takes precedence over the DB-cached plan to avoid`
> `// showing "Switch to Annual" immediately after an upgrade (before webhook fires).`

`price` is derived from `sub`, which is the **`stripe.subscriptions` mirror** — a row the webhook *writes*, not live Stripe data. So the value given precedence was precisely the one that lags, while `appSub.plan` — written synchronously by the entitlement refresh the moment the switch succeeds — was correct throughout. **The guard produced the exact symptom it was written to prevent.** Someone read "from Stripe" as "live".

Live evidence from the dev DB at the moment of failure: `membership_entitlements` read `plan = annual`, `active`, period end 2027-08-29, `updated_at` 04:46:20Z — the moment of the click. The mirror row for the same subscription still carried the monthly price id and `recurring.interval = "month"`, `_last_synced_at` 04:43:04Z, about three minutes *earlier*. No sync ran in between.

Not the documented stale-state path: the switch route returned success, not `localStateStale`, so no amber notice appeared and none should have.

**Blast radius:** all five consumers of the stale `price`, enumerated before the fix:

| Site | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `planLabel` | mirror interval beat `appSub.plan` → card read **Monthly** | reads one derived `planInterval`, app DB first |
| `isMonthly` | mirror interval won → **switch re-offered** | same derived value |
| price line | rendered **$3.99/month** | shown only while the mirror agrees about the plan |
| `annualPriceAvailable` | keyed on `price?.id`; cross-product fallback still resolved | unchanged — no visible effect either way |
| `savingsPercent` | computed for a switch already made | unchanged; unreachable once the button is correctly hidden |

Nothing outside this component reads `price` — it is a local derivation, and `grep` for it in the file returns only the rows above plus the type declaration.

**Why the amount stays on the mirror:** it is the one field with no app-DB fallback — only Stripe knows what was actually charged. Rather than re-derive or guess it, it is now suppressed while the mirror contradicts the authoritative plan. A stale amount beside a corrected plan label reads as authoritative and is wrong; no amount is the honest answer until the sync lands. That asymmetry is deliberate and is the one judgement call in this diff worth challenging.

## Verification

Proven against the bug — reverted the fix, kept the tests:

```
$ npx vitest run src/__tests__/SubscriptionPanel.test.tsx    # fix reverted
 × reports the annual plan from the app DB while the mirror still says monthly
 × suppresses the charged amount rather than showing the pre-switch price
 Tests  2 failed | 8 passed (10)

$ npx vitest run src/__tests__/SubscriptionPanel.test.tsx    # fix restored
 Tests  10 passed (10)
```

Exactly the two new tests fail, and #600's five still pass — so this neither regresses the sibling fix nor passes for the wrong reason. Five tests total added, including the mirror-caught-up case, the both-agree case, and an app-DB-silent case proving the mirror fallback survives.

```
$ npx tsc -b            # exit 0
$ npx vitest run        # Test Files 97 passed (97) | Tests 1008 passed (1008)
$ pnpm run build        # Done
$ pnpm run check:docs   # ✓ 149 files
```

**To observe the fix:** as a monthly subscriber, switch to annual. The card reports **Annual** with the renewal date a year out, and no longer offers a switch. The `$X/month` line stays absent until Stripe's copy catches up, then reappears as `$24.99/year`.

## Post-merge verification (live environment)

none needed — the stale-mirror condition is reproduced deterministically in the regression suite. No migration, no config change, nothing environment-specific in the diff.

## Checklist

- [x] **Docs stay true** — `pnpm run check:docs` passes. PR #600's UAT script is updated here because this merge invalidates its blocker notes. The precedence rule this restores is stated in the code; a durable write-up is queued in #599's harvest notes for the batched pass.
- [x] **Build gate reproduced when relevant** — frontend change, `pnpm run build` green.
- [x] **General fix, not one example** — one derived value replaces two independent re-derivations, so the class is closed by construction rather than patched twice; negative cases cover mirror-agrees, mirror-caught-up and app-DB-silent.
- [x] **Ship the surface** — the fix *is* the UI surface; UAT doc ships on this PR.
- [ ] ~~**Async shows status**~~ — n/a.
- [ ] ~~**Human decisions preserved**~~ — n/a.
- [ ] ~~**Migration safety**~~ — n/a.
- [x] **In scope** — one derived value plus its tests, and the two doc edits this merge forces. The `POST /stripe/checkout` double-subscribe gap found alongside this is deliberately not touched; it is a product question for David.

author: os-sales
body:
Fixes #6059

Triage picked option 1: *"Export the pair from the package entry and rebind the hand-composed site(s)."* No behaviour change on either chain — the card says so outright, and the pin below is what holds it.

## The gate first: is a new dependency edge being added? No.

The card's own body flags the cost triage did not: option 1 *"makes the console's form page import a heavy React widget package for a pure function."* Measured on this branch's base (`546f61099`) before anything was edited:

| Question | Reading | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Does `apps/console` declare `@object-ui/plugin-form`? | yes, `workspace:*` | `apps/console/package.json`, `devDependencies` |
| Does `apps/console/src` already import it at runtime? | yes, a side-effect import | `apps/console/src/register-plugins.ts:29` |
| Is that import on the app's eager path? | yes | `apps/console/src/main.tsx:30` imports `./register-plugins` |

So the edge already exists and the "heavy React widget package" is already paid for on every console page load. The new import in `FormPage.tsx` joins two modules that are **both** already in the eager closure — `main.tsx` reaches plugin-form through `register-plugins`, and `App.tsx:49` reaches `FormPage` — so it adds no chunk and no bytes to it. (`check:eager-closure` weighs the real number in CI off a console build.)

Had the answer been no, this PR would not exist: the order was to stop and report, because option 2 — moving the composed helper down to `@object-ui/core` beside the two predicates, as objectui#4085 already did for `isRuntimeDefault` — would then be a decision rather than an implementation choice.

## What became importable, and why not one name more

`packages/plugin-form/src/index.tsx` now re-exports exactly two names from `schemaDefaults.ts`:

- **`omitServerResolvedDefaults(values, objectSchema)`** — the rule the card is about: drop the keys a CREATE payload must leave to the producer.
- **`isRequiredInForm(field, isCreateForm)`** — its documented pairing, named by triage.

They travel together because each one's docblock names the other as its half: excusing a server-owned field from `required` and then submitting the key anyway is not half a fix, it is no fix, and a consumer able to reach one but not the other can build exactly that state.

**Deliberately withheld:** `seedCreateValues`, `schemaDefaultValues`, `isSeedableDefault`, `isCreateFormMode`, `SeedContext` — adjacent, not asked for, and every added name is published surface somebody then has to keep. `isRuntimeDefault` stays out for a stronger reason: it is `@object-ui/core`'s to publish (that is what objectui#4085 settled), and this module only re-exports it for its own call sites.

That negative half is asserted, not left to the reviewer's eye — `packages/plugin-form/src/__tests__/entrySurface-6059.test.tsx` pins that the entry adds these two and no other name from that module, and that each is the *same function object* the package's own containers call rather than a second implementation.

## The rebind

`apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx` `omitServerOwnedBlanks` keeps the two things that are genuinely this renderer's — the create-mode gate, and the projection of its own rendered rows onto the shape the helper reads — and delegates the rule:

```ts
if (!isCreateForm) return values;
return omitServerResolvedDefaults(values, {
  fields: Object.fromEntries(fields.map((f) => [f.name, { defaultValue: f.defaultValue }])),
});
```

`isMissingForRequired` is no longer imported here. `isRuntimeDefault` still is — objectui#5727's seeding fence is *one* predicate, not a composition, and its sibling deliberately differs about `null`.

The rows rather than `loaded.objectSchema`: the previous verdict was a function of the RENDERED rows, and `RenderableField.defaultValue` is copied straight off the object field in `buildSections` with no FormView override for that key, so the projection carries exactly the defaults the deleted code consulted, for exactly the same names. Passing the whole object schema instead would have been a behaviour change in the case where the payload holds a key no row declares — which this card does not license.

## The pin, and it is RED against a wrong composition

`apps/console/src/components/FormPage.omitBlanksRebind.test.ts`. The oracle is the code this PR deleted: `handComposed` is the pre-#6059 body verbatim, and 94 cases — every default shape (absent / static / runtime token / CEL envelope) crossed with every value spelling a control on this page writes back (`''`, `null`, `undefined`, `[]`, `false`, `0`, a typed value), in both modes, plus payloads holding a key no row declares — must agree with it on value **and key order**.

"Agrees with the reference" is satisfiable by a matrix too narrow to tell two implementations apart, so the suite also carries four ways of getting this rule wrong (`or`, `no-create-gate`, `blank-string-only`, `value-only`) and asserts the shipped function disagrees with each of them at a named case.

Two ablations, run against the committed implementation, each with the mutation confirmed on disk by counting the removed and injected text and the restore proven by an empty `git diff HEAD` plus a blob-hash match:

| Mutation | Pin |
|---|---|
| `&&` to `\|\|` in `omitServerResolvedDefaults` (plugin-form) | **RED** — 4 failed, 6 passed |
| create-mode gate deleted from `omitServerOwnedBlanks` (console) | **RED** — 3 failed, 7 passed |
| restored tree, re-read | green — 10 passed |

The first leg is the one worth noting: a one-character edit in **another package** turns the console's pin red with no build step, because both `vitest.config.mts:285` and `apps/console/vite.config.ts:456` alias `@object-ui/plugin-form` to `packages/plugin-form/src`. The delegation is really being exercised, not a stale `dist`.

## Verified — all readings on `66e7bc548`

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-form/ apps/console/src/components/ apps/console/src/__tests__/` — **114 files, 1363 tests passed**. The existing end-to-end payload pin (`FormPage.serverDefaults.test.tsx`, objectui#5883) is in there unchanged and green, which is the create-payload behaviour asserted through the real render and the real request body.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-form type-check` / `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console type-check` — both `exit 0`, after building the console's dependency closure (34 tasks); before that, the TS2307s are stale-`dist` noise.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-form lint` / `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console lint` — `0 errors` each.
- Gates: `check:readme-exports` OK (`383 real, 0 wrong-path, 0 fabricated`, `0 unbuilt` — the two new names judged `real` at README lines 95/96/334), `check:phantom-deps` OK, `check:self-import` OK, `check:control-bytes` OK, `check:doc-fences` OK, `check:esm-specifiers` OK, `check:published-dist` OK, `check:changeset-presence` OK, `check:changeset-no-major` OK.

Repo-wide `pnpm lint` and `check:eager-closure` (which needs a console `dist`) are left to CI, which runs the farm exactly once either way.

## Changeset

`.changeset/6059-publish-omit-server-resolved-defaults.md` — `@object-ui/plugin-form: minor` (published surface grows), `@object-ui/console: patch`. It spells out exactly what becomes importable and what stays private. Not `major`: objectui's major tracks `@objectstack`'s.
