author: sgajbi
body:
Closes #108.

## The defect

The golden determinism assertion computed its *expected* value by calling the production function under test on the banked PDF:

```python
assert result.diagnostic.bounded_determinism_fingerprint == service._compute_bounded_determinism_fingerprint(expected_pdf)
```

So a weakened `_compute_bounded_determinism_fingerprint` (broadened regexes, or `return ""`) would move the render output and the expected value together, and all five fixtures would still pass. The strictness of the "bounded determinism" comparison — the repo's core proof of deterministic output — was an **untested property of production code**, not a tested one. There was also no test proving the function ever distinguishes two different documents.

## The fix

- **Bank the fingerprint as a literal** per fixture in `producer-fixtures.v1.json`, and assert the render output against that constant. The banked literal is an independent oracle: only the real render can match it, so a weakened function now breaks the golden test.
- **Discrimination (negative) test** pinning both halves of the bounded contract: volatile-only differences (`/CreationDate`, `/ModDate`, `/ID`, `xmp:*`) collapse to one fingerprint, while a one-figure change in the rendered content does not.

## Evidence

- Both new assertions **verified to fail** when `_compute_bounded_determinism_fingerprint` is stubbed to a constant (all five golden fixtures + the discrimination test go red), and pass on the real function. The old self-referential assertion passed the stub silently.
- Full suite **237 passed**; whole-repo ruff/format/mypy (71 files) clean.

## Scope

This is the oracle-integrity half. Broadening the banked *surface* (advisory sections, degraded paths, non-default locales) and the e2e-renders-nothing gap are #109, which depends on this so new goldens assert against an independent oracle.

author: justin808
body:
Adds an `## Install Node Dependencies First` section to AGENTS.md.

## Why

Two separate failures during the v10.3.2 release traced to the same cause — a missing `node_modules` in a fresh worktree — and neither said so:

**1. The release aborted after tagging.** `prepublishOnly` runs `yarn build && yarn type-check`; `tsc` lives in `node_modules/.bin`:

```
> shakapacker@10.3.2 prepublishOnly
> yarn build && yarn type-check
/bin/sh: tsc: command not found
npm error code 127
rake aborted!
```

By then `Release 10.3.2` and tag `v10.3.2` were already committed and pushed, so the repo sat tagged-but-unpublished until the publish was rerun manually.

**2. The lint-staged hook silently reverted a staged commit.**

```
[STARTED] prettier --write
[FAILED] prettier --write [ENOENT]
[STARTED] Reverting to original state because of errors...
✖ Task failed to spawn: prettier --write
```

The commit was discarded — but the following `git push` still ran, publishing a branch at the unchanged base commit. That one is easy to misread as a successful push.

Neither message mentions dependencies, which is what makes this worth writing down rather than leaving to inference.

## What it says

Install first; check `ls node_modules/.bin` before diagnosing a `command not found`; and don't route around it with `--no-verify` — if a hook truly cannot run, run the check it would have run and say so.

## Scope and limits

Documentation only. **This does not make the failure impossible** — it only helps agents. A human running `rake release` in a fresh clone still hits the same wall after tagging.

The durable fix is a `verify_node_modules!` preflight in `rakelib/release.rake`, alongside the existing `verify_npm_auth`, `verify_gh_auth`, and `ensure_clean_worktree!` checks, so the release fails *before* the commit-and-tag step instead of after. Filed separately rather than widening this docs change.

## Validation

- `npx prettier --check AGENTS.md` → clean
- Markdown-only PR, so Node based checks run pre-merge here thanks to #1266

body:
### Motivation
- Real iPhone evidence showed avatars appearing then disappearing because full-body calibration was too strict and tracking loss could cause the avatar to effectively vanish, so calibration gating and loss behavior needed repair without touching the retarget architecture.
- Make calibration robust to mobile confidence (≈0.30) while preserving stricter limb/head retarget thresholds and existing WebGL performance semantics.
- Ensure the avatar remains rendered during HELD/LOST states and smoothly returns to neutral rather than being hidden or instantly snapping. 
- Add diagnostics to prove whether disappearance is CSS/hide/scene-detach/transform-out-of-view and to identify exact calibration rejection reasons. 

### Description
- Introduced independent full-body calibration options and guards in the solver by adding `fullBodyCalibrationConfidence` (default 0.30) and `minimumCalibrationBodyHeight` (default 0.10) while leaving per-limb/head `minimumConfidence` unchanged at 0.50. 
- Rewrote `fullBodySample()` to return explicit rejection diagnostics and per-joint confidences (e.g. `LOW_LEFT_ANKLE_CONFIDENCE`, `BODY_AXIS_MISSING`, `SUBJECT_TOO_SMALL`, `SUBJECT_INCOMPLETE`) and expose `fullBodyCalibrationRejectedReason` and `fullBodyCalibrationJointConfidences`. 
- Kept pre-calibration limb retargeting active when full-body calibration is not ready, preserving existing limb motion path and stricter limb confidence for rotations. 
- Implemented lost-state lifecycle improvements so TRACKING→HELD→LOST keeps the model visible and uses existing smoothing to lerp/slerp the root/torso/limbs/head back to neutral; added `validRootTarget()` to guard against NaN/Infinity in root position and quaternion and record `rootTransformRejectedReason`. 
- Added runtime proof fields to the solver diagnostics (e.g. `solverState`, `fullBodyCalibrationState`, `lastValidFullBodyAt`, `rootTransformValid`, `avatarRootPosition`, `avatarRootQuaternion`) and to the mirror diagnostics (canvas found/display/visibility, computed visibility, model visible/attached, sampled world bounds). 
- Propagated authoritative `renderer`, `scene`, and `canvas` into the mirror session from the workout page so bounds and canvas diagnostics can be cheaply sampled at a throttled rate. 
- Bumped the three coupled runtime asset cache id to `2026-08-29-full-body-loss-recovery-v1` for `normalized-pose.js`, `avaturn-live-pose-solver.js`, and `live-avatar-mirror.js`. 
- Added focused automated tests that cover realistic mobile calibration acceptance, explicit rejection reasons, limb retarget before calibration completes, LOST smoothing and visibility preservation, invalid root transform rejection, calibration reset/reacquisition, and cache-coherence wiring. 

### Testing
- Unit + focused integration: ran `node --test test/avaturn-live-pose-solver.test.js test/live-avatar-mirror.test.js` and related wiring tests and the new/updated tests reporting all focused assertions passed (solver/mirror focused tests: 16/16 passed, wiring/cache coherence and related production wiring checks passed). 
- End-to-end/local suite: `npm run lint` and `npm run security:check` succeeded and `git diff --check` returned clean. 
- Full repository test run: `npm test` (full suite) reported failures that are unrelated to this focused repair (pre-existing stale expectations in unrelated modules), so the focused regression and affected suites passed while the full suite has unrelated failures. 
- All added/changed tests included in this PR passed locally in the environment; no physical iPhone test has been performed yet.

author: mahesh-sangawar
body:
Closes #436.

## What was actually wrong

`migrations/000004_orders_seq_eager.up.sql:33-60` installs an `AFTER INSERT ON stores` trigger creating **two** sequences per store (`mk_seq_order_<id>`, `mk_seq_return_<id>`). Nothing ever drops them — `TRUNCATE` does not touch catalog objects, and `tenantpurge` had zero sequence handling.

The dev database reached **27,990**, all of them orphaned (`stores` = 0 rows), at which point `pg_dump` failed outright:

```
pg_dump: error: out of shared memory
HINT: You might need to increase max_locks_per_transaction.
```

`pg_dump` takes `ACCESS SHARE` on every relation in one transaction, and `max_locks_per_transaction` is 64 with `max_connections` 100 — roughly 6,400 slots.

## Correcting my own issue title

**This is not a production emergency.** `docs/ops/2026-07-29-bondi-sequence-ownership.md:26` records **16 `mk_seq_order_*` sequences** in production as of 2026-07-29 — 16 stores, 32 sequences, growth proportional to real stores. The 27,990 was a dev/test pathology. The issue is retitled accordingly.

Two real bugs remained, both smaller than the original title implied.

## 1. Tenant purge left them behind (production-relevant, small)

A purged tenant orphaned two catalog objects per store, permanently. Fixed by dropping each purged store's sequences inside the same purge transaction, after the final `stores` delete — DDL is transactional in Postgres, so it commits or rolls back atomically with the purge.

**It could not be a `deleteStep`**: those carry *parameterised* statements, and a sequence name is an identifier, not a bind value. A pure `storeSequenceNames` helper parses each id as a uuid and errors on anything else, so a malformed id aborts the purge rather than silently dropping nothing.

**Excluded from `Report`, deliberately.** `Report` documents every step *of the plan*, and this is not one. `TableResult` is a `(table, rows)` pair; `RowsAffected` is meaningless for DDL, and a synthetic zero-row entry would read to an operator as "a table that held nothing" — a different and false claim. `countPlan` derives from `purgePlan`, so it could not preview a DROP in principle.

## 2. Test fixtures leaked them — and the first fix was not enough

`SeedStore` now drops both sequences before deleting the store row (sequences first, so a `RESTRICT`-blocked delete still reclaims the catalog objects).

**But `SeedStore` turned out to be one of at least seventeen sources.** After sweeping the dev database to zero, a single suite pass put **4,152 back**: nineteen test files `INSERT INTO stores` directly and only three drop sequences, and handler tests create stores over HTTP. A per-fixture drop cannot reach them, and the next fixture added leaks again with nothing failing.

So `testdb.NewDB`'s cleanup now sweeps orphans whenever it truncates `stores` — the operation that creates them. That is self-healing and needs no discipline from whoever writes the next test. Measured across the two guarded packages: **586 → 2**.

The work is bounded (`LIMIT 500`, so a backlog drains over runs rather than stalling one) and best-effort (a sweep failure never fails a passing test).

## 3. The dev database

Swept 27,990 → 0. The orphan predicate was verified in **both** directions before dropping anything: the negative half (`live_store_seqs = 0`), and the positive half by inserting a probe store inside a rolled-back transaction and confirming the predicate classified exactly 2 as live and excluded them. Without that second check, a predicate matching *everything* would look identical against an empty `stores` table.

Batched at 2,000 per transaction — one transaction would have exhausted the same lock table that broke `pg_dump`.

**`pg_dump` now succeeds**: 254,525 bytes.

## Test plan

All runs used `TEST_DATABASE_URL='postgres://dev:dev@192.168.1.110:5432/marketplace_db?sslmode=disable'` with `-p 1 -count=1`, all EXECUTED.

- [x] `TestSeedStore_CleanupDropsPerStoreSequences` — **mutation:** remove the drop loop → fails `expected: 0, actual: 2`
- [x] `TestIntegration_Purge_DropsPerStoreSequences` — **mutation:** `return nil` instead of `dropStoreSequences` → fails `expected: 0, actual: 2`
- [x] The first test **must** use `testdb.NewDB`, not `NewTx` — under `NewTx` the trigger's `CREATE SEQUENCE` rolls back and the assertion would hold with or without the fix
- [x] `pkg/testdb` and `internal/tenantpurge` green; the sweep verified to drop 584 orphans in one run
- [x] `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go vet -tags=integration ./...`, `gofmt` clean

**On the intermittent failures seen during development:** `internal/tenantpurge` failed on some runs while a concurrent worktree held ~44 sessions against the same database. Ruled out as environmental by running the identical package combination at base and at HEAD once contention cleared — **0 failures in every case**, and `tenantpurge` alone is green.

## Not done

The long-term fix is retiring catalog objects for document numbering — a per-store counter *row* in the `store_transactional_counter` shape, which would be purgeable by a plain `DELETE`. Migration 000003 pivoted *away* from that on contention grounds (p99 ~244ms → ~60ms), so it needs re-benchmarking against the 75ms M1 gate before adoption. Worth noting the numbers are explicitly **not** required to be gapless (`000004:29-31`), so the counter could commit in its own short transaction rather than being held for the life of the order-create transaction — which is likely the whole difference. Out of scope here.

Adds a read-only migration preflight for the current ArkShop backend drift.

The preflight compares SQLite and MySQL without logging player IDs, balances, Kits JSON, database names, or credentials. It emits only aggregate counts and SHA-256 digests of player identity/state.

It distinguishes:
- exact state match (safe switch candidate)
- SQLite authoritative / MySQL empty
- MySQL authoritative / SQLite empty
- same players with state drift
- backend player-set mismatch
- duplicate player IDs

No database writes, ArkShop config writes, reloads, restarts, or backend switching are included in this PR.

author: yukon-autoresearch[bot]
body:
Yukon submission `5573ea76-a597-4945-841c-dfd68be40af8` against https://github.com/Layr-Labs/mlxfast-gemma4-26b-a4b-engine at `38269aa8323dd65597d8cfb648d0c6194b8c16dd`.

Current best score: 1.80490404511208. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
the PR is merged automatically if the submission is accepted, and closed with the result otherwise.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: Claude Opus 5
Harness: Claude Code

The shared reduction preamble in the fused layer-glue kernels opened by zeroing
all 32 shared slots and needed a barrier to publish that zeroing. Only 22 slots
are ever written, so the zeroing is replaced by selecting zero on the read
side. One file, one preamble; no gate, shape, dispatch geometry, dtype or
numeric format changes.

## File

`Vendor/mlx-swift-lm/Libraries/MLXLLM/Models/Gemma4Text.swift`, inside
`private enum Gemma4FusedLayerGlue`.

## Before

```
acc = simd_sum(acc);
if (simd_group_id == 0) local_sums[simd_lane_id] = 0;
threadgroup_barrier(mem_flags::mem_threadgroup);
if (simd_lane_id == 0) local_sums[simd_group_id] = acc;
threadgroup_barrier(mem_flags::mem_threadgroup);
if (simd_group_id == 0) {
    acc = simd_sum(local_sums[simd_lane_id]);
    if (simd_lane_id == 0) {
        SLOT = metal::precise::rsqrt(acc / 2816.0f + 1e-06f);
    }
}
threadgroup_barrier(mem_flags::mem_threadgroup);
```

Each thread accumulates four squares, folds them with `simd_sum`, publishes one
partial per simdgroup into `threadgroup float local_sums[32]`, and simdgroup
zero folds those partials again and writes the inverse scale.

## After

```
acc = simd_sum(acc);
if (simd_lane_id == 0) local_sums[simd_group_id] = acc;
threadgroup_barrier(mem_flags::mem_threadgroup);
if (simd_group_id == 0) {
    acc = simd_sum(
        simd_lane_id < 22 ? local_sums[simd_lane_id] : 0.0f);
    if (simd_lane_id == 0) {
        SLOT = metal::precise::rsqrt(acc / 2816.0f + 1e-06f);
    }
}
threadgroup_barrier(mem_flags::mem_threadgroup);
```

## Why 22

`Gemma4FusedLayerGlue` declares `rows = 8`, `axis = 2816`, `nReads = 4` and
`tgThreads = 704`, and every wrapper dispatches
`grid: (rows * tgThreads, 1, 1)` against `threadGroup: (tgThreads, 1, 1)`.
A threadgroup of 704 threads is exactly 22 simdgroups of 32, so
`local_sums[simd_group_id] = acc` only ever writes slots 0 through 21. Slots 22
through 31 are never written, and the zeroing pass existed solely so that the
second fold, which reads `local_sums[simd_lane_id]` across all 32 lanes of
simdgroup zero, would see defined values there.

Selecting zero for those lanes on the read side supplies `simd_sum` exactly the
32 values the zeroing pass produced: the 22 real partials in the same slots and
zero in the rest. Adding an exact zero leaves any partial unchanged and the
reduction tree still spans the same 32 lanes in the same order, so every inverse
scale is bitwise what it was.

## Why the remaining barriers are enough

Two barriers remain. The first publishes the partials before simdgroup zero
reads them; the second publishes the finished slot before the rest of the
threadgroup reads it, and it is also what makes back-to-back reductions safe,
because a later reduction's write to `local_sums[simd_group_id]` cannot start
until every thread has passed it. The barrier that is removed only ordered the
zeroing against the partial writes, and with no zeroing there is nothing for it
to order: the write `local_sums[simd_group_id] = acc` is the first access to
each slot in every reduction.

The kernels that take several reductions in a row still read each inverse scale
out of `local_inv` into a register before a later reduction can overwrite that
slot, which is unchanged.

## Scope

No weight is re-quantized, re-represented, or changed in numeric format. No
cache is added. Nothing keys on prompt content: the predicates in `admits()`
are dtype, rank, dimension and the `eps == 1.0e-6` check, and none of them
moved. Input and output names, counts, shapes and dtypes are as they were, and
the kernels remain `ensureRowContiguous: true` `static let` members.

`DARKBLOOM_GEMMA4_LEAN_RMS=0` restores the zeroing pass and its barrier in the
same binary, which is how the two forms were compared.

## Measured

`swift test --force-resolved-versions` passes. Local
`./benchmark.sh --local-iterate` passes correctness at 130 checked steps with
the switch in either position.

## Where the preamble is used

`rmsReduce` is the shared text every glue kernel builds its reductions from,
so the change reaches all of them at once:

- `gemma4_glue_norm_residual_*` takes one reduction over its input before the
  weighted norm and the residual add.
- `gemma4_glue_dual_prenorm_*` takes one reduction and emits two pre-normed
  copies from it.
- The tail kernels take three reductions in a row: one over each branch
  output, then one over their weighted sum, and the chained variant takes a
  fourth over the finished row to emit the next layer's normalized input.

The tails are where the saving concentrates, because the removed write and
barrier come off once per reduction and those kernels run three or four.

## What is not changed

The accumulation itself is untouched: four squares per thread in the same
order, `simd_sum` over the same 32 lanes, one partial per simdgroup into the
same slot index, and the same
`metal::precise::rsqrt(acc / 2816.0f + 1e-06f)` written by lane zero of
simdgroup zero. `local_sums` keeps its declared size of 32; only the write
that filled slots 22 through 31 is gone, and those slots are now read as an
immediate zero rather than from threadgroup memory.

Nothing downstream of the preamble moves. Every kernel reads its inverse
scales out of `local_inv` exactly where it did, applies the same weights with
the same roundings, and writes the same outputs.

author: zinntikumugai
body:
公式プログラミングガイド3本を索引化して全機能を棚卸しし、ロードマップを
「AIエージェントが回路調査を自力で進められるか」の軸で組み替えたうえで、
最優先と確定した M4(測定)と M5(トリガ)を実装しました。**MHO98 実機で
全数検証済みです。**

## 何が変わるか

**穴は未実装サブシステムではなく、実装済みサブシステムの内側にありました。**

| サブシステム | 変更前 | 変更後 |
|---|---|---|
| `:MEASure:ITEM` | 41トークン中 **10** | **41**(全項目) |
| `:TRIGger` | 20種中 **EDGE の1種** | **16種**(標準搭載すべて) |
| 測定統計 / 測定区間 / しきい値 | 未実装 | `configure_measurement` / `get_measurement_statistics` |

登録Tool数 38 → **40**。トリガは `configure_trigger` に `type` + `settings` を
足す形で、新Toolを増やしていません(`configure_decode` と同じ構造)。

## 実機検証(MHO98 / fw 00.01.00)

read-only **19 passed** / write **41 passed**(トリガ16種を全数往復、復元漏れゼロ)。
記録: `docs/verification/mho98-m4-m5.md`(IP・シリアル非記載)。

**実測で実装バグ6件・機器の限界1件・ガイドの誤植1件が判明し、いずれも反映済みです。**

M4(測定):

1. **しきい値に小数形を送ると黙って壊れる** — `:MEASure:SETup:MAX 88.0` は
   エラーキューが `0,"No error"` のまま値が 100 へ張り付く。ガイドの型は
   Integer。absoluteモードは小数が要るが整数形も受理するので「整数値のときだけ
   小数点を落とす」で両立させた
2. **`:MEASure:AMP:TYPE` は長形 `MANual` が `-222` で拒否され、短形 `MAN` が通る**
3. **同時に有効化できる測定項目は12程度が上限**(16以上で番兵値が収束しない)。
   `RELIABLE_MEASUREMENT_BATCH = 12` を置いて警告を添える(拒否はしない)

M5(トリガ):

4. **`get_trigger_position` が `NameError`** — ユニットテストが無く実機で初めて発覚
5. **`pattern` / `duration` の `pattern` は ch別のリスト**。単一の列挙値として
   実装していたため**両種別が丸ごと使えなかった**
6. **`:TRIGger:LIN:DATA?` は2進のビットマスク文字列**(`'01100100'` / 未設定は
   `'XXXXXXXX'`)。ガイドは「整数を返す」と書いているが実機は違う

**V-9 決着**: `:TRIGger:WINDows:SLOPe` のガイド Range欄 `RFALI` は誤植。
Remarks欄の `RFALl` が正しい(`RFALI` は `-222` で拒否される)。

> **検証の教訓**: 最初は3種(edge / pulse / i2c)だけを回して「検証済み」と
> 判断しかけました。16種すべてを送って初めてバグ3件(4〜6)が出ています。
> 項目表が同じ機構でも、種別ごとの応答形式は実際に送らないと分かりません。

## その他、実機で判明した挙動

- **種別を切り替えるとトリガレベルがサブツリー間で伝播する**。復元は種別を
  戻したうえでレベルも明示的に書き戻す必要がある
- **`:MEASure:AREA ZOOM` は遅延掃引が無効だと無言で無視される**(エラーを積まず
  読み戻しも変わらない)。`applied` の不一致で検出できる
- `delay` の時間値は機器が量子化する(9e-06 → 8.999999e-06)。requested/applied
  の差として正しく現れるので実装側の対処は不要

## ガイドの罠(いずれもテストで固定)

- `:TRIGger:MODE` のトークンとサブツリー名が一致しない種別が2つ —
  `WINDow`(単数)/ `:WINDows`(複数)、`SETup` / `:SHOLd`
- `WHEN` の値域が種別ごとに違う(共有の表にすると値域外を送る)
- 同じ `POSitive`/`NEGative` でも polarity(パルスの正負)と slope(エッジの
  向き)で意味が違う
- SPI の `CLK`/`SCL`・`MISO`/`SDA` は同義の別名。片方だけ公開した

## ロードマップの再編

章立てを「機器の機能順」から**優先度順**へ(1章=高 / 2章=中 / 3章=低 /
4章=対象外 / 5章=機種プロファイル / 6章=既知の残件 / 7章=検討事項)。
完了済みの経緯は末尾へコメントアウトで退避し、残っていた課題だけを本文へ
引き上げました。他文書からの旧章番号参照18箇所も追従させています。

見送り判断のうち2件を覆しました — `:SEARch`(`COUNt?` が整数、`VALue?` が
各イベントの時刻を返すので全異常の時刻リストが画面遷移なしに作れる)と
`:MASK`(合否件数が整数で返り、ポーリングだけで長時間監視が成立)。
逆に `:LA` は当初格下げしたものを撤回しています(D0-D15 はソースとして各所で
受理され、`bus_width > 4` のパラレルデコードは `:LA` の有効化が前提のため)。

## 残件

- オプション必須のトリガ3種(FlexRay / I2S / MIL-STD-1553)は未実装。
  ライセンスは適用済みなので実機検証の障害は無い
- `VIDeo` トリガは優先度「低」のため未実装
- CURRbit / CODE(データのビット単位マスク編集)は未対応。LIN の `:DATA?` が
  マスクを返すと分かったので、着手するならこの機構と合わせて設計する

## 検証

- `uv run pytest` **1606 passed / 66 skipped**(変更前 1527)
- 実機 read-only 19 passed / write 41 passed
- `git grep "172\.16\."` 空
- 調査に使ったガイド抽出物と118行の対応表は `tmp/`(gitignore)に置き、
  コミットしていません

body:
**What:** Replaced `innerHTML` string concatenation in `setSpeedDisplay` and `setAdvRpmDisplay` functions with a DOM node pooling strategy in the Advanced, Simple, and Shared HUD overlays. 
**Why:** The previous approach forced the browser to parse HTML and destroy/recreate `<span>` nodes up to 60 times a second on high-frequency telemetry updates (speed and RPM changes).

**Measurement:** By reusing existing DOM nodes and strictly mutating `textContent` only when values differ, we eliminate string generation and layout thrashing for continuous readouts, lowering overall GC pressure during active telemetry streaming.

author: yschimke
body:
The CMP/Wasm parity comment had two ways of claiming a regression that was never observed. Both surfaced on #4761.

## A cancelled run still commented

The step was gated on `always()`, which includes cancellation. A fast-follow push cancels the in-flight run via this workflow's concurrency group — so on #4761 the base-player build died mid-flight, `compare` never ran, and the PR got:

> ⚠️ CMP/Wasm parity moved against the pull request base.
> ```
> the comparison did not produce a report
> ```

…seven seconds after a push, describing a comparison that had not happened. Every superseded run does this.

`!cancelled()` keeps the step for real outcomes and drops it for superseded runs. The successor run posts the actual verdict a moment later, which is exactly what happened on #4761: the same comment was patched to `✅ 0 regression(s), 62 unchanged` once the fresh run completed.

## A skipped comparison read as an adverse one

The headline was a two-branch `if`: `success`, else *"parity moved"*. But `compare` is **`skipped`** whenever an earlier step in the job fails — the corpus fetch, either player build, either render — and then the verdict is *unknown*, not adverse.

The body already said so (`the comparison did not produce a report`); the headline directly above it contradicted that, and sends a reviewer hunting a regression nobody measured. It is now a three-way case:

| `steps.compare.outcome` | headline |
| --- | --- |
| `success` | ✅ No CMP/Wasm parity regression against the pull request base. |
| `skipped` | 🚧 CMP/Wasm parity could not be measured — a step before the comparison failed, so this is not a verdict on the diff. |
| anything else | ⚠️ CMP/Wasm parity moved against the pull request base. |

## Test plan

Non-visual change — no render evidence applies.

author: mobeenabdullah
body:
Closes two review findings on #1332 that turned out to be the same function, and one fix answers both.

### The defect

`companionHasColumn` attempted a statement naming the column and read **any** failure as "the column is not there":

```ts
try {
  await adapter.executeQuery(`SELECT ${q(column)} FROM ${q(table)} LIMIT 0`);
  return true;
} catch {
  return false;
}
```

A dropped connection answers `false`. A role permitted to write the companion but not read the catalogue answers `false`. Both are indistinguishable, to every caller, from a companion provisioned before the column existed — and callers treat that answer as a fact about the schema.

`restoreI18nArchive` is where it does damage rather than merely misreporting. It reads this to choose between clearing a locale's `_updated_at` and omitting it. On `false` it omits, so an existing locale row keeps its **newer** timestamp while its content is replaced with **older** archived material. The translation then reads as current when it is not, and the restore reports success, so nothing surfaces.

### The fix

Answered from the table's own column list, through `introspectLiveSnapshot`.

This is not a new position in this file. `mainTableHasColumns`, forty lines above, already chose introspection over a probe and wrote down why:

> Goes through the same introspection the schema pipeline uses rather than a `SELECT ... LIMIT 0` probe. That matters beyond convention: a probe cannot tell "this column does not exist" from "the database is unreachable" [...] Introspection fails loudly, and this deliberately does not catch.

Its sibling then did exactly the thing that comment warns against. This makes the two agree. It also removes the last hand-built statement from the localization write path, which is what `AGENTS.md:273` asks for.

A companion that does not exist has no columns and so still answers `false` — unchanged from the probe, which failed its statement on the missing relation.

### What is deliberately NOT changed

`companionTableExists` stays a plan-only probe, and the contrast is documented at both sites rather than left looking like an oversight. It backs the cached readiness verdict that **every localized write** consults, so it runs on the request path; a catalogue read there would reintroduce exactly the per-write introspection cost `companion-readiness` exists to remove. The column probes run on schema changes and migrations, where one extra round trip is not measurable. It is also already safe in the way a bare `catch` is not — `isMissingTableError` verifies the dialect's own missing-relation wording and everything else propagates.

### Also in here

- **`RestoreArchiveAdapter` deleted.** It was a hand-copied duplicate of `CompanionIntrospectAdapter` (its own comment: "Minimal adapter surface this helper needs — matches DrizzleAdapter"), and it carried an `eslint-disable no-explicit-any`. The Drizzle handle is now declared as the two statements the helper actually drives, in the same shape `teardown-entity-i18n` uses.
- **Two dispatcher fakes returned a bare `[]` from a postgres `execute`.** node-postgres returns `{ rows }`. Those doubles only ever passed because the old `catch` swallowed the resulting `TypeError` — so the swallow was holding up two tests built on a shape postgres never returns.

### Evidence

Six new tests, break-verified individually against the pre-fix implementation rather than as a suite:

    × reads presence from the column list, not from a statement that parses
    × answers false for a column the table does not carry
    × answers false for a companion that is not there at all
    × does not name another table's columns as its own
    × propagates a failure to READ the shape instead of reporting the column absent
    × propagates a permission refusal, which reads exactly like an absent column
     Tests  6 failed (6)          <- no survivors

and green on the fix:

    cd packages/nextly && pnpm run test               -> 790/790 files, 9792 passed | 42 skipped
    pnpm run check-types                              -> 0
    pnpm run lint                                     -> 0
    node scripts/check-comment-convention.mjs         -> 0
    pnpm exec changeset status                        -> 0
    integration (sqlite), restore-archive + companion-transition + companion-lifecycle
                                                      -> 3 files, 18 tests passed

The wider i18n integration run shows one failure, `enable-disable.integration.test.ts`. That is inherited from `main` and unrelated: a positional `INSERT` the companion outgrew. Fixed separately in #1338.

## 배경
#671 의 첫 `skill_audit_log` 기록에서 backend-developer 에 **배정된** `api-design` 의 `inject` 가 찍히지 않았다. 추적 결과 2겹:

1. **manifest 부재** — `SkillRepository.createSkill`·`upsertSystemSkill`·`skill-creator` 가 `skill_manifests` 를 만들지 않는다(git-ingest 만 08-16 부터 동반). 주입 SoT 가 `skill_manifests` JOIN 이라 active 스킬 **21건**이 배정돼 있어도 한 번도 주입되지 않았다 — user 3 ecc 14(07-17 배정)·시스템 4(`system-skill-author-guide`, superpowers 유틸 3)·auto-llm 2·user 11 1.
2. **카테고리 필터가 명시 배정까지 걸러냄** — `buildManifestPrompt` 는 manifest category ≠ 에이전트 category 면 제외(`user-` 접두 id 만 예외). 에이전트에 직접 배정한 ecc 스킬(`skill-…` id)은 manifest 가 생겨도 걸러진다.

## 변경
- `data/repositories/skill-manifest-sync.ts` `upsertSkillManifest()` — 022/111 과 같은 yaml, sha256 checksum, `ON CONFLICT (id,version) DO UPDATE`. `createSkill`/`upsertSystemSkill`/skill-creator 가 호출(fail-soft), `updateSkill` 은 UPDATE→upsert(레거시 스킬도 갱신 시점에 manifest 가 생김).
- `db/migrations/111_backfill_skill_manifests.sql` — manifest 없는 active 스킬 백필. `signature='backfill-111'` 이 롤백 마커(`rollbacks/111`). **운영 DB 트랜잭션 드라이런: 21건 삽입·checksum 일치·잔여 0 (롤백함)**.
- `agents/manifest-injection-filter.ts`(순수) — 명시 배정(에이전트/`user:<id>`)은 카테고리 무관, `__global__` 만 종전 카테고리 필터, triggers 게이트 유지, 중복 배정 dedupe. `buildManifestPrompt` 가 `asa.agent_id AS assigned_to` 를 SELECT 해 사용.

## 검증
- 신규 테스트 8건(manifest-sync 3·injection-filter 5), 관련 46 스위트 397 테스트 통과, `tsc`·eslint 통과
- 배포 후: 부팅 자동 마이그레이션이 21건 백필 → backend-developer 로 라우팅되는 질문 1회 → `GET /api/agents/skills/usage/summary?days=1` 에 `api-design`·`backend-patterns`·`postgres-patterns` 의 `inject` 확인 예정

## ⚠️ 동작 변화
07-17 에 배정해 둔 ecc 스킬(본문 2~12KB)이 이제 실제로 주입된다 — backend-developer 는 턴당 약 28K 자(api-design·backend-patterns·postgres-patterns) 가 더 들어간다(manifest 블록은 `MAX_SKILL_CONTENT_LENGTH` 절단 대상이 아님). 원치 않는 배정은 풀면 되고, `inject` 로그로 실제 주입을 관측할 수 있다.

Fixes #2488.

## What changed

- Validate `wait_guest_ssh` timeout input as a bounded decimal before deadline comparison/arithmetic.
- Fall empty, nonnumeric, whitespace-bearing, zero-padded/leading-zero interval, or shell-overflow values back to documented finite defaults.
- Tighten package-metadata timeout/interval ingestion with POSIX `case` validation plus numeric range belts.
- Accept SSH and metadata timeouts in `0..86400`; accept canonical metadata intervals in `1..3600`.
- Preserve timeout `0` as a deliberate probe-once/fail value and preserve positive in-range caps exactly.

No external parser, regex process, or dependency was added. The only fail-open `-ge ... && die` deadline shape in `image-upgrade.sh` is now validated before entering its loop; other configured deadline shapes exit to existing explicit failure/activation paths and were not expanded into this ticket.

## Test-first proof

The original five-row selector failed three rows against untouched production: nonnumeric SSH timeout hit the outer salvage cap instead of the crafted 600-second failure; trailing-whitespace SSH timeout was accepted as 7 seconds; trailing-whitespace metadata interval was accepted as 7 instead of falling to 5. Review then found all-digit overflow, zero-padded-zero, and octal-shaped interval classes. Five added frozen rows failed against the prior implementations for exact reasons: huge metadata/SSH timeouts looped, `00` pinned elapsed at zero, huge interval reached the raw sleep value, and `09` aborted in shell arithmetic. author: kulrashm-jpg
body:
**MEDIA-SEC-002** — an authenticated user could attach their media to another company's campaign, injecting it into that company's analytics and AI context.

## Exploitability: confirmed, with zero existing impact

Ownership has been safe since #67 — `user_id` is always the authenticated principal (MEDIA-SEC-001). The **association** was not.

`campaign_id` came straight off the upload form and was persisted verbatim, and [viralitySnapshotBuilder.ts:305](backend/services/viralitySnapshotBuilder.ts#L305) reads campaign media with no user or company scoping:

```ts
.from('media_files').select('*').eq('campaign_id', campaignId)
```

So any authenticated user in Company A could name Company B's campaign. Note who reads it: `/api/campaigns/[id]/virality/assess` authorizes the **caller**, so the attacker cannot read B's data — **the victim** consumes the injected asset while running their own assessment, and it flows into their AI context.

**Verified read-only against production before fixing** (step 8): `media_files` carries the `campaign_id` column — so the write is genuinely possible, not blocked by a missing column — and **0 of 8 rows** currently hold one. Nothing is contaminated today; no remediation of existing data is required, and none was performed.

## Security boundary: the write, not the read

| Option | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **1. Validate at upload** | **Chosen.** This is where untrusted input enters, and `requireCampaignTenantAccess` already exists for exactly this. |
| 2. Scope analytics reads | **Rejected on architecture.** The snapshot builder's signature is `(campaignId)` — it has no request and no principal to authorize against. And `media_files` is USER-anchored (no `company_id`), so scoping the read would mean inventing a second ownership model — explicitly forbidden — and would risk dropping legitimate media uploaded by *other members of the same company*. |
| 3. Defense in depth | Not implementable here without doing (2), so it would buy a conflicting ownership model rather than depth. |

## The fix

The upload route now runs `requireCampaignTenantAccess` whenever a `campaign_id` is supplied. It resolves the campaign's `company_id` **from the database** — never from client input — and delegates to the canonical TenantGuard:

| | |
|---|---|
| unknown campaign | **404** `CAMPAIGN_NOT_FOUND` |
| campaign in another tenant | **403** |
| no principal | **401** |

It runs **before** the file is read or stored, so a refused attempt leaves neither a storage object nor a row, and the parsed temp file is cleaned up. An upload with no `campaign_id` is untouched.

No new auth mechanism, no second ownership model, TenantGuard not bypassed.

## Files — 2

```
pages/api/media/upload.ts                                  +34
backend/tests/unit/mediaSec002CampaignAuthorization.test.ts +246  (new)
```

## Tests — 12

Driving the **real** route and the **real** `requireCampaignTenantAccess` + `assertTenantAccess`; only the data layer, the auth reader and the storage service are scripted, so the guard's actual query shape and HTTP contract are exercised.

| | Scenario | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A | member → own company's campaign | succeeds, association recorded |
| A | no campaign id | unaffected |
| **B** | **Company A → Company B's campaign** | **403, nothing persisted** |
| B | refused request | no row, no storage object, temp file cleaned up |
| B | attacker → their **own** campaign | still succeeds |
| C | unknown campaign | 404, no orphaned association |
| D | unauthenticated | 401, nothing written |
| E/F | analytics consequence | only the victim's own media remains on their campaign |

Plus two MEDIA-SEC-001 non-regression cases, including the one that matters most: **a spoofed `user_id` cannot buy access to another company's campaign**, because the guard sees the authenticated principal.

**Mutation-checked**: removing the guard reproduces the exploit — cross-company attachment succeeds — and fails 5 of the 12.

## Certification

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `typecheck:ci` | 3/3 clean, baseline 0 / actual 0 |
| Backend-tests certification | 260/260, net-new 0 |
| MEDIA-SEC-002 | 12/12 |
| MEDIA-SEC-001 (both suites) | 45/45 |
| 17 closed-issue suites (AUTH-CTX-001, BLOCK-1/2/3, CP-STRUCT-002/003/005, tenant/media) | 221/221 |
| Sweep | 15 failed suites / 35 failed tests — **every one reproduced on a pristine-main baseline** (4 known + 11 pre-existing, run explicitly on `fa92f7c6` to confirm) |

## Remaining media-security debt

`viralitySnapshotBuilder`'s campaign-scoped read is still unscoped by owner. That is now defence-in-depth only — no route can create a cross-tenant association — but it remains true that the builder trusts whatever `campaign_id` associations exist. Any future writer of `media_files.campaign_id` must authorize the campaign the same way this route now does.

author: toddagent01
body:
## What & why

Fixes #6975.

Superset can already open a workspace through a native link such as `superset://v2-workspace/<id>`. The problem is that services such as Linear only accept HTTP(S) links. The existing web URL requires sign-in and does not hand the workspace to the desktop app.

This PR gives integrations one supported HTTPS link that attempts to open the exact workspace in Superset Desktop and leaves a clear fallback when the app is unavailable.

## What changes

- Adds one shared builder for native workspace links and public HTTPS workspace links.
- Adds the public route `/open/v2-workspace/<id>`.
- The page attempts the native handoff automatically, provides an **Open Superset** retry button, shows the full native link, and links to the download page.
- Adds `webUrl` to the JSON returned by `superset workspaces open`.
- Documents the new link for CLI users and Linear integrations.
- Localizes the new page in all supported languages.

## Safety and compatibility

- Workspace IDs must be valid UUIDs.
- Only `chatSessionId`, `terminalId`, and `focusRequestId` may pass through the public URL.
- The public page performs no workspace lookup and exposes no workspace data. The desktop app remains responsible for finding the workspace and reporting missing or inaccessible workspaces.
- Existing native `url`, `--print` output, and desktop-opening behavior are unchanged.
- Self-hosted web origins continue to work through `SUPERSET_WEB_URL`.

## How I tested it

- `bun run lint`
- `bun run typecheck` — 38/38 packages
- `bun run --cwd packages/i18n check`
- Release type and version checks
- 82 affected URL, route, and CLI tests — all passing
- 117 i18n tests — all passing
- A fresh Chromium profile confirmed the route works without authentication, rejects malformed IDs, removes unapproved query parameters, and keeps the fallback visible when no native handler exists.
- A real macOS development deep link opened the exact desktop workspace route with the three supported parameters intact.
- A real CLI call returned both the existing native `url` and the new `webUrl`.

The whole-repository test run still has two unrelated `packages/agent-setup` failures that reproduce unchanged on upstream `main`. This PR does not touch that package.

I verified the positive native path through Superset's development URL scheme because the test host intentionally has no production desktop app installed. The same production main-process handler is used after the scheme is registered.

## Checklist

- [x] PR title follows conventional commits
- [x] `bun run lint` and `bun run typecheck` pass
- [x] Allow edits from maintainers is enabled

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added HTTPS workspace sharing links that open the Superset desktop app.
  * Added an **Open Superset** retry button and download option when the app cannot be launched.
  * CLI workspace-opening output now includes a shareable `webUrl` alongside the native desktop link.
  * Handoff links preserve supported session context while preventing unrelated parameters from being passed through.
* **Documentation**
  * Added guidance for sharing workspace links and troubleshooting desktop handoff behavior.
* **Localization**
  * Added workspace handoff translations across supported languages.

author: juliaregistrator
body:
- Registering package: SimpleSolvers
- Repository: https://github.com/JuliaGNI/SimpleSolvers.jl
- Created by: @michakraus
- Version: v0.13.2
- Commit: dbb787d80baa13821e890a926f7e870510e7bd04
- Reviewed by: @michakraus
- Reference: https://github.com/JuliaGNI/SimpleSolvers.jl/commit/dbb787d80baa13821e890a926f7e870510e7bd04#commitcomment-198181717
- Description: Simple linear and nonlinear solvers in Julia
- Release notes:
<!-- BEGIN RELEASE NOTES -->
`````
Adds the `NeuralNetworkParameters` extension, closing three of the eight type-piracy sites recorded in [GeometricOptimizers#16](https://github.com/JuliaGNI/GeometricOptimizers.jl/issues/16).

### The extension

`GradientAutodiff(F, ps)`, `GradientFunction(F, ∇F!, ps)` and `alloc_h(ps)` for a set of neural network parameters. All three were `GeometricOptimizers`' until 0.6.1, and all three were type piracy there: the functions are this package's and the parameter type is `NeuralNetworkParameters`', so that package owned neither side of any of the three signatures — and piracy is *global*, changing what those functions mean for any session that loads the package, directly or through a dependency. A weak dependency puts the methods with the functions and costs nothing to a caller who does not load `NeuralNetworkParameters`.

A solver here works on a flat `AbstractVector`; a set of parameters is a tree. These three methods are the whole of the seam — `flatten` once, capture the layout in the closure, hand the solver the vector. The layout is a **value**, not a chain of closures, which is what makes it storable and the same on every call.

`alloc_h` sizes `Q` by the **intrinsic** dimension: `flatlength` of a *zero* of the parameters, so a manifold leaf contributes its horizontal lift rather than its dense matrix. For a bare `StiefelManifold` of size `(3, 1)` the generic `x * x'` fallback gives `3 × 3` where the lift has 2 free parameters, and the cache and the state then disagree about how big `Q` is.

### Also added

`GradientAutodiff(F, x::AbstractMatrix)`, which carried the `Matrix` case in `GeometricOptimizers` until 0.6.1 where it was likewise piracy. `AbstractMatrix` and not `Matrix`, so a package with its own matrix-like iterate can reach it by falling through — and can take precedence with a method on that type, which is what `GeometricOptimizers` does for a `Manifold`, where the reconstruction is the manifold's constructor rather than a `reshape`.

### Migrating

The three extension methods take a `NetworkParameters`, `NeuralNetworkParameters` 0.3.0 having removed the `ParameterSet` union they were first written on. A caller holding a bare `NamedTuple` wraps it — `NetworkParameters(ps)` shares the leaf arrays rather than copying them.

### Requires

`NeuralNetworkParameters` 0.3.0.
`````
<!-- END RELEASE NOTES -->

author: hughcameron
body:
`HEXGRID_STROKE` and `GEO_STROKE_COLOUR` in `mark.rs` were raw `Color::new([...])` constants — the last two drawing-path colours the canvas palette did not resolve. Both now come off `ChartInk`, read from the `ScaleSet` the renderers are already handed.

## What the dark values are, and why

Measured against `chrome::INK_DARK.surface` (#161413), WCAG 2.1:

| paint | before, in dark | after | token |
|---|---|---|---|
| geo basemap outline | 1.21:1 | **15.84:1** | `INK_DARK.ink_primary` #efeeec |
| hexgrid mesh | 9.26:1 | **2.95:1** | `GRAY_DARK[7]` #64605c |

The two failed in opposite directions and both are the same defect. A stroke-only basemap **is** the content — there is no fill under it and nothing else on the plot — and #262626 on the dark surface is painted and invisible. The mesh is scaffolding, and #b8b8b8 on the dark surface reads 9.26:1 against the default mark ink's 4.75:1: a bright white lattice laid over the data.

Neither dark value is invented. `ink_primary` is where the geo literal already sat in light (#231f1c against its #262626 — 15.93:1 against its 14.74:1). Warm gray step 8 is where the mesh literal already sat (#b7b3ae against its #b8b8b8, within 10/255 on every channel). The pairing is **step-for-step in the Radix scale rather than ratio-matched**: gray step 8 reads 2.95:1 in dark where its light twin reads 2.03:1, and the ratio-matched alternative — step 7 at 1.99:1 — was rejected because a 0.75px hairline at that ratio on this surface lands back where this started. That is the one judgement here a reviewer might take differently.

**No light value moves.** The light halves stay byte-identical as private consts in `ink.rs`; binding them to their nearest tokens would move values that ship today, which is a separate decision. The tokens are named in the doc comments so the mapping is recorded either way. No committed baseline moved: `snapshot`, `dashboard_baseline` and `surfaces` all pass with a clean `tests/snapshots/`.

## The guard

The check that closed the previous mode-blind-ink work is `grep -rn 'INK_LIGHT\|_LIGHT' crates/brightfield-render/src/`. It catches a paint bound to the wrong mode's *token* and cannot catch a paint bound to no token at all — which is why these two survived it.

Widening the grep to match `Color::new(` buys one round. The next literal is spelled `Color::from_rgba8`, or `0xb8b8b8`, or built from a `[f32; 4]` two lines up. Four strings, one defect.

So `crates/brightfield-render/tests/mode_blind_ink.rs` reads no source text. It drives all 30 renderers in `default_renderers()` over six fixtures, twice each — `ChartInk::LIGHT` and `ChartInk::DARK` — and compares the colours vello encoded into `draw_data`. A paint that took its value from the mode is in one set and not the other. Two claims: no colour is in both modes' scenes, and the set of renderers that drew nothing equals `SILENT`, which is **empty** and asserted as equality rather than as a superset.

Data ink is exempt via `on_the_fill_ramp`, which asks the *scale* whether it can produce the colour rather than naming `Heatmap` and `Raster` — naming them would exempt whatever else those modules ever paint. Residual hole, stated in the file: a hand-typed colour landing within one 8-bit step of the viridis polyline is exempted.

## The pixel gate

`crates/brightfield-shell/tests/dark_mark_ink.rs` composes a dataless hexgrid and a stroke-only basemap through parse → lower → execute → compose → the same `VelloRenderer` the window uses, in `Mode::Dark`, and reads the answer off the raster.

The measurement is cropped to the plot frame, and that line is load-bearing. Over the whole image the brightest pixel of a dataless hexgrid is not its mesh — it is the axis tick label at 3.54:1, out in the margin. Mutating the mesh to gray step 3 and measuring uncropped reports **3.54:1 against 3.60:1**: the two label inks, a verdict with nothing to do with the mesh.

Not `#[ignore]`d and behind no feature, following `snapshot.rs`, `sorted_bar_ink.rs` and `frame_ink.rs`: `test.yml` runs the whole suite on `macos-15` because it is the hosted runner with a real wgpu adapter.

## Every new test broken on purpose

| mutation | test that reddened |
|---|---|
| `hexgrid_stroke` → `Color::new([0.72,0.72,0.72,1.0])` | `every_registered_mark_repaints_when_the_mode_changes` — `Hexgrid … draws #ffb8b8b8 in BOTH modes` |
| same colour as `Color::from_rgba8(0xb8,0xb8,0xb8,0xff)` | same test, same message — the class claim |
| `geo_stroke` → `Color::new([0.15,0.15,0.15,1.0])` | same test — `Geo … draws #ff262626 in BOTH modes` |
| hexgrid `render` returns early | `the_marks_these_fixtures_drive_are_the_committed_set` — and the sweep above went GREEN, which is the vacuity that test exists for |
| dark hexgrid left on the light value | `dark_moves_every_paint_off_its_light_value` |
| dark geo → `gridline` | `the_dark_marks_clear_a_stated_contrast_and_the_literals_do_not` |
| dark hexgrid → gray step 12 | same — `15.84:1 against the default mark ink's 4.75:1` |
| light hexgrid rebound to `GRAY_LIGHT[7]` | `light_resolves_to_the_retired_consts` |
| geo literal restored | `the_dark_basemap_outline_clears_wcag_aaa_on_the_page` — measured **1.21:1** |
| hexgrid literal restored | `the_dark_hexgrid_mesh_is_visible_and_stays_under_the_data_ink` — measured **9.06:1** |
| dark hexgrid → gray step 3 | same test — measured 1.46:1 against the light mesh's 1.91:1 |

The eighth row is why one commit exists on its own: `light_resolves_to_the_retired_consts` first compared the field to the very constant `for_mode` reads, so it was asking whether the field equalled itself and stayed green over a moved light value. Running the mutation found it; reading the test would not have.

## Not done

No new PNG baseline was authored. A dark hexgrid/geo baseline would be a recording of what this branch drew, graded by the branch that drew it. The dark coverage those two mark types now have is the pixel gate above, which reddens on a revert and does not redden on a font bump.

author: averywhitted
body:
## Summary

Implements the "user-generated format template" idea: instead of hand-tuning the shared parser heuristics for every new screenplay layout (the exact whack-a-mole problem the scorecard oracle exists to prevent), a user can now teach the parser one specific script's conventions, per project.

- After importing a script, a **calibration sheet** appears with a live checklist of the six elements the parser needs to identify (character cue, dialog, stage direction, parenthetical, scene heading, overlap indicator). The user tags a few example lines for each from real sample blocks pulled from the actual PDF, or removes an item that doesn't apply to that script — "Continue to Parse" only enables once every item is resolved one way or the other. "Skip — Use Automatic Detection" is always available.
- The derived `FormatProfile` (per-role x-position range + style predicate) seeds/overrides the parser's per-document `DocumentModel` for that project only — it never touches the shared `CONVENTIONS` scorer or `corrections_config.json`.
- Profiles can be **saved to a reusable library** (named, tagged with the originating script) and applied as a starting point for a different project via "Choose from Library…".
- A **"Recalibrate Format…"** toolbar button reopens the sheet later for a project that's already been calibrated.

## Backend (`backend/parser.py`, `backend/audio_worker.py`)

- New `extract_sample_blocks`, `FormatProfile`/`RoleGeometry`/`TaggedExample` dataclasses, `derive_format_profile`, `_classify_block_by_profile`, `_apply_format_profile_to_model`.
- `parse_pdf`, `_build_document_model`, `_classify_blocks`, `_block_parse` all gain an optional `format_profile`/`profile` parameter defaulting to `None` — every existing call site (including all 7 scorecard corpus scripts) is unaffected.
- New `sampleBlocks` / `deriveFormatProfile` bridge commands; `formatProfile` threaded through `parse`, `generate`, `voices`, `checkOutputFiles`, `estimateOpenAI`.

## Swift (`Sources/TableRead/`)

- New `FormatProfile`/`RoleGeometry`/`SampleBlock`/`TaggedBlockExample` models (Models.swift), mirroring the backend's camelCase JSON exactly.
- New `FormatTemplateLibrary` — a cross-project store (sibling to project folders under the same base directory, so it doesn't collide with `ProjectStore`'s project scan).
- `Project.formatProfile` / `formatCalibrationCompleted` (both optional, so old `project.json` manifests decode unchanged).
- New `FormatCalibrationView.swift` — the calibration sheet and library picker.
- `AppState` gains `formatProfile`/`formatCalibrationCompleted`/`showFormatCalibrationSheet` plus `applyFormatProfile`/`skipFormatCalibration`/`startFormatRecalibration`, and threads the profile through every parse/generate/voices/estimate call.

## Testing infrastructure hardening

Testing this PR live in Xcode surfaced a real gap: `scripts/test.sh` was fully green, but the running app returned `Unknown command: 'sampleBlocks'` — a command `audio_worker.py` actually implements correctly. Root cause was two-fold, both now fixed:

- **No test exercised the Swift↔Python subprocess boundary.** Every existing backend test imports `parser`/`audio_worker` in-process; nothing ever spawned `audio_worker.py` the way `PythonBridge.swift` really does (JSON on stdin/stdout). New `backend/tests/test_worker_contract.py` does exactly that for every `"command": "..."` string scraped directly out of `PythonBridge.swift`, asserting none come back "Unknown command". Verified it actually catches this bug class: temporarily renamed the `sampleBlocks` dispatch branch, confirmed the test reproduces the user's exact error, then reverted. Runs in ~2s, no PDF/Xcode needed, as part of the existing `pytest backend/tests/` run.
- **The app bundle can go stale even on correct source.** Xcode's "Copy Python Runtime" build phase copies `backend/*.py` into the app bundle unconditionally, but its declared `inputPaths` only tracked `vendor/python` — so an incremental build could skip re-copying `backend/*.py` after a source edit. Added `alwaysOutOfDate = 1` to that build phase, and `scripts/test.sh`'s Swift suite now diffs the built bundle's copy against source right after building, failing loudly if they ever differ again.

## Testing

- `python scripts/scorecard.py --check` → **exact HOLD, zero delta**.
- `bash scripts/test.sh python` → **82 passed** (80 feature tests + 2 new contract tests).
- CI's **Swift build & tests** and **Python backend tests** are both green on the current head. This session's sandbox has no local Swift/Xcode toolchain, so CI was the first real compile of the Swift changes — it caught two real issues along the way (new files not registered in `TableRead.xcodeproj`, and a test helper missing a `@MainActor` annotation), both fixed and now passing. The new bundle-freshness shell check is syntax-validated locally but hasn't run against a real `xcodebuild` — that still needs a macOS run to confirm end-to-end.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash scripts/test.sh swift` equivalent — CI's Swift build + XCTest job is green on the current head
- [ ] Manual: import a script the parser misclassifies, confirm the calibration sheet appears, tag/exclude items, confirm "Continue to Parse" gating, confirm corrected classification after continuing
- [ ] Manual: save a template to the library, start a different project from it via "Choose from Library…"
- [ ] Manual: "Recalibrate Format…" from the dashboard toolbar, and "Skip — Use Automatic Detection" reverting to today's parse
- [ ] Rebuild in Xcode on the machine that hit the original `sampleBlocks` error and confirm it's resolved

author: vixygrey
body:
Closes #613. Reported in play: **a croc and a silt croc on the same tile** in a salt marsh.

## What was wrong

`SaltMarshZoneGlobals` is a flat list of independent `Chance` rolls, not a `pickone`. So a coat
merged in beside its parent was a *second* roll — the marsh expected **1.0 crocs where vanilla
expects 0.5**, and a quarter of marshes got both.

**30 creatures had drifted the same way. Median 1.6x, worst 2.11x.** Dogs, goats, boars, baboons,
beetles, dragonflies, glowfish. The croc is just the one somebody stood next to.

## The fix

Each group merges vanilla's own entry down and gives the difference to the coats:

```xml
<!-- Croc was 50 in vanilla; now 25 for it and 25 for the variant -->
<object Chance="25" Blueprint="Croc" />
<object Chance="25" Number="1" Blueprint="Vixy_SiltCroc" />
```

`PopulationObject.MergeFrom` overwrites `Chance` and `TryFindSimilar` matches on blueprint name, so
this edits vanilla's entry rather than adding a third. **27 of 30 land on vanilla's figure exactly**;
the other three are within 4.4%, because a chance is an integer and 5 does not divide three ways.
The allocation is hill-climbed per group rather than rounded, which is what got the worst case from
20% down to 4.4%.

## The option had to change with it

This is the part I would look at hardest. `ApplyCreatureVariants` used to **detach** variant entries
when switched off. That is now wrong: a brindle dog and a dog are one dog's worth of chance between
them, so deleting the brindle half would take that dog out of the world rather than repainting it.

It now sets the entry's blueprint to the one it inherits from. **Off means ordinary, not absent** —
and because `Chance` and `Number` never move, density is identical in both states with no arithmetic
at all. It stays idempotent and reversible like the rest of that class.

## Why nothing caught it, and what does now

`scatter-share` measures this fork's share of a merged table against a 50% ceiling.
`SaltMarshZoneGlobals` is about **a tenth** ours while holding twice vanilla's crocs, because 260
watervine and brinestalk drown one reptile. **Share is a property of a table; density is a property
of a blueprint.**

`variant-density` asks the second question, against a new `variant_parent_quantities` snapshot
section. That section stores vanilla's expectation **and** the entry's `Number` midpoint, which is
not redundant: a merge that lowers a `Chance` states no `Number`, so `MergeFrom` leaves vanilla's in
place, and without the midpoint this fork's own side of the sum cannot be computed.

Verified in both directions — it reports **30 findings against the pre-fix tables** and is clean
after, with three unit tests covering fire, clean, and the no-vanilla-figure boundary.

## The stacking itself is vanilla's, and I left it alone

`PlaceObjectInArea` guards against two creatures in one cell, then guards again on the way out:

```csharp
else if (gameObject.IsCombatObject() && Z.GetCell(location2D).HasCombatObject())
    Z.GetCell(location2D).getClosestPassableCell().AddObject(gameObject);
```

`getClosestPassableCell()` sorts every passable cell by distance **from the cell it was called on**,
and a cell is at distance 0 from itself. Creatures are `Physics Solid="false"`, so the occupied cell
is passable — and comes back. The object lands exactly where the branch exists to prevent.

Reaching that would need Harmony or a replacement zone builder; rule 5 refuses the first and the
second is a large new capability for somebody else's defect. What this fork controls is how often
placement gets there. It is recorded in `docs/LESSONS.md` instead — **along with a correction to the
entry that claimed creatures were exempt from this whole class of bug.** That claim was a true fact
about a real line of code, and the conclusion still did not hold, because I had read one guard in a
method with two.

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 tools/validate_mod.py` — clean; **30 `variant-density` findings** when the old tables are restored
- [x] `python3 tools/compile_scripting.py` — 51 files, 0 warnings
- [x] `python3 tools/check_docs.py` — figures, links, sections, check names clean
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tools.test_validate_mod tools.test_snapshot_qud_api tools.test_check_docs` — 223 + 144, all pass
- [x] Density verified independently against vanilla's tables: 30 groups, worst deviation 4.4%
- [ ] **Not played.** The arithmetic is checked; a salt marsh with one croc in it is not

author: netlify-coding[bot]
body:
🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/stepitupstrategies/agent-runs/6a9268b5ab35995e39bb6704

🤖 **Agent:** Claude

💬 **Prompt:** The Netlify deploy errored, with the following guidance provided:

The build failed before it could even start compiling—this is a repository preparation error, not a code or dependency error.

**Cause of the error**

[Line 2](#L2) and [line 5](#L5) ...

✅ **Result:** Yes — the SEO work was substantially in place but not finished. An audit of every route found five
real problems, all of which have now been fixed.

## The homepage service markup was hand-written and contradicted the site's own entity rules

The `#services` section of the homepage carried a hand-maintained block of nine `Service` records,
written out as literal JSON separately from the service content that renders the visible cards. It
had three problems at once.

Each of the nine restated the company inline as its own bare organization carrying nothing but a
name. The site's structured data is deliberately built as a single entity graph in which every
page-level record references the one sitewide business, precisely so the company resolves as one
entity rather than many — and this block broke that rule nine times on the most important page,
creating nine thin duplicate companies competing with the real one.

None of the nine carried a URL or an image, so nothing connected a service described on the homepage
to the detail page that actually covers it. Search engines had no way to tell the two were the same
service.

Being hand-written and duplicating copy that already exists in the service data, it was also free to
drift out of sync with the visible text, and adding a tenth service category would have silently left
it out.

It is now generated from the same data that renders the cards, so it cannot drift and new categories
are covered automatically. Every entry references the sitewide business instead of restating it, and
each carries the URL and image of its detail page. All nine were verified to produce valid, unique,
complete markup.

## The nine services existed twice over in the graph

Separately, the homepage and each service detail page both described the same service, but neither
gave it an identifier, so each page created an anonymous record. The detail page's capabilities and
FAQs attached to one copy of a service and the homepage's description to another, and neither
accumulated the strength of both.

Both pages now describe each service under one shared, stable identifier, so the two descriptions
merge into a single entity carrying everything known about it.

## The insights archive and every article were impersonating the homepage

`/insights` and every article beneath it set no metadata at all. That left them inheriting the
sitewide defaults — including the homepage's title and description and an instruction to index —
so dozens of article pages were presenting themselves to search engines as identical copies of the
homepage, competing against the page they were impersonating.

Insights remains outside the SEO system by request, so it gained no canonical URLs, share cards,
sitemap entries, or article markup. What both routes now carry is a directive keeping them out of
the index, which removes the duplication without pulling them into a system they were deliberately
excluded from. Article pages additionally set their own title, since a page held out of the index
still shows its title in a browser tab, a bookmark, and a pasted link — none of which the robots
directive covers.

Two details there are deliberate and worth preserving. Crawlers are still told to follow links,
because these articles link to the service pages that are meant to rank and discarding those links
would waste them. And there is no crawl block in `robots.txt` for insights: a URL that crawlers are
forbidden to fetch is never read, so the noindex instruction would never be seen and the pages could
still be indexed via an external link. Keeping crawlers allowed in is what makes the directive work —
the opposite of the belt-and-braces treatment the hidden form stubs get.

## An unlinked leftover route was indexable and wearing the homepage's metadata

`/products/:productId` was scaffolding left over from the marketing template the site began as.
Nothing linked to it, but it was a live, crawlable route with no metadata of its own, so it inherited
the sitewide title, description, and instruction to index. Every product id was an indexable page
presenting itself as the homepage.

The route and its data file have been deleted outright, along with their entries in the generated
route tree, so there is no longer anything to keep out of the index. One image in the public folder
was referenced only by that data and is now unused; it was left in place because nothing depends on
it either way.

## The service area had already drifted

The list describing where the business operates was retyped in each place that needed it, and the
copies had diverged — the service detail pages omitted Florida while the sitewide markup included it.
This is exactly the failure the shared name/address/phone triple exists to prevent: two different
answers to "where does this business operate" read as two different businesses. The list is now
defined once and shared, which also corrected the inconsistency.

## The business had no link to its off-site profile

The organization markup declared no equivalent profiles elsewhere, so the site's entity and the
business's real Instagram profile — which the footer already links to — were two unconnected
look-alikes rather than one entity, and none of the profile's standing counted toward the site. The
verified profile is now declared, held with the other shared SEO values behind an explicit warning
that only verified URLs belong there, since a wrong one merges this company's entity with someone
else's.

The Better Business Bureau accreditation advertised by the seal on every page belongs in the same
list and would be a stronger signal, but the seal's script only exposes an internal business
identifier, not the public profile address. Rather than guess at a URL — where a wrong one is worse
than none — it was left out, and can be added in a single line once the real address is known.

## What was already correct

The audit also confirmed the parts that needed no change: every indexable page sets its own title,
description, canonical URL, and share card; the sitemap lists exactly the fourteen real URLs with no
fragment duplicates; the root deliberately sets no canonical, so pages do not all collapse onto the
homepage; unknown service slugs are already held out of the index; and the notary page's local-search
markup, the geographic metadata, the robots file, and the crawl directives are all intact.

The project's architecture notes were updated to match the code, including why the shared service
identifier is load-bearing rather than cosmetic, why insights is noindexed but still crawlable, and
that the products scaffolding is gone. Everything type-checks clean, and the generated service markup
was validated directly rather than assumed correct.

author: coisa
kamira
body:
`subprocess.run(..., text=True)` decodes the child's output with **the caller's locale codec**. On a cp950 machine, UTF-8 bytes raise `UnicodeDecodeError` *inside the reader thread* — which is not the calling thread. The call does not fail:

```
stdout : None    returncode 0
```

**A successful call with no output.** Every caller checks the return code and sees `0`.

## What it silenced

`ledger_check._at()` returns `done.stdout if done.returncode == 0 else None`, and `None` there means *no baseline to compare against*. So the id-collision guard added by CHG-20260828-06 **passed without checking** — precisely when a change title contains an em dash, which every title in this repository does.

`cli.py` has the same shape where the runner reads an agent's reply: not a crash, not a refusal, an answer that isn't there. `worktree.py` shows the other half of the story, reading `(done.stdout or "")` in four places — defending against a `None` somebody clearly met, at the reading end rather than at the cause.

## Not hypothetical

`main` was **red on this machine**:

```
FAILED tests/test_ledger_check.py::test_a_second_change_taking_a_taken_id_is_refused
FAILED tests/test_recording.py::test_a_multibyte_character_split_across_two_reads_survives
2 failed, 1599 passed, 4 skipped
```

Both pass with `PYTHONUTF8=1` and fail without it. **Whether this suite passes depended on an environment variable nobody in this project sets.**

## The change

Eleven call sites now pass `encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"`. `frozen_tree.py` already had both. `session_record.py` had the argument written down — *"`text=True` alone decodes with the caller's locale and this repository's own messages are full of em-dashes"* — and it was applied in that one file and nowhere else.

Three more things this turned up:

**`session_record` decoded UTF-8 while doing nothing to make the child *write* UTF-8.** A Python child on Windows writes stdout in the ANSI codepage, so every non-ASCII character arrived as `U+FFFD` — decoded without error, wrong in every glyph, and indistinguishable from the chunk-boundary corruption its own test exists to catch. `PYTHONIOENCODING` now sits beside the `PYTHONUNBUFFERED` already there.

**`mutation_check` ran every mutation in a locale no ordinary run has.** It passed `PYTHONUTF8=1` to every pytest (CHG-20260823-47, to get pytest's output down the pipe). That switch *also* makes `locale.getpreferredencoding()` return UTF-8 **inside the suite**, which is what subprocess text mode reads — so no guarantee about decoding could be pinned there. Measured, not reasoned about:

| switch | `getpreferredencoding()` | `sys.stdout.encoding` |
|---|---|---|
| `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` | `cp950` | `utf-8` |
| `PYTHONUTF8=1` | `utf-8` | `utf-8` |

Swapped for the narrow one. The tests that care clear both variables themselves — a test that inherits them asserts something about whoever ran it.

**The suite found the half I had not looked at.** Naming UTF-8 on the parent's side changed the bytes on the wire, and the order-serialisation test went red on `972 == 969`. The agent was reading its stdin in the locale codec, so the CJK in `role_label` arrived as six characters where three were sent. `cli.py` now tells the agent which codec its order is written in.

## And a test that reads the syntax tree

Eleven sites fixed by hand is a twelfth waiting to be written. Anything under `src/` or `tools/` that starts a process in text mode without an `encoding` fails the suite — the same argument `graph.module_cycle()` makes about deriving instead of listing.

Its first draft flagged `self.turn(INSTRUCTION, nth=nth, text=text)`: **a name standing in for a constraint, written into the guard against exactly that.** It now matches a text switch **and** a keyword only a process launcher takes. Both the false positive and `run=subprocess.run` are pinned by their own tests.

## Verification

- `tests/test_subprocess_codecs.py` — 7 cases; one new case in `tests/test_cli.py`
- `tools/mutation_check.py --only codecs` — **6/6 caught**
- Full suite — **1609 passed, 4 skipped**, with no `PYTHONUTF8` in the environment

## Not claimed

- **That CI would ever have caught this.** GitHub's Windows runners are `cp1252`, which decodes those bytes into *different characters* without raising. The guard fails differently there — comparing mangled text rather than skipping. Green on both runners, reading the wrong thing on one.
- **That a non-Python child can be made to emit UTF-8.** `PYTHONIOENCODING` reaches Python children only. `errors="replace"` keeps ANSI output from killing the read; it does not make it correct.
- **That `subprocess` is the only place a locale leaks in.** Only `subprocess` was surveyed, on the syntax tree.

author: sucheet2000
body:
## Please read this first

**The notebook has not been run against the live API.** The single convert cell has not executed and ships empty. The canonical key, the disk cache and the replay simulator are plain standard library with **149 tests that run and pass today**.

## Why a client-side cache at all

The SDK's own `enable_cached_responses` flag does not help on the current voice. Its docstring, quoted verbatim in the README and **pinned by a test that reads the installed SDK**:

> Enable caching for the request. When enabled, identical requests will return cached audio instead of regenerating. Default is false.
> **Note:** Currently in beta and only available for bulbul:v1 and bulbul:v2 models.

`bulbul:v2` is deprecated and `v1` is not in the model Literal — so server-side caching is unavailable on `bulbul:v3`, and every repeated IVR prompt, alert template or UI label costs a full round trip. If the SDK ever extends caching to the current model, the pinned test fails and the README's claim gets revisited rather than silently rotting.

## The Indic care lives in the key

Byte-different spellings that sound identical hit one cache entry:

- both Unicode forms of a nukta letter fold together (U+0958–U+095F are composition exclusions — carried from this series' earlier finding)
- zero-width characters are stripped **under a stated assumption** that they do not change sound — documented as the recipe's decision, testable in both directions
- whitespace collapses; a trailing danda equals a full stop
- **folding native digits to ASCII is off by default**, because whether ० and 0 yield identical audio is unverifiable without a key — the README says exactly that instead of assuming

Every layer is separately toggleable, and a **replay simulator** over an authored request log (invented traffic, stated as invented) reports the calls each layer recovers cumulatively — the value of every fold is measured, not asserted.

**Every synthesis parameter that changes audio is part of the key** — model, speaker, language, pace, pitch, loudness, sample rate. Dropping any one of them from the key fails 88 tests.

## The cache itself

Content-addressed files with a JSON index, eviction at a pinned default, deterministic behaviour, and a truncated entry is a miss, never a crash. A key-version bump deliberately invalidates the index — exercised against a genuinely different version, not the constant echoed back.

## Tests

**149 tests**, written before the implementation and watched failing first; 24 standalone traps run with no module, including the docstring pin. Mutation testing:

```
speaker dropped from the key            CAUGHT (88 failed)
pace dropped from the key               CAUGHT (88 failed)
DEFAULT_MAX_ENTRIES 128 -> 12800        CAUGHT (1 failed)
DEFAULT_MAX_ENTRIES 128 -> 2            CAUGHT (2 failed)
KEY_VERSION 1 -> 2                      CAUGHT (3 failed)
```

Kept in the open: the first mutation pass found the three cache-management constants unarmoured — every test passed an explicit size, so the default was never exercised, and every version reference read the constant on both sides so a bump changed nothing observable. Three forcing tests were added (default eviction pinned numerically, index invalidation against a genuinely different version, the key prefix pinned literally) before this PR was opened. 8 of 8 mutants now die.

## Checks

```
python3 -m pytest tests/ -q                                              231 passed
python3 scripts/validate_recipe.py examples/indic-tts-phrase-cache --strict   PASS, 0 errors
python3 scripts/ci_validate.py --base-ref main                           PASS, 0 errors (committed diff)
```

Module imports: `hashlib`, `json`, `pathlib`, `unicodedata`, `collections`, `dataclasses`, `base64` — standard library only. The notebook's convert cell uses `bulbul:v3` explicitly with the key passed explicitly. Plain UTF-8, no BOM, no emoji, empty outputs.

## Overlap

No open PR or issue touches caching or API-usage efficiency. This is the first efficiency-focused recipe in the repo, and its premise rests on the SDK's own documented limitation rather than on any benchmark we could not run.

body:
## What changed or was removed

- Replaced the dual runtime ToolCall representation with one flat internal and persisted contract: `id`, `type`, `name`, object `arguments`, `thought_signature`, and `tool_feedback_explanation`.
- Moved OpenAI-compatible nested `function` objects and JSON-string arguments entirely into provider-local wire adapters. Gemini, Anthropic, Bedrock, OAuth, CLI, and Responses adapters now convert once at their boundaries.
- Removed the historical normalizer, Google dual-shape helper, compatibility facade test, duplicated cloning and comparison branches, serialized-argument fallbacks, and the second coding-quality harness family.
- Made the JSONL reader reject unknown/non-current fields instead of silently decoding old nested calls into incomplete messages.
- Kept `bus.OutboundToolCall` separate intentionally: it is a sanitized display/outbox DTO that excludes provider-only metadata and truncates arguments.

## Why

Tool calls previously carried the same name and arguments twice: a flat execution map and an OpenAI-shaped nested function with a JSON string. Every consumer then needed precedence rules, synchronization, mismatch validation, cloning branches, and persistence fallbacks. One canonical representation removes those failure modes while preserving external protocols at explicit adapters.

## User and developer impact

- Runtime behavior and external provider protocols remain supported through their adapters.
- Internal code must use the flat ToolCall fields; there is no legacy reader or dual write.
- Existing deployed session JSONL is intentionally not compatible with this binary until a coordinated one-time migration. A read-only audit found 20,191 deployed tool calls in the old nested form. Production remains on the old binary; this PR performs no deploy or production mutation.
- The coding-quality harness now tests the one supported current contract instead of manufacturing two internal shapes.

## Validation

- `make fmt`
- `make lint` (`0 issues`; docs lint OK)
- `scripts/pre-push-lint.sh --changed` (`0 issues` across 19 changed packages)
- `go test ./pkg/providers/... ./pkg/utils/... ./pkg/tokenizer/... ./pkg/seahorse/... ./pkg/session/... ./pkg/memory/... ./pkg/testharness/codingquality ./web/backend/api/...`
- `go test ./pkg/agent/...`
- Race tests passed for providers, memory, session, Seahorse, tokenizer, utils, and agent. The full combined race run exposed an existing `Cmd.Wait` race in untouched `web/backend/api/gateway_test.go`; the exact test reproduces on the identical `origin/main` tree. Normal web API tests pass.
- `git diff --check`

## Later PRs

- After merge and separate deployment authorization: stop the relevant services, back up session state, atomically migrate deployed JSONL tool calls to the flat contract, verify the migrated corpus, install/restart, health-check, and retain rollback artifacts.
- Repeat the zero-legacy audit after this contract reset.
- Track the pre-existing web gateway test race separately; it is unrelated to ToolCall representation.
