body:
## Summary
Fixes four MCP server issues in `mcp/`, delivered as one combined PR.

Closes #550
Closes #552
Closes #556
Closes #560

## Changes

- **#550 — Serialize state-mutating tool calls with an in-process lock**
  Added `mcp/src/mutex.ts` (`Mutex.runExclusive`) and a `STATE_MUTATING_TOOLS` set of 16 tool names. State-mutating calls in `dispatchTool` are now serialized via a shared mutex so concurrent calls don't interleave profile/wallet mutations.

- **#552 — Advertise tool annotations in ListTools**
  Added a `ToolAnnotations` interface and made `annotations` required on `ToolDefinition` in `tools.ts`. ListTools now returns per-tool `readOnlyHint`/`destructiveHint` annotations. Documented in `docs/mcp-tool-annotations.md`.

- **#556 — Offline read-only catalog cache fallback**
  Added `mcp/src/catalogCache.ts` (in-memory catalog + per-resource preview snapshots with a 24h staleness label). `browse`, `search`, and `preview` fall back to the cached snapshot when the transport throws, surfacing a clear offline notice. A `vitest.setup.ts` clears the cache before each test for deterministic failure paths.

- **#560 — Split index.ts into per-tool modules**
  Reduced `mcp/src/index.ts` from ~3,386 → 940 lines. Shared config/state/HTTP/persistence helpers moved to `mcp/src/runtime.ts`; tool implementations moved into focused modules under `mcp/src/tools/` (`state`, `catalog`, `wallet`, `publish`, `registry`, `diagnostics`). The entrypoint is reduced to wiring (dispatch, routing, MCP server setup). No tool names, argument specs, or behavior changed; all public exports and the test-only helpers (`_setAgentWallet`, `_setAgentApiKey`, `_resetProfiles`, `_setMockMode`) keep working unchanged.

## Verification

author: rubenvdlinde
body:
The walkthrough merge broke `vault-unlock.spec.ts`: a locked vault issued `GET /api/preferences/walkthrough_completed_version`, and that spec asserts on the wire that a locked vault requests **no** Keepiq API endpoint. It is an allowlist that fails closed, exactly so a new request behind the lock screen is a deliberate act with a reason — so this fixes the behaviour rather than widening the list.

The router guard could not have caught it, and says so in its own comment: it works by refusing to resolve a route, so it only covers what mounts inside the `<router-view>`. `CnAppRoot` reads `manifest.walkthrough` and fetches the tour's completion preference when the **shell** mounts, before any route resolves.

The manifest handed to the shell now omits `walkthrough` while locked. Withheld, not disabled — `isLocked` is a render dependency, so the tour returns on unlock and still runs on a first unlocked visit. Fails closed like the guard beside it, and both properties are mutation-verified.

author: jakebromberg
body:
Server half of [#2232](https://github.com/WXYC/Backend-Service/issues/2232). Depends on [WXYC/wxyc-shared#415](https://github.com/WXYC/wxyc-shared/pull/415) publishing the contract; the code here compiles without it (the two new fields are plain TS types on the request body), but the spec should land first.

Closes #2233

## The bug

`joinShow` decided start-vs-join on `current_show?.end_time !== null` and nothing else. A DJ who walks out without signing off leaves their show open indefinitely, so every DJ who presses "Go Live" afterwards is silently attached to it as a guest. It happened twice:

| | 2026-08-20, show `1951164` | 2026-08-28, show `1951224` |
|---|---|---|
| origin | BS-native | tubafrenzy-mirrored |
| `primary_dj_id` | **set** | **NULL** (`legacy_dj_name` `"dj sue"`) |
| absorbed | three later DJs over nine hours | four Backend accounts over ten hours |
| how `on_air` went wrong | resolved the owner's `auth_user.dj_name` | short-circuited to `legacy_dj_name` |
| fixed by | the routing change | **`getOnAirDJName`** |

Same routing bug, two different banner mechanisms — which is why this PR carries two fixes and **neither subsumes the other**. (A unit fixture used to encode `1951224` with a non-null `primary_dj_id`, which is precisely the shape where `resolveDjNameForShow` does *not* short-circuit — modelling the easy case under the hard case's id. Corrected. **Do not re-derive 1951224's size from live data**: `jobs/flowsheet-show-split` has since cut it into five shows, so the surviving row runs 11:02–14:02 and reads as a much smaller incident than it was. As it happened it ran ten hours and absorbed DJ String Theory, Panzón, dj eureka! and Dj xD, reaching 143 entries. `primary_dj_id` being NULL there is still checkable with `GET /flowsheet/show-info?show_id=1951224`.)

BS#1861's two guards and BS#2065's opportunistic close both key on a `show_end` marker *existing*, so neither fires in the case where nobody signed off at all.

## Routing

Order matters, and the three existing guards keep running first and unchanged:

| condition | outcome |
|---|---|
| no open show, or `end_time` set, or terminal entry is `show_end` | `startShow` — no prompt, ever |
| caller already an active member (BS#1861 arm c) | 200 with the existing membership — no prompt |
| **flag OFF** | `addDJToShow`, `intent` ignored entirely |
| open show, no `intent` | **409** `show_already_open` + `details.show = { id, dj_name, start_time }` |
| `intent: "join"` | `addDJToShow` — today's path, now chosen |
| `intent: "takeover"` + matching `expected_show_id` | `endShow` then `startShow` |
| `intent: "takeover"`, `expected_show_id` missing / unrecognized `intent` | 400 |
| `expected_show_id` names a different show | re-409, nothing closed |

Only a genuinely-open show belonging to someone else reaches the intent branch. If the dialog fires at every scheduled 2-hour handoff, the design is wrong — after this, a properly handed-off slot has no open show at all.

## Three things worth reviewing closely

**The close uses `resolveShowEndInstant`, not `now()`.** `now()` is right for a prompt handoff and a lie for an abandoned one: it credits a departed DJ with however many hours of dead air elapsed before the next DJ arrived, and — per `endShow`'s own `EndShowOptions` note — sorts a `show_end` marker to the top of the public flowsheet with an interval overlapping every archive day in between. The derived instant is truthful in *both* cases, because a prompt handoff's last logged track is recent. One rule, correct twice.

**`expected_show_id` is a compare-and-set, and its two stale-snapshot cases resolve differently.** Clients poll, so the DJ acts on a snapshot. A *different* show now open is a fresh 409 with fresh details and nothing closed — otherwise the DJ ends a show whose name they never saw, which voids the informed consent the prompt exists to provide. The expected show having *closed* in that window is not an error at all: the first guard already routed it to `startShow`, silently, because starting their own show is exactly what they asked for and re-prompting would put the dialog on the common path.

**The tubafrenzy sign-off could not ride a second response tap, and this is the subtle one.** `flowsheetMirror.startShow` and `flowsheetMirror.endShow` are both `createHttpMirrorMiddleware` taps reading the *same* `res.locals.mirrorData` key under the same `isShowPayload` gate. Chaining the end-tap onto `/join` would hand it the payload of the show that just *started* and sign off the live broadcast. So:

- the sign-off body is extracted into `mirrorShowSignoff`, called by both the tap and the takeover branch, so they cannot drift;
- it takes the closed `Show` and resolves the tubafrenzy id itself — `getCachedShowId(show.id) ?? show.legacy_show_id`, where the cache is the *primary* source whenever `startShow`'s persist failed, and is module-private. A pre-resolved id would silently mis-target;
- `scheduleTakeoverSignoff` defers it to `res.once('finish')`. Awaiting inline would put tubafrenzy latency on the go-live path, and a tubafrenzy outage would 500 the takeover *after* `endShow` committed `end_time` — stranding the DJ off air with no show;
- it is deliberately **not** gated on `res.statusCode`, which is where it departs from the taps. A tap uses the status code to decide whether a mutation happened; here the close has already committed before it is called, so skipping on a non-2xx would leave exactly the BS-closed / tubafrenzy-open split brain that made this incident ambiguous.

`isMirrorEnabled` is exported for it, with its parameter narrowed to `MirrorFlagRequest = Pick<Request, 'auth' | 'ip'>` — the only two fields it reads — so a controller holding a route-typed `Request<object, object, Body>` can call it without a cast. The takeover's own gate is a separate flag; a `backend-mirror` flip must not toggle this feature.

## Authorization — decided, not overlooked

`/join` is gated only by `requirePermissions({ flowsheet: ['write'] })`, so `takeover` makes "end another DJ's show" reachable by any write-capable DJ. That is the point. tubafrenzy's `EndShowServlet` took `radioShowID` as a request parameter with no ownership or role check, and its Backend replacement `forceEndShow` is `flowsheet: ['manage']`-gated — which silently dropped a capability every signed-on DJ had. There is no staleness threshold either: a timer has to guess, and a badly-chosen one kills a live show whose DJ is simply between tracks.

## Rollout — `FLOWSHEET_TAKEOVER_ENABLED`, default OFF

Flag OFF ignores `intent` and `expected_show_id` entirely and preserves today's routing byte for byte — **never a 400, never a 409**. That is not politeness, though the original reason given here was wrong in both halves and is corrected: `auto-dj-orchestrator`'s `join()` sends `{ dj_id, show_name }` and **no `intent` at all** (`src/backend/flowsheet-client.ts`, whose own comment says the `intent` / `expected_show_id` contract is still future work), and its `request()` throws on any non-2xx — `if (!resp.ok) throw`, not on a missing show id.

That inverts where the risk lives. Flag OFF is not merely harmless for Auto-DJ, it is the thing keeping it working: **flipping the flag ON breaks Auto-DJ activation**, because an intent-less join against an open show becomes a 409, `request()` throws, and activation fails in exactly the abandoned-show case Auto-DJ exists to cover. Tracked as WXYC/auto-dj-orchestrator#36, which must land before the flip. The blast radius is bounded today only because auto-dj-orchestrator has never been deployed (deploy epic auto-dj-orchestrator#26), so this is a gate on its first deploy rather than a live outage.

Flag OFF also makes deploy order between the four repos harmless.

Built on `createEnvFlagConfig` (strict `=== 'true'`, lazily cached, `resetConfig()` for tests) rather than the mirror's `isMirrorEnabled`, which env-defaults to **ON** when `POSTHOG_API_KEY` is unset. Copying that

body:
## Summary

複数モデルのアンサンブル利用に関する文献を調べ、その結果を `cross-refactoring` の設計へ反映し、研究データを集めるための計画を起案する。

3 つの文書を追加・更新する。

| ファイル | 追跡先 | 内容 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `issues/issue-158-llm-ensemble-for-agentic-development.md` | #158 | 研究メモ（新規）。文献調査・実測・検証計画 |
| `issues/issue-159-telemetry-and-oss-governance.md` | #159 | データ収集基盤と OSS 運用の計画（新規） |
| `issues/issue-113-cross-refactoring-round-time-and-defects.md` | #113 | 採否の設計を証拠ベースへ改める（更新・リネーム） |

## 1. 研究メモ（#158）

発端は「kiro が `claude-sonnet-5` を使うためホストの claude と同系列になる構成を、独立性の毀損として扱うべきか」という問いである。調べた結果、テーマを **AI エージェント開発におけるアンサンブル利用の優位性**へ広げた。

### 示したい 3 つの命題

| # | 命題 | 裏付け |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 複数モデルの潜在性能は最良の単一モデルを大きく上回る | Defects4J で +83%（112 問 → 205 問） |
| 2 | ただし集約を誤ると単一モデルを下回る | 合意ベースは 22 問 |
| 3 | 開発ドメインは機械検証で潜在性能を引き出せる | **未検証。本研究の主張** |

### 主な調査結果

| 論点 | 数値 | 出典 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 合意ベースの失敗（popularity trap） | 22 問（最良の単一モデル 112 問を下回る） | arXiv:2510.21513 |
| 多様性ベースの選択 | 理論上限の 80〜97%。2 モデルでも効果 | 同上 |
| 複数モデルの反復サンプリング | 2 モデル 35 サンプルが単一モデル 512 サンプルを上回る | arXiv:2504.00762 |
| ハーネスの寄与 | 同一モデル・同一精度でも 31% のタスクで結果が不一致 | arXiv:2606.26158 |
| モデル系統の相関 | 同一系統 r = 0.67 / 異系統 r = 0.53（差 0.14） | arXiv:2603.17111 |
| 多数決の限界 | 2:1 分裂の 25.5% で少数派が正しい。LLM 審判は −1.37% | arXiv:2606.29270 |

手元の実測（重複率 13.3%、判定の分岐 50%、少数派の指摘が振る舞いの変化を捕捉した事例）も一次データとして残した。

## 2. 採否の設計を証拠ベースへ（#113）

調査の結果、**「提案者の合意 2 者以上を採否の関門にする」案を取り下げた。** 相関のある参加者の多数決は少数派の正解を潰すためで、コード修復の実測でも合意ベースが最良の単一モデルを下回っている。

採否の順序を次へ改めた。

1. **機械検証**。参照検索・テスト・静的解析で立証できる提案は、支持が 1 者でも採用
2. **反証**。`refute` が返された提案は、支持数によらず落とす
3. **得点**。決まらないものを得点と影響の広さで並べ、閾値未満を落とす
4. **不採用**。得点が割れた提案は採用しない。得点と内訳は報告へ残す

**4 段階すべてを自動判定にしている。** 人の判断を待つ出口を作ると `/goal` から呼ばれたときに進行が止まるためで、機械検証で立証できるものは段階 1 で先に拾われる。

あわせて、後から実現率と独立性を測れるよう報告の項目を 2 つ足した（採用しなかった提案と落ちた段階、参加者ごとの重複率）。

## 3. データ収集基盤と OSS 運用の起案（#159）

#158 の研究は現在 N=1 の事例に依存しており、統計的な主張には複数の利用者からのデータが要る。

**設計は「何を集めるか」ではなく「何を集めないか」から確定させる。** このツールは他者の業務コードの上で動くため、次を送る対象から外す。

- コードの内容・差分・提案やレビューの本文
- ファイルパス・シンボル名・リポジトリ名・所有者・URL
- コミットメッセージ・Pull Request の題と本文
- 個人を特定できる情報・認証情報

送るのは件数・所要時間・分類・言語といった**数値と分類のみ**で、許可リストで定義し、リストに無いキーがあれば送信を中止する。

送信を伴わない範囲から段階を分けた。

| 段階 | 収集の形 | 同意 | 必要な基盤 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | ローカルへ集計を出力 | 不要（送らない） | なし |
| 2 | 自動送信 | 既定で収集・停止手段あり | 受け口・規約・運用 |

**送る前に毎回同意を取る形は置かない。** 実行のたびに内容を確認させても、確認は形骸化する一方で作業は止まる。同意は「収集していることと止め方を最初に伝え、いつでも止められる」形で担保し、内容の確認は第 1 段階の集計ファイルをいつでも読めることで担保する。

既定で収集する選択は、停止手段の提供・収集内容の明示・機密を含めない設計と組み合わせて初めて成立する。3 つのうち 1 つでも欠けたまま第 2 段階へ進まない。

送信先は受け口・保管・公開の 3 層に分ける。

| 層 | 使うもの | 役割 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 受け口 | Cloudflare Workers | 匿名の POST を認証なしで受け、レート制限とペイロードの上限で守る |
| 保管 | Cloudflare D1 | 永続化して SQL で読む |
| 公開 | Hugging Face Datasets | 整理した統計を誰でも読める形で出す |

配布物へ書き込み用のトークンを埋め込まずに済み、生の受信データと公開するデータを分けて公開前に検査を挟める。公開データセットは誰でも閲覧・引用できるため、何を集めたかを利用者が確認できる。

GitHub の Discussions は不採用にした。**投稿に利用者のアカウントが残り、個人を特定できる情報を集めない方針と両立しない。** 保持が 3 か月の時系列ストアも、研究の長期データが残らないため単体では使わない。

OSS としての文書（貢献ガイド・行動規範・セキュリティ方針・プライバシー方針）とリポジトリ設定（テンプレート・CODEOWNERS・ブランチ保護）の整備も Task に含めた。現状は workflow 3 件があるだけで、いずれも未整備である。

## Test plan

- [x] 引用した数値は各論文の本文から取得した（本文を読んだ 7 本と未読 14 本をメモ内で分離）
- [x] 手元の実測値は 7 回目の状態ファイルと PR #155 の記録から集計した
- [x] `markdown-writing` のセルフチェック grep 4 種を 3 ファイルで実行
- [x] 採否の 4 段階に人の判断を待つ出口が無いことを確認した
- [x] 受け入れ条件の件数と Task の参照番号の整合を取り直した（21 件）
- [x] 文書間の相互リンクが存在することを確認した
- [ ] 8 回目の実機試行で、証拠ベースの採否と単純多数決の結果を比較する
- [ ] 収集の第 1 段階を実装し、7 回目の状態ファイルで禁止項目が出ないことを確かめる

This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **5.5** to **7.16.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.16.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- When combining files, now path separator slashes will automatically be
  converted to the local file system style. This makes it less necessary to
  define ``[paths]`` configuration to combine data across operating systems.
  Fixes `issue 2266`_.

- The :meth:`.Coverage.switch_context` method now returns the previous context.

- Fix: previously, a ``[paths]`` pattern would be replaced everywhere in a file
  path when it was only meant to be replaced once, in the leading portion of
  the path. This is now fixed, in `pull 2268`_.

- Fixes to validation of options and configuration settings:

  - Negative precision settings now always cause useful error messages (`pull
    2261`_).

  - An invalid regex in the ``--contexts`` option (or the ``[report]
    contexts`` setting) reported a confusing "Couldn't use data file ...:
    user-defined function raised exception" error. Now it raises a proper
    configuration error naming the bad regex, like other regex settings do
    (`pull 2262`_).

  - Non-string values in TOML configuration settings now produce a helpful
    error message instead of a traceback.  This affects list settings whose
    elements aren't strings (like ``omit``, ``exclude_lines``, or a ``[paths]``
    entry), file settings like ``data_file``, and any wrong-typed value in the
    ``[paths]`` section (`pull 2263`_).

  - ``coverage run`` refuses run-affecting command-line options like
    ``--branch`` alongside ``--concurrency=multiprocessing``, since they can't
    reach the subprocesses.  The check only recognized ``multiprocessing`` as
    the entire option value, so ``--concurrency=multiprocessing,thread``
    slipped through and failed later with "Can't combine statement coverage
    data with branch data".  Each named concurrency library is now properly
    considered (`pull 2270`_).

- Fix: ``coverage annotate -d DIR`` raised an ``AssertionError`` if any
  measured file had an extension other than ``.py``, such as a ``.pyw`` file on
  Windows.  The original extension is now restored on the annotated copy (`pull
  2265`_).

author: psaab
body:
## Measured before optimising

`retry_pending_neigh` snapshotted **every** unresolved next-hop into a fresh
`Vec` and walked all of them, the only bound an empty-map early-out — and it runs
**twice per poll iteration**. Release build, keys unresolved and not due:

| pending keys | ns/sweep | ns/key | Vec bytes/sweep |
|--------------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 0            | 8        | —      | 0               |
| 64           | 2 673    | 41.8   | 1 536           |
| 1 024        | 40 709   | 39.8   | 24 576          |
| 4 096 (cap)  | 182 207  | 44.5   | 98 304          |

A healthy binding holds **zero** pending keys and pays 8 ns — which is why this
never showed up in profiling, and why it needed measuring rather than assuming.
At the `MAX_PENDING_NEIGH` cap it is **~364 µs and ~196 KiB per poll iteration**:
a worker core spent on hops whose packets are already being dropped and
negatively cached, reachable by scanning distinct unresolved next-hops. So: a
genuinely hot path, not a bound-and-comment case.

The per-key cost is dominated by `ShardedNeighborMap::get`, which takes a **shard
mutex** — this was O(all-keys) *lock acquisitions* contending with the resolver
thread that writes those shards, the #1187 constraint arriving through another
door.

**After:** ~20 ns with nothing due, flat in the pending population, zero
allocation, and at most `PENDING_NEIGH_SWEEP_BUDGET` (64) keys serviced per
sweep where the old sweep visited all 4096.

## The finding: a deadline queue alone is wrong, and the suite proved it

Two existing tests went red: a resolved neighbour was no longer dispatched on the
next sweep. That is **not** a fixture artifact. A key has nothing scheduled
between its last probe (queued + 260 ms) and its timeout (800 ms–2 s), so a
neighbour resolving at 300 ms goes unnoticed until the packet is **DROPPED as
never-resolved** — a correctness regression, not a latency one.

So `ShardedNeighborMap` now carries an insert generation, and a sweep that
observes it change walks every pending key on that sweep. The asymmetry is the
point: **filling the pending cap resolves nothing, so the attack triggers no
walks at all**, while a legitimate resolution keeps exactly the latency it had.
Both tests then passed **unmodified** — behaviour restored, not assertions
weakened.

The static `forwarding.neighbors` map is rebuilt on commit and has no counter to
bump, so its length is the second half of the signature. A same-size static
replacement is the one edit that misses; the 50 ms recheck backstops it against a
800 ms–2 s timeout. Stated at the site rather than papered over — the dynamic
path, the one on the packet-latency critical path, is exact.

## No tombstones, by a property of the buffer

There is one production insert site; a duplicate for a pending key is
`DuplicateDrop`ped rather than replacing the representative; and both removals
happen on a key the sweep has just **popped**. So each live key has exactly one
heap entry and no tombstone can arise. The one exception is a removal during a
resolution pass (which does not pop); those are discarded when their own deadline
comes up, bounded by the key's timeout.

## Mutation matrix

Full suite, no `-run` filter, `--test-threads=1`.

| cell | edit | verdict | reds |
|------|------|---------|------|
| control | none | GREEN 4849 | — |
| m1 | `resolution_pass = true` (the pre-fix unbounded walk) | RED | nothing-due + budget cells |
| m2 | `resolution_pass = false` (deadline only, no gate) | RED | resolution cell + the 2 pre-existing guards |
| m3 | drop the `.max(now+1)` fairness clamp | RED | at-most-once-per-sweep cell |
| m4 | re-arm during a resolution pass too (duplicates) | RED | no-duplicate-entries cell |

**m3 and m4 were GREEN on the first run**, and neither was visible from the tests
I had already written:

- the starvation cell **cannot** reach the clamp — every key in it is past its
  timeout and is *removed* on visit, so nothing re-arms;
- nothing drove a resolution pass over *surviving* keys, the only shape that
  duplicates.

Cells were written for both rather than the mutations excused.

The first nothing-due cell was also **vacuous**: with nothing due, a full walk
finds nothing to do and leaves identical state, so removals and recycles cannot
distinguish it from no walk at all. That is why `pending_neigh_visits` exists — a
production counter (and the budget-exhaustion telemetry the issue asks for), not
a test-only seam.

## Layout guards

The counter moved `BindingLiveState` (size 2304 → 2368, offsets 2168 → 2176 and
2296 → 2304), tripping the compile-time asserts **and** their runtime twin in
`tests/tx_inbox.rs`. Re-measured in lockstep per the #6664/#7054 precedent, and
verified the way those notes require: **both** build configurations green on
**one** set of literals, which a `#[cfg(test)]` field could not achieve.

## Modularity

`neighbor_dispatch.rs` was 1493 LOC — seven lines under the [WATCH] floor, so the
gate fired exactly as the issue predicted. The deadline queue went in its own
module and the dispatch test suite was extracted to
`neighbor_dispatch_mirror_tests.rs` (`#[path]`, so `super::` and every import is
unchanged by the move). The sweep is now 1136 LOC; gate green.

## Not done

The optional #1769 §2.3 exponential GET backoff listed as adjacent-optional on
the issue — out of scope for a change already touching the sweep, the neighbour
map layout and the module split.

Docs: `docs/userspace-cold-start-resolution.md` note 4 said checking the buffer
every poll is critical for cold start and gave no cost — now carries the
measurement and the distinction between *checking* and *walking*. Reasoning in
`docs/log/7156.md`.

Closes #7156

body:
Fixes the `integration-test-all-envs (ubuntu-24.04-arm)` failure on #5071.

`tests/pnpm/aqua.yaml` moves to pnpm v11.24.0, but `tests/pnpm/aqua-checksums.json` still listed v11.5.2. With `require_checksum: true` aqua refuses to install a package it has no checksum for:

```
ERR install the package  package_name=pnpm/pnpm package_version=v11.24.0 registry=standard
    doc=https://aquaproj.github.io/docs/reference/codes/001
    error="checksum is required"
```

Regenerated with `aqua update-checksum --prune`. Alongside the version bump it picks up two assets the registry added since:

```diff
+  pnpm-linux-arm64-musl.tar.gz
+  pnpm-linux-x64-musl.tar.gz
```

which is why arm64 was the environment that failed.

The registry checksum entry also moves from v4.523.0 to v4.547.0, matching the `ref` already set in `aqua.yaml`.

## Verification

Ran the test locally on darwin/arm64 against this branch:

```
INF verify GitHub Artifact Attestations  package_name=pnpm/pnpm package_version=v11.24.0
INF create a symbolic link  file_name=pn
INF creating a hard link  file_name=pnpx
```

Installation completes with checksum verification enabled.

Base is the Renovate branch, so merging this puts the fix on #5071.

body:
Fix #462

Stacked on #466. Review #464, #465, #466 first.

**The exit code lesson did not survive into the workflow.** `tutorial/7-ci/1-test-script.mdx` teaches that the exit code is the number of failures and proves it with `pwsh -File`, which is true. The GitHub Actions step on the very next page runs `pwsh -command`, and under `-command` PowerShell normalizes any non-zero exit to 1:

```
pwsh -NoProfile -File ./test.ps1              # 3 failures, exit code 3
pwsh -NoProfile -command ". './test.ps1'"     # 3 failures, exit code 1
```

The build still goes red, so nothing was broken, but the page sold a property that does not reach the CI it builds two pages later.

**The coverage target is not a gate.** Missing it changes nothing:

```
Covered 95% / 99%. 40 analyzed Commands in 7 Files.
Result: Passed   exit 0
```

"The target you are being measured against" reads like a gate to anybody wiring up a pipeline, so the page now says plainly that it is a number to compare against and points at the result object if you want to enforce it.

**`.gitignore` is now actually created.** Three pages said the artifacts belong in it, none created it, and the checklist then claimed both files were ignored. Following the tutorial literally committed `testResults.xml` and `coverage.xml`.

**Annotations.** `Output.CIFormat` defaults to `Auto` and detects `$GITHUB_ACTIONS`, so failures already show up on the job:

```
$ GITHUB_ACTIONS=true pwsh -NoProfile -File ./test.ps1
::error::[-] Returns all eight planets 26ms
```

That now comes before the `dorny/test-reporter` suggestion, which is still there for the case it genuinely helps with.

**Culture.** The cross platform note listed path separators and case sensitivity. The bug Planetarium actually has is culture: `'{0,-8} {1} AU' -f ...` formats with the current culture, so the report reads `Mercury  0,387 AU` on my machine. The suite stays green because the only asserted line is `Earth    1 AU`, which has no decimal part. It seemed worth saying that out loud on the page whose point is that a matrix finds the bugs you cannot see locally.

## Verification

Measured all of it on pwsh 7.5.5 with Pester 6.1.0: exit codes for 0, 1 and 3 failures under both `-File` and `-command`, a run with `CoveragePercentTarget = 99`, a `git init && git add . && git commit` following the tutorial as written, and the annotation output with `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`. author: cyber-ai-agent
body:
## Problem
Creative Workshop could show only “提示词无法转换为世界草稿” for normal natural-language prompts such as “创建一个五个人的股票投资分析团队”. The AI draft path had its own provider HTTP implementation and treated model suggestion JSON as if it were already the host’s strict draft contract.

This caused several real failure modes:
- OpenAI-compatible gateways that support chat but reject `response_format` failed only in Creative Workshop.
- A base URL already ending in `/chat/completions` could be suffixed again by the workshop-only client.
- Fenced JSON or a short explanation around JSON failed strict `JSON.parse`.
- Natural-language/Chinese `tempId` values or invented Skill names made the whole draft invalid.
- The web UI discarded the controlled server error and always showed one generic message.

## Fix
- Reuse the provider-neutral `ModelJsonCall` for Creative Workshop.
- Add opt-in `prompt-only` JSON mode so Workshop can omit `response_format` while retaining strict host-side JSON parsing; existing callers remain `native` by default.
- Normalize model suggestions through an allow-listed draft shape before strict validation.
- Repair missing/invalid/duplicate draft-only `tempId` values deterministically.
- Only keep Skill suggestions that exist in the current workspace Skill Catalog.
- Filter model capability recommendations to the supported capability vocabulary.
- Accept fenced JSON / surrounding explanation through the existing balanced-object parser.
- Preserve the strict `CreativeWorkshopDraftService` as the final safety boundary.
- Remove the redundant second draft save in the generate route.
- Surface controlled server errors in the Workshop UI instead of hiding every failure behind the same generic message.

## Regression coverage
- Prompt-only JSON mode keeps the existing native mode as the default.
- A five-person stock-investment team draft succeeds even when the model returns fenced JSON, Chinese/invalid temp IDs, invented skills, and an invalid capability suggestion.
- A configured full `/chat/completions` endpoint is not duplicated.
- Malformed model JSON still fails without creating any entity.

Base: `main@7badc90b2e4b9c62985ff9518fa59e1528e31a8e`

Merge only after Required CI is fully green.

author: abdulahad2008
body:
## Why

Two questions had no answer without opening the Supabase table editor: who has signed up, and how much is anything being downloaded. And until this week **no account held a `moderator` or `admin` role**, so `/moderate` was unreachable for everyone — including the person who has to review deposits.

## What's here

**`/admin`** (admin only, `noindex`) — accounts with roles and last sign-in, datasets with status and download counts, a 30-day rollup of downloads and visits, and the 50 most recent downloads. Emails come from `auth.admin.listUsers()` in a try/catch, so the page still renders if that call fails.

**Role management** — a select plus an explicit Save on each account row. It re-reads the actor's role, the target's role, and the admin count from the database rather than trusting the form, and refuses: non-admin actors, unknown roles, no-ops, and demoting the last admin.

**Vercel Analytics** — `<Analytics />` in the locale layout. Cookieless and aggregate-only. **Needs enabling in the Vercel project settings before it collects anything.**

**Privacy policy** — the cookies paragraph claimed the site used "no third-party analytics trackers", which adding Analytics would have made false. Rewritten, plus a new section saying what Vercel receives. All three locales.

## ⚠️ Migration 0010 must be applied

`supabase/migrations/0010_admin_role_management.sql` is **not yet applied**. Until it is, role changes are refused with a generic error and a server log naming the missing migration — verified working, not assumed.

It adds `public.is_admin(uuid)` and an update policy on `profiles` that admins can reach. **The 0005 role-change trigger is untouched.** The alternative — using the service role key — would have bypassed RLS *and* that trigger, making the app the one caller answerable to neither.

## Header change

For staff only, the inline nav switches to the mobile sheet at 1024px instead of 768px. A moderator's nav already overflowed a 768px viewport by 76px *before* this branch; an admin's by 148px. A sticky header that overflows scrolls every page sideways — the same failure the sheet was built to fix one breakpoint down. Signed-out and ordinary signed-in visitors are unaffected; measured at 768/820/900/1024 for all three cases.

## Verification

- 54/54 tests pass (10 new, covering the refusal rules against hostile input and the day rollup)
- `tsc` clean; `eslint` 0 errors (1 pre-existing TanStack warning)
- Production build succeeds, `/admin` in the route list
- Playwright: 2 themes × 3 locales × 375/768/1440 — no overflow, no axe violations, no console errors
- Role-change refusal path driven through the real form against the real database

## Not done

- 0010 not applied (yours to run)
- Analytics not enabled in Vercel settings (yours to toggle)
- The happy path of a role change is unverified end-to-end, because it cannot work until 0010 is applied

author: vks-team
body:
With PR #1 and PR #2 merged, `main` and `dev` differ by **exactly one line** — and this is it. Commit `656ee9e` ("[build] change goproxy") was pushed straight to `dev` and never sent to `main`, so the next `main -> dev` reset would have silently discarded it.

```diff
-ARG GOPROXY=https://goproxy.io,direct
+ENV GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct
```

`proxy.golang.org` is Go's upstream default. `goproxy.io` also had to be replaced in `vngcloud-manage-csi-driver` after it broke image builds there, so this is not an isolated preference.

## Also: stop letting the shell parse GOPROXY

`${GOPROXY}` was unquoted in the Dockerfile `RUN` line and in `Makefile:62`. This changes nothing today — the current value has no shell metacharacters — but it is a trap that has already cost a debugging round in the sibling repo.

The moment anyone writes a fallback chain, the build breaks in a way that never mentions GOPROXY:

```
$ G="https://a.io|https://b.org,direct"
$ sh -c "echo GOPROXY=${G} x"
sh: 1: https://b.org,direct: not found
```

And a fallback chain is exactly what someone reaches for **when a proxy goes down** — which is exactly when this trap springs. Worth knowing why the chain is tempting:

| separator | falls through when |
|---|---|
| `,` | only on **404 / 410** |
| `|` | on **any** error, including a dead proxy |

`vngcloud-manage-csi-driver` already carries `https://goproxy.io|https://proxy.golang.org,direct` and needed quoting in both places for precisely this reason.

## One decision for you

`ENV` instead of `ARG` means this can **no longer be overridden** with `--build-arg GOPROXY=...`. Nothing does today — only `VERSION` and `REGISTRY` are passed — so there is no practical loss right now.

If you want that flexibility back, or want the two CSI repos to use an identical value, the alternative is:

```dockerfile
ARG GOPROXY=https://goproxy.io|https://proxy.golang.org,direct
```

which is override-able, falls through on any error, and matches manage-csi exactly. It is safe **only** with the quoting in this PR. Say the word and I will switch it.

I kept `ENV ... proxy.golang.org,direct` because that is what has actually been building on `dev`, and I would rather not quietly change a value you chose.

## Verification

`make build` passes. **Not verified:** the image build itself — the Docker daemon is not reachable from my machine, and `ci.yml` does not build images (`build_dev` does, on push to `dev`). The Dockerfile change is a one-line value swap plus quoting, and the `ENV` form is already proven by every dev build since `656ee9e`.

author: atniclimate
body:
Roadmap task DDM-P0-T04 asks for detection of "when main and the deployed Pages build remain different after a grace period." The post-deploy proof merged as pull request 31 did not meet that goal on its own: it fires only when a deploy SUCCEEDS, and asks whether that build reached the content delivery network. The likelier divergence is the deploy that never succeeded, a red browser shard, the `pages` concurrency group superseding a run, or the freshness gate refusing an obsolete rerun: no completion event fires, nothing is verified, no issue opens, and the live site quietly keeps serving an older commit. This pull request adds the compare that asks the stated question directly: main is at X, is X live?

## What changed

- `scripts/lib/live-receipts.mjs`: new pure, exported `resolveLiveExpectation(input)` plus `LIVE_COMPARE_GRACE_MS` (30 minutes). No network, no I/O. Given the event, the `workflow_run` payload, main's head sha, that commit's committer date, the recent `deploy.yml` runs for main, `now`, and a grace period, it returns one of three verdicts:
  - `verify` with `{ sha, nonce, reason }`. For a successful `workflow_run` the sha and nonce are the deploy run's own (unchanged behavior). For schedule or dispatch they are main's head and the id of the LATEST successful deploy run of that head.
  - `in-flight`: a deploy of main's head is queued or running, or the head is younger than the grace period with no successful deploy yet. The job writes a summary line and ends green, without verifying and without touching issues.
  - `undeployed`: the head is past the grace period with no successful deploy. The job files the divergence and fails.
- `scripts/resolve-live-expectation.mjs`: a thin driver. Reads the facts as JSON from stdin or `--input`, writes `verdict`/`sha`/`nonce`/`reason` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` (or `--output`), appends one verdict block to the job summary, exits 2 only on a usage or parse error. Every value is collapsed to one line so it is also safe to copy into `$GITHUB_ENV`.
- `tests/live-receipts.test.mjs`: 14 new assertions across every branch, including a successful deploy with a newer rerun of the same sha (pick the latest successful), a success that coexists with an in-progress rerun, a success for an OLDER sha only, no runs at all, a custom grace period, and the input errors. `npm run test:live-receipts` is already inside `npm run gate`.
- `.github/workflows/verify-live.yml`: adds `schedule` (`15 14 * * *` UTC) and `workflow_dispatch`. Daily rather than hourly because the compare only has something new to say when a deploy failed or was cancelled, that failure already emails the owner, and a red deploy deserves a durable issue within a day; 14:15 UTC sits after the 13:00 upstream monitor and the 13:30 source-health probe so the three receipts do not contend for runners. The owner can tune the cron or dispatch a compare at any time. The job `if` still skips non-success `workflow_run` events; the job-level concurrency group is `verify-live-main` for schedule, dispatch, and successful `workflow_run` events and `github.run_id` otherwise; `cancel-in-progress` is now `${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_run' }}`, so a scheduled compare QUEUES behind an in-flight post-deploy proof rather than destroying the receipt for a real release in order to re-ask a question the running job is already answering. Checkout is `${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.sha }}`, and a small align step re-points the working tree at the resolved commit when a late-starting scheduled run finds main has moved, so the PMTiles range checks read the archive list the verified build shipped. The verify step, receipt upload, freshness check, issue open/append, issue close, and fail step keep their semantics behind `verdict == 'verify'`. The `undeployed` path opens or appends to the SAME marker-keyed (`<!-- ddm-verify-live -->`) `deploy-divergence` issue with its own wording, so there is ever one issue.
- Permissions gain `actions: read`. `gh run list --workflow=deploy.yml` reads `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow_id}/runs`, which the fine-grained permission reference lists under the Actions repository permission at read; unlisted scopes become `none` once any scope is named, so the scheduled compare cannot see the deploy runs without it. Confirmed against docs.github.com (REST permissions reference and the workflow-syntax `permissions` page), not assumed. `contents: read`, `issues: write`, and `pages: read` are unchanged.
- Injection posture: the `workflow_run` fields reach the shell only through `env:`, the deploy runs and branch head reach `jq` as JSON, and the resolver's text reaches `$GITHUB_ENV` through `env:` indirection. No API text is pasted into a command line.
- Docs: `DEVELOPER.md` ("GitHub Pages and release evidence") gains what the scheduled compare proves, its grace period, and its three verdicts; `docs/RELEASE_NOTES.md` gains a `### 2026-08-29: main and live are compared on a schedule` subsection under the `## v0.6.25` preamble that says plainly the post-deploy proof alone did not meet DDM-P0-T04's stated goal, and what is still not proved. The header comment of `verify-live.yml` and both comments in `deploy.yml` that described the proof as post-deploy only were updated. No status fields were added to `docs/ROADMAP.yaml`; no receipt gained a body or a screenshot (hard rule 1; `src/layers/aiannh.ts`).

Verified: `npm run test:live-receipts` (21 tests, 21 pass, 0 fail); `npm run scan:emdash` (clean); PyYAML `yaml.safe_load` over all seven files in `.github/workflows/` (all ok) plus a structural dump confirming the three triggers, the job `if`, the concurrency key, the four permissions, and every step condition; driver smoke with fixture JSON for all three verdicts, by `--input` file and by stdin, checking the `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` lines and the summary markdown, plus `--help` and the bad-input path (exit 2); and a replay of the workflow step's exact `jq` assembly against canned `gh run list` and `gh api branches/main` payloads, piped into the driver, for both a `schedule` and a `workflow_run` event.

Not run: `npm run gate` (it builds; nothing here touches the application bundle), any Playwright spec, `vite preview`, and `actionlint` (not installed on this workstation; PyYAML parsing is the substitute). The live proof itself was not run against the public seat from this branch.

## What this PR cannot prove

A `schedule` or `workflow_dispatch` trigger only exists once the workflow file is on `main`, so nothing in this branch can exercise either one; Validate here proves the repository checks, not the new cadence. The resolver's judgment is fully proved offline, but the wiring around it (the `gh` calls, the `jq` assembly under `set -euo pipefail`, the `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` and `$GITHUB_ENV` handoff, and the align-checkout step) is proved only by local replay against canned payloads. Suggested first action after merge: dispatch "Verify the live build" by hand from the Actions tab and read its job summary. On a healthy repository it should print the `verify` verdict naming main's head and the deploy run that published it, and then run the full live proof; if `main` is ahead of the live build right now it should instead print `undeployed`, open the one `deploy-divergence` issue, and fail, which is the behavior this pull request exists to add.

author: ashishawasthi
body:
A resource name is the one place a rename costs a rebuild — Cloud Run URLs and KMS ring names cannot be changed in place — so these are worth fixing before the next deployment rather than after.

- `name_prefix` `hrz9` → `journey`: service names, service accounts, the CMEK ring and the VPC-SC perimeter title.
- Five service-account display names read `Hrz9 …`.
- **App ids become repository names**: embedded services are `journey-cdd-sow-research-{api,ui}` not `journey-doc1-*`, and users land on `/apps/credit-memo-drafting/` not `/apps/doc2/`.

**Two defects the rename exposed**, both of which would bite any id longer than four characters:

- The app-id pattern was `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,30}$` — sized for `doc1`/`mkt6`. `performance-marketing-optimisation` (34) was refused outright. Widened to 63, the label limit these ids must satisfy as Cloud Run name components.
- The canonical `/agent` mount resolved a hardcoded `doc1`, so every request to it 404'd once the id moved.

Verified against a baseline rather than assumed: 1 pre-existing failure → 80 with the rename → **0** after the two fixes. Both stacks `terraform validate` clean.

Not applied to the running deployment — that comes with the next rebuild, which is what makes these names worth landing first.

body:
Fixes #118.

Invalid UTF-8 in a lesson collapsed its dedup key to `sha256("")` (`e3b0c442…`), so every such lesson collided with every other one and was silently dropped. Adopted invariant (from @pm25coder's two-path analysis, issue comment 5430526039): **a dedup key must never be computed from an empty normalized string.** Design = option 1 (fail-closed guards at every caller + empty-normalized refusal inside `candidate_lesson_hash`) + option 3 (reject invalid UTF-8 at flush-intake with a visible `rejected=` receipt counter). Both independent failure paths are closed: Path A (BSD awk abort, previously swallowed) via status guard + empty-output refusal; Path B (python NFKC stage failure, previously unchecked in `candidate_lesson_hash`) via strict `.encode("utf-8")` + status propagation — deterministic on platforms where awk passes invalid bytes through instead of aborting.

Commits: `634f537` (core fix + regression suite) + `31c9fd7` (3-seat review adoptions: last unguarded caller in the openclaw adapter, per-guard pin tests, quiet Path B refusal, docs). Reviews ran at pre-rebase SHAs `ba2a366` / `29638d2`; rebased onto current main with `git range-diff` showing `=` for both commits (byte-identical content), post-rebase `make test` 42/42 + `make lint` re-run.

`git diff --stat origin/main...31c9fd7` matches the list above exactly (verification below).

   `normalize_state_candidate_key_text` guards the awk stage (status + empty-output-for-non-empty-input refusal, lib-state-fold.sh:132-138) and propagates the python stage's exit. body:
Yukon submission `96688a42-30b3-4a45-b54d-1d42364e46bc` against https://github.com/Layr-Labs/mlxfast-gemma4-26b-a4b-engine at `c357cb76129a6dbdf800779921a9f8fa6ff4bc7b`.

Current best score: 1.80810847810405. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
the PR is merged automatically if the submission is accepted, and closed with the result otherwise.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: MiniMax M3
Harness: Command Code

Gemma4Text.swift — implementation changes in the promoted source

This revision reshapes the Gemma 4 path inside the continuous-batching V2 stack and trims a parallel layer of gating in the wider MLX surface. The end-state behavior is the same model, but with a much narrower decode-specialised surface and with several promotion ladders removed rather than turned off.

The most visible change in `Gemma4Text.swift` is the removal of the explicit CBv2 graph-submission ladder. The `resolveGemma4DecodeAsyncEvalLadderEnabled` helper, the `gemma4DecodeAsyncEvalLadderEnabled` constant, the `gemma4ShouldSubmitDecodeAsyncEvalLadder` policy function, and the `DARKBLOOM_GEMMA4_DECODE_ASYNC_EVAL_LADDER` environment-variable read all leave the file. The previous default had the ladder engaged for B=8, L=1, isCBv2, non-prefill traffic at layer indices 0, 1, 5, 11, 17, 23 and 27. The new file does not contain any of that boundary logic; the boundary is no longer expressed in this source. The remaining attention path calls `qProj` and `oProj` directly rather than routing through `tierProjection` and `outputProjection`, so the tight-grid B=8/L=1 host that previously re-dispatched the promoted matrix-unit tier's text with `grid.x = 1` is gone, and the per-attention Q, K, V and output matmuls revert to whatever the layer module dispatches for the current shape.

The Q/K/V RMSNorm kernel loses its `KEY_VALUE_SHARED` specialisation. The old kernel guarded the V branch with `!KEY_VALUE_SHARED && row >= Q_ROWS + K_ROWS`, advanced a `shared_value_output` pointer for K and V rows, and wrote V using the live normaliser and the shared raw key. The new template drops the `KEY_VALUE_SHARED` parameter; the V branch is taken whenever `row >= Q_ROWS + K_ROWS`, the shared-output pointer setup is gone, and the in-loop V write is gone. The host wrapper `gemma4FusedQKVNorm` correspondingly drops the `keyValueShared:` argument, drops the `!keyValueShared || v.shape == k.shape` guard, drops the `keyValueShared` template entry, and computes the launch grid as `(qRows + 2 * kRows) * threads` directly. The K-eq-V fast path is no longer expressed in this kernel.

The shape-specialised GeGLU path is also gone. The `gemma4SafeGeluProductShaped` closure, the `gemma4ShapedGeluFuseEnabled` constant driven by `DARKBLOOM_GELU_SHAPED_FUSE`, the `geluFusionClaimsPinnedDecode` admit predicate, and the `gemma4GeluProduct` router all leave the file. The retained `gemma4SafeGeluProduct` is the same body as before but traced under `shapeless: true`, with a fallback to the un-compiled closure when `gemma4CompiledDecodeSupported` is false. So a single GELU-product body remains, traced without shape specialisation, and decode traffic goes through it like every other shape.

`SwitchLayers.swift` loses the same shape-specialised GeGLU entry point. The `compiledGeGLUShaped` closure, the `switchGeluFuseEnabled` constant read from `DARKBLOOM_GELU_SHAPED_FUSE`, and the `geGLUClaimsPinnedDecode` predicate all leave; the surviving selector falls through to the unshaped compile path or to the un-compiled closure. The `isCompiledDecodeSupported` lookup against `MLXHardwareInfo` is preserved, but the dispatch is now the same as the generic GeGLU site.

In the continuous-batching V2 attention files, the ragged two-pass decode path loses its `DARKBLOOM_GEMMA4_D512_DECODE_SDPA` read. The `ProcessInfo` lookup, the `processInfo` reference, and the `gemma4ShouldSubmit` style gate all leave `RaggedTwoPassDecodeAttentionV1.swift`; the new kernel name `cbv2_ragged8_sdpa_2pass_b_bf16_d256_b_v1` is the only decode D=256 entry that the file registers, and the D=512 composed path is no longer presented as a scored option in this source. The `AttentionV1.swift` file drops `CBv2EngageMark`, the `effectiveSinks` materialisation, the `d512sdpa` reference, and the `CBv2RaggedComposedD512DecodeAttentionV1` selection — the surviving selection is the plain two-pass attention. `EngineLoopV2.swift` drops `CBv2OrderOnlyLogits` and the `withOrderOnly` wrapper, so the engine no longer has a separate order-only logits stage wired in here. `LogitsPipelineV2.swift` correspondingly drops `CBv2OrderOnlyLogits` and the `orderOnly` field, the `Bool` plumbing through `CBv2SamplingParams`, and the `isEmpty` / `allSatisfy` short-circuits on `topLogprobs`, `logitBias`, `repetitionPenalty`, `repetitionContextSize`, and `greedyEpsilon`. The pipeline struct still holds those sampling parameters, but the order-only short-circuit is no longer encoded in this file.

`DFlashDraftModel.swift` is the speculative draft model file; the diff is consistent with the same kind of cleanup of environment-driven decoders in the speculative path, with no new knob introduced.

On the MLX side, `quantized.h` and `quantized.cpp` register a new triple-stream variant of the affine4 quantised matmul. The new entry point is `qmv_affine4_g64_triple_stream_impl`, which takes the same inputs as the existing pair-stream form and produces two output rows per launch instead of one. The shared scaffolding `load_vector`, `METAL_FUNC`, the `uint3` grid mapping, `threadgroup_position_in_grid`, `simd_gid`, `simdgroup_index_in_threadgroup`, `thread_index_in_simdgroup`, `num_simdgroups`, and `SIMD_SIZE` are retained, and the `tail_values` / `active_tail_lanes` tail handling is reused. The per-pair leader / pair follower split is explicit: each leader carries an `x0_idx` / `x1_idx` and a `pair_w` / `pair_scales` / `pair_biases` triple plus a `pair_x0` / `pair_x1` input pair, and produces `pair_y0` / `pair_y1`; the immediately-following odd-position rows are produced by the leader, not by a separate dispatch. The compiled-in default is therefore that the host picks the triple-stream entry when its shape predicate matches, and the older pair-stream kernel is still callable but is no longer the selected path for matched shapes.

`quantized_nax.h` and `quantized_nax.cpp` drop the `MLX_MTL_CONST` annotation around the `kGatherRhsSortedEndpointElide` constant. The constant is still a compile-time-elided gather switch for the sorted-endpoint NAX path; the only change is whether it is declared with the Metal constant-address-space attribute, which means the new compiled default is an ordinary `constexpr` rather than a `constant` template parameter. `sdpa_vector.h` is updated in line with the same kind of cleanup; no new entry point is named in the diff for that header.

`spec-decoder-head.manifest.json` is updated to reflect the new compiled surface. The set of files and entry points it enumerates matches the survivors listed above: the shapeless GeGLU trace, the unspecialised Q/K/V RMSNorm, the plain two-pass D=256 ragged decode attention, the triple-stream affine4 quantised matmul, and the non-`MLX_MTL_CONST` NAX gather constant. The `DARKBLOOM_GEMMA4_DECODE_ASYNC_EVAL_LADDER`, `DARKBLOOM_GEMMA4_D512_DECODE_SDPA`, and `DARKBLOOM_GELU_SHAPED_FUSE` environment reads that used to gate the now-removed specialisations do not appear in the manifest.

In summary, the landed behavior is: a single GELU-product body traced with `shapeless: true` and used uniformly, a Q/K/V RMSNorm that always treats V as a separate bank, attention that calls `qProj` and `oProj` directly, no per-layer graph-submission ladder for B=8/L=1, no order-only logits short-circuit in the V2 pipeline, no D=512 composed decode attention in this source, and a new triple-stream affine4 quantised matmul with the previous pair-stream form retained but no longer the selected path. Two changes to `resolveHelperReturn`, which reads a project's own response helper (`return json(200, payload)`):

author: ritsukai2000
body:
## Problem

`autopilot issue triage` threw **before applying anything** when no Project iteration covered the current date:

```text
autopilot: No current Sprint iteration is configured;
select or create the active iteration before applying triage
```

So the entire mutation — Issue Type, Project membership, Status, Blocked on, Effort, Priority — was refused over a field nothing requires.

## Sprint is not an eligibility requirement

Claiming needs board membership, Issue Type, Priority, and `Blocked on ≠ Human` ([snapshot.ts:1055](https://github.com/Jinn-Network/autopilot/blob/main/src/lifecycle/snapshot.ts)). Sprint is not in that set.

The engine's own triage path proves it: child issues and review follow-ups are filed, triaged, prioritised and worked every cycle with Sprint left empty. Sampled live on mono — `#3271`, `#3276`, `#3278` all carry `sprint=` (blank), all on the board at P2–P4, all being worked normally.

So two triage paths in one codebase disagreed: the engine triages hundreds of issues a day without an iteration, while the operator command refused.

## Why the calendar is empty

A Project with no open iteration is an ordinary state — nobody has started the next sprint. `Jinn-Network/mono` has had none since Sprint 3 ended on 1 June. That made operator triage impossible on a Project the engine works happily; a 92-issue triage had to be completed by writing the fields directly.

Creating an iteration is not a workaround available to the tool either: `ProjectV2Iteration` input is `{startDate, duration, title}` with **no `id`**, so `updateProjectV2Field` cannot append one without rewriting the whole configuration by value and putting existing completed iterations at risk.

## Change

`currentSprintId` returns `undefined` instead of throwing, and `applyTriage` skips only the Sprint edit.

A **mismatched** Sprint field still throws — that is a real configuration fault, not an empty calendar. The preview line now reads "set Sprint to the current Project iteration when one is open".

## Verification

TDD, watched failing with the production error before the fix:

```text
× applies triage when the Project has no current Sprint iteration
    → promise rejected "Error: No current Sprint iteration is con…" instead of resolving
```

The companion test pins that a Project **with** an open iteration still gets `--iteration-id`, so the working path is unchanged.

author: venetanji
body:
## Why desktop had no buttons

`app.css` carried this, and it was deliberate:

```css
@media (pointer: fine) {
  .side-rail .rotate-btn, .side-rail .bond-btn, .side-rail .demo-btn,
  .side-rail .thaw-btn, .side-rail .auto-btn, .side-rail .cancel-aim-btn { display: none; }
  .kbd-hint { display: flex; }
}
```

On a mouse/trackpad the rail shed **every game button** — rotate, Bond Breaker, Demolition, the Thaw Lance, the Autoloader — leaving fullscreen and pause, and the controls were taught instead by a line of text along the foot of the field ("Q/E rotate · W/S aim · Space fire"). `layout.ts`'s `railSlotsFor` knew about it too and budgeted the desktop column at 2 slots.

The reasoning was sound as far as it went (a keyboard already covers those keys), and it produced a build where the mouse player could **read** what rotates the piece and had nothing to click, several hundred pixels from the machine, while the phone build had a column of real buttons doing that exact job. One game, two shapes — which is what the owner is objecting to: *"the key hints are in the HUD, but that's not an action place, we mimic the mobile structure so they're also clickable and coherent."*

## What shipped

**The rail is the same column on every pointer**, in the same order, with the same visual language. Only the cancel ✕ stays touch-only — it exists to be hit by a *second finger* mid-drag, and a fine pointer has neither a second contact nor (since the aim rework) a drag to abort.

**Each button carries a legend row under its glyph, showing the ACTIVE input's chip and nothing else.** Three chips are in the markup — the keycap, the Xbox mark, the PlayStation mark — and exactly one is ever drawn, chosen by `<html data-profile>` (the input family, which follows the last input seen) crossed with `<html data-pad>` (which controller is attached).

A keyboard player sees `Q`. The moment they press a button on a DualSense the same rail says `L1`. Put the pad down, touch the mouse, and it says `Q` again — the global keydown listener and the pointerdown capture already flip the profile, so the return trip needed no new code. On **touch** the profile is `touch` and nothing draws at all, which keeps a phone's rail exactly the button it has always been.

The gate is the profile rather than `@media (pointer: fine)` on purpose: a media query answers "could this device have a keyboard", and the question a legend answers is "what is this player holding right now". It also makes the two halves mutually exclusive by construction — a desktop with a pad matched *both* `pointer: fine` and `[data-pad]`, which is how the first cut drew a keycap and a pad mark together.

- Fullscreen gets no legend: it is a browser affordance with neither a key nor a pad button, and an empty row under one button in a column whose whole argument is that the slots line up would be a hole.
- 41px of content (22px glyph + 3px + 16px row) inside a button that is 44px at the WCAG floor and 60px wherever the solver has room, so no window size has to choose between the legend and the tap target.

**And the HUD keeps no shortcuts at all.** The key-hint strip along the foot of the field is gone — not trimmed. What went with it: `armKeyHints`/`dismissKeyHints`, the dismissed flag, the once-per-session re-show and its 15s timer, `hintsDismissed` on every HUD render, `settings.seenKeyHints` (and its three fixture literals), `hintStripHTML`, `HINT_SEP`, `hintParts`'s `full` flag, `.hud__bottom`, and ~100 lines of app.css — the field-relative centring, the 18px lane fit, the wrap bound, the z-index rung above the plant panel. Every one of those was the cost of putting keyboard shortcuts on a live bay.

Nothing dangles. The pause card was always *"the permanent home the transient strip retires to"*; it is now simply the home, and it needs no lifecycle because it is behind a button. It carries strictly more than the strip did — the strip's content was a subset — including the mouse wheel, the menu gestures, and the parts no button anywhere carries: the aim/power keys, and the stick. The coach still teaches the shot on a first run through the same hint table, and the touch drag hint is untouched.

So **every control instruction in the game is now in one of exactly two places: printed on the control, or on the pause card.** There is no third place, so there is no third place to go stale — which is what a new pin asserts, by counting bare `.kbd` chips in the HUD and finding none.

## Legends render from `bindings.ts`, never from typed letters

`components.ts`'s `railLegendHTML(action)` asks `keyFor`/`padFor` — a rebind on the Controls screen re-letters the rail. Writing it caught two standing lies: the Autoloader's badge was the literal string `"F"` and the plant panel's three ability chips were `"B"`, `"X"`, `"C"`, all typed into `screens.ts`. They read the table now, and the pin that proves it **rebinds first, then asserts**.

## Pad families

`bindings.ts` named the standard mapping in Xbox lettering on the note that "a PlayStation player reads positions, which match". True of the face diamond, false of everything around it — a DualSense has no button labelled LB, RB, LT, RT or Start. There is a table per family now:

- `padFamilyFromId(id)` keys on Sony's `054c` and Microsoft's `045e` **vendor ids** (the half that cannot be spelled a second way — Firefox reports a DualShock 4 as just `054c-09cc-Wireless Controller`), with the human-readable names as fallback and Xbox as the default for an unknown pad.
- `padLabel(button)` follows the connected pad, so the pause card and the Controls screen's rebind rows re-letter with it.
- `padChip(button, family)` is the rail's compact form: Xbox's **coloured letter**, PlayStation's **four marks** (`icons.ts`, same 16×16 grid), `LB/L1`-style text for the shoulders, one shared bar-stack for the button that is Start on one pad and Options on the other.

**Button 2 is why the PlayStation half is drawn and not lettered**: it is Square on a DualSense and X on an Xbox pad, so a chip reading "X" would name the right button on one and the wrong one on the other.

No trademarks, no logos. The Xbox letter colours are existing tokens (`--success`, `--danger`, `--piece-j`, `--piece-o`); contrast against `--surface-3` is measured in the stylesheet (10.51 / 4.10 / 3.73 / 11.75 : 1, all clear of SC 1.4.11's 3:1, and the letter is never the only carrier).

Keeping all three chips in the markup is the load-bearing part: switching input mid-bay, or swapping a pad for one of the other family, re-letters the whole rail **with no re-render** — these buttons sit beside instruments that animate, and a rebuilt element restarts its animation from frame one.

## It costs no field

Worth checking rather than assuming, since the solver reserves the rail's band *before* fitting the world. It does not: "snug" reserves `RAIL_MAX + 2*RAIL_PAD` = 84px whatever the slot count, and `railColumnCap` only bites when the column is taller than the window — at eight slots that needs 410px of height, and the shortest browser row in the matrix is 600.

| window | mode | band | button | field | before → after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1280×720 | snug | 84px | 60px | 1196×673 | unchanged |
| 1269×663 | snug | 84px | 60px | 1179×663 | unchanged |
| 1600×900 | snug | 84px | 60px | 1516×853 | unchanged |
| 1920×1080 | snug | 84px | 60px | 1836×1033 | unchanged |
| 2560×1080 | wide | natural gutter | 60px | 1920×1080 | unchanged |
| 1000×760 | tall | bottom strip | 60px | 1000×563 | unchanged |
| 800×600 | tall | bottom strip | 60px | 800×450 | unchanged |

So `RailLoadout.finePointer` is **removed** rather than kept as a flag that always reads false. A browser window dragged under ~410px tall now takes the bottom-strip fallback — the same answer, for the same reason, a 360dp phone already gets.

Mouse behaviour is untouched: these are the same `<button data-game="…">` elements the phone build has always had, so the `[data-action]`/`b

author: mikalstill
body:
Documentation only, one commit: the phase 6 plan, its Execution-table row,
and the two corrections at source the plan commits to.

## The finding that reshaped the phase

Phase 6's stub told this phase to rule out a competing explanation for #3565
before spending its decision budget. That instruction is discharged, and the
answer is neither of the two mechanisms the plan documents argue about.

A fully traced occurrence was posted to #3565 on **2026-08-26** — after phase
4a fixed #3813 on 2026-08-24, so from a cluster where the spreader works. The
candidate set had already collapsed to **one node** before affinity was
scored. inst3 requested anti-affinity, correctly scored that node `-100`, and
placed there anyway, because a scorer given one candidate has nothing to do.
The issue's own words:

> here it did not lose a tiebreak, it was **never consulted** in any
> meaningful sense

And the half of the assertion that *passed* was the same forced choice. The
run says nothing about affinity in either direction.

It is not lost spreading, and it is not affinity losing a tiebreak to load
ordering.

## The decision most likely to be argued with

**F2 closes #3565 on a test change, not a scheduler change.** That is the
shape of an excuse and should be pushed on. The defence is the trace and only
the trace. Against a single-candidate set:

- D6 position 1 (hard require only) turns the flake into a 507 — which the
  issue itself calls "the same ejection with a different traceback".
- D6 position 2 (soften the ceiling) has nothing to soften: the affinity
  target *was* the surviving candidate, and the instance was placed on it.
- D6 position 3 is the issue's candidate fix 2 under another name, and is the
  one the evidence supports.

The honest framing: #3565 was mostly a specification bug. The product never
promised co-location under contention; the test assumed it did, and every
investigation since has hunted a scheduler defect behind an assertion that was
too strong.

**F7 declines** D6's ceiling-softening rather than deferring it. A preference
that can raise a ceiling puts a ranking input inside the transaction whose
correctness argument depends on it being arithmetic — which is exactly what
phase 3 spent its effort establishing.

**F3 keeps this from being flake suppression**: the rewritten test *skips
rather than passes* on a degenerate candidate set. A single-candidate run
carries no information, and a green there is the same false pass the trace
describes.

## Other survey findings

- **The binary affinity model does not exist at all.** None of
  `require_with_tag` / `require_without_tag` / `prefer_with_tag` /
  `prefer_without_tag` appear anywhere in the tree. This is a first
  implementation, not a migration.
- **`test_affinity` is itself a user of the weighted form it deprecates**
  (`{'first-node': 100}` / `{-100}`), so the transition mapping is exercised
  from the moment it exists and the weighted form cannot be removed in the
  same change.
- **The binding stage has moved from CPU to memory** — a fix aimed only at
  `sufficient_idle_cpu` would now miss.
- **The audit events already carry what the test needs**, and
  `_add_scheduler_detail()` already fetches them, which makes the
  expensive-looking half of the phase cheap.
- **D6's line references have all moved** (`:473-481` → `:487-501`, `:611-631`
  → `:529-600`, `:260` → `:187-256`).

## Explicitly not adopted

The `507 ... sufficient_idle_cpu` family (#3772). It comes from an admission
stage that runs *before* ranking; when it refuses every candidate no ranking
model would have helped. `PLAN-ci-cloud-sizing` owns it and has the better
analysis. Written into the plan as F6 because it is the loudest
scheduler-shaped signal in CI and is repeatedly mistaken for evidence about
ranking.

## Corrections at source

The master plan's phase 6 stub gains the traced mechanism, keeping the
superseded reasoning beneath it. D6 gains current line references and the
CPU→memory note. D6's three positions are left as written — a decision record
should show what was on offer.

## Checks

The definition-of-done checks were **run at planning time, not merely
written**. One was wrong: `grep "inst\['node'\]"` matches nothing, because the
assertions name `inst1`/`inst2`/`inst3`. Corrected to the grep that works,
with the lines it actually returns (125, 129). Finding 7's line references
corrected from 79/98 to 80/99.

`pre-commit run` passes: documentation links and anchors resolve, plan
statuses and index arithmetic agree. (The status vocabulary check caught
`Planned` as invalid and it is now `Not started`, matching phase 4c.)

author: charlesvestal
body:
Adds `short_name` to this module's parameters, so the Schwung knob grid can
label each cell with the word that identifies it rather than a squeezed
abbreviation of the full name.

Part of a fleet-wide pass over every catalogued module. Each name was chosen
by hand against the page it appears on: where a page is already called
"Filter Envelope", its cells say ATTACK and DECAY rather than F.ATK and FENVDEC.

### What changes

- **eucalypso** — 8 parameters labelled

Nothing else is touched: no version bump, no behaviour change, no new params.

### eucalypso — rendered

![eucalypso](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/charlesvestal/schwung-catalog-site/label-review/audit/label-review/eucalypso.png)

Left is what the grid draws today, right is with this change — 8 of 12 changed pages.

### Before / after

| page | key | grid drew | now draws |
|---|---|---|---|
| Main, Lane 1 | `lane1_enabled` | ON | **L1** |
| Main, Lane 2 | `lane2_enabled` | ON | **L2** |
| Main, Lane 3 | `lane3_enabled` | ON | **L3** |
| Main, Lane 4 | `lane4_enabled` | ON | **L4** |
| Note Register | `register_mode` | RMODE | **MODE** |
| Note Register | `held_order` | NOTORD | **ORD** |
| Note Register | `missing_note_policy` | MISPOL | **POL** |
| Note Register | `scale_rng` | SCARNG | **RNG** |

The page matters where a name repeats: the same role under two sections
gets the same short name, and the section it sits under is what tells
them apart.

### The full name is not lost

A short name is what the **cell** says at rest. The moment a knob is
touched, the header shows that parameter's **full name and its value** —
so nothing becomes unidentifiable, it just stops being shouted at you
eight times on one page.

![touched](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/charlesvestal/schwung-catalog-site/label-review/audit/label-review/eucalypso-touched.png)

`global_v_rnd` on **Global - 2**: the cell reads **VEL** at rest, and the header reads **VEL RND** under the finger.

### Safe to merge now

`short_name` is a new field — it lands in the next Schwung release. On the
currently released host (v0.12.1) it is simply ignored.

This was checked rather than assumed: for every file here, the **v0.12.1**
page planner was run against the module contract before and after the change
and asserted to produce byte-identical pages — same page count, same cells,
same order. Merging today changes nothing; the labels appear when users update.

### Not included — these live in your DSP

14 more parameters take their metadata from the plugin's `chain_params` at runtime, so they
cannot be labelled from `module.json`. Adding `short_name` beside each one
in your `chain_params` JSON is all that is needed. Suggested values:

```
global_v_rnd  ->  Vel                         # Global - 2
global_g_rnd  ->  Gate                        # Global - 2
global_rnd_seed  ->  Seed                     # Global - 2
rand_cycle  ->  Cyc                           # Global - 2
held_order_seed  ->  Rand Seed                # Note Register
missing_note_seed  ->  Seed                   # Note Register - 2
lane1_drop_seed  ->  Drop                     # Lane 1 - 2
lane1_oct_rng  ->  Rng                        # Lane 1 - 2
lane2_drop_seed  ->  Drop                     # Lane 2 - 2
lane2_oct_rng  ->  Rng                        # Lane 2 - 2
lane3_drop_seed  ->  Drop                     # Lane 3 - 2
lane3_oct_rng  ->  Rng                        # Lane 3 - 2
lane4_drop_seed  ->  Drop                     # Lane 4 - 2
lane4_oct_rng  ->  Rng                        # Lane 4 - 2
```

### If a label is wrong

These are suggestions from someone reading the grid, not from the person who
wrote the synth. Change any of them in this branch, or close it — no hard
feelings either way. Layout problems are a separate matter and will come as
their own issues.

author: erikrikarddaniel
body:
## PR checklist

- [x] This comment contains a description of changes (with reason).
- [x] Module has been tested locally with real Docker runs (not just lint), see below.
- [x] `nf-core modules lint` passes clean.
- [x] Test data is available (nf-core/test-datasets#2247, not yet merged, so CI here won't be green until it lands).

## Description

Collects one or more `subread/featurecounts` raw output files (typically one per sample, for the same feature type/ORF caller) into a single long-format table (`orf`, `chr`, `start`, `end`, `strand`, `length`, `sample`, `count`, `tpm`), computing per-sample TPM and dropping zero-count rows.

Ported from two independently-hardened, now-functionally-identical local modules — nf-core/magmap's and nf-core/metatdenovo's own `COLLECT_FEATURECOUNTS` — as part of a cross-repo effort to share their summary-table-generation code (tracked in [nf-core/magmap#237](https://github.com/nf-core/magmap/issues/237)). Both pipelines' local copies were first made caller/pipeline-agnostic by moving their one pipeline-specific ID-reconciliation special-case (magmap's genome-accession join, metatdenovo's Transdecoder `cds.`-prefix stripping) into small local post-processing steps — see nf-core/magmap#238 and nf-core/metatdenovo#483.

`tpm` is rounded to 6 decimal places. This carries over a fix from nf-core/metatdenovo#483/[#484](https://github.com/nf-core/metatdenovo/issues/484): when the same underlying counts get independently re-computed elsewhere (e.g. after a caller-consolidation step using a different R backend — `dtplyr`/`data.table` here vs plain `dplyr` there), the unrounded double can round its last significant digit differently for the same mathematical value, which made an exact-equality test downstream intermittently fail. Rounding here keeps output stable regardless of which backend a consumer uses to recompute the same value.

### Testing

Verified with real Docker runs against two new fixtures (two samples, mixed zero/non-zero counts, one shared multi-exon gene) — nf-core/test-datasets#2247. `tpm` correctly sums to exactly `1e6` per sample after rounding, zero-count rows are dropped, sample names are correctly stripped of their `.sorted.bam` suffix.

author: akvinayaktiwari
body:
Resolves **Open Question #10**, deferred in the 2026-07-26 journeys design and again in the 2026-07-29 addendum. Design doc: `docs/designs/journey-observability.md`.

## Why

There was no way to answer "which journeys are running, and are they working" from inside the product. The proof: answering "which journey is active on my account" required `aws dynamodb scan` against three tables by hand.

This was **not** a logging gap. The engine already wrote `journey_started`, `journey_step`, `tool_call`, `handoff` and `message_out` to `lead_events`, with `bundleId` and `stepId` on every row. Two things were missing:

- **`journey_ended` was declared at `types/index.ts:147` with zero call sites.** A journey that finished cleanly and one that died on step 4 were indistinguishable.
- **No index on `bundleId`**, so reading events per-journey was a full table scan.

## What changed

**The terminal event.** Journeys used to end at whichever step happened to have no `next` — `End: true` scattered across four step types, observed by nothing. Every exit now routes through a synthetic terminal state that records the ending with an outcome, the final step, the error, and the execution ARN.

- `__journey_completed` — ran off the end
- `__journey_handed_off` — reached a human_handoff step
- `__journey_failed` — records, **then** transitions to a `Fail` state, so Step Functions' own status stays honest

Every Task gains a `States.ALL` Catch routing to the failed terminal. On `await_reply` it is ordered **after** the existing `States.Timeout` catch — States.ALL matches a timeout too and Step Functions takes the first match, so the other order would turn every unanswered message into a failed journey.

Outcomes are only the three that something actually writes. `cancelled` and `timed_out` were in the approved design and are deliberately omitted: a stopped execution runs no further states, so nothing can report them. Declaring them would repeat the exact defect this PR fixes.

**The read path.** Sparse `bundleId-ts-index` GSI, `GET /api/journeys/:botId/:bundleId/executions` (derived on read, never stored), and an Activity tab per journey.

**The cross-bot index.** `GET /api/journeys/active` plus an "Active across all bots" strip, and the bot dropdown now defaults to a bot that has a live journey. Previously it defaulted to `myBots[0]` — whichever `botId` sorts first — so a client with 23 bots and one live journey opened on a bot with nothing running.

## Deploy order — this matters

1. **Run `scripts/provision-journey-executions-index.sh` BEFORE merging.** The executions endpoint 500s without the GSI.
2. **Republish every live journey after deploy.** Existing executions run their old state machine version and will never emit a terminal event — they sit at "In flight" forever. The UI says so explicitly rather than implying they are alive.

## Reviewed

Self-review found and fixed two real problems:

- **`LeadTimeline.tsx` rendered every `journey_ended` as "Journey finished".** Now that the event carries an outcome, a *failed* journey would have read as "finished" in the one timeline a client sees — the exact ambiguity this PR removes, reproduced client-side.
- **The executions header said "12 runs"** when it is a window over the last N events, not a total. Now "12 recent runs".

**Codex was unavailable (usage limit, resets Sep 10), so this diff has had NO independent cross-model adversarial pass** — on the change that alters the compiled state machine for every journey. Worth a second pair of eyes before merge, or a `/code-review ultra` run.

## Known gap, tracked as P1 in TODOS.md

A `condition` step compiles to a Choice reading `$.replied` / `$.lead_score` / `$.appointment_booked`, none of which are ever written into the execution state — they live in `lead_state`. That was already broken. What is new: ASL forbids `Catch` on a Choice, so this is now the **only** failure class that ends a journey without recording it. No shipped template uses a condition step, so it has never fired.

## Tests

1040 passing (748 backend, 292 frontend), both projects typecheck clean. New coverage: terminal-state compilation and catch ordering, outcome recording and error flattening, the executions reduce, the cross-bot index and its partial-failure degrade, and the trust boundary — the GSI is keyed by `bundleId` alone, so ownership is checked **before** the index is read.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
