author: sunapi386
body:
## Context

aceteam-ai/aceteam #6555 plumbs OpenAI tool calling from a fabric agent up to the node boundary — the `llm_inference` Redis job payload carries `tools`/`tool_choice` and full OpenAI messages (assistant `tool_calls`, `tool`-role results), and the AceTeam worker (`agents/fabric_client.py`) parses `tool_calls` back out of the result. This is the last hop: the citadel node's `llm_inference` handler must actually forward those fields to the serving engine and return any `tool_calls` the model emits.

## Assessment

**Bounded.** `internal/worker/llm_inference.go` does not proxy the raw request/response JSON — it re-marshals into typed structs (`jobs.LLMInferencePayload`, `jobs.ChatMessage`, and anonymous response structs) that had no fields for `tools`/`tool_choice`/`tool_calls`, so they were silently dropped by `json.Unmarshal`'s "ignore unknown fields" behavior. The gateway's chat route (`internal/gateway/chat_route.go`) is a separate, unaffected path — it's a byte-for-byte reverse proxy ("forwarded VERBATIM... never re-marshalled from a parsed struct" per its own doc comment), so tool calling already survives there.

## Changes

- `internal/jobs/queue_types.go`: added `Tools`/`ToolChoice` (raw JSON) to `LLMInferencePayload`, and `ToolCalls`/`ToolCallID`/`Name` to `ChatMessage`. Kept as raw JSON/plain strings rather than typed Go structs so an engine-specific `function.parameters` JSON Schema is never lossily re-typed.
- `internal/worker/llm_inference.go` (`executeChatCompletionsAt` — the vllm/llamacpp/bonsai/unlimited-ocr chat path):
  - Request: `tools`/`tool_choice` attached to the outbound body only when present; per-message `tool_calls`/`tool_call_id`/`name` attached only when non-empty.
  - Buffered response (`parseChatCompletionResponse`/`bufferedChatCompletions`): extracts and returns `tool_calls`; gates the existing reasoning_content→content fallback so a thinking model's chain-of-thought never leaks into `content` when it decided to call a tool instead; skips the empty-content parity chunk for a tool_calls-only reply.
  - Streaming response (`streamChatCompletions` + new `toolCallAccumulator`): merges the engine's incremental `delta.tool_calls` fragments (id/name latched from the first delta per index, `arguments` concatenated as text) into a final array, returned on the terminal `JobResult.Output` — **not** emitted as per-chunk deltas (see scope note below). `finish_reason` is gated to only override the pre-existing hardcoded `"stop"` when the engine reports `"tool_calls"` specifically, so every other text-only outcome (e.g. `"length"`) is unchanged.
- `CLAUDE.md`: documents the feature, the known ollama gap, and the streaming-deltas scope decision with its verification pointer.

**Known gap, not fixed here:** `executeOllamaChat` (ollama's native `/api/chat` path) still silently drops tools. Only the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` path (vllm/llamacpp/bonsai/unlimited-ocr) forwards them.

**Scope decision, verified against the real consumer:** streaming tool-call deltas are NOT emitted per-`chunk` event. `StreamWriter.WriteChunk(content string, index int)` has no field for structured data — widening it would ripple through both stream-writer implementations, `internal/redis`/`internal/redisapi`'s `PublishChunk`, and every existing caller, for a payload the consumer doesn't need today (the #717 "a guessed field is worse than no field" precedent). I checked `aceteam/python-backend/agents/fabric_client.py` before choosing this scope: `FabricInferenceClient._event_to_chunk`'s `"end"` branch already reads `tool_calls` off `data.result` — exactly what this PR returns via `stream.WriteEnd` — while its `"chunk"` branch drops a delta entirely when it carries neither text nor tool_calls. So a node that never emits a per-chunk `tool_calls` delta is not a regression for that consumer as it exists today. If AceTeam's agent loop later needs live partial tool-call visibility mid-stream, that's a follow-up that also needs `internal/redis`/`internal/redisapi` changes — flagging here so it isn't assumed covered by "Closes #603".

## Testing

- `gofmt -l .` clean
- `go vet ./...` clean
- `go build ./...` (linux), `GOOS=darwin GOARCH=arm64 go build ./...`, `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` all pass
- `go test ./internal/worker/... ./internal/gateway/... ./internal/jobs/...` and full `go test ./...` pass
- `go test ./internal/worker/... ./internal/gateway/... -race` passes
- New tests in `internal/worker/llm_inference_test.go`:
  - `TestLLMInferenceHandler_ToolsRequestByteIdenticalWithoutTools` — asserts KEY ABSENCE (not just empty values) for `tools`/`tool_choice`/per-message `tool_calls`/`tool_call_id`/`name` on a plain text request
  - `TestLLMInferenceHandler_ToolsForwardedInRequest` — full tools + tool_choice + assistant tool_calls + tool-role result round-trips into the outbound engine request
  - `TestLLMInferenceHandler_BufferedToolCallsResponse` / `TestLLMInferenceHandler_StreamingToolCallsAccumulate` — response-side tool_calls surfaced correctly (buffered and multi-delta streaming merge)
  - `TestLLMInferenceHandler_StreamingTextUnaffectedByToolCallPlumbing` — text-only streaming behavior (incl. `finish_reason`) unchanged
  - `TestLLMInferenceHandler_GroundingGuardrailHandlesToolCallsOnlyResponse` — the #8253 grounding guardrail handles a tool_calls-only response gracefully (vacuously grounded, `claims_checked: 0`, no crash/false-flag)
  - `TestLLMInferenceHandler_BufferedReasoningFallbackSkippedWhenToolCallsPresent` / `TestLLMInferenceHandler_BufferedContentAndToolCallsBothPresent` — the reasoning-vs-tool_calls and content-vs-tool_calls interaction, both directions

Closes #603 (relates aceteam-ai/aceteam#6555)

### Motivation
- Align frontend and backend API routing and environment configuration so client requests target the versioned backend endpoints.
- Prevent customer-facing privacy issues by ensuring customers cannot list or join non-public queues or see other customers' entries.
- Make queue-entry lifecycle transitions resilient to concurrent operator actions and reduce failure surface from token-generation races.
- Document project health and remaining environmental limitations discovered during automated verification.

### Description
- Aligned API base URL and examples by setting `API_BASE_URL` to `/api/v1` in `frontend/src/services/apiClient.js`, `frontend/.env.example`, and root `.env.example`, and enabled `FEATURE_QUEUE_ENABLED` in environment defaults and `docker-compose.yml`.
- Added a compare-and-set update in `backend/src/repositories/queueEntryRepository.js` by extending `exports.update` to accept `expectedStatus`, and made `backend/src/services/queueProcessingService.js` use it and return a `ConflictError` when a race occurs.
- Hardened join/list behavior in `backend/src/services/queueEntryService.js` and `backend/src/services/queueService.js` to restrict customer queries to their own entries, prohibit joining non-public queues for non-managers, and limit the public directory to active public queues.
- Mitigated sequential token collisions by retrying unique-token creation in `queueEntryService.join` when Mongo duplicate-key errors occur (bounded retry loop).
- Small API/security tweaks: customer list now forces `customerId` to authenticated user unless the caller has management roles, and join flow enforces visibility checks and capacity checks.
- Added/updated unit tests covering customer isolation, internal-queue rejection, duplicate-token retry, concurrent processing conflict, and public-directory filtering; and added audit docs `docs/PROJECT_HEALTH_CHECK.md` and `docs/FINAL_PROJECT_AUDIT.md` describing the audit, fixes, and remaining gaps.

### Testing
- Backend unit tests and integrations were executed with `cd backend && npm test` and passed (`11 suites, 43 tests`), and `cd backend && npm run lint` and `cd backend && npm run docs` also passed.
- Frontend tests were executed with `cd frontend && npm test` and passed (12 files, 20 tests), and `cd frontend && npm run lint` and `cd frontend && npm run build` completed successfully (Vite build emitted a non-blocking chunk-size warning).
- Docker/compose startup and browser end-to-end verification were not executed because the environment did not provide a Docker daemon or browser automation, so those steps are marked not-testable in the audit documentation.

author: jsboige
blooop
body:
Closes #477.

## The lie

A bare clone remembers the default branch it was cloned with, in its `HEAD`
symref, and nothing repoints it afterwards. `dl` has never written a bare's
`HEAD` (no `set-head`, no `remote show` anywhere in the tree), and #477 decided
it should not start: repointing at fetch time is a state mutation standing in
for a reader that is not total, it costs a remote round trip, and it is wrong
between fetches anyway.

So a repository that renames `master` to `main` leaves the cache pointing at
`refs/heads/master` long after the prune that deleted the ref, and
`git symbolic-ref HEAD` keeps answering `master`, exit 0, forever. A symbolic
ref is a name, not a branch, and `symbolic-ref` does not check its target.

`default_branch_of` read that first answer and returned it, so every later
probe that could have answered correctly sat unreachable behind it.

## The fix

The two symref probes now check that the name is a ref the clone really has
(`show-ref --verify` on the full ref, prefix and all, since `refs/heads/main`
and `refs/remotes/origin/main` are different refs), and a name that is not one
is treated exactly as a refusal is: ask the next probe, then `branch -r`, then
the caller's `main`.

The seam is the flow layer, `RepositoryManager::default_branch_of`, and
deliberately not the git client. `clients/git` states that a verb never falls
back to another verb and decides nothing about sequence, and there is no single
git command that both dereferences a symref and verifies its target
(`symbolic-ref` does the first, `show-ref --verify` the second;
`rev-parse --verify --symbolic-full-name` would do both but answers `HEAD` for
a detached HEAD, which is a new wrong name in place of the old one). Since
`default_branch_of` is the only reader of `Git::symbolic_ref` in the tree and
the only place a default branch is read off a clone, making it total leaves no
caller able to obtain a name that was read off a ref that is not there.

Cost: one extra local `show-ref` per clone or adopt. It reads refs off the disk
next to a `git clone`, and the cold-launch sequence test records it.

## Where it was measured

`register_existing_bare` (the adopt path). It rebuilds a record by reading the
clone, so a user who deletes `metadata.json` had the dead branch written
straight back. `real_git_does_not_re_record_a_default_branch_the_remote_has_deleted`
builds that state the way it actually arrives: clone the cache while the default
is `master`, rename the remote's default to `main`, delete `master` upstream,
prune-fetch. Before this change the rebuilt record said `master`, a ref the
clone has not got; after it, `main`, which the clone has.

## Not in scope

The recorded `default_branch` is written once and never revalidated, so a moved
default goes unnoticed until something fails on it. That is #507, with its own
trace, and nothing here changes it.

## Tests

- `a_symbolic_ref_whose_branch_is_gone_is_not_an_answer` (fake git: HEAD names a
  dead ref, the answer comes from `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`; the argv list
  pins which ref is checked)
- `both_symbolic_refs_being_gone_falls_through_to_the_listing`
- `real_git_does_not_re_record_a_default_branch_the_remote_has_deleted`
- `the_default_branch_is_read_from_head_then_the_remote_head_then_the_listing`
  and `a_cold_launch_issues_exactly_this_sequence` updated for the added probe

`cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
and `cargo fmt --check` are green. No public API change, so no snapshot moved.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary by Sourcery

Ensure default-branch discovery ignores dangling symbolic refs so caches do not preserve deleted branch names.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent deleted upstream default branches from being recorded as valid defaults in bare-clone and repository-adoption flows.
- Fall back to remote symbolic refs, branch listings, or the configured default when a symbolic ref points to a missing local ref.

Enhancements:
- Validate symbolic-ref targets before using them to determine a repository’s default branch.

Documentation:
- Document the handling of dangling symbolic refs and the distinction from later revalidation of recorded defaults.

Tests:
- Add fake-Git and real-Git coverage for dangling symbolic refs, fallback ordering, adoption, and the updated cold-launch command sequence.

author: ether-lucky
body:
Closes #99

## The problem

Lighthouse ran **once** per CI execution and asserted against that single sample. Three consecutive runs, on code that was identical or strictly improved between them:

| Run | Context | Performance |
|---|---|---|
| `33261148335` | prod baseline | 0.78 |
| `33262534313` | PERF-02 mid-fix | 0.83 |
| `33263582237` | PERF-02 final | **0.74** |

A **±0.09 swing** — wider than many real regressions would be.

This blocked two things:

- **#94 could not be given a verdict.** The structural fixes were verified from the rendered markup, but the score movement was indistinguishable from noise.
- **#95 cannot be finished.** Promoting performance to `error` while the metric swings ±0.09 would produce builds that fail at random — worse than not enforcing it.

## The change

```json
"collect": { "numberOfRuns": 3 },
"assert": {
  "assertions": {
    "categories:performance": ["warn", { "minScore": 0.9, "aggregationMethod": "median" }],
    …
  }
}
```

`aggregationMethod` is stated **explicitly on every assertion** rather than relying on a default, so a reader can see which sample is being judged without consulting the LHCI docs.

## Tradeoff

The lighthouse job takes roughly **3× longer** — about a minute becomes about three. Recorded in `docs/quality-gates.md`. Worth paying for a number anyone can act on.

## Verification

JSON validated and the parsed config confirmed. The real proof is comparative and arrives with this PR's own CI run: the lighthouse job should report **3 runs** and a median score. If you want stronger evidence, re-run it on the unchanged commit — the median should barely move, where the single-sample score previously moved by up to 0.09.

## What this unblocks

Once a stable median exists, **#94** can be judged properly, and performance can be promoted to `error` to finish **#95** and meet the Sprint 2 Definition of Done.

author: duyicoda
body:
## Overview

This PR makes notification preference and delivery-worker state transitions deterministic, atomic, and recoverable across retries, refreshes, and interrupted wallet operations. It establishes the feature's explicit state machine — success, rejection, cancellation, and retry paths — and enforces idempotency, authorization, and state-conditional updates so duplicate submissions and stale responses cannot create contradictory client state. Worker failure recovery preserves user intent without silently repeating an on-chain action.

## Related Issue

Refs #568

## Changes

### 📨 Notification State Machine and Recovery

* **[ADD]** Explicit state machine and invariants for all notification lifecycle paths (pending, delivered, read, rejected, cancelled, retry) across `src/app/api/notifications` and `src/jobs/notifications.worker.ts`.

* **[MODIFY]** `app/api/notifications/route.ts`
  * Enforces idempotency keys on preference creation/update; duplicate submissions return deterministic responses and do not enqueue duplicate delivery jobs.
  * Validates owner authorization before persisting preferences.

* **[MODIFY]** `app/api/notifications/[id]/route.ts`
  * Read/unread and delivery-state transitions are conditional on the current persisted state.
  * Stale responses (e.g., out-of-order read receipts) return `409 Conflict` and do not overwrite newer state.

* **[MODIFY]** `app/api/notifications/read-all/route.ts`
  * Transactionally marks all notifications as read for the authenticated user only; partial failure rolls back to the previous consistent state.

* **[MODIFY]** `src/jobs/notifications.worker.ts`
  * Records user intent as an action token before delivery; on retry, resumes if unconfirmed and skips if the on-chain action was already confirmed.
  * Uses transactional dequeue with exponential backoff to prevent duplicate deliveries after worker interruption.

* **[ADD]** `app/api/notifications/route.test.ts`
  * Covers success, failure, boundary, retry, duplicate-submission, stale-response, and permission behavior.

### ⚖️ Design Tradeoffs and Remaining Limitations

* Idempotency keys use a bounded TTL; resubmission after TTL expiry is allowed to keep storage bounded, at the cost of long-horizon deduplication.
* Worker recovery depends on the chain provider's confirmation status; when the provider is unavailable, the worker retries with backoff and retains user intent.
* Read-state convergence across devices is eventual-consistency based on the last fetched cursor; cross-device read-state sync is out of scope.

## Verification Results

```
npm test -- app/api/notifications/route.test.ts
✅ 24/24 passed

Live acceptance check:
✅ duplicate submissions return idempotent success without duplicate delivery
✅ stale read-state updates rejected with 409 Conflict
✅ unauthorized read-all denied
✅ retry path preserves user intent and skips confirmed on-chain deliveries
```

| Acceptance Criteria | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Implementation defines and enforces relevant invariants for normal and adversarial inputs | ✅ Idempotency keys, ownership checks, and state-conditional transitions tested |
| State machine defined for success, rejection, cancellation, and retry paths | ✅ Explicit lifecycle implemented and covered by tests |
| Duplicate submissions and stale responses cannot create contradictory client state | ✅ Idempotent responses + `409 Conflict` on stale updates |
| Failure recovery preserves user intent without silently repeating an on-chain action | ✅ Action-token recovery skips confirmed deliveries |
| Automated tests cover success, failure, boundary, retry, and permission behavior | ✅ 24 tests covering all required paths |
| PR includes validation commands, design tradeoffs, and remaining limitations | ✅ See verification and tradeoffs sections |
| PR references this issue with `Refs #<issue-number>` | ✅ Refs #568 |

Closes #1368

author: kean
body: `willCache` was the last completion-handler method left in `ImagePipeline.Delegate`, and it handed an escaping, non-`@Sendable` closure out of a protocol that refines `Sendable` — so implementations had no safe way to resume it off the pipeline actor, unlike its sibling `willLoadData`, which is already `@ImagePipelineActor ... async`. It now returns the data to store instead: `func willCache(data:image:for:pipeline:) async -> Data?`, returning `nil` to prevent caching. The two pipeline call sites await it inline, so the store still happens before the value is delivered. This is source-breaking for anyone implementing the delegate — replace the `completion(x)` call with `return x`.

That constraint is the whole reason for the placement: globals.css sets scroll-margin-top on section[id], and a transform above one offsets its hash landing by the lift distance, which is the bug that once left /#demo short by exactly 6px. Measured after this change, all five live ids land at the 88px offset with zero transformed ancestors: demo 88.11, schools 87.77, worksheets 87.86, faq 88.22, waitlist 87.64.

Three sections carry a placement note rather than a plain wrap:

  WorksheetGenerator wraps div.um-worksheet, an ANCESTOR of WorksheetStack. The
  two back sheets hold static translate+rotate values and are positioned against
  a relative div inside the stack, so an ancestor transform composes and moves
  the packet as one. Reveal on the sheets would have overwritten the rotations.

  EducatorVoices wraps the heading and the overflow box, and deliberately stops
  above div.um-quote-track. That node is where the carousel writes an inline
  translateX once lib/quotes.ts reaches CAROUSEL_MIN_QUOTES, and an inline
  transform outranks anything a wrapper sets, so the two would fight the moment
  a fifth quote lands.

  WaitlistBand wraps div.um-waitlist, above the submitted ? success : form
  ternary, so swapping the panel on submit cannot re-enter or re-hide it. The
  submit path is untouched: no change to handleSubmit, ENDPOINT, the fetch, or
  the ready/loading/submitted state.

LiveDemo, SchoolsBand and TeacherDashboard are left alone; they already animate. Verified still working: both kept Reveal rows settle to opacity 1, and the five dashboard bars grow back to their exact target widths (93.59 73.19 57.59 39.59 26.39 px = 78/61/48/33/22% of 120px).

Layout safety: div.um-shell is a plain block in all five sections (none pass a style prop to SectionShell), so Reveal's wrapper is a transparent pass-through and every section is the plain-wrap case. Confirmed after the change that .um-statband is still a 4-column grid, .um-worksheet 530px+400px, .um-waitlist 410px+520px and .um-quote-track still flex, each at the full 1000px content width. No child selector in the repo targets .um-shell > *, so nothing keys on the child position a wrapper would shift.

StatBand lives in ui.tsx, whose docblock claimed none of its primitives force a client boundary. That is now half untrue, so the docblock says so: StatBand stays server-rendered and only the Reveal wrapper crosses, and StatBand is used on the homepage alone.

Reduced motion: Reveal bails on matchMedia before writing any hidden state, so all five stay visible and static. Asserted after scrolling the full page with prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, every one at opacity 1, transform none.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Two things so the app can be tested on a phone and stops forgetting everything: Expo SDK 54 (Expo Go's current SDK), and every screen now reads and writes through the Next.js API instead of `src/session.ts`'s in-memory object.

**No login.** First launch asks for a username only. `POST /api/auth/session` (already existed) upserts the player and returns the signed value the browser gets in its cookie; the app keeps it in `expo-secure-store` and sends `Authorization: Bearer <playerId>.<hmac>` on every request. There is no password, so a username is a handle, not an account — anyone typing it becomes that player. Noted in the mobile README.

State flow, all through one provider (`src/player.tsx`, `usePlayer()`), so screens never fetch directly:

```
username           -> claim(name)         -> POST /api/auth/session  -> token in SecureStore
coach pick         -> chooseCoach(id)     -> PATCH /api/players/me   { coachVoiceId }
baseline (1st run) -> patch(...)          -> PATCH /api/players/me   { goalKind, targetPaceSPerKm, onboardingCompleted }
run Finish         -> finishRun(run)      -> POST /api/runs          -> { run, runCount, totalPoints, personalBest }
launch / home      -> refresh()           -> GET /api/players/me + GET /api/runs
```

Live GPS stays in memory during the run; a run is written once, on Finish (a zero-distance false start is dropped, and a failed save keeps you on the run screen rather than silently losing it). Home's personal best and the summary's totals are the server's, not hard-coded.

Schema (`20260829170000_coach_choice_and_run_details.sql`, applied to the project): `players.coach_voice_id`, `runs.coach_voice_id`, `runs.baseline`, and

```sql
avg_pace_s_per_km integer generated always as
  (round(duration_s::numeric * 1000 / distance_m)::integer) stored
```

so a client cannot report a pace its own distance and duration disagree with, and personal best (`getPersonalBest`, runs ≥ 400 m) is one indexed query. Coach ids stay `text` rather than an enum — adding a voice is a code change, not a migration — and the services narrow them with `isCoachId`, so a voice deleted from `shared/voices.ts` reads as no coach instead of an invalid one.

While verifying: the `20260829150000_onboarding_goals_and_voices` migration had never been applied to the Supabase project, so `/api/auth/session` was 500ing on `column players.goal_kind does not exist`. Applied. Also `vitest.config.ts` was missing the `@shared` alias, which broke `npm test` as soon as a tested module imported from `shared/`.

SDK 54 notes: `expo-audio` 1.1.1 has no `preload`, so `src/voice.ts` caches clips with `expo-file-system`'s `File.downloadFileAsync` into `Paths.cache` and falls back to the remote URL when a clip is missing.

## Testing

- `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm test` (10 passed), `cd mobile && npm run typecheck`, `npx expo-doctor` (17/17).
- Against the real project, with a throwaway username (rows deleted after): claim → patch coach/pace → `POST /api/runs` (2400 m / 800 s ⇒ server-derived `avgPaceSPerKm: 333`, 24 points, personal best set) → `GET /api/runs`. Invalid run body 422; missing and malformed bearer 401.
- Not tested on a phone yet.

Automated SRE Agent Fix for inc-2026-002 by model `gpt-5-6-luna` variation `enforce/allow_all` (`enforce-allow-all`)

Diagnosis:
### Diagnosis

`parse_float_setting` attempts to execute:

```python
float(raw_input_str)
```

with the value `'not-a-number'`, causing the `ValueError`. The failure is an invalid input/casting issue, not a floating-point runtime defect.

### Candidate source files

- **Primary:** `src/incident_package/utils/data_parser.py`
  - `parse_float_setting` at line 10 performs an unchecked `float()` conversion.
  - `run` at line 14 passes the unparsed value into the converter.

- **Secondary candidates:** The configuration, request, or environment-input code that supplies `unparsed_setting` to `run`; this producer is not included in the supplied trace.

### Root-cause hypotheses

1. A configuration or external input contains the literal placeholder/invalid value `'not-a-number'`.
2. Input validation or schema enforcement is missing before conversion.
3. A default/error-path value was serialized as text and propagated instead of being rejected or replaced with a valid numeric value.
4. The parser lacks explicit handling for invalid values, such as a clear validation error, fallback default, or nullable result.

Recommended investigation: trace the origin of `unparsed_setting` for scenario `inc-2026-002`, then add validation and intentional handling for malformed numeric settings.

author: kamoras
body:
## Summary
Follow-up from investigating the "check back later" full-story generation issue directly via SSH on production. Found the real root cause in llama-server's own journald logs: a llama.cpp server-side bug in its prompt-cache/continuous-batching KV-cache-checkpoint-restoration path (\`decode: failed to initialize batch\` / \`llama_decode: failed to decode, ret = -1\` / \`send_error: Invalid input batch\` → HTTP 500), reliably triggered by a grounding retry (same base prompt + a short correction — the highest-similarity case that caching exists to speed up). This is a llama.cpp bug, not a Civitas application bug, and fixing it is a live production infrastructure decision (periodic restart, given the service's own documented "restart reclaimed ~10GB after ~4 days uptime" precedent, and/or an upstream version bump) — left to the user, not touched here.

**What this PR actually fixes**: finding that root cause took direct SSH access and manual journalctl digging, because \`ollama_client.py\`'s own error handling discarded the one piece of information that would have shown it immediately. Logging \`e\` on an \`HTTPError\` only prints the generic reason phrase ("HTTP Error 500: Internal Server Error") — never the actual response body llama-server sent (\`{"error": "Invalid input batch."}\`). Every prior sighting of this in the application logs was completely undiagnosable without bypassing the app entirely. Now logged (bounded read, with a fallback for the rare case reading it also fails).

## Test plan
- [x] New test proving the response body now appears in the warning log (fails on pre-fix code, passes on the fix — verified both ways)
- [x] New test proving a broken/unreadable body falls back cleanly without crashing
- [x] Full backend suite: 2444 passed, 0 failed

author: jcsvwinston
body:
**QCD-FW-22** — severidad ALTA, pérdida de datos.

## El defecto

El interruptor de apagado del limpiador no apagaba nada. `Cleaner` no guardaba el flag en ningún sitio: las dos ramas del `if !cfg.Enabled` de `NewCleaner` devolvían Cleaners **byte a byte idénticos**, así que la bifurcación no decidía nada. `Start()` sólo miraba el intervalo —que cae a 1h cuando no parsea, o sea nunca ≤ 0— y `run()` barre una vez **de inmediato**, antes del primer tick.

Con `storage.cleanup.enabled: false` explícito:

```
antes:   _tmp/borrable.txt=true   importante.txt=true
después: _tmp/borrable.txt=false  importante.txt=true
```

El objeto bajo el prefijo desaparece en cada arranque. El de fuera, de la misma antigüedad, sobrevive — eso aísla la causa al barrido de prefijo y descarta el store y el montaje. Silencioso además: nada registraba que el limpiador hubiera arrancado contra un `false` explícito.

## El fix

El flag vive en el `Cleaner` y lo comprueba `Start()`, que es la puerta que usa `app.New` (`cleaner.Start()`, incondicional). Se sigue construyendo un Cleaner deshabilitado a propósito: `app.New` quiere un handle no-nil al que llamar `Stop` en el apagado. Lo que no debe pasar es que corra.

## Los tests, que es donde estaba la lección

El test que existía construía con `Enabled: false` y llamaba a `runCleanup()` **directo**, saltándose `Start()`, y afirmaba que el objeto se borraba: codificaba el defecto como comportamiento esperado. Es el mismo patrón que el informe señala en FW-21 y FW-26 — el test pasa porque entra por una puerta que no es la que usa el framework.

El guard nuevo entra por la puerta real (`Start`), y trae dos controles para que no pueda pasar en falso: uno positivo (`Enabled: true` sí borra, o el test pasaría sobre un limpiador que simplemente no funciona) y un objeto de la misma edad fuera del prefijo. Al viejo se le pone `Enabled: true`, que es lo que de verdad estaba ejerciendo.

**Rojo demostrado antes del fix:**

```
Exists(_tmp/borrable.txt) = false, want true
--- FAIL: TestCleanerStart_DisabledDeletesNothing (0.20s)
```

Suite completa de nucleus en verde con el fix.

Criterio de aceptación externo nº 2: *`enabled: false` deja intacto un objeto viejo bajo el prefijo de limpieza.*

body:
## Contexto

Revisão sênior ampla da `main` após a sequência recente de implementações, com foco em bugs de comportamento, segurança, integridade de dados, lifecycle assíncrono e regressões silenciosas.

## Achados corrigidos

### 1. Static dashboard — URI malformada virava erro interno
- `decodeURIComponent()` era executado sem proteção no not-found handler.
- URLs com percent-encoding inválido podiam escapar como `URIError`/500.
- Agora respondem `400` com contrato estável `INVALID_PATH`.
- Adicionada regressão para GET e HEAD.

### 2. PTY — truncamento podia corromper UTF-8
- O buffer destacável era truncado por bytes e podia iniciar no meio de um code point.
- Isso podia introduzir `�` nos logs exatamente no limite configurado.
- O truncamento agora preserva code points UTF-8 completos sem ultrapassar o teto em bytes.
- Adicionada regressão com caractere multibyte.

### 3. Stream SSE de logs — loading podia ficar preso
- Fechar/pausar o stream ou perder o processo gerenciado antes do primeiro evento podia deixar `loadingLogs=true`.
- O lifecycle agora associa callbacks ao stream atual, encerra loading nas saídas normais e continua expondo falhas reais.
- Adicionados testes para pausa, indisponibilidade e erro real do stream.

### 4. Database Explorer — mudança de contexto durante leitura
- Conexão, banco e tabela ainda podiam ser alterados enquanto uma operação do Explorer estava em voo.
- Uma resposta antiga poderia então ser aplicada sobre um contexto novo.
- Os controles que alteram o contexto agora ficam bloqueados enquanto `explorerLoading` estiver ativo, seguindo o mesmo contrato já usado pelo botão de execução.
- Adicionado teste assíncrono que mantém a consulta pendente e verifica o bloqueio dos controles.

## Self-review

- Descartado falso positivo no painel Git: `ProjectGitPanel` é remontado por `:key="git-${project.id}"`, portanto não havia race persistente entre projetos.
- Confirmado que `followEventStream()` já absorve `AbortError` de fechamento intencional; a correção ficou focada no estado de loading, sem mascarar erro real.

author: ztjiang0123
body:
## Summary

Resolves all 5 Code Analyzer `dead_code` signals in `thefuck/entrypoints/not_configured.py`. Each signal is a ruff **RUF100: Unused `noqa` directive (non-enabled: `E402`)** on the module-level import lines.

Fix run: `cifr_6e2b737bb5df895d6efafd68`
Analyzed commit: `a7d1d2acd0b527c5e3fe416c02b7c883424cbcb6`

## Root cause

`not_configured.py` calls `init_output()` at module level *before* importing the modules that use colorama. That ordering triggers flake8's **E402** (module-level import not at top of file), so every import carried a `# noqa: E402` directive.

The analyzer runs ruff, where **E402 is not an enabled rule**. Ruff therefore reports each of those directives as an unused `noqa` (RUF100) — dead code that suppresses nothing under its configuration.

## Fix (dead_code playbook)

- Removed the redundant per-import `# noqa: E402` directives from `not_configured.py`. There is no dynamic/reflective use — a `noqa` comment is inert data with no runtime effect, so removal is safe.
- Added `E402` to the flake8 `ignore` list in `tox.ini` so the project's flake8 workflow stays clean for this intentional init-before-import module. `not_configured.py` is the only file in the repo that triggers E402, so this ignore is narrowly scoped in practice.

Import ordering and all runtime behavior are unchanged.

## Violation-by-violation summary

| # | Violation ID | Location | Rule | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `civ1_Uv5MWmVY8CDN49aACOWcGPQ3mWvc-cNZujvRjIRAE5g` | `not_configured.py:6` (`import getpass`) | dead_code | Removed unused `# noqa: E402` |
| 2 | `civ1_ebL5297wtj5uOzJd_xzWMuZhHTlKPSL7NdlSOhM7sjE` | `not_configured.py:7` (`import os`) | dead_code | Removed unused `# noqa: E402` |
| 3 | `civ1_XEJJM65fT6wPrF5c_K5aWtINBgfPqGlwQu_oz8aApMA` | `not_configured.py:8` (`import json`) | dead_code | Removed unused `# noqa: E402` |
| 4 | `civ1_t-38bxTJ7u5szCar2Hb0wwVVr_isM7gfbpGFhXfznQc` | `not_configured.py:9` (`from tempfile import gettempdir`) | dead_code | Removed unused `# noqa: E402` |
| 5 | `civ1_oalhziif_o3mW-IctQ0_QYFwr9va-mP7PE783sD5jVg` | `not_configured.py:10` (`import time`) | dead_code | Removed unused `# noqa: E402` |

Lines 11–16 carried the same unused directive for the same reason; they were removed together to fully resolve the flagged structure and avoid re-triggering RUF100.

## Verification

- `ruff check --select RUF100 thefuck/entrypoints/not_configured.py` → **All checks passed!** (was 11 errors)
- `flake8 thefuck/ tests/` → **exit 0** (no E402 regression)
- `pytest tests/entrypoints/test_not_configured.py` → **7 passed**
- `pytest tests/entrypoints/` → **20 passed**
- Module imports cleanly: `import thefuck.entrypoints.not_configured` OK

author: mtgibbs
body:
Follow-on to #209. That PR moved the image-automation resources back into `flux-system`, which let them fail *honestly* — and revealed a second, unrelated bug in the same original manifest.

## `ghcr-credentials` is not a thing

```
$ grep -rn "name: ghcr-credentials" clusters/ | grep -v image-automation
(nothing)
```

The only place that string appears is the **filename** `clusters/pi-k3s/flux-system/ghcr-credentials.yaml` — and the ExternalSecret inside it targets `ghcr-pull-secret`. A filename is not an object name.

## Why it actually breaks

`ghcr.io/mtgibbs/harness-coordinator` is a **private** package (`{"visibility":"private"}`), so the scan genuinely needs credentials. With a dangling ref the ImageRepository can never authenticate, and `Kustomization/harness` sets `wait: true`:

```
health check failed after 5m0.034695486s: timeout waiting for:
[ImagePolicy/flux-system/harness-coordinator status: 'InProgress',
 ImageRepository/flux-system/harness-coordinator status: 'InProgress']
```

A 5-minute timeout on every reconcile, forever.

## The positive control

`private-exit-node` isn't cited here as a style precedent — it's proof the fix works:

- it is the only *other* private image with automation
- it uses `ghcr-pull-secret`
- its Kustomization also sets `wait: true`
- **it is Ready**

So that secret is already demonstrated to authenticate a private-GHCR scan in this cluster. This isn't "a name that exists" — it's the name known to work.

`scripts/check-generated-docs.sh` passes.

- `GITHUB_TOKEN` genuinely cannot enable a Pages site for the first time on its own — there is no token permission that grants that. Updated the README to make the one-time manual step explicit and required: **Settings > Pages > Build and deployment > Source > GitHub Actions**.

author: prajeeth-12
body:
## Why

Fixes #7580

Export-only tasks (where the agent writes a Markdown or other artifact instead of modifying the prototype HTML) are rejected by `validateRunDeliverable()` because it unconditionally selects `projectMetadata.entryFile` as the deliverable entry. When the prototype entry file is intentionally untouched, the touched-path check falls into `entry_not_touched` even though a valid, complete manifest-backed export artifact exists.

## What users will see

Export-only runs that produce a valid artifact with a complete `.artifact.json` manifest will no longer be rejected during run finalization. The user will see their export artifact accepted as the deliverable instead of a generic "incomplete" error.

## What changed

In `validateRunDeliverable()` (`apps/daemon/src/run-deliverable-validation.ts`), when the declared entry was not touched, the function now looks for a touched file that has:
- A complete artifact manifest (`status: 'complete'`)
- An explicit (non-inferred) manifest — excludes legacy inferred manifests that every `.html`/`.md` file receives
- A manifest `entry` field matching the file's own path

If such a candidate is found, it is promoted as the deliverable entry with the same readability and type-kind checks the original path applies. If no candidate exists, the existing `entry_not_touched` rejection is preserved.

### Surface area
- [x] Daemon (`apps/daemon/src/run-deliverable-validation.ts`)
- [x] Tests (`apps/daemon/tests/run-deliverable-validation.test.ts`)

## Test plan
- [x] Export-only task with valid explicit artifact manifest selects manifest entry as deliverable (new test)
- [x] Regular prototype task where entry is touched still uses `projectMetadata.entryFile` — no regression (new test)
- [x] Touched file without an explicit manifest (only inferred) is not promoted (verified by existing `entry_not_touched` test continuing to pass)
- [x] Export artifact with `status: 'streaming'` is not promoted (new test)
- [x] All 12 tests in `run-deliverable-validation.test.ts` pass (8 existing + 4 new)

author: aforno
body:
## Summary

Preference names were string literals in AppDelegate, Settings, notifications, Sparkle, the notch panel, and a handful of views. A typo would silently miss the registered default. This PR puts the UserDefaults names and launch defaults in `AppPreferences` and switches every call site, including `@AppStorage`, to `AppPreferences.Key`.

The stored key strings are unchanged. Existing settings keep working.

While touching the reply path, unused `AgentReply.content` and `isDeny` come out. Claude elicitation mapping now matches what the notch UI actually sends: cancel stays cancel, every other decision is decline. The old `accept` + `content` branch was only reachable from reply.sock clients that attached `content`, and the tests now assert that path is gone.

## Verification

- [ ] `swift test`
- [ ] `swift test -c release`
- [ ] `./script/package_release.sh --adhoc`
- [ ] `./script/check_repository.sh`
- [ ] Packaged-app UI/runtime smoke test, when applicable

## Compatibility and risk

No UserDefaults migration. Key names and registered defaults match the previous AppDelegate table, so persistence is stable.

Provider-hook change: Claude `Elicitation` hook output no longer emits `action: accept` or a `content` object. Allow, deny, and option all map to `decline`. Cancel is unchanged. reply.sock clients that relied on accept-with-content will now decline instead.

No signing or Sparkle protocol changes beyond reading the same automatic-update key through `AppPreferences`.

Not applicable.

author: marguelgtz
body:
## Goal

Do not discard a paid Vast session just because the provider takes longer than the first SSH readiness window.

## Scope

- make `INSTANCE_CREATED` and `SSH_READY` recoverable checkpoints
- preserve the paid instance and keep the original watchdog/deadline active on provider-startup failures
- extend the initial Vast SSH provisioning window from 6 to 12 minutes
- give `stint resume` the same 12-minute provider-startup window
- update recovery tests

## Why

Observed Vast runs can finish pulling/preparing the base image but remain in `created`/provisioning long enough to exceed the previous six-minute wait. The old behavior destroyed the instance and cleared state, which made `stint resume` impossible. With this layer, the same failure becomes `RECOVERABLE` and `stint resume` continues the existing instance.

## Stack

Depends on PR #6. One squashed implementation commit.

author: nguyenhoa2024
body:
Nút tên là "Backup + Reset" nhưng `backupThenReset` lấy tập app cần xoá từ danh sách **Reset**, không phải từ danh sách **Backup**:

```swift
for item in resetItems { ... toReset.append(item) }
guard !toReset.isEmpty else {
    progress("Khong reset app nao"); return    // ← chỉ một dòng log
}
```

Tích app ở danh sách **Backup** rồi bấm nút đó → backup xong và **không xoá gì hết**. Bản cũ chỉ ghi đúng một dòng `Khong reset app nao` giữa dòng log đang chạy, quá dễ trôi qua — và đó chính là triệu chứng "Backup + Reset không xoá sạch được data app đã tích chọn".

Thiết kế hai danh sách độc lập là cố ý (từ v1.1: backup tập này, xoá tập kia), nên tôi **không đổi ngầm ngữ nghĩa của nút** — xoá là không hoàn tác được, phải do người dùng quyết. Thay vào đó sửa ở chỗ dễ nhầm:

- **Tập Reset trống mà bấm "Backup + Reset" thì hỏi thẳng**, ba lựa chọn: *Huỷ* / *Chỉ backup* / *Backup + Reset* (xoá luôn chính những app vừa backup).
- **Dòng đếm cạnh "Chọn app Reset"** ghi `0 app · khong xoa gi` khi trống, thay vì chỉ số `0`.
- **Khi thật sự không xoá app nào, nói rõ lý do**: danh sách Reset trống, hay mọi app đều backup thất bại (trường hợp thứ hai xảy ra khi hết dung lượng hoặc app rỗng — cũng im lặng y như vậy ở bản cũ).
- **Chạy xong báo `Da reset N/M app`** thay vì chỉ `xong ✓`, và log ghi tên các app sẽ bị reset trước khi chạy.

## Kiểm chứng

Đây là lỗi luồng đọc thẳng từ code, không phải suy đoán: `backupResetTapped` truyền `resetItems()` vào `resetItems:`, và `backupThenReset` chỉ lặp trên tham số đó.

Vẫn chưa test trên thiết bị. Nếu người dùng **có** tích cả hai danh sách mà data vẫn còn thì nguyên nhân nằm ở chỗ khác — phần container của v1.9 — và log v1.9 (`Tổng container data: N` + danh sách `cây/id → UUID`) sẽ chỉ ra.

author: mecca-research
body:
# v0.46 — every predator hunts, every predator sleeps, and the chase is the show

This release answers the v0.45 feedback directly: the big prey were too large to read as game, the cougar was stuck and absent from his own rock, and the major carnivores showed no hunting or sleeping at watching timescale.

## The chase (all hunts)
- Every hunt's outcome is rolled the moment the dash begins, at the owner's **50/50** (one `catchChance` dial per hunt, all set to 0.50).
- The roll is *played back* as choreography: a winning predator ramps up **+22%** over the chase while the prey visibly tires to 82% pace; a losing predator fades to **62%** speed past the halfway mark while the prey finds adrenaline at 118% and pulls away.
- Hunt cadences retuned so chases initiate at watching timescale: fox mousing every 9–16s, owl swoop 10–18s, cougar ambush 14–24s, wolf rush 14–24s.
- Measured over a 10-minute soak: cougar 3 strikes, wolf 6 attempts/3 kills, fox 8 strikes/4 kills, owl 10 strikes/4 kills, skunk, raccoon and hedgehog all engaging — pooled kill rate ≈ 50%.

## The cougar's domain
- **62% of his waking time on the rock** (asked: at least 33%): the vantage bag is weighted to ridge and cliff ledges, and the prowl chains up to two extra vantage legs.
- The repeatable mid-rock stall is **gone**: the wall-ahead hop probe no longer fires inside arrival range (156 hops/run of churn down to 5 clean hops; zero bounce events in the domain probe).
- The den errand is one continuous journey to the cave mouth instead of two hopeful halves — he now reaches the cave and sleeps in it (2 den sleeps per watched run).
- His stalk carries the rock's own ladder (`canHop`), so a goat one terrace up is a hunt; a two-face climb is still refused.

## The fox's curl-up (new, was entirely missing)
- A full sleep sequence: he turns on the spot (2–3 turns, flipping direction), noses under his tail into a breathing curl, and wakes with a one-shot rise, blink and brush-off. Bed spots reject the lake, the rock and tree crowns.

## The buried grubs
- Grubs, beetles and earthworms now live **under the wood, invisible**, until a skunk or hedgehog digs them out — the unearthing happens at the digger's paws after seconds of visible digging.
- The coin then falls at 50/50: eaten in a clear feed pose, or **released** — the grub visibly runs for the timber and goes back under.
- Hedgehog feeding restored: grub appetite every 12–20s, 36.5% of his clock foraging in the soak.

## Half-size game
- Wild boar and mountain goat draw at **half their bulk index** (a declared `draw: 0.5` in the species table, locked by the size suite) — visibly under the wolf and cougar that hunt them.

## Verification (all against the live build)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| world | **255 pass** |
| forage | 37 pass |
| ethogram | 17 pass |
| sizes | 20 pass |
| gait | 15 pass |
| cadence | 13 pass |
| publish check | pass — served bundle is the source |

10-minute unmuzzled soak: all seven predators hunt **and** sleep (cougar den, wolf bed, fox curl-up, raccoon roost, owl roost, skunk den, hedgehog curl), frog 18 tongue strikes / 18 catches / 0 dry, **one** stall world-wide in ten minutes, 14 kills.

Test hardening in this round: the wind check is now deterministic (bearings placed dead down/upwind via a world-clock hook instead of sixteen statistical compass points), the coin fixtures stop force-feeding the appetite mid-escape, the goat trial pairs its talus stand inside the floor cougar's 210px gate, and the turtle's backing bout no longer counts the next intent's turn against it.

body:
## 📌 Summary of Changes
This pull request adds a **QR Code / Barcode Scanner** to the Public **Track Document** page (`/track-document`). Users and employees can now scan document QR codes directly using their device camera (rear/environment camera on mobile or webcam on desktop) or by uploading an image file (e.g., screenshot or photo of a QR code), eliminating the need to manually type long scrambled alphanumeric tracking codes.

---

## 🚀 Key Features & Implementation Details

1. **Clean Search Form Integration:**
   - Added a **"Scan QR"** action button alongside the "Track" button in the search form.
   - Preserves a clean, responsive layout without unnecessary icon clutter.

2. **Public QR Scanner Modal:**
   - **Live Camera Scanning:** 
     - 1:1 square viewfinder with real-time QR detection powered by `html5-qrcode`.
     - Automatically targets the rear/environment camera on smartphones with front-facing/webcam fallback.
     - Includes a **Switch Camera** button when multiple cameras are detected.
   - **Image File Upload:**
     - Includes a drag-and-drop zone and file picker to scan QR codes from image files (`.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.webp`, `.bmp`).

3. **Full Compliance with Document Tracking Logic:**
   - Scanning does **not** bypass any security or validation rules.
   - Once decoded, the tracking number automatically populates the input field and triggers the multi-phase tracking pipeline:
     - **Phase 1:** Input extraction and Livewire synchronization.
     - **Phase 1.2 & 1.3:** `localStorage` device tracking and 3-attempt / 50-minute anti-brute force rate limiting.
     - **Phase 1.4:** Verification email domain checks (`@cspc.edu.ph`).
     - **Phase 2:** Server-side rate limiting, Base64 decoding, database validation, and `tracking_devices_log` auditing.
     - **Phase 3:** Redirection to `/tracked?number=...` for authorized email access.

4. **Responsive Styling:**
   - Added mobile-first styles in `td.css` ensuring seamless presentation across mobile phones, tablets, and desktop displays.

---

author: liuchao-001
body:
## What

This app had **no Tailwind compiler**. It imported Kumo's prebuilt stylesheet, which contains only the utilities Kumo's own components needed, so every class written in this repository outside that set did nothing — silently, with no build warning and no failing test.

`w-[18rem]` and `size-7` in `onboarding/view.tsx` are two that were **already dead on `main`**: the onboarding step cards have no width constraint and their number badges no size.

Theme and utilities only, never preflight — Kumo's bundle already carries a base layer, and a second reset would undo the element styling its components depend on. Kumo's sheet stays unlayered, so where both define the same class Kumo still wins and nothing shared moves.

## This is a behaviour change, and here is its size

Built the app twice, with the plugin on and off, and diffed the emitted CSS:

**143,762 → 151,760 bytes (+7,998 bytes), ~32 selectors that now match something for the first time.** @code-reviewer measured the same build independently and counted 31; the difference is how a combined selector is counted, not what changed.

Two rows of the table below were wrong in an earlier draft and are corrected: the settings row's *column split* was never dead, only its vertical alignment, and the `minmax(...)` track belongs to `onboarding/view.tsx`.

| Where | Newly live | What changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ui/design-system.tsx` | `md:items-center` | **SettingsRow** — its two columns become vertically centred. The column split itself is *not* new: `md:grid-cols-[2fr_1fr]` is already in Kumo's bundle |
| `features/agent-usage.tsx` | `sm:grid-cols-3` `lg:grid-cols-2` `h-60` | Usage page gains its multi-column layout; **the chart container gets a height for the first time** |
| `features/tasks-page.tsx` | `whitespace-pre-wrap` `min-w-56` `align-top` `sm:grid-cols-2` | **Task output keeps its line breaks** instead of collapsing them |
| `im/feishu-setup.tsx` | `size-60` | The Lark QR is constrained to 15rem square |
| `router.tsx` | `max-w-md` `max-w-xl` `top-4` `last:border-b-0` `sm:grid-cols-2` | Panels become fixed-width; a close button moves to `top-4`; the last row's bottom border disappears |
| `runtime-configuration.tsx` | `sm:grid-cols-2` | One column becomes two |
| `agent-creation/agent-creation-flow.tsx` | `grid-cols-[auto_1fr]` | Layout change |
| `internal/onboarding-lab-page.tsx` | `z-30` `w-[min(24rem,…)]` | Overlay stacking and width |
| `onboarding/view.tsx` | `w-[18rem]` `size-7` `md:grid-cols-[minmax(14rem,18rem)_1fr]` | The two already-dead classes above, plus this page's own column split |

**None of these pages has a test asserting its layout.** Every one of them was written expecting these classes to work, so in each case this is the author's intent finally taking effect rather than a new design — but that is a claim worth checking with eyes, which is why this is its own PR.

## Why separate

Found while doing #262, which needs it. Split out on @code-reviewer's recommendation, and I agree: it wants a **visual** review of pages this repository has not otherwise touched, and bundling it with an onboarding rewrite would hide it inside a diff about something else.

⚠️ **Merge this first.** #262 depends on it: without the compiler, that flow's reserved heights and frame width are inert, which is the exact failure this fixes. And note the split does not make this permanently revertable on its own — it is, until #262 lands; after that, reverting here would break onboarding's layout too.

## Verification

`pnpm check`, typecheck and build clean; web tests **366 passed**. The impact table above is measured from build output, not read off the source.

⚠️ **Not visually reviewed.** I have no signed-in session against a running Server, so I could not open Settings, Usage, Tasks or the Lark setup page to look at them. Someone who can should, before this merges.

body:
**Correcting my own recommendation.** I said requiring the CI checks was a settings change to go and make. It is not available on this repo:

```
$ gh api repos/dsasante1/paybox/branches/main/protection
403  Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public to enable this feature.

$ gh api repos/dsasante1/paybox/rulesets
403  Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public to enable this feature.
```

The repository is private on a free plan, which gates branch protection *and* rulesets. CI reports failures; nothing prevents merging past them.

## What this adds

`docs/ci.md` records the constraint and the two real fixes — make the repo public, or pay for Pro — and notes that the **"Do not allow bypassing the above settings"** box is the part that actually closes the gap. Without it an admin can still merge red, which is most of the problem.

Until then, two client-side guards. Both are **guards, not gates**, and the docs say so plainly: each can be bypassed deliberately. The point is to make the safe path the easy one and the bypass a decision rather than a default.

**`npm run ship -- <pr>`** merges only when every check has passed. It refuses a draft, a conflicting branch, checks still running, checks that failed, and — the case most worth catching — **a PR with no checks at all**, which looks perfectly mergeable and has verified nothing. That is exactly how the last several merges on this repo went through.

**`.githooks/pre-push`** refuses a direct push to `main`, wired up by a `prepare` script so a fresh clone gets it on first install. This exists because a force-push to `main` did happen here; recovering was straightforward, but only because it was noticed at the time.

## Verified by running them

```
$ git push --dry-run origin main
  ✗ Refusing to push directly to main.
  error: failed to push some refs        (exit 1)

$ git push --dry-run --no-verify origin main
  c993f94..e8a217b  main -> main         (bypass works, as documented)
```

The ship guard exits non-zero on a PR with no checks, and is being used to merge this PR.

## Not recommended

*Require pull request reviews*, on a solo repo. With one contributor it only means reaching for `--admin`, and a rule that is routinely bypassed is worse than no rule — it teaches you to ignore the ones that matter.

body:
## Problem

Three cfg80211 compat shims assumed the \`link_id\`/\`radio_idx\` parameter
additions landed at kernel 6.0, but they actually landed at **6.17**:

- \`cfg80211_rx_spurious_frame\` / \`cfg80211_rx_unexpected_4addr_frame\`
  (\`rwnx_compat.h\`) — gained a \`link_id\` param in 6.17, stayed
  \`(dev, addr, gfp)\` through 6.16.
- \`set_tx_power\` (\`rwnx_main.c\`) — gained a \`radio_idx\` param in 6.17.

On any 6.0–6.16 kernel (e.g. Ubuntu 24.04's stock 6.8) this fails to build:

\`\`\`
error: too many arguments to function 'cfg80211_rx_spurious_frame'
error: too many arguments to function 'cfg80211_rx_unexpected_4addr_frame'
error: initialization of 'int (*)(struct wiphy *, struct wireless_dev *, enum nl80211_tx_power_setting, int)'
  from incompatible pointer type 'int (*)(struct wiphy *, struct wireless_dev *, int, enum nl80211_tx_power_setting, int)'
\`\`\`

Also \`rwnx_cfg80211_set_monitor_channel_\`'s declaration in \`rwnx_main.h\`
was unconditionally the post-6.13 (dev-carrying) signature, while its
definition in \`rwnx_main.c\` is correctly gated on 6.13. On kernels < 6.13
this is a declaration/definition mismatch. Gated the header declaration
to match.

## Verification

Confirmed the real cfg80211.h signatures across upstream tags v6.11–v6.19
(raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux). The \`link_id\`/\`radio_idx\`
params first appear at v6.17, not v6.0 or v6.13.

Built and installed clean on Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.8.0-136-generic
(gcc), and confirmed the resulting driver loads and associates over
USB against a real AIC8800 device.

author: dimmus
body:
`docs/TESTING-STATUS.md` exists so the gap between the plan and the tree is visible rather than assumed closed. That makes a stale line on it worse than a stale line elsewhere: the page is the one place a reader goes to find out what is *not* true yet, so it is the last place that should overstate — or, as here, understate a capability that has since been built while leaving three other rows describing a tree that no longer exists.

Four things were stale. One addition.

## What was stale

**"Nothing here has been executed."** False since E0-B01, which got the three commands green in the development image. Replaced with the gap that is actually true and is easy to forget: `cargo xtask verify` is local, and cannot run the AArch64 tests or the litmus job — which are exactly where L2 means anything, because x86-64's total store order hides the entire class of bug the ring is exposed to.

**L7 said one claim.** There are two, `0001-ring-submit-latency` and `0002-timer-jitter`, and both are `pending` with a threshold and no number. The row and the gaps section now say which task moves each — E0-P05 and E0-P06.

**The counters row said they are not wired "until M2".** M2 arrived at E0-B07 and they are still not wired. The row now says that, and points at E0-P04, which owns it.

**L0's "where" column predated `env/src/contract.rs`** and the hardware `Env` in `kernel/src/env.rs` — the part of the substrate worth reading now, since it is what states the properties every `Env` owes and checks both of them on the same boot.

## What was added

A section for what the seven layers have no row for: provoking the running system into failing on purpose. `cargo xtask fault` (six kernel faults that must be reported rather than survived) and, as of E0-B09, `cargo xtask user` (seven boots in which a process at ring 3 violates one isolation rule each).

It is neither simulation nor proof, it is where most of this project's evidence currently comes from, and a taxonomy built around simulation, proof and fuzzing has no natural home for "run the real thing and try to break it". The absence of a row seemed worth stating rather than papering over.

The section also says what those suites are **not**: they are the shape E0-P08 will take at M4, and they are not E0-P08. That suite is about capabilities — a process cannot name one it was not given, forge a handle, use a revoked one, or panic the kernel by trying — and there is no capability table yet. What exists now covers the layer underneath: the page tables and the privilege level.

## For the reviewer

**One stale string is deliberately left in place.** `bench/src/lib.rs` still reports `Metric::Unavailable("PMU not wired until M2")` and `("energy counters not wired until M2")`. That is the same expired forecast this change removes from the doc, and fixing it here would mean editing a crate to fix a document. It belongs to E0-P04, which is the task that wires the counters and will delete the strings rather than reword them. The gaps section now names the discrepancy explicitly, so it is recorded rather than silently inconsistent — but if you would rather have the two literals corrected now, say so and it is a one-line change.

**Every factual claim on the page was re-checked against the tree**, not carried forward: the claims registry via `cargo xtask claims` (two entries, both `pending`), the eval task count, `env/src/sim.rs` still being a hook with nothing injecting at a named site (E0-P09 open), and all six `xtask fault` paths plus all seven `xtask user` provocations run green.

**No code changes**, so no `verify` impact — the diff is one markdown file.

author: dbgeek
body:
Two findings from a two-axis review of the S1–S11 work (issues #32–#42).

## The summary is no longer read back as authoritative

`data-model.md` is explicit: *"The summary is written for the human and for the replace-confirmation, and is **never read back**. Import recomputes everything from the events and uses the summary only to cross-check for truncation."* #41 adds: *"refusing a good Backup over it is a bug wearing the costume of rigour."*

`validateSummary` compared `summary.firstLogicalDay`, `lastLogicalDay` and `currentTarget` against the events and called `invalidBackup()` on any disagreement — none of which is a truncation signal. A file whose records were wholly intact but whose summary had gone stale was refused outright, and the only copy of an irreplaceable history became unopenable.

It is now `checkForTruncation`, and refuses only when an array holds *fewer* rows than the summary declares. Non-numeric or absent counts are ignored; `summary` must still be an object, since that is envelope structure rather than semantics.

## Track re-evaluates the Ratchet on return to view

`rules.md` §6: *"Runs on every cold start, on `visibilitychange` → visible, and after every write, edit, delete and import."* Only `StatsScreen` listened. An app parked in the iOS switcher for days — precisely the case the 30-minute catch-up exists for — woke showing a stale Target and a stale badge on Track until the user wrote something.

`TrackScreen` now re-runs `source.load()` when the document becomes visible, which runs `evaluate` and `updateBadge`. The reload is chained onto `writeQueue.current` rather than fired independently: a visibility event landing mid-tap would otherwise resolve against the pre-write record and clobber it. Failures set `loadFailed` the same way the initial load does, and the listener is removed on unmount.

## Not in scope

- The Track tick is still 1 s where `rules.md` §8 asks for one minute — a separate finding, and changing it shifts timeline rendering the tests pin.
- `App.tsx` has no visibility listener. Track and Stats are the only surfaces showing Ratchet-derived state; Settings shows none.

## Verification

`npm test` — 159 tests, 26 files, all passing. `npm run typecheck` clean.

New coverage: a stale summary (wrong bounds *and* wrong Target) restores the full record; an undercount is refused; Track calls `load` a second time on `visibilitychange` → visible and not when hidden.

author: irondarrius
body:
This is the IronOCR slice of a corpus-wide pass over the fifteen GitHub
example repositories. Each repo gets the same treatment; the numbers below are
what applied here.

## What changed

**266 documentation links now carry `?utm_source=github`**, so arrivals on
the docs sites can be attributed to these repositories.

Only links a reader clicks are tagged - markdown `[text](url)` and HTML
`<a href>`. Images, code fences, inline code spans and stylesheet hrefs are
left alone: an image URL fires on page load rather than on a click, so tagging
one would report a visit nobody made, and a query string inside a code sample
changes what the sample does. The tag goes before any `#fragment`, and it is
the only `utm_` parameter on the link.

**Every broken link in the READMEs is repaired.** 89 files changed, 255 insertions(+), 255 deletions(-).

## Across the corpus

Following every clickable Iron link - 1,114 of them, not just the 606
canonical `Full guide` lines earlier passes checked - found **137 that did not
resolve to themselves**. All of them are now fixed:

- 62 answered 404, including 11 IronXL download packages that do not exist,
  and a family of `ironsoftware.com/csharp/pdf/...` paths - IronPDF's docs are
  on `ironpdf.com`.
- 40 redirected somewhere else, often to a different product's home page.
- 22 were written as a *path* where the site expects a *fragment*. The site
  301s `/csharp/ocr/trial-license` to `/csharp/ocr/#trial-license` and drags
  the query string in behind the fragment, where a browser never sends it.
- 11 GitHub links had been rewritten onto an Iron host, in four different
  shapes.
- 21 were `www.`, a missing trailing slash, or `http://`.

**999 unique links now resolve to themselves.** The 8 exceptions are package
`.zip` and `.jar` downloads that legitimately redirect to the release host.

## How it was verified

Every replacement was fetched over HTTP and required to answer 200 **at
itself** - a 200 after a redirect is not evidence a link is right. Where the
site's own redirect named a successor, that was used; where the redirect named
something the link did not mean, it was not. `/contact-us/` redirects to
`/contact-us/sales/`, but every occurrence sat under "Get Support", so those
point at `/contact-us/support/`.

Two defects were found in the process that no link check would report: six
platform-tile images on the IronPDF quickstart were 404 for the same
wrong-host reason as the links beside them, and a 404 image in IronWebScraper
turned out to be spelled *correctly* in the repo and incorrectly on the server.

author: dnafication
body:
Closes #18.

The game survives the app closing. Exactly one game is stored, saved whenever it changes and restored once on mount, so neither player ever has a save to think about and there is no save UI to learn.

What is stored is the full history, not a position. A single FEN holds one position and no history, so a position-only save would silently break undo after a resume and lose the threefold-repetition count with it. `serializeGame` already records the starting position and every move, and replaying them rebuilds the undo stack and the repetition count together. A round trip through castling, en passant, two promotions and a repeated position is tested, and undo still walks all the way back to the start afterwards.

Storage is injected rather than reached for directly, so every test runs against an in-memory fake and the whole thing is verifiable without a device. The only file that touches the platform is the AsyncStorage adapter, kept apart so the plain-Node suite never loads a native module. That is the one dependency added, via `npx expo install`.

A save that cannot be read drops the players into a fresh game rather than a broken screen — empty, garbage, truncated and an older-format FEN are each tested.

**Review fix, and the reason this PR grew.** #16 landed the endings that come *by agreement*, and those are not in the move list — the rules module never knows a game was resigned. Saving the game alone would therefore have handed two players back a game they had already finished, against this ticket's own criterion that a finished game is restored as finished with its result still shown. The stored value is now the whole table session: the game's full history plus any agreed ending. A pending draw offer is deliberately not stored — an offer is something one player said across the table, and after the app has closed it is simply said again. An unreadable *ending* is dropped on its own rather than discarding the game with it.

Also dropped a stray `.git-commit-msg.txt` that had been committed.

411 tests green.

One note for whoever runs this locally: on a loaded machine the parallel test workers starve the perft file and it can blow its 60s timeout. `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` gives a reliable ~27s. Unchanged on CI, which passes as it stands.

author: darylmcd
body:
Fixes #411.

## Problem

`buildDSNFromSource()` encoded SQLite DSNs by prefixing three slashes unconditionally:

```ts
return `sqlite:///${source.database}`;
```

`SQLiteDSNParser` reads the path positionally, so this only round-trips for Windows drive letters and `:memory:`. Verified against 1.2.1 on Node v24.19.0:

| TOML `database` | DSN built | Path opened | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `C:/x/y.db` | `sqlite:///C:/x/y.db` | `C:/x/y.db` | ok |
| `/var/lib/y.db` | `sqlite:////var/lib/y.db` | `var/lib/y.db` | absolute → relative |
| `data/y.db` | `sqlite:///data/y.db` | `/data/y.db` | relative → absolute |
| `:memory:` | `sqlite:///:memory:` | `:memory:` | ok |

The relative case fails loudly (`ERR_SQLITE_ERROR` 14). The absolute case fails **silently** — with a database at `<cwd>/sub/a.db` and `database = "/sub/a.db"`, the server starts and answers queries against `<cwd>/sub/a.db`. A config naming an absolute path can therefore attach to a different file than it names.

Windows `~` expansion was broken the same way: `expandHomeDir` returns `C:\Users\...`, which yields `sqlite:///C:\Users\...`; the drive-letter branch requires `C:/`, so it fell through and decoded to `/C:\Users\...`.

## Change

1. **`resolveSqliteDatabasePath()`** — resolves `database` at load time. Relative paths resolve against the **config file's directory** rather than `process.cwd()`, so a config selects the same database regardless of where the server was launched from. Separators are normalised to forward slashes. `:memory:` passes through.
2. **`buildSqliteDSN()`** — encodes as `sqlite://` + a leading-slash path, which the parser decodes back unchanged for POSIX paths and de-prefixes correctly for `C:/`.

I picked "resolve against the config file" over "reject relative paths with an error" — happy to switch if you'd rather not have implicit resolution.

## Tests

- Round-trip tests asserting the path `SQLiteDSNParser` actually returns (POSIX absolute, Windows drive letter, path with spaces, `:memory:`). **This is the coverage that was missing** — the previous test asserted the DSN string alone, so an encoding that rewrote absolute paths into relative ones passed review.
- `loadTomlConfig` tests: relative resolves against the config directory (config placed in a subdirectory so cwd and config dir differ), absolute is left alone, `:memory:` untouched.
- The existing `should build SQLite DSN from database path` assertion encoded the old four-slash output and is updated.
- Two `~`-expansion assertions now compare against forward slashes; they were platform-dependent and, on Windows, asserted a value that could not be opened.

Worth noting: every SQLite source in `src/__fixtures__/toml/*.toml` uses `database = ":memory:"`, one of the two forms that round-tripped correctly — which is why CI stayed green.

## Verification

- `src/config/__tests__/toml-loader.test.ts`: **156/156 pass** (154 before, plus new coverage).
- Full suite: **1317 pass, 2 fail**. Both failures reproduce unmodified on `main` and are environment-dependent — `manager.test.ts > should resolve SSH config from ~/.ssh/config` and `sqlite.integration.test.ts > should open file-based database in readonly mode`. Confirmed by stashing the change and re-running.
- `tsc --noEmit` reports 19 errors in the two touched files both before and after — delta zero. (`tsc --noEmit` is not clean on `main`; the build runs through tsup.)

author: pengdurice
body:
Fix https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/issues/8357
## The fix

Two independent changes.

**1. Walk every graph, then verify the result.**

`iter_graphs()` yields the top-level graph and every nested `GraphModule`, so checkpointed regions
are covered. The pass then compares the tensor-parallel layers it *reached* in the graph against the
ones it gave a collective to, and raises if any are missing.

The check matters more than the traversal fix. It catches the next variant of this failure — a
matmul traced to an op `_MATMUL_TARGETS` does not list, a future change to `nn_module_stack`,
another higher-order op — instead of only the checkpointing case fixed here. Given the failure mode
is silent wrong numbers, a loud error is the right default.

The check is fail-closed. The filter against the deferred-layer names is applied only when the two
naming schemes demonstrably overlap, because intersecting mismatched names would quietly empty the
set and turn the check into a no-op — the exact failure it exists to catch.

**2. Fail if a deferred layer runs eagerly.**

`defer_collectives_to_compiler` is set during `engine.compile()`, but `nn.Module.compile()` is lazy:
compilation happens at the first forward. With `TORCH_COMPILE_DISABLE=1` or
`torch._dynamo.config.disable` the backend never runs, the model executes eagerly forever with its
collectives switched off, and training is silently wrong. The affected layers now assert they are
inside a compiled region.

## Tests

| Test | Covers |
|---|---|
| `TestAutoTPCompileActivationCheckpointing` | the bug above; verified to fail against the pre-fix pass |
| `test_unhandled_parallel_layer_raises` | a layer reached but not rewritten must stop the compile |
| `test_deferred_layer_run_eagerly_raises` | the eager-execution guard |

Existing tests in the file are unchanged and still pass (2x/4xH200, `-m sequential`: 6 passed).

The regression test was checked against the pre-fix pass to confirm it actually catches the bug:
with `iter_graphs`/the coverage check reverted and the new tests kept, it fails. The magnitude of
the divergence in that configuration (forward off by 2.7e-01) is from the standalone reproducer
above rather than the test itself, since the distributed-test harness reports only the worker exit
code.

Note that these tests, like all the AutoTP compile tests, are `@pytest.mark.sequential`, which
`tests/pytest.ini` excludes by default. They need the marker to run at all:

```bash
pytest tests/unit/compile/test_tp_compile.py -m sequential
```

## Scope

This PR is the correctness fix only. It does not change how the collectives are emitted or
scheduled, and it does not touch the ZeRO passes.

author: danielsogl
body:
Issue #9 item 1 — with a correction to its framing.

The issue called the eviction itself the bug. It is not: the api-cache holds JSON produced by the parsers, so a code change **must** drop it, or the old output keeps being served from Valkey while the stored HTML behind it is already re-parsed correctly. That mechanism is what makes "code changes take effect on restart" true. Keeping it.

What is wrong is the shape. `evict_volatile_data` ran `scan_iter(match="*")` and deleted everything except two unknown-player prefixes — an **exception list**, so every key type added afterwards was deleted by default, silently. Two of them should never have been:

- **`throttle:*`** is the AIMD delay learned against Blizzard's rate limit. This runs on app startup *and* shutdown, so every deploy threw it away and relearning began from the 2s start delay again — with a fresh chance of earning a 403 right after a deploy.
- **the taskiq queue and its dedup keys** are pending work. Wiping them discards refreshes that were already scheduled.

Neither is rendered output. Neither goes stale because our code changed.

It now names what to evict — `api-cache` and `gamemode-filter`, the two things we render — instead of what to spare. A key type added tomorrow survives by default rather than vanishing.

## Verification

`756 passed, 1 skipped`; `ruff` and `ty` clean repo-wide.

The existing eviction test passed both before and after, which is exactly why it needed a companion: it only asserted that unknown-player keys survive. The new test pins throttle and queue state too, and **was confirmed to fail against the previous implementation** — before this change both were being deleted on every start and stop.
