body: Closes #7883 Allow `OpenAIProvider(api_key=...)` to receive the async API-key callback accepted by the OpenAI Python SDK. This makes short-lived credentials usable without supplying a prebuilt `AsyncOpenAI` client. New public surface: `OpenAIProvider(api_key=Callable[[], Awaitable[str]])`. User-visible behavior: applications can pass an async credential callback directly to `OpenAIProvider`. Verification: `git diff --check`. The existing SDK callback path is exercised in `tests/realtime/test_openai.py`; no additional targeted test is included pending maintainer feedback. What changes for existing users: nothing; existing static keys and prebuilt clients retain their behavior. ### Checklist - [x] Any **AI generated code** has been reviewed line-by-line by the human PR author, who stands by it. - [x] No **breaking changes** in accordance with the [version policy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/main/docs/version-policy.md). - [x] Any permitted **compatibility impact** has a label, warning, migration, release note, and exact API-check waiver. - [x] **PR title** is fit for the [release changelog](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/releases).

author: jsg3121
body:
# 작업 내용

## 📋 작업 유형

- [ ] ✨ 새 기능 (New Feature)
- [x] 🐛 버그 수정 (Bug Fix)
- [x] 🚨 핫픽스 (Hotfix)
- [ ] 🔧 리팩토링 (Refactoring)
- [x] 🚀 성능 개선 (Performance)
- [ ] 🔍 SEO 개선 (SEO)
- [ ] 🎨 디자인 변경 (Design)
- [ ] 📝 문서 (Documentation)
- [ ] 🔨 Breaking Changes

---

## 🎯 변경 사항

1.58.2 배포에서 CloudFront 무효화가 누락되어 **사이트 전체가 클릭 불가 상태**가 되는 장애가 발생했다. 그 대응과, 함께 발견된 정적 자산 캐싱 누락을 처리한다.

### 🐛 장애 내용

메인·도감에서 포켓몬 카드를 눌러 상세로 이동한 뒤, 뒤로가기로 돌아와 다른 카드를 누르면 무반응이었다. 새로고침하면 그 카드는 동작하지만 뒤로가기 후 다시 먹통이 됐다. 콘솔·네트워크 로그에 아무것도 찍히지 않고 로컬에서도 재현되지 않아 원인 파악이 어려웠다.

**원인**: CDN이 들고 있던 옛 배포의 HTML.

HTML에는 배포마다 해시가 바뀌는 JS 청크 파일명이 박힌다. CloudFront가 옛 HTML을 서빙하면 그 HTML이 요청하는 청크가 서버에 없다. 실제 확인 시 메인 페이지가 참조하는 17개 청크 중 3개가 404였고, 그중 하나가 **웹팩 런타임**이었다. 이것이 없으면 hydration이 시작조차 못 해 `<Link>`에 핸들러가 붙지 않는다.

| 관찰 | 원인 |
| --- | --- |
| 화면은 정상 표시 | SSR로 서버가 HTML을 그려 보냄 |
| 카드 클릭 무반응 | hydration 실패로 이벤트 핸들러 미부착 |
| 새로고침하면 이동됨 | `<Link>`는 실제 `<a href>`라 JS 없이도 동작 |
| 콘솔 로그 없음 | `removeConsole: true` 설정 |
| 로컬 미재현 | CDN이 없어 HTML과 청크가 항상 같은 빌드 |

카드 이동 코드 자체에는 문제가 없었다. `PokemonCardShell`은 순수한 `<Link>` 하나만 쓰고, `preventDefault`나 클릭 가드가 코드베이스 전체에 존재하지 않는다.

**타임라인** (UTC): 13:54 무효화(배포 전 작업) → ~14:55 옛 HTML 캐싱 → 14:59 배포 → **배포 후 무효화 없음** → 16:15 긴급 무효화로 해소

---

## ✨ 변경 내용

### 1. `deploy.sh` 추가

빌드부터 무효화까지를 한 스크립트로 묶어 절차 누락 자체를 없앤다.

```bash
git pull --ff-only → npm install → npm run build
→ pm2 restart → 헬스체크 → CloudFront 무효화
```

**설계상 중요한 두 가지**

- **무효화를 기동 확인 뒤에 배치**: 무효화는 캐시를 비울 뿐 이후 요청을 막지 않는다. 새 빌드가 응답하기 전에 비우면 그 틈의 요청이 옛 응답을 다시 캐싱한다.
- **기동 실패 시 무효화 건너뜀**: 죽은 서버 상태에서 캐시를 비우면 CDN이 오리진 에러를 캐싱해 더 나빠진다. 옛 캐시라도 남는 편이 낫다.

환경변수로 설정을 받는다. `CF_DISTRIBUTION_ID`만 필수이고, 없으면 `git pull` 이전에 중단한다.

| 변수 | 필수 | 기본값 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CF_DISTRIBUTION_ID` | O | — |
| `APP_DIR` | X | 스크립트가 놓인 디렉토리 |
| `HEALTH_URL` | X | `http://localhost/` |
| `HEALTH_TIMEOUT` | X | `60` |

### 2. 페이지 캐시 상한 1년 → 1일

`s-maxage=31536000`은 "도감 데이터는 배포 전까지 안 바뀐다"는 판단이었으나, **캐싱 대상은 데이터가 아니라 HTML 문서**다. 한 문서에 수명이 다른 두 가지(콘텐츠 / 청크 파일명)가 섞여 있고, 캐시 수명은 짧은 쪽에 맞춰야 하는데 긴 쪽에 맞춰져 있었다.

1년은 무효화가 한 번이라도 실패하면 **자연 복구 경로가 없어** 수동 개입 전까지 장애가 방치된다. `deploy.sh`가 무효화를 자동화하므로 이 값은 그것이 실패했을 때만 쓰이는 안전망이고, 안전망은 짧을수록 좋다.

`stale-while-revalidate`도 제거했다. CloudFront가 지원하지 않고(엣지의 stale 서빙은 오류 응답 한정), 브라우저는 `max-age`가 이미 커버한다.

| 경로 | 변경 전 | 변경 후 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/` | `max-age=0, s-maxage=86400, swr=600` | `max-age=0, s-maxage=86400` |
| `/list`·`/detail/*` 외 17건 | `max-age=10800, s-maxage=31536000, swr=60` | `max-age=10800, s-maxage=86400` |

`/assets/*`(해시 URL, `immutable`)와 `/favicon.ico`는 유지한다.

### 3. 웹폰트 캐싱 헤더 추가

`/fonts/*`에 캐시 정책이 없어 CloudFront가 전혀 캐싱하지 못하고 **매 요청이 오리진까지** 도달하고 있었다.

| 파일 | 크기 | 변경 전 | 변경 후 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GmarketSansBold.subset.woff2` | 301KB | `max-age=0` / Miss | `max-age=86400, s-maxage=31536000` |
| `GmarketSansMedium.subset.woff2` | 299KB | `max-age=0` / Miss | 동일 |

합계 약 600KB가 방문마다 새로 나가던 상태였다. 백엔드 측 액세스 로그로도 **일 7,700회 오리진 도달**이 확인됐다.

파일명에 해시가 없어 `immutable`은 붙이지 않았다. 서브셋을 다시 뜨면 같은 파일명으로 내용만 바뀔 수 있어 하루마다 재검증할 여지를 남긴다.

---

## ✅ 검증

| 항목 | 결과 |
| --- | --- |
| `headers()` 반환값 | 22건, 페이지 규칙 19건 전부 `s-maxage=86400` |
| 1년 값 잔존 | 정적 자산 3건만 (`/assets/*`, `/favicon.ico`, `/fonts/*`) |
| `stale-while-revalidate` 잔존 | 없음 |
| `/fonts/:path*` 경로 매칭 | 점 2개 파일명 매칭 확인, `/favicon.ico` 침범 없음 |
| `deploy.sh` 문법 (`bash -n`) | 통과 |
| `CF_DISTRIBUTION_ID` 미설정 시 중단 | 통과 — `git pull` 미실행 확인 |
| 헬스체크 실패 시 무효화 차단 | 통과 — 닫힌 포트로 실제 확인 |
| Prettier | 통과 |
| Changelog MDX | 통과 |

리뷰 생략 요청에 따라 QA 종합 검증·E2E는 실행하지 않았다.

---

## ⚠️ 배포 시 필요한 작업

**1. EC2 환경변수 설정**

```bash
echo 'export CF_DISTRIBUTION_ID=<배포ID>' >> ~/.bashrc && source ~/.bashrc
```

IAM 역할에 `cloudfront:CreateInvalidation` 권한은 부여 완료.

**2. CloudFront에 `/fonts/*` 전용 동작(Behavior) 추가**

없으면 기본값(`*`) 동작의 캐시 정책을 타서 `s-maxage`가 그 정책 Max TTL로 잘린다. `/favicon.ico`는 1.58.2에서 추가 완료.

**3. 이후 배포는 `deploy.sh`로 수행**

**4. 오리진 부하 관찰**

캐시 상한을 낮춘 만큼 오리진 도달이 늘 수 있다. 서버는 t3.small 한 대에 Postgres·GraphQL 백엔드가 함께 올라가 있다. 부하가 문제되면 값을 올리면 되지만, 반대로 이미 캐싱된 1년짜리는 무효화 없이 내릴 수 없어 낮은 값에서 시작한다.

---

## 📝 Changelog

- `changelog/blog/1.58.3/2026-08-30-font-cache.md`
- `changelog/blog/1.58.4/2026-08-30-deploy-script.md`

author: mohitkourav01
body:
Closes #1969.

`arrearsCalculator.js` produces the arrear and `tdsEngine.utils.js` taxes it in the month it is paid. Both are right on their own terms. Neither produces the relief the Act gives *because* of that bunching, and this module is the difference between the two.

### Relief is a difference between two rate environments, so every rate is dated

Rule 21A(2) asks what each relation year would have borne **at that year's rates on that year's income**. `taxCalculator.js` holds one current slab set, and running a 2021-22 relation year against 2026-27 slabs collapses the two environments into one — nil relief in the ordinary case and an indefensible figure in the rest.

`TaxRateTable` is keyed on assessment year **and** regime together, and `resolveRateTable` returns `null` rather than the nearest match. A year with no table comes back as a gap with its reason, never as a zero — a zero in the additional-tax column is a claim, and the module has not made it. `incompleteRelationYears` is counted and surfaced, because a relief computed over a subset of the years it relates to is not a smaller relief but a wrong one.

### The computation is kept in its terms

The employee signs a return carrying this number and defends it personally, so `computeRelief` returns the tax on the year of receipt with and without the arrear, the tax on the bunching, and the additional tax across the relation years as four separate figures. Table A and Annexure I are built from that same result rather than re-derived, so the form can never disagree with the screen.

### Relief is floored at nil, and the floor is reported

Where the relation years were assessed higher than the year of receipt the difference goes negative. Section 89 gives relief; it does not create a recovery. That is `NO_RELIEF_ARISES` with its reason rather than a liability carried back.

### The relief and the authority to give it are two answers

Section 192(2A) lets the employer reduce the deduction only against a Form 10E, and since AY 2015-16 the relief is disallowed outright without one. So:

- `reliefComputed` and `reliefApplicable` are both on every response — a relief of ₹40,000 that cannot yet be applied is not a relief of nil;
- the furnishing is a row with a **date** rather than a boolean, because furnished after the return the relief is gone and furnishing it late does not revive it;
- `PATCH /claims/:id/apply` is the one place the module refuses, and it returns the server's own reason so the user knows what would let them proceed.

A payroll that reduced the deduction on the computed figure alone has short-deducted, and the section 201(1A) interest is the employer's.

### The allocation comes from the revision's own dates

Split by days rather than evenly — a revision effective 1 November spans two years in a 5:7 ratio, and an even split moves relief between years with different rates, which is the only variable the whole computation turns on. A recorded allocation wins over the derived one, because a backdated bonus referable to a single year is not proportional to time and the module cannot tell that from the dates.

Two arrears received in one financial year are one bunching. The roll-up names those years rather than adding the two reliefs together, which would double-count the year-of-receipt term.

### Permissions

The split is on which name can move a relief without touching a claim. `MANAGE_TAX_RATE_TABLE` holds the dated slabs and a past year's assessed income; changing either moves every relief ever computed against that year, for every employee, with no claim record changing and nothing on any screen saying why. `MANAGE_RELIEF_CLAIM` is clerical against documents.

### Included fix

`frontend/src/config/navigation.js` does not parse on `main`. The Recognition Wall entry lost its `icon` and gained a duplicate `},`, and the Learning Tracker entry was spliced into the middle of the labour welfare fund entry's comment, leaving one comment line orphaned outside any object literal and a second stray `},` behind it. Both are syntax errors in the module that defines every route in the app, and the pre-commit hook cannot format the file until they are fixed. Repaired here.

### Scope

Nothing here reopens a payroll period, recomputes an arrear or files anything. The employee furnishes Form 10E; this records that they did.

### Tests

41 new unit tests in `backend/src/utils/__tests__/sectionEightyNineRelief.test.js`, covering the dated-rate resolution and its refusal to substitute, the day-weighted allocation and its reconciliation, all four Rule 21A(2) terms, the nil floor, the gap-not-zero rule on Table A, and the section 192(2A) branch in both directions.

author: nao1215
body:
## Summary

gup targets three operating systems and two architectures, but the pipeline around it did not: the E2E suite ran on Linux alone, the release smoke test unpacked the Windows zip on Ubuntu and called it verified, `completion --install` refused to work on Windows at all, and nothing stopped two gup processes from rewriting `gup.json` at the same time. This branch closes those gaps, adds Go 1.27 support with an explicit supported-version policy, publishes to Scoop, and adds a govulncheck workflow. Tests now enforce the agreement between the Go versions CI runs, the toolchain releases are built with, the architectures GoReleaser emits, and what README and the website tell users to download.

## Changes

- **Go 1.27** — `.github/workflows/unit_test.yml` names 1.25/1.26/1.27 explicitly and moves latest-Go tracking into its own job, so a break on the newest toolchain is distinguishable from a break on a supported one. `release.yml` and `release-smoke.yml` build with the latest Go 1.27 patch; `build.yml` keeps `go.mod`'s Go 1.25 so the declared minimum stays provably buildable. No source change was needed. README and `website/content/install.md` gained a "Supported Go versions" section, including the macOS 13 Ventura floor Go 1.27 imposes.
- **Concurrency lock** — new `internal/lockfile` (CGO-free, `O_CREATE|O_EXCL`, per-OS PID liveness in `process_unix.go` / `process_windows.go`), `config.LockFilePath`, and `cmd/statelock.go` wiring it into `update`, `import`, `export`, `migrate`, `remove`, `pin`, and `unpin`.
- **PowerShell completion** — new `internal/completion/powershell.go`: `completion --install` on Windows writes `gup.completion.ps1` beside the profile and adds one marked, `Test-Path`-guarded dot-source line to the profile. `cmd/completion.go` no longer rejects Windows.
- **Cross-platform E2E** — `e2e/run.sh`'s bootstrap moved to `e2e/runner` (Go), `e2e/os_matrix.tsv` classifies all thirteen specs by OS with a written reason for every exclusion, `e2e/osmatrix.go` + `e2e/osmatrix_test.go` enforce it, and `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` runs Linux + Windows on pull requests and adds macOS on push, schedule, and dispatch.
- **Release verification** — `scripts/smoke_artifacts.sh` grew from four checks to ten (inventory, archive contents, per-binary GOOS/GOARCH via `go version -m`, native execution with `--version`/`--help`/`list --json`/`check --json`, `.deb` install, `.rpm`/`.apk` file trees, Scoop and winget manifests), `scripts/verify_artifact.ps1` covers the Windows leg, and `release.yml` is now three jobs with publishing gated on all of the smoke ones.
- **Distribution** — `.goreleaser.yml` states `goarch: [amd64, arm64]` (the default list was also building 386) and adds a `scoops:` block publishing into this repository's own `bucket/`. README and the website document Scoop plus `dpkg -i` / `rpm -Uvh` / `apk add --allow-untrusted`.
- **Supply chain** — new `.github/workflows/govulncheck.yml` (pull requests, main, daily, dispatch; `contents: read`; pinned `govulncheck@v1.7.0`), and the four remaining tag-pinned actions in `website.yml` are now commit SHAs.
- **Guardrails** — `release_test.go` and `doc_sync_test.go` gained tests for SHA pinning, the govulncheck workflow's triggers and permissions, the GoReleaser build matrix and Scoop bucket, the release job's `needs` gating, the E2E OS matrix, and README/website install-command agreement.

## Design Decisions

The lock is an exclusively created file holding the owner's PID, host, command, and start time rather than `flock`/`LockFileEx`, because `O_CREATE|O_EXCL` is atomic on every filesystem gup targets and needs no CGO or build tags. What such a lock normally gets wrong is the crash case, so it is reclaimable two independent ways: a lock whose PID is gone on this host is taken over immediately, and a lock nobody is refreshing ages out — the latter covering what the PID check cannot answer, such as a lock file written by another machine on a shared home or a PID that has been reused. `gup update` outlives any fixed timeout, so liveness is proven continuously instead of assumed from the acquisition time. Read-only commands deliberately do not take the lock: every write lands through an atomic rename, so making readers block would trade a race that cannot happen for a `gup list` that hangs behind a long update.

The E2E bootstrap is Go rather than bash because the Windows leg must not depend on Git for Windows being installed — a suite that passes because of the runner image is testing the image. Not every spec can run on Windows: one that asserts a `$GOBIN` path or an exact binary name is asserting a POSIX-only string, since `go install` writes `name.exe` there. Making those portable would mean a second copy of each scenario differing by a suffix, which is duplication rather than coverage — the behavior under test has no OS-specific branch, and the `.exe` normalization is already unit-tested. The danger is not the exclusions but their invisibility, so `e2e/os_matrix.tsv` records every one with a reason and a test fails when a spec is added without a decision.

Release artifacts are built once by cross-compilation and then run on the OS that can actually run them, because "the zip contains something that says it is a Windows binary" is a weaker claim than "the Windows binary runs" — and a bad artifact cannot be recalled once a tag is published. Anything a host cannot check is recorded with its reason and printed in a closing scope report, since a smoke test that hides what it did not look at is worse than none.

The Scoop bucket lives in this repository under `bucket/` rather than in a dedicated bucket repository: Scoop accepts either, and keeping it here means GoReleaser publishes the manifest with the workflow's built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN`, with no cross-repository token to provision and no second repository holding one generated file. govulncheck is a separate workflow rather than another golangci-lint linter because it answers a different question from gosec — known advisories reachable from gup's call graph, versus insecure code gup writes — and its scheduled leg is the point, since the advisory database changes when gup does not.

## Limitations

- The macOS and Windows E2E legs and the per-OS artifact smoke jobs were authored but could not be executed locally; their first real run is on this pull request's CI.
- `goreleaser check` exits non-zero on the pre-existing `brews:` deprecation. Migrating to `homebrew_casks` would change `brew install nao1215/tap/gup` from a formula to a cask for existing users, so it is left alone here.
- `.rpm` inspection degrades to a magic-number check when `rpm` is not installed; CI installs it so the full file-tree listing runs.

author: tannevaled
body:
The SVG rasteriser handled `path`/`rect`/`circle`/`image` but silently skipped
`<polygon>` and `<polyline>`, so some icon-pack glyphs (e.g. a file-type mark
built from a polygon) drew nothing — which is why a couple of vscode-icons glyphs
had to fall back to the default.

`drawPoly` parses the `points` list (x,y pairs, comma/space separated), `MoveTo`s
the first and `LineTo`s the rest, `Close`s for a polygon (left open for a
polyline), then fills + strokes through the same paint path as every other shape.
Fewer than two points draws nothing.

`drawPoly` is 100% covered: a filled triangle, a stroked polyline, a `fill=none`
polygon, and the no-/too-few-/empty-points edge cases. Full svg suite + vet green.

author: alanhuangyoo
body:
Problem 2 of #8353 — the diagnosis there is @pengdurice's, this is the fix for that half. It does **not** touch problem 1 (the init-time transient in the AutoEP replacement path), which is a separate, larger change.

### What retains the model

`deepspeed/utils/debug.py` keeps two module-level dicts:

```python
module_names = {}
param_names = {}

def debug_extract_module_and_param_names(model):
    module_names = {module: name for name, module in model.named_modules()}
    param_names = {param: name for name, param in model.named_parameters()}
```

Dict keys are strong references, and these are module-level globals, so they live as long as `deepspeed.utils.debug` is imported. The call order seals it:

```
engine.py:402   debug_extract_module_and_param_names(model)   <- snapshots the model
engine.py:965   debug_clear_module_and_param_names()          <- only in destroy()
```

Anything that swaps a submodule out between those two points cannot release it. `setattr(parent, name, replacement)` unlinks the old module from the tree, but every one of its parameters is still a live key, so the refcount never reaches zero. Expert-parallel replacement is where #8353 hit it; kernel injection replaces modules the same way.

Replacing all 16 blocks of a 64 MiB model:

```
master     replaced 64.0 MiB, still resident 64.0 MiB   (16/16 tensors)
this PR    replaced 64.0 MiB, still resident  0.0 MiB   ( 0/16 tensors)
```

### Why not WeakKeyDictionary

It is the obvious fix and it does not work. `WeakKeyDictionary` stores `weakref.ref` objects as keys, and `weakref.ref.__eq__` forwards to the referents when both are alive. Comparing two live parameters runs `Tensor.__eq__`, which returns a tensor:

```
>>> d = weakref.WeakKeyDictionary({p: n for n, p in model.named_parameters()})
>>> d[some_param]
RuntimeError: Boolean value of Tensor with more than one value is ambiguous
```

So the entries go in fine and every lookup raises.

Keying on `id()` and dropping the entry from a `weakref.finalize` keeps exactly the identity semantics the dicts already had — the previous code compared parameters by `Tensor.__hash__`, which is id-based. `deepspeed/utils/pin_memory.py` already tracks its allocations this way, in the same package.

The public surface is unchanged: `debug_module2name` / `debug_param2name` still do `in` then `[]`, and still return `"unknown"` for anything absent.

### Test

`tests/unit/utils/test_debug_name_maps.py` — lookups and the `"unknown"` fallback, release of a replaced submodule, clear/re-extract, and that a recycled `id()` is not a stale hit.

On master:

```
1 failed, 3 passed
tests/unit/utils/test_debug_name_maps.py:65: AssertionError    (test_replaced_submodule_is_released)
```

With this PR:

```
4 passed
```

The other three pass either way — they are there so the behaviour this preserves stays preserved.

```
tests/unit/utils/   21 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed
yapf --diff / flake8   clean
```

The one failure is `test_pin_memory_tracker.py::test_checkpoint_emits_info` (`assert 2 == 1`). It fails identically on master with this file reverted, so it is not from this change.

body: ## Summary CogniRun is used on a phone while running, but the CSS was desktop-first with a single `max-width: 420px` override tacked on the end. This rewrites `style.css` mobile-first (narrow phone is the base, `min-width: 600px` is the enhancement) and gives it a dark "sports watch" look: near-black background with a fixed radial glow, translucent blurred cards, tabular-nums metrics, fluid `clamp()` type. Behaviour, event wiring, element ids and the class strings the tests match on are unchanged. The changes that aren't obvious from the diff: - **The question modal becomes a bottom sheet.** It stays `position: sticky; bottom: 0` inside `#question-slot` rather than becoming `fixed` — it has to stay in normal flow above the demo scrubber, so the pairing is `.modal { z-index: 1 }` / `.scrubber { z-index: 0 }`. It gets a grabber bar (`::before`), a slide-up keyframe, and on phones the submit row collapses to a single column so `#submit` spans the full width in thumb reach; at ≥600px it goes back to `label | button` on one line. - **Chip rows scroll instead of wrapping.** `.modes`/`.multipliers`/`.courses` are `flex-wrap: nowrap` + `overflow-x: auto` + scroll-snap with the scrollbar hidden, so `x1 x10 x100 x1000` stays one row on a 360px screen instead of breaking into ragged lines. They need `min-width: 0; flex: 1 1 auto` to actually shrink inside `.row`. - **Safe areas.** `.screen` and `.scrubber` padding use `max(12px, calc(12px + env(safe-area-inset-*)))`, so on a notched phone nothing hides under the notch or the home indicator, and desktop keeps the plain fallback. `index.html` gains `viewport-fit=cover` (required for those `env()` values to be non-zero) plus `theme-color` and the web-app-capable metas. - **Two markup changes only:** a `.heroes` wrapper so heart rate and points sit side by side on a phone (`live.js`), and a `.table-scroll` wrapper so the 5-column results breakdown scrolls horizontally instead of overflowing the page (`results.js`). `.breakdown` gets `min-width: 500px` *only* inside `.table-scroll`, so the 3-column leaderboard table is unaffected. - `formatPace` renders `5:42/km`, which wrapped to two lines and made the middle tile of the 3-up grid taller than its neighbours; `.grid .metric strong` is now `clamp(16px, 4.8vw, 24px)` with `white-space: nowrap`. - Fixed a pre-existing display bug: the mic status is written with `textContent`, so its `&` rendered literally as `&` on screen. The `MIC_LABELS` entry is written with `innerHTML` and keeps its entity. - `vite.config.js` allows `.trycloudflare.com` hosts so the dev server can be opened on a real phone through a quick tunnel. - Every animation introduced here is disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`, hover styles are behind `@media (hover: hover)`, focus rings moved to `:focus-visible` with an accent outline, and `--muted` was lightened for contrast against the darker background. ## Testing `npm test` (101 passing) and `npm run build`. Rendered in Chrome at 390×844 and 360×640 across setup / live / open question / results, asserting `documentElement.scrollWidth <= innerWidth` on each. ![setup](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..2v5iOUd0bqFe1Zyl6wy3xUhvbP9rHrZK1Vhe76fmdLA) ![live](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..ApU78AfkcJNGIYpGiTnNl3Sz7JOcbUba1-gMy5IasQM) ![question sheet](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..Hn3WGcvLSIzVwUZic_0MYdu1mYxwEeCcDW-YraKcMgM) ![results](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..yLlZxpU22nJTDj1q76au5jkR8quXJIrnXdWCYds8KTo) Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/81a0c3e751744b62a24767a3055d80f7 Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/81a0c3e751744b62a24767a3055d80f7?variant=devin Requested by: @LissanKoirala ---

author: s1lent4gnt
body:
## Title

fix(utils): make bimanual lifecycle cleanup fail-safe

## Summary / Motivation

`BimanualMixin` currently connects both arms sequentially without safely undoing a partial startup if either connection fails. Its disconnection also stops after the first exception, potentially leaving the other arm connected or torque-enabled.

This PR makes bimanual lifecycle handling atomic and best-effort across robots and teleoperators. Failed startup releases both arms while preserving the original error, and disconnection remains safe after partial startup or repeated calls.

## Related issues

- Fixes / Closes: #4529
- Related: None

## What changed

- Roll back both arms when either arm fails during `connect()`.
- Clean the right arm first after failed startup because it may be partially initialized.
- Preserve the original connection exception while logging cleanup failures.
- Always attempt to disconnect both arms, even if one fails.
- Make `disconnect()` safe after partial startup and on repeated calls.
- Ignore `DeviceNotConnectedError` during cleanup because an arm may already be disconnected or may never have connected.
- Add `_disconnect_arm_after_failed_connect()` as an override point for hardware requiring stronger failure cleanup.
- Remove the bimanual-level `check_if_not_connected` guard from `disconnect()`. A partially connected device reports `is_connected=False` while still owning resources that must be released.
- Add focused lifecycle tests in `tests/utils/test_bimanual.py`.
- No user migration is required.

## How was this tested (or how to run locally)

Tests cover:

- Left-arm connection failure.
- Right-arm connection failure.
- Right-before-left rollback order.
- Preservation of the original error when rollback fails.
- Continued disconnection when one arm fails.
- Partial and repeated cleanup.
- Hardware-specific failed-startup cleanup hooks.

Run locally:

```bash
uv run --frozen pytest tests/utils/test_bimanual.py -q
uv run --frozen pytest tests/utils -q
pre-commit run --files src/lerobot/utils/bimanual.py tests/utils/test_bimanual.py
```

Results:

- 6 focused bimanual tests passed.
- 207 utility tests passed, 5 skipped.
- Formatting, Ruff, mypy, Bandit, and other targeted pre-commit checks passed.

Manual hardware validation:

- Tested on a physical bimanual reBot B601 setup.
- Verified a failed bimanual startup releases the arm that connected successfully.

## Checklist (required before merge)

- [x] Linting/formatting run (`pre-commit run -a`)
- [x] All tests pass locally (`pytest`)
- [x] Documentation updated (not required; no user-facing configuration changed)
- [ ] CI is green
- [ ] Community Review: I have reviewed another contributor's open PR and linked it here: #

## Reviewer notes

- Please focus on partial-startup rollback, repeated-disconnect behavior, and preservation of the original connection exception.
- `disconnect()` intentionally has no connection-state decorator because cleanup must work in every lifecycle state.
- `_disconnect_arm_after_failed_connect()` allows motorized followers to enforce stronger safety behavior, such as disabling torque regardless of their normal disconnect configuration.
- Anyone in the community is free to review the PR.

author: ubeast
body:
**Problem:** when the linter anchors on a stray `REF*GS*` deep in transaction data because the file has no GS functional-group envelope, it reported `isa.separator-count-high` — describing the symptom (too many separators in the run), not the problem (the ISA segment has no GS header).

**Change:** the `> 16` branch now emits `isa.no-functional-group`, leading with the structural fact:

> a `b'GS*'` sequence sits 119 byte(s) past the ISA tag, but 19 element separator(s) precede it — an ISA header has 16, so this is not the functional-group header. No GS envelope bounds the ISA segment (the match is inside a later segment), or `b'*'` occurs inside ISA06/ISA08 data.

`isa.separator-count-low` (`< 16`) is unchanged — that case genuinely is about the ISA segment itself being deficient.

Pre-1.0 rename (no external consumers yet). 34 tests pass; `design.md` and generated `diagnostics.md` updated.

author: jeffresc
body:
Closes #430

## Summary

The `recycle_mode` comment in `config.example.yaml` said `snapshot_rollback` is "much faster on storage without linked clones" and "requires snapshot-capable storage", but did not state what happens on storage that cannot snapshot at all. Raw disks and raw-on-NFS support neither linked clones nor snapshots, so an operator could reasonably expect recycling there — where in fact every clone-time snapshot fails and the VM silently falls back to the destroy path.

This clarifies the comment: it lists LINSTOR among the snapshot-capable backends and states plainly that snapshotless storage (raw, raw-on-NFS) is not supported and falls back to destroy, so no recycling happens.

## Changes

- `config.example.yaml`: expand the `recycle_mode: snapshot_rollback` comment with the storage requirement and the silent destroy fallback.

author: jiaweine
body:
## Goal
Remove the measured async event-loop starvation caused by many short synchronous EventStore writes, without weakening durability, hash-chain order, realtime sink semantics, or plugin compatibility.

## Why this target
Merged #44 measured EventStore at ~86% of steady-state writer transactions (27.781 writer tx/task). Merged #45 then showed the apparent PTC latency was scheduler delay: `ptc._one` p99 ~0.104ms and local tools were tiny, while 10ms heartbeat event-loop lag reached p50 ~605ms / p99 ~1365ms. Ordinary synchronous EventStore append remained the largest measured leaf wall share.

## Runtime design
- add optional `append_grouped()` only on the built-in `BundledEventStore`; the base EventStore/plugin contract remains unchanged
- sinkless Engine emits await grouped persistence; realtime sink runs keep the existing append -> sink ordering
- one loop-local worker preserves enqueue order and drains bounded batches of at most 64 requests
- run SQLite group transactions via `asyncio.to_thread`, so durable writer work does not freeze unrelated async tool/reasoning tasks
- resolve each caller only after the shared SQLite transaction has committed
- same-session requests advance one transaction-local hash-chain tail in enqueue order
- if a shared batch fails, roll it back then retry requests individually off-loop so one malformed session/payload does not poison unrelated callers
- caller cancellation is deferred until queued durability is known; worker cancellation explicitly resolves submitted vs not-yet-submitted requests instead of allowing ambiguous late commits or leaked pending Futures
- checkpoint/checkpoint-audit writes remain outside this grouping change

## Invariants/tests
- a separate EventStore instance sees grouped rows immediately after `await` returns
- same-session grouped calls retain contiguous seq/hash order
- 130 same-session calls are bounded into 64 + 64 + 2 transactions without reordering
- synthetic 120ms persistence work does not freeze a 20ms event-loop heartbeat
- cancelling a caller after enqueue yields a durable row before `CancelledError` is observed
- a failed mixed group rolls back then isolates good/bad requests
- realtime sink never uses grouped path
- plain/custom EventStore without grouped API keeps legacy behavior

## Final same-run A/B
3 alternating experiments, 64 sessions × 4 event rounds, same process/runner:
- writer transactions: 256 legacy -> 4 grouped; ratio 0.0156 (98.44% reduction)
- median wall: 0.2002s -> 0.0166s; ratio 0.0829
- synchronized completion p99: 49.332ms -> 3.487ms; ratio 0.0707
- event-loop p99 lag: 46.424ms -> 0.656ms; ratio 0.0141
- all event sequences/hash chains valid; 0 failures

## Steady-state writer profile
32 concurrent tasks:
- total writer transactions: 361 = 11.281/task, down from #44's 32.312/task
- EventStore transactions: 215 = 6.719/task, down from #44's 27.781/task
- grouped ordinary events: 37 transactions = 1.156/task
- checkpoint+audit remains separate at 3.562/task
- 0 unattributed transactions / 0 failures

## Full runtime pressure
All levels 1/8/32/64/120/240 completed with 0 failures. Current hosted-runner sample:
- 32: 51.902 tasks/s, p99 0.6163s
- 64: 52.741 tasks/s, p99 1.1407s
- 120: 39.156 tasks/s, p99 2.9125s
- 240: 52.014 tasks/s, p99 4.1948s

These absolute hosted-runner numbers are not treated as guaranteed production percentages; the same-process A/B and deterministic transaction-count reduction are the primary performance evidence.

## Independent event-loop profile
120 tasks on a separate runner:
- 58.06 tasks/s; task p99 1.9149s
- event-loop lag p50 10.253ms / p99 324.134ms, versus #45 baseline p50 ~604.6ms / p99 ~1365.5ms
- heartbeat samples increased from 7 to 34
- `ptc.execute` fell to 34.767ms/task total and p99 32.183ms/call, while `ptc._one` remains ~0.476ms/task / p99 0.149ms
- actual local tools remain sub-millisecond per task

This confirms group commit removes most of the scheduler starvation previously misattributed to PTC. The remaining p99 event-loop tail is the next optimization target.

## Validation
Final head `956c9354` passes regression, Python 3.14 compatibility, browser E2E, bootstrap A/B, group-commit A/B, writer-stage profile, full pressure, independent runtime-profile, security, packaging, container and CodeQL.

author: jackculpan
body:
## Why

`server.json` in the app repo pointed at `jackculpan/awardtravelfinder`, which is **private**. That means:

- The official MCP registry listing links to a 404 for everyone but the owner.
- Glama cannot index it at all — it needs a public repo.
- Cline and the awesome lists both require a public repo URL.

It was also a personal account rather than the company.

## What changed

- **`server.json` moves here**, under the company namespace **`com.awardtravelfinder/mcp`** instead of `io.github.jackculpan/awardtravelfinder`, pointing at this public repo. Version bumped 0.1.0 → 3.0.0 to match `Mcp::ServerFactory::SERVER_VERSION`, and the bogus `"subfolder": "mcp-server"` (a path that never existed) is dropped.
- **Repo renamed** `award-travel-finder-plugin` → `mcp`. GitHub's redirects are permanent while we hold the old name in the org, so existing `/plugin marketplace add AwardTravelFinder/award-travel-finder-plugin` installs keep resolving. New copy uses `AwardTravelFinder/mcp`.
- README reframed from "plugin repo" to "public home for every AI/MCP surface", with a support contact.

## Namespace

`com.awardtravelfinder` is DNS-verified, so it is independent of whichever GitHub org or account we use, and it presents as the company in every downstream aggregator that ingests from the registry. Publishing is blocked on one TXT record at the apex — the registry rejects the record under a selector.

All four flagged calls started the flow with `data` prefilled, which no user can do. Split into `async_init`, assert the form, then `async_configure`.

Three of them followed an `async_init` that had already opened the form and then threw that flow away to start a second one. They now continue the flow they opened. In `test_user_errors` that also means the recovery happens in the same flow, which is what a user does after seeing the error.

author: stephenberry
body:
`glz::tuple` was a refactor of [tuplet](https://github.com/codeinred/tuplet), which is not MIT licensed. This replaces it with a new implementation behind the same API, leaving no third-party lineage in the header.

### Design

Each element lives in its own `elem<I, T>` base, so `get<I>` is a single always-inlined `static_cast` to a base rather than an N-candidate `operator[]` overload set. The element type comes from `__type_pack_element` where available, with a portable deduction fallback (`GLZ_DISABLE_TYPE_PACK_ELEMENT` forces it). Nothing is recursive, so cost grows linearly with element count.

### Compile time

Apple clang 21, minimum of interleaved runs:

| Workload | Change |
| --- | --- |
| 40 tuples × 40 reference elements (`tie` + `get`) | −41% |
| 64 tuples × 32 elements | −36% |
| full `glaze.hpp` TU, 12 structs × 20 members | −1% |
| full `glaze.hpp` TU, 8 structs × 48 members | −1% to −3% |

### Runtime

Unchanged. At `-O2` the object file is identical in size and the instruction stream diffs clean against the old implementation. Debug objects are ~1.6% smaller, since `get` no longer calls through `operator[]`.

### Header move

The implementation lives at `glaze/core/tuple.hpp`. `glaze/tuplet/tuple.hpp` forwards to it and is deprecated. `glz::tuplet` keeps `make_tuple`, `forward_as_tuple`, `tuple_cat` and `convert`; its internal metaprogramming helpers (`tag`, `type_list`, `base_list`, `tuple_elem`, ...) are gone.

### GLZ_NO_UNIQUE_ADDRESS ordering

`GLZ_NO_UNIQUE_ADDRESS` tested the standard `[[no_unique_address]]` before `[[msvc::no_unique_address]]`. The MSVC ABI accepts the standard spelling but gives it no layout effect, so testing it first can select the inert form and silently drop the empty member optimization. The MSVC spelling is now tested first, with a static assertion guarding it in the new test. This may shrink `glz::tuple`, `glz::lazy_document` and `glz::ordered_map` on MSVC.

### Testing

New `tests/tuple_test` (44 tests) covers construction, CTAD, traits, `get` value category and constness, reference elements, assignment, comparison, `for_each`/`any`/`all`, `apply`, `make_tuple`/`forward_as_tuple`/`tie`/`tuple_cat`/`convert`, and JSON/BEVE round trips. Full suite passes on clang (libc++, ASan + UBSan), GCC 14 and GCC 15, with both element-lookup paths.

Feature macros `glaze_v8_3_0_tuple` and `glaze_v8_3_0_msvc_no_unique_address` assume the next release is 8.3.0.

author: arrdel
body:
## Summary

Adds a `cascade()` scorer: it runs scorers in the order given and stops at the first that settles a sample, so an expensive grader model only runs on the samples that cheaper scorers (exact match, symbolic equivalence) did not settle.

This implements the design proposed by @Mamiglia in #5054 and converged in that thread. The concrete motivation there is `inspect_evals/math`, which attaches three scorers that report three disagreeing accuracies and always calls the grader model; a cascade gives one score to report and skips the grader on samples exact match already settled.

## Behavior

- Scorers are passed as keyword arguments so each stage is named explicitly; `**scorers` preserves call order, which is the order stages run in.
- A stage settles the sample when `value_to_float(score) >= threshold` (default `1.0`, i.e. `CORRECT`), and the cascade short-circuits.
- A stage that declines (`None`) or is unscored (`nan`) is skipped.
- If no stage settles, the last stage that produced a real score is returned. If every stage declined, the result is `Score.unscored()`.
- The returned score carries `decided_by` in metadata, naming the deciding stage.

## Notes for reviewers

- Metrics are fixed to `accuracy()` + `stderr()` rather than inherited from the sub-scorers the way `multi_scorer` does. `value_to_float` warns and returns `0` for list/dict values, so cascade is intended for scalar `CORRECT`/`INCORRECT`-style scorers, which is documented on the function. Happy to switch to sub-scorer metric inheritance if that is preferred.
- Only the deciding stage's score is recorded, not each stage's, since stages are invoked directly. The `decided_by` metadata identifies which stage decided.

## Test plan

- `tests/scorer/test_cascade.py`: short-circuit on first settle, fall-through to the last scored stage, decline-skip, unscored-skip, both sides of the threshold boundary, metadata preservation, single stage, and an end-to-end task eval asserting the `cascade` score, its metrics, and `decided_by`.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `mypy` pass on the new files. Full `tests/scorer/test_cascade.py` is green (10 passed).

### AI tooling

Authored with Cursor.

### Agent review

Reviewed by Claude Opus 4.8 in a single fresh-context pass (separate agent, no prior conversation), which also ran `ruff`, `mypy`, and the test suite. Findings:

- CHANGELOG entry referenced an issue number and exceeded the length guideline. Fixed: reduced to one outcome-focused sentence with no issue number.
- `@scorer` hardcodes `accuracy`/`stderr` instead of inheriting sub-scorer metrics like `multi_scorer`. Acceptable and documented as scalar-only; called out under Notes above for maintainer input.
- Individual stage scores are not recorded, only the decided score. Intended; noted above.
- A stage cannot be named `threshold` (reserved parameter). Documented in the docstring.
- No blocking issues; all loop paths (settle, fall-through, all-declined, threshold boundary) verified empirically.

author: aniruddhaadak80
body:
## Why this change is needed

When `api_url` includes a path prefix (common in self-hosted deployments behind nginx or other reverse proxies), `_build_url` dropped the prefix because `urljoin` with a leading-slash relative reference replaces the entire base path.

Example: `urljoin("http://host/firecrawl/", "/v2/search")` → `http://host/v2/search` (prefix lost).

This breaks all self-hosted deployments exposed under a non-root path. Reported in #4339.

## What behavior changed

- **`apps/python-sdk/firecrawl/v2/utils/http_client.py`**: Replaced `urljoin(base_str, endpoint)` with `urlunparse`-based path combination for relative endpoints. Now parses `api_url`, appends the endpoint path to the base path via `f"{base_path}/{ep_path}"`, and reconstructs with `urlunparse` preserving `scheme`, `netloc`, `query`, and `fragment`. This fixes both the prefix loss and the raw-concatenation edge case where `api_url` contains query/fragment (cubic P2). Removed unused `urljoin` import.
- **`apps/python-sdk/firecrawl/__tests__/unit/v2/utils/test_http_client.py`**: New test file with 9 regression tests covering path-prefix preservation, trailing slashes, relative endpoints without leading slash, absolute URLs (same/different host), and protocol-relative URLs.

## Exact tests / checks ran

```
py -m pytest apps/python-sdk/firecrawl/__tests__/unit/v2/utils/test_http_client.py -v
# 9 passed

py -m pytest apps/python-sdk/firecrawl/__tests__/unit/v2/utils/ -v
# 111 passed in 1.21s (102 existing + 9 new)
```

No harness needed — SDK-only unit tests.

## Configuration, migration, security, or deployment impact

None. SDK-only change, no environment, migration, or deployment impact. No credentials in commits. Backwards-compatible — default `api_url` (`https://api.firecrawl.dev`) unchanged; only self-hosted prefix deployments gain correct behavior.

## Before / After

| `api_url` | `endpoint` | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| `https://example.com/firecrawl` | `/v2/search` | `https://example.com/v2/search` | `https://example.com/firecrawl/v2/search` |
| `https://example.com/proxy/firecrawl` | `/v2/scrape` | `https://example.com/v2/scrape` | `https://example.com/proxy/firecrawl/v2/scrape` |
| `https://api.firecrawl.dev` | `/v2/scrape` | `https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/scrape` | `https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/scrape` (unchanged) |

Fixes #4339

author: jeremyerard
body:
Raising the socket timeout to 900s (#30) unblocked ingestion but did not make
it cheap, and the cost grows with the graph. This removes the cost.

graphiti-core builds only range + fulltext indexes for FalkorDB, so its entity
dedup runs, once per extracted entity:

    MATCH (n:Entity) WHERE n.group_id IN $group_ids
    WITH n, (2 - vec.cosineDistance(n.name_embedding, vecf32($v)))/2 AS score
    WHERE score > $min_score ... ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT $limit

a full scan of every Entity with a 1024-dim cosine per node, then a sort. LIMIT
bounds what comes BACK, not what is scanned, so NODE_DEDUP_CANDIDATE_LIMIT does
not help. At 25-50 extracted entities per episode that is tens of thousands of
vector comparisons per ingest.

Verified by downloading and reading 0.29.3, the latest release: identical query
at the same graph_queries.py:158, still no db.idx.vector call anywhere in the
package. Upgrading does not fix this, so we route around it.

We already did exactly this for RELATES_TO.fact_embedding, whose own docstring
records the same O(N) scan costing ~28s on a 7k-edge graph. The node half was
never done. IndexedFalkorSearchOperations overrides node_similarity_search to
call db.idx.vector.queryNodes, and IndexedFalkorDriver installs it via the
driver's existing _search_ops seam -- a subclass, not a monkeypatch.

Deliberate limits:
  - A populated SearchFilters falls through to graphiti's own query. The index
    procedure cannot take those composed WHERE clauses, and dropping them
    silently would WIDEN the search rather than speed it up.
  - Any failure -- no index, or a FalkorDB build without vector support --
    falls back to the scan. Slower is acceptable; failing an ingest over a
    missing index is not.
  - The index is ensured on the INGEST path, not in _search_fast. The edge
    index serves search; this one serves dedup. The provenance search contract
    caught that placement error and it was right to.
  - The graph handle is selected ONCE and shared with the provenance anchor
    write, so the ingest contract's single-select assertion still holds rather

## Summary

The staleness sweep no competitor ships: a note whose verified_at ages past its class horizon is demoted one authority level in recall (never below casual, announced beside the hit) until someone re-verifies it. Absence of a clock is counted as its own honest state, never as fresh or stale.

python3 tools/test_bm_vault_staleness.py exits 0; tools/test_bm_vault.py still 36 OK. Real vault census: 842 notes, 187 fresh, 0 stale, 366 unverified-no-clock, 289 exempt, arithmetic cross-checked against the 202 dated verified-by notes.

Zero stale today means the demotion path fires only in fixtures until the corpus ages; the boundary tests are the guarantee it will fire honestly when it does.

## Summary

- preserve the caller's current CUDA device while freeing device allocations and streams
- preserve the worker's current CUDA device while releasing pooled Disco CUDA IPC allocations, including exceptional paths
- add multi-GPU regressions for NDArray garbage collection and stream destruction
- skip the three default `fast_topk_clusters` correctness cases because the FlashInfer reference omits an input bounds check and does not initialize or reset its shared threshold bin; strict registry import coverage remains enabled

author: curtisgalloway
body:
Adds `ox-review`, a Claude Code skill that turns `ox` into a second-opinion code
reviewer, plus a `--skill` flag on all four tools so an agent that only has them
on `PATH` can find the runbook.

## What the skill does

`.claude/skills/ox-review/` is a runbook and three stdlib-only Python 3.9+
scripts — the same floor the rest of oxbox holds to, so they run wherever the
tools do.

| | |
|---|---|
| `scripts/preflight.py` | Finds ox, picks the current survey manifest, asks `ox --dry-run` where it *would* send, runs the exposure gate. Exit 0 ready+public, 10 needs a human, 1 cannot run. |
| `scripts/exposure.py` | Answers "can a stranger already clone this?" Verdicts: `public`, `not-public`, `unknown`, `no-remote`, `not-a-repo`. Only `public` clears. |
| `scripts/oxreview.py` | Runs one review batch, serialized machine-wide by a directory lock, with the measured 120-second retry floor. |

The flow is: preflight → exposure gate → batch the diff (≤5 files / ~40 KB) →
one subagent per batch → each verifies its findings against the real source →
one ranked list. It produces findings, never changes; `--mode review` returns no
patch by design, and model-produced patches still belong in the `oxseed` /
`oxapply` / `oxbox` sandbox flow.

## Why the fan-out stops at the request queue

Subagents fan out, but every one of them sends through `oxreview.py`'s lock, so
exactly one request is ever on the wire. That is not caution, it is the
measurement already recorded in AGENTS.md: the free cloaked listing shares one
upstream quota across everyone using it, so **concurrency is the trigger, not
volume**. A serial queue with a 120-second floor cleared every 429 within three
attempts; three concurrent requests were refused immediately.

So the fan-out buys *verification* concurrency, not more requests. While one
batch is on the wire the others are reading source and checking claims, and none
of the raw review dumps land in the orchestrator's context. `oxreview.py` offers
no bypass and does not expose `--force`.

The verification step is the other half. The model's characteristic failure is
output that looks right and is subtly wrong in both directions — a real bug
described with the wrong mechanism, and a confident finding about code that does
not exist. Refuted findings stay in the report rather than being dropped: how
often the reviewer is wrong is half of what a survey is measuring.

## Why the exposure gate probes instead of matching hostnames

Everything `ox` sends is logged and shared with whoever owns the model, and the
free cloaked listings only work with prompt logging switched *on*. Sending code
anyone can already clone costs nothing new. Sending code nobody outside can read
**publishes it**, permanently, and nothing unpublishes it.

A hostname cannot answer that question. `github.example.com` looks exactly like
`github.com`, and an enterprise install, a renamed repo, or a self-hosted
Forgejo are all indistinguishable by pattern. So the gate makes a real
unauthenticated request carrying no credential of any kind — `git info/refs`,
plus the provider API on GitHub/GitLab/Codeberg/Bitbucket/Gitea for a more
precise report. The API table only buys better reporting; the anonymous-clone
probe is what decides, and unlisted hosts still get it.

`unknown` sits on the same side of the line as `not-public` — a probe that could
not reach the host has not cleared anything. Uncommitted and unpushed changes
are deliberately *not* blockers: reviewing work before you push it is the point.

## `--skill` on all four tools

Prints SKILL.md with the runbook's script paths rewritten to wherever that
install found the skill. Document to stdout, provenance to stderr, so
`ox --skill > runbook.md` gives a clean file. Lookup uses the same two-location
rule as `jail.sb`: beside the script, or `../share/oxbox/`. `oxbox` and `oxseed`
gained real usage blocks, since neither had a working `--help` for the flag to
appear in.

Per the packaging rules, `find_skill`/`print_skill` is duplicated in all four
tools on purpose, like `VERSION` — each tool is a standalone script. What makes
four copies safe is the check: wiretest runs `--skill` on all four and asserts
identical stdout, a zero exit, and a provenance line naming the tool you
actually ran.

Supporting changes: `packaging/nfpm.yaml` ships the skill to
`/usr/share/oxbox/ox-review`; the release smoke test runs `--skill` on all four
installed tools and `cmp`s them; guardtest gained 4 cases and wiretest 3; README,
AGENTS.md and `.gitignore` updated.

## Version

All four tools move 0.1.0 → 0.2.0 together. `v0.1.0` is already tagged and
released and points at the current tip of main, so leaving the constant alone
would put `--skill` on main under a version whose published .deb has neither the
flag nor the asset. The release workflow refuses a tag that disagrees with
`ox --version`, so the bump had to happen before the next tag either way.

## Verification

macOS 15 (darwin, seatbelt backend, normal user uid 501):

- `guardtest.py` — **26/26**, 0 skipped
- `wiretest.py` — **47/47**
- `jailtest.py` in the jail — **13/13**, 0 skipped

Linux (bubblewrap 0.9.0, running as root), from the branch's earlier session:

- guardtest 26/26, wiretest 47/47
- jailtest 10/11 — the single FAIL is `fs read: /etc/shadow`, which reproduces
  identically on pristine `origin/main`. That is uid 0 bypassing DAC, not a leak
  and not from this branch. It cannot arise on macOS: `oxbox`'s
  `sensitive_paths()` adds `/etc/shadow` only when `sys.platform != "darwin"`,
  so the macOS run is a genuine 13/13 rather than a silent skip.

Also checked by hand: all four `--skill` outputs are byte-identical
(`1b91ad21…`), the provenance line names the tool that ran, an installed-prefix
layout (`bin/` + `share/oxbox/ox-review`) resolves and rewrites correctly, and a
prefix with the asset removed refuses cleanly with exit 1 while naming both
search locations.

Windows (real host: Python 3.13, PowerShell 7.6, ANSI codepage 1252) — this is
where the branch had a genuine bug, which CI caught and a fifth commit fixes:

`--skill` printed the runbook through text-mode `sys.stdout`, which on Windows
encodes in the locale codepage and translates newlines. cp1252 renders
SKILL.md's 26 em dashes as `0x97`, so `ox --skill > runbook.md` there produced a
file no UTF-8 reader could open — and `guardtest` died on the decode with a
traceback rather than a red line, taking the rest of the section with it.

All four tools now write the document as UTF-8 bytes through
`sys.stdout.buffer`, the stdout counterpart of the `write_lf` helper that
already exists for exactly this hazard on the file side. macOS and Linux are
byte-identical either way, which is why only CI saw it. `guardtest` gains an
explicit assertion on the bytes — no CRLF, decodes as UTF-8, em dashes intact —
so the contract states itself and a regression reports as one FAIL instead of
aborting the suite. AGENTS.md records the rule beside its `write_lf` sibling.

Verified on the Windows host rather than by CI round-trip: a pristine checkout
of the parent commit reproduces the traceback at the same byte and offset; with
the fix, guardtest is **20/20** (3 skipped, no jail backend) and wiretest
**47/47** there. Mutation-checked on that host too — the new guardtest against
the old `ox` reports `crlf=True decoded=False` and the suite still completes.
The printed document is byte-identical to the macOS one once the install path it
rewrites is normalized.

All six CI jobs now pass: guards on ubuntu / macos / windows / the 3.9 floor,
and jail on ubuntu / macos.

Every new test assertion was mutation-checked — break the behaviour in the tool,
confirm that case and only that case goes red.

Never exercised against a live venue: no API key was available, so all ox-facing
paths were tested with `--dry-run` and a stub `ox`.

## The skill's first live run — and the bug it found

Run end-to-end against a real venue with the real survey manifest
(`oxbox-ma

body:
Closes #132796

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the light-theme message queue painted one pixel beyond the connected Goal, creating visible steps along both sides of the composer stack.

## Why This Change Was Made

The queue and Goal already share identical 768 px layout rectangles. The mismatch came from the queue's external 1 px light-theme ring while the connected Goal had no external side stroke. The fix gives connected Goal rows matching left/right strokes without adding a horizontal divider, and extends the existing full-stack browser regression to cover bounds, radii, attached surfaces, and the painted side edge.

## User Impact

Progress, neutral queued messages, Goal, and composer now read as one aligned stack in the light theme. Dark-theme rendering is unchanged.

## Evidence

Equivalent neutral/pending queue state and 1440×1000 viewport. “Before” disables only the new Goal side strokes; “after” uses the production CSS. Every image was visually inspected before upload.

| Theme | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Light | ![Light theme before, neutral queue](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f30a945-0caa-4de2-9606-5d68d9704034) | ![Light theme after, neutral queue](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/521dd1cc-2477-4d27-a4f8-4ef38e12d373) |
| Dark | ![Dark theme before, neutral queue](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/191e5ae0-c077-42ec-b244-8c66c66790b7) | ![Dark theme after, neutral queue](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/08caeed5-2855-438a-bd87-e9bd6dccc649) |

Measured together at viewport 1652×686: progress, queue, Goal, and composer are all `left=571`, `right=1339`, `width=768`. Computed top radii are `25px`, `25px`, `0px`, `25px`; all side borders are `1px`. Before the fix, Goal had no shadow while queue painted a 1 px outer ring. After the fix, Goal paints matching `-1px` and `+1px` side strokes.

Focused automated checks were intentionally not run locally because `.lanes/composer-stack-prompt.md` prohibits local tests, builds, and typechecks for this lane; CI remains the execution gate.

Codex autoreview (`gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning, branch against `origin/main`): clean, zero accepted/actionable findings.

## Scope Gate

- `ui/src/styles/chat/composer-queue.css`: owns the queue/Goal connection and its light-theme outline; adds only the missing connected Goal side strokes.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-responsive.browser.test.ts`: the existing owner-boundary scenario renders all four surfaces together; now asserts bounds, radii, attached backgrounds, and the Goal side strokes.
- No harness, snapshot, generated, lockfile, config, or documentation files are included.
- Production LOC: `+11/-0`. Test LOC: `+43/-0`.

## Shared Producer / Named Consumers

The shared queue/Goal connection rule changed. Nominal consumers checked together: `.session-progress-card--composer`, `.chat-queue`, `.agent-chat__goal`, and `.agent-chat__input`. The selector applies only when Goal directly follows `.chat-queue` or `.agent-chat__progress-float`; standalone Goal and dark theme are unaffected.

## Test-Audit Gate

- Observable invariant: all attached composer surfaces share outer left/right edges and computed background.
- Credible regression: restoring `content-box` progress sizing, narrowing the goal float, or assigning a divergent attached surface fails these assertions.
- Existing coverage gap: it checked only the progress card's width and icon axes, not all four surface bounds/backgrounds.
- Production seam: none.

author: berketpbs
body:
The last number in the query path that had never been measured. It could not be until now: the stream was populated on **one write path of seven** (#66, #67), so any weight put on it was a weight over an empty table.

`anamnesis eval --embed` embeds the corpus page by page and every question with the same model, through the same call the server makes. Off by default, as it is in production — the three SQL streams should not need a model download to say anything about themselves.

## What it earns

```
retrieval   fts 0.800/0.800   entity 0.600/0.600   links 0.300/0.400   vectors 0.403/0.700
crowded     fts 0.900/0.933   entity 0.267/0.267   links 0.256/0.333   vectors 0.308/0.533
```

**Second-best recall of the four streams in both**, well ahead of entity and links. And the measure that says more than either: with the stream on, the questions **only** full text can answer drop from **3 → 1** on the retrieval suite and **8 → 2** on the crowded one. It independently reaches most of what full text alone was reaching.

Its weight stays at `1.0`. Among the best-scoring settings, 0.5 and 1.0 appear alike; nothing separates them.

## Why nothing else changes

Twelve of 6048 settings do beat what ships — 1.000/1.000 on both suites against 1.000/0.967 — and **every one of them needs embeddings on *and* a candidate pool of ten rather than thirty**.

The suites are ten and twenty-two pages, where ten candidates and thirty are nearly the same request. On a real wiki a shallower pool is exactly where recall would go. That is a measurement these corpora cannot make, so it is not one to act on. Without `--embed`, 0 of 6048 settings beat what ships.

## Two things fell out of running it

**The acceptance rule was wrong at the ceiling.** It demanded a rise on *every* suite — written before either could reach a perfect score. Once `retrieval` sat at 1.000 nothing could raise it, so a setting taking `crowded` from 0.967 to 1.000 was reported as no improvement at all: six thousand rows, none accepted, and the grid was not the thing at fault. It now asks that nothing falls anywhere and something rises. Both cases are tested.

**A sweep with embeddings would have made fifty thousand model calls for twenty-five distinct answers.** Query embeddings are memoized for the run; the corpus is embedded once and reused across the grid for the same reason. 6048 settings in 3m20s.

## Verification

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` — 614 tests, green. Measured against a real all-MiniLM-L6-v2 downloaded by the opt-in path itself.

author: yhan-sun
body:
## Scope and revisions

This PR fixes only the first-stage Path State Machine acceptance gaps. It does not add DPLPMTUD runtime integration, metrics infrastructure, NAT strategies, UI changes, version changes, tags, signing, or release changes.

- Base: `6c618e2fa5b5ddec855d56856dbc1c4074158bf3`
- Head: `2638b0594e108ff26e2e61f2ce16222efe1a892c`
- Branch: `fix/path-state-machine-acceptance-20260830`

## Exact Relay blackhole root cause

Primary artifact: [Actions run 33264591658](https://github.com/yhan-sun/p2wlan/actions/runs/33264591658). A first bounded-wait implementation exposed the final missing piece in [superseded-SHA attempt 2](https://github.com/yhan-sun/p2wlan/actions/runs/33270318539/attempts/2): after `initiator_publish_probe_binding_writer_wait timeout_ms=250`, neither `writer_available` nor `writer_timeout` was ever emitted.

The long-lived blocker was not a reader guard held for three minutes. It was a fair `PeerManager.connections` writer waiter whose future and timeout were owned by the cooperatively-polled control-loop `slow_work` set.

The exact cycle was:

1. `run_relay_peer_probe_loop -> relay_probe_targets -> PeerManager.connections.read()` held the production Relay target snapshot when initiator publication ran.
2. `run_reserved_initiator_handshake -> try_stage_probe_session_binding` observed contention, then the old implementation queued `PeerManager.connections.write().await` inside a `FuturesUnordered<ControlEventWork>` future and yielded.
3. Tokio's writer-fair `RwLock` placed that writer ahead of all later readers.
4. The artifact had already queued a roster update (`poll_peers: 1 updated` at `19:28:57.031`, before daemon event processing at `19:28:57.924`). The serial loop selected `ControlEvent::PeerUpdated`, acquired the per-peer handshake arbiter, then entered `PeerManager.get_connection -> connections.read().await` behind the first queued writer.
5. The serial loop was now awaiting the later reader and could no longer poll the earlier `slow_work` writer future or its 250 ms timer. This is the cooperative polling inversion.
6. `/status` readers queued behind the same fair writer and eventually returned 503. Relay TCP keepalive stayed healthy because it does not need this map; no WireGuard session was published, so both `RelayPeerConfirmed` counts stayed zero.

Thus the call chain that initially held the read lock was the real Relay target scan; the call chain that made the wait permanent was `run_control_event_loop(PeerUpdated) -> get_connection -> connections.read().await` waiting behind the initiator's unpolled writer barrier.

## Lock order before and after

Before:

1. initiator acquired per-peer emit guard;
2. initiator acquired network epoch guard;
3. initiator tried the `connections` writer;
4. on contention it released epoch and emit, but retained the writer wait and timeout inside control-loop `slow_work`;
5. a later `PeerUpdated` control branch acquired the handshake arbiter and waited for a `connections` reader behind that writer;
6. the serial owner could no longer poll the earlier writer/timeout, starving setup and diagnostics indefinitely.

After:

1. canonical publication still acquires emit, then epoch, and performs only a nonblocking `connections` writer attempt;
2. on contention it releases epoch and emit immediately and marks the reservation `ProbeBindingRetryDeferred`, so `run_event_initiator_handshake` does not start an unrelated candidate-publication fallback;
3. the cooperative initiator future returns in the same poll that records contention;
4. an independently scheduled task, holding no emit, epoch, handshake-arbiter, connection, or other upper guard, races reservation cancellation against a 250 ms writer-availability bound;
5. writer availability or timeout removes the fair writer barrier, cancels only the exact current reservation owner, emits structured diagnostics, and bumps the shared path-setup watch edge; normal maintenance then starts a fresh transaction and revalidates generation/session state;
6. PeerLeft, generation cleanup, or owner replacement wins through the reservation watch/owner check: the old waiter exits without publishing a stale retry edge.

No unconditional sleep, topology timeout increase, ignored 503, or weakened NAT assertion was added.

## Relay-only retention

For a generation advance where old active is Direct, Direct is not retainable, and a confirmed Relay has `PathRetention::Relay`, the reducer atomically commits:

- active path: Relay;
- compatibility projection: `ConnectionState::Relay`;
- recovery: `Degraded { from: Direct, fallback: Some(Relay) }`;
- committed business-path mirror: the retained Relay identity stamped with the new generation.

It no longer projects `Unavailable`.

## Event-wide idempotency

`PathTransitionDecision` distinguishes `Applied`, `AcceptedObservation`, `Duplicate`, and typed rejection outcomes.

Durable typed receipts cover `PeerOnline`, `NetworkGenerationAdvanced`, `RelayPeerConfirmed`, directional `RelayBusinessUsable`, and `DirectCommitted`. Relay health uses a separate bounded identity `(owner_token, request_id)`.

- `Duplicate` returns before compatibility projection, side-effect closure, caches, health/candidate counters, timestamps, event rings, commit sequence, or business markers.
- A new typed health/business observation may be `AcceptedObservation` and execute once even when the path-state enum itself is unchanged.
- Exact replay becomes `Duplicate`; receipts are pruned when their generation/path identity is no longer current.

## New and changed regression tests

Relay liveness and cancellation:

- `relay_probe_snapshot_contention_detaches_writer_wait_unblocks_readers_and_reschedules_initiator`
- `detached_probe_binding_writer_wait_cancels_without_stale_reschedule`
- `initiator_publish_releases_epoch_while_connection_writer_is_contended`

The main concurrency test pauses the actual production `relay_probe_targets()` snapshot, directly polls the same cooperative initiator future, and fails if that future returns `Pending` after queuing the writer. It then queues a real status read behind the detached writer, proves emit/epoch guards are free, proves the 250 ms bound unblocks the status read while the Relay snapshot is still held, consumes the maintenance edge, and verifies a fresh reservation stages the Probe binding. This is not only a manually-held read-lock/release test.

Relay-only retention:

- `network_generation_relay_only_retention_falls_back_from_direct_to_relay`
- `candidate_refresh_relay_only_retention_commits_relay_fallback_mirror`

Idempotency and side effects:

- `observations_are_accepted_once_per_typed_identity_without_state_churn`
- `duplicate_path_events_preserve_revision_counters_timestamps_and_markers`
- `independent_relay_health_observations_apply_once_each`

These assert reducer state/revision plus health counters, candidate-pair counters, commit sequence, event ring, timestamps, and business markers.

## Commands executed and results

Final local Head verification:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — PASS
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — PASS
- `cargo test --workspace` — PASS; daemon lib 1164/1164, all workspace and doc tests passed
- targeted Relay liveness/cancellation, retention, reducer idempotency, PeerConnection mirror, and health-observation tests — PASS
- `git diff --check` — PASS
- `bash scripts/nat-sim/run-ci-topology.sh relay` — local macOS prerequisite failure before topology execution because GNU `timeout` is unavailable (exit 127); no test result was claimed from this invocation
- the same underlying Relay-only topology command used by the wrapper (`ROUNDS=1 MODE=relay-only LOSS=0 REORDER=0 STRICT_FILTERING=0 DIRECT_TIMEOUT_S=60 OVERLAY_TIMEOUT_S=90 OVERLAY_BURST=64 RELAY_COUNT=1`) — PASS; RelayConfirmed A/B 1/1, Direct A/B 0/0, overlay A/B 132/132, zero drop/replay/invalid, ready-to-usable 39 ms/1 ms

body:
Last of the four Phase 0 trust repairs.

## Dismiss was a blacklist

```ts
updated.dismissedSuggestions = [...(updated.dismissedSuggestions ?? []), sport]
```

One tap on "Not now" silenced that sport's calibration **permanently** — even as the evidence behind the suggestion kept getting stronger — with no way back short of clearing storage. Both `useMIMCalibration` and `useDOMSCalibration` had the identical bug.

Dismissal is now a **30-day snooze**, shared by both hooks through one tested utility:

- Re-snoozing restarts the clock rather than stacking duplicate entries.
- Expired entries are dropped on write, so the list cannot grow without bound.
- **Legacy dismissals migrate** to snoozes running from first read — old choices fade out instead of either lasting forever or all firing at once on upgrade. The athlete did say no once; that's respected, just not permanently.

## Empty states assumed a Garmin

Two empty states told *every* athlete to "Connect Garmin and sync" — including the ones wearing an Apple Watch, which the app already supports:

- `Dashboard.tsx:427` (readiness)
- `PerformanceChart.tsx:49` (performance trends)

Both now read "Connect your watch — Garmin or Apple — and sync…".

The places that genuinely mean Garmin are deliberately **left alone**: the workout push button, the EPOC provenance note, the Settings section header, the onboarding option card. There, Garmin is the truth, and genericising it would be its own kind of dishonesty. A test enforces the distinction rather than banning the word.

## Validation

- 2,805 tests pass (215 files) — eight new.
- `npm run build` clean.
- eslint clean on changed files except one `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warning in the calibration hooks, verified pre-existing on base. Untouched.

---

This completes Phase 0. Five of the audit's ten themes are closed, none of it depending on the redesign.

author: bohdankhrystov
body:
`TASK-120503`, under `STORY-1205` — round 1 of `/qa-cycle regression`.

**A harness repair under `ADR-0089` §4**: `docs/test-plan.md` only, no production code, and none may
change to satisfy it.

## The defect

Five cases across the `EPIC-04` and `EPIC-05` suites assume a device with **no finished duel**. That
holds under an `epic`-scoped round and is false under `regression`, where the CORE suite necessarily
plays duels on the only two browser profiles before those suites run. The cases were not wrong about
the product — they were unrunnable under a scope obliged to run them.

Both suites were authored on 2026-08-29 from merged sources and marked `> **Provisional**`.
`ADR-0090` §5 predicted exactly this: a merged decision proves what was *decided*, not what
*shipped*, so a suite authored that way is provisional until its first round. This is that round,
and the notes are deleted with it.

## Why `04-02` was urgent

Its old `expect` pinned the literal `−1 Duel coins`. `TASK-120501` fixed the sign-up write path in
this same round, so a round-2 retest against that stale literal would have gone red **on a product
that just improved** — inflating `B(2)` and risking a false `STOP_DIVERGING`. It now compares the
balance read before the claim against the one read after, which is what the case was always trying
to say.

## `05-03` was not passing

Round 1 recorded it green, but it passed only by a **silent deviation**: the tester checked a delta
between two readings instead of the absolute values the row named. A case that can only be passed by
not doing what it says is a broken case, not a passing one. The row now asks for the delta it
actually needs, plus agreement with each player's own `duel_result` season sum.

## Not weakened

The risk in a repair like this is rewriting a row into something that cannot fail — which is worse
than the broken row, because it is green forever (`ADR-0088` §2). Each rewritten row keeps a failure
condition that can be true:

| Case | What makes it red |
| --- | --- |
| `04-01` | the strip never reaches `<n> Duel coins`, or the duels screen shows its load-failure text — an account-less device being refused |
| `04-02` | the balance read before the claim differs, in any character, from the one read after |
| `05-01` | the `Leaderboard` control is missing, the ladder shows load-failure text, or `Back` fails to return to `Create a duel room` |
| `05-02` | the rendered self line disagrees with `GET /api/standings` for this device, in either direction |
| `05-03` | either player's second standing is not exactly one more or fewer than their first, or disagrees with their own `duel_result` season sum |

## One caveat the coder disclosed and the reviewer settled

`05-01`'s new wait target is the season line (a month name), used as a synchronisation marker. The
coder could not verify it is absent from the lobby — `web-client` source was outside its read budget
— and said so rather than implying otherwise. **The reviewer checked**: `seasonName()` lives in
`ladder-text.ts`, is imported only by `LadderScreen.tsx`, and is rendered nowhere else. The wait
cannot succeed before the ladder loads.

## Noted, not fixed

`05-04` pins L's post-duel standing at exactly `−1`, inherited from the same zero-baseline
assumption removed from `05-03`, so it likely carries the identical defect under a `regression`
scope. It is not one of the five and not in `verify:`, so it is correctly untouched here and filed
separately rather than folded in (`CLAUDE.md` rule 4).

The `Provisional` gate is case-sensitive (`grep -c Provisional`). The two real epic notes are
**deleted**; the generic template exemplar under *Per-epic suites* — which documents the convention
for suites not yet written — is lowercased to match the surrounding prose rather than removed.
Confirmed by the reviewer as deletion rather than three lowercasings, which would have satisfied the
grep while leaving both suites still marked provisional.

## Review

`pass`, no findings. Table shape intact (rows still parse to 7 `awk -F'|'` fields — several gates
are `awk` keyed on column position), and every `source` column unchanged.

author: danilodme-rgb
body:
O calendário deixava abrir um dia anterior e cadastrar atividade nele. Este PR fecha esse caminho, sem tirar o acesso ao histórico nem à cobrança das pendências.

## O que muda

Em qualquer data anterior a hoje:

- **"Nova atividade", "Imprevisto" e "Recalcular" ficam desabilitados**, com uma nota no lugar explicando o motivo. `formularioTarefa` e `fluxoImprevisto` também recusam a ação por conta própria, então o bloqueio não depende só do estado visual do botão.
- **A repetição por dias da semana e a cópia de dia descartam destinos anteriores a hoje** (`gerarDatas` filtra pelo dia corrente; a cópia ignora datas passadas), e os campos de data ganharam `min`, de modo que o seletor nem oferece um dia anterior.
- A lista vazia de um dia passado passa a dizer que nada foi programado, em vez de convidar a programar.

Em dias futuros, o horário inicial sugerido passa a ser `08:00`, em vez de um horário derivado do relógio de agora — que não fazia sentido para outro dia.

## O que continua liberado, de propósito

- **Consultar o histórico** e **resolver check-in/check-out em aberto** de dias anteriores. É por ali que o app cobra o que ficou pendente; travar isso deixaria a pergunta "você iniciou isso ontem?" sem resposta possível.
- **Copiar um dia passado** para os próximos, útil para repetir uma rotina que deu certo.
- **Hoje em qualquer horário**, inclusive um já vencido, para registrar algo que começou há pouco e não estava programado.

Efeito colateral assumido: não é mais possível lançar retroativamente uma atividade de ontem que ficou sem programar.

## Como testei

Em navegador, com relógio fixado em 29/08/2026 09:00:

| Cenário | Resultado |
| --- | --- |
| Ontem (28/08) e 20/08, aberto pelo calendário | botões desabilitados, nota visível |
| Clique forçado via evento nos botões desabilitados | nada abre; aviso "Este dia já passou — programe a partir de hoje." |
| Hoje e amanhã | tudo liberado; em amanhã o início sugerido vem `08:00` e o campo "repetir até" tem `min` no próprio dia |
| Copiar 24/08 (segunda passada) para segunda a sexta, até 04/09 | grava 31/08, 01, 02, 03 e 04/09 — nenhuma data entre 25 e 28/08 |

O fluxo completo do app (criar atividades, aviso de 5 minutos, check-in atrasado, check-out, imprevisto com recálculo, relatório e persistência após recarregar) continua passando, e os cinco modais seguem sem sobreposição nem rolagem interna em tela de 360px. Sem erros de console.
