author: le-polemil
body:
Closes #78

Sixième et dernière PR de la pile : **#82 → #83 → #84 → #85 → #86 → celle-ci**.
Dernier ticket de la **Vague 2**.

La capture de #52 écrivait **en aveugle** : un clic, une pastille, la tâche était
en base. On ne voyait pas ce qui avait été retenu et on ne pouvait rien corriger.

Surtout, **l'URL était perdue**. `titleFrom()` ne s'en servait que comme titre de
repli — le lien disparaissait donc dès qu'il y avait une sélection, c'est-à-dire
dans le cas le plus fréquent et le plus utile.

## Trois couches

**`task_attachments`** — une table et pas une colonne : une tâche porte plusieurs
liens, une issue et sa PR, un article et sa discussion. Le schéma `http(s)` est
contraint **en base** et pas seulement à la saisie : un `javascript:` entré par
l'API — un client tiers, une version future du front qui oublierait de valider —
finirait cliquable dans l'app web. Le front valide **aussi**, pour le message ;
la base valide **pour de bon**.

**Web** — des pastilles sous la carte, ouvertes en nouvel onglet avec
`rel="noopener noreferrer"`. Une tâche **sans** lien n'affiche rien du tout : pas
de pastille vide, pas de bouton. L'ajout vit dans le menu `⋯`. Chargement
paginé — le piège des 1000 lignes de #40 vaut ici aussi.

**Extension** — un formulaire relit la capture avant de l'écrire : titre, lien et
matrice préremplis et modifiables. Le brouillon vit dans `chrome.storage.session`
(une URL visitée n'a pas à traîner sur le disque, ni à survivre au navigateur).
Si `chrome.action.openPopup()` manque ou échoue, on retombe sur l'écriture
directe : une capture perdue en silence serait pire que l'absence de formulaire.

**Aucune permission ajoutée** : `storage` couvrait déjà `session`. Manifeste
1.1.0 → 1.2.0, permissions identiques, aucune autorisation d'hôte. La revue du
Web Store reste standard, comme le prévoit `work/publication-extension.md`.

## Deux défauts trouvés au navigateur

- **La destination retombait sur la première matrice.** L'entrée de menu annonce
  « Ajouter à « X » », mais `null` était transmis tel quel et le formulaire
  choisissait `boards[0]` — une destination que rien n'avait annoncée. Résolu
  dans le service worker, à la même source que le titre du menu.
- **Le brouillon perdait un champ sur deux.** `patchPending` faisait
  lire-puis-écrire : deux frappes rapprochées dans deux champs différents
  lisaient la même version, et la seconde écrasait la première. La fonction a été
  supprimée — le formulaire tient déjà le brouillon entier et l'écrit en entier.

## ⚠️ Migration

`apps/supabase/migrations/20260829180000_task_attachments.sql` est à appliquer
**en production avant** ce front — comme celles de #45, #39 et #50.

## Vérifications

`npm test` (146), `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run build:ext` : verts.

**Web**, sur le Supabase local : lien ajouté / visible / cliquable, `javascript:`
refusé **par le champ et par la base** (`23514` via l'API), RLS refusant d'écrire
pour un autre utilisateur (`42501`), plusieurs liens supprimés un à un, cascade au
vidage définitif, et une tâche sans lien strictement inchangée.

**Extension** : Chrome 151 refuse `--load-extension` et ne laisse pas attacher le
service worker. Le formulaire a donc été validé servi hors extension, avec un
bouchon `chrome.storage` fidèle et une **écriture réelle** dans Supabase — tâche
et lien créés dans « À trier » de la bonne matrice, brouillon survivant à une
fermeture. **Non vérifié par moi** : l'appel réel à `chrome.action.openPopup()` et
le chemin du menu contextuel. Le repli est le code de #52, inchangé et déjà en
production. Le détail est dans `work/stories/light/2026-08-29-pieces-jointes/dev.md`.

author: alsalahiahmed051-pixel
body:
## 1) 🚨 إصلاح تعطّل الموقع
كان الموقع يسقط بـ **"Application error: a client-side exception has occurred"**. شغّلت الموقع في متصفح حقيقي وأمسكت السبب: **ثلاثة اختلافات hydration** بين ما يرسله الخادم وما يبنيه المتصفح:

| السبب | الإصلاح |
|------|---------|
| `useStored` كان يقرأ `localStorage` أثناء أول رسم — فأي بيانات محفوظة (الوضع الليلي، المهام، الملف) تجعل رسم المتصفح مخالفًا للخادم | يرسم القيمة الأولية أولًا، ثم يتبنّى المحفوظ بعد التركيب |
| التحية والتاريخ ومؤشّر النصيحة كانت تُحسب من الساعة أثناء الرسم (وقت الخادم ≠ وقت الزائر) | انتقلت لما بعد التركيب |
| `@import` داخل `<style>` كانت علامات اقتباسه تُرمَّز على الخادم فقط | حُذف — الخط محمّل أصلًا عبر `<link>` |

**التحقّق في متصفح فعلي: أخطاء hydration من 40+ ← صفر.** ✅

## 2) 💰 مجاني أولًا + حدّ للمدفوع لا يمكن التلاعب به

**الترتيب صار: المجاني أولًا** (Groq → Gemini → OpenRouter)، والمدفوع (Anthropic) **آخر خيار فقط**، ولا يُستهلك الرصيد إلا عند نجاح رد مدفوع فعلًا.

**الحدّ: 5 رسائل يوميًا للشخص** من المزوّد المدفوع (`PAID_AI_DAILY_LIMIT`)، ويُحتسب على **هويتين معًا** ويؤخذ الأشدّ:

1. **كوكي جهاز موقّع (httpOnly)** — الـ `httpOnly` يمنع أي كود في الصفحة من قراءته أو تعديله، فمسح `localStorage` أو تغيير الخطة/المسار داخل الموقع **لا يؤثّر عليه إطلاقًا**. وهو موقّع بـ HMAC، فأي كوكي مزوّر يفشل التحقّق ويُستبدل.
2. **بصمة عنوان الـ IP** — وهذه هي التي تُمسك من يمسح الكوكيز كليًا أو يفتح نافذة خفية.

بهذا، التحايل يتطلّب **جهازًا جديدًا وعنوانًا جديدًا معًا** لا مجرد ضغطة في المتصفح. وعند نفاد الرصيد لا يظهر خطأ — يُكمل بالمزوّدات المجانية.

### التحقّق الفعلي (بحدّ = 3 للاختبار)
| السيناريو | النتيجة |
|-----------|---------|
| شخص يحتفظ بكوكيه | 3 ردود ✅ ثم **محظور** ⛔ |
| **يمسح الكوكيز كل مرة (محاولة التحايل)** | **محظور فورًا** ⛔ |
| كوكي مزوّر التوقيع | **مرفوض** ويُستبدل ⛔ |
| شخص مختلف (IP جديد) | **مسموح** ✅ برصيده |

`next build` يترجم بنجاح واللينت نظيف.

> ملاحظة: العدّاد يستخدم Upstash إذا توفّر (حدّ عالمي صارم)، وإلا يعمل داخل نسخة التشغيل. إضافة `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL/TOKEN` تجعل الحدّ دقيقًا عبر كل نسخ Vercel.

body:
## Problème

`build.sh:57-64` retélécharge le manifeste des dictionnaires avant chaque build et l'écrit par-dessus `src-tauri/crates/jona-engine-spellcheck/manifest.json`, **fichier suivi par git**.

La CI du repo de dicos réestampille `generated_at` à chaque régénération, que les dictionnaires changent ou non. Résultat : chaque `./build.sh` laisse un `manifest.json` modifié, pour un diff d'une seule ligne :

```diff
-  "generated_at": "2026-03-16T07:30:57Z",
+  "generated_at": "2026-08-24T07:06:48Z",
```

Ce n'est pas que du bruit visuel : sur ce poste, ça a bloqué un `git pull` avec *« Veuillez les valider ou les remiser »*.

## Correctif

Le fetch reste — le fichier est embarqué via `include_str!`, il doit être à jour à la compilation. Seule **l'écriture** devient conditionnelle : les deux fichiers sont comparés timestamp neutralisé, et le fichier n'est réécrit que si les dictionnaires ont réellement changé.

Ignorer `generated_at` ne perd rien : le champ n'est jamais désérialisé, `struct Manifest` ne lit que `languages` (`lib.rs:20-23`).

**Pourquoi `sed` et non `grep -v` :** ma première version supprimait la ligne avec `grep -v`. Sur un manifeste minifié, tout tient sur une ligne : `grep -v` ne sort rien, renvoie 1, et sous `set -o pipefail` le pipe échoue — la comparaison serait toujours fausse et le fichier réécrit à chaque build, soit le bug d'origine restauré en silence. La normalisation par `sed` ne dépend pas du découpage en lignes.

## Vérifications

`bash -n` passe, et la logique est testée sur cinq cas :

| Cas | Attendu | Obtenu |
|---|---|---|
| Indenté, seul `generated_at` diffère | `unchanged` | ✅ fichier intact |
| Les langues changent | `updated` | ✅ nouvelle langue écrite |
| Destination absente | `updated` | ✅ |
| Minifié, seul `generated_at` diffère | `unchanged` | ✅ |
| **Réel** : vraie URL, manifeste de `main` (16/03) vs amont (24/08) | `unchanged` | ✅ arbre propre |

Le dernier reproduit exactement le cas signalé : `Manifest unchanged`, fichier non touché, `git status` vide.

Aucun test Rust ou TypeScript n'est rejoué : le diff ne touche que `build.sh`, qui n'entre dans aucune chaîne de compilation. La CI le confirmera.

author: johnrtipton
body:
Closes #2425.

`json.dumps` does not call `str()` on a non-`str` dict key. It has its own
five-entry coercion table, and CPython's `c_make_encoder` writes it in this
order: `str` unchanged, then the three JSON literals for `True` / `False` /
`None`, then `float.__repr__`, then `int.__repr__`, then `TypeError`. djust
routed the key through `ObjectKey::to_display_string()`, so

```
{{ p|json_script:"d" }}     p = {True: "b", None: "c"}

django  <script id="d" …>{"true": "b", "null": "c"}</script>
djust   <script id="d" …>{"True": "b", "None": "c"}</script>
```

One new sibling of `json_float_body` (#2270) — `json_key_body` — called from
the single object-key site in `value_to_json`. The `#2249` count pin still sees
its four `json_string_body` sites, because the helper wraps the ARGUMENT rather
than adding a fifth escape.

## The re-derived divergent-key set

The issue's table listed nine key types and concluded *"the `int` and `float`
arms agree by coincidence, because `str(0)` and `str(1.5)` are already the JSON
forms"*. Re-derived by running `json.dumps` + live Django + djust over **29**
key types rather than inheriting that list, the premise is **wrong rather than
incomplete**: the old coercion was never `str()`.

`ObjectKey::to_display_string()` is the key's TEMPLATE display — what
`{% for k in d %}{{ k }}{% endfor %}` writes — and it parts company with
`float.__repr__` well before infinity:

| key | `str()` | `to_display_string()` (old) | `json.dumps` / Django |
|---|---|---|---|
| `True` / `False` | `True` / `False` | `True` / `False` | `true` / `false` |
| `None` | `None` | `None` | `null` |
| `float('inf')` / `float('nan')` | `inf` / `nan` | `inf` / `nan` | `Infinity` / `NaN` |
| `1e16` | `1e+16` | `10000000000000000` | `1e+16` |
| `1e-5` | `1e-05` | `0.00001` | `1e-05` |
| `0`, `1.0`, `1.5`, `-3`, `12345678901234567890`, `""`, `"a"` | — | — | agrees |
| `str` subclass, `int` subclass, `IntEnum`, `str`-Enum | — | — | agrees (subclass rows CPython accepts) |
| `tuple`, `()`, `frozenset`, `bytes`, object, `Decimal`, `complex`, `date`, `Enum`, `range` | — | — | **`TypeError`** — see below |

Only the middle band of small finite floats coincided, and that is the band the
issue sampled. The non-finite keys came out of the key-type sweep; **the
exponent band came out of the gate-off** — deleting the `Float` arm reddened
`1e16` and `1e-05`, which nothing had predicted.

The refusal set is also wider than the issue's four: `Decimal`, `date`,
`complex`, `Enum` and `range` keys are refused by `json.dumps` too, while
`IntEnum` / `str`-Enum / `str`-subclass / `int`-subclass keys are ACCEPTED (they
are `int` / `str` subclasses and CPython calls `int.__repr__` / passes the `str`
through). The issue's guess that the key type "may need to be preserved across
the PyO3 boundary" is also already false — `ObjectKey` (#2339) carries `Tuple`,
`Decimal`, `BigInt` and `Other { display, repr }` — though `Other` collapses
`bytes` / `frozenset` / `Enum` / an instance into one variant, so Django's
type-named message is not reproducible from Rust as things stand.

## Key-vs-value refusal: why the refusal half is NOT closed here

The design question was settled by measuring what djust does with an
unserialisable **VALUE**, not by preference:

| p | django | djust |
|---|---|---|
| `{"a": object()}` | `TypeError: Object of type Obj is not JSON serializable` | renders `{"a": "OBJ"}` |
| `{"a": b"k"}` | `TypeError: … bytes …` | renders |
| `{"a": {1}}` | `TypeError: … set …` | renders |
| `{"a": complex(1,2)}` | `TypeError: … complex …` | renders |

**djust is exactly as permissive in the value position.** Refusing keys alone
would make the two positions disagree — a new inconsistency wearing a fix's
clothes rather than a narrowing. So this PR closes the SPELLING half only, and
the refusal half is filed as **#2429** as one decision covering both positions.

It is pinned live in `TestTheRefusalHalfIsNotClosedHere`, whose second method
asserts the value position is permissive and *is* the reason the first is left
alone: if the value position is ever made strict, that method goes red and the
key position must follow in the same change. The `date` key is the sharpest
argument for taking them together — `DjangoJSONEncoder.default` serialises a
date VALUE (both engines agree) while a date KEY never reaches the hook, so any
refusal design has to model the encoder hook, not `json.dumps`'s bare table.

## Differential, before → after

Two builds of djust, side by side (HEAD's `filters.rs` built into a separate
tree, this branch in the worktree):

| axis | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| key types (29) | **18 divergent** | **10 divergent** (0 moving the other way) |
| `scripts/filter-parity-differential.py` corpus, argument-less `json_script` (41 INPUTS) | 1 (`d-typed-key`) | 1 (`d-typed-key`) |

The 10 remaining key types are exactly the refusal set. `d-typed-key` stays
divergent because of its `(1, "t")` key, not its `True` / `None` ones — so
#2413's scope claim survives this fix, and is re-worded to say why, plus to say
that it is a claim about the CORPUS and was silent about this axis (the corpus
carries no non-finite and no exponent-form float key).

## Tests

`python/tests/test_json_script_typed_keys_2425.py` — 11 test cases, 38 with
parameterisation. `TestEveryKeyTypeReDerived` is the sweep above, kept as a test
so the next key-type question is answered by running it.

#2413's `test_a_bool_or_None_KEY_is_spelled_Python_not_JSON` went red exactly as
its class docstring said it should, and is flipped to
`test_a_bool_or_None_KEY_is_now_spelled_the_JSON_way`.

### Gate-off

Five mutations, each rebuilding the crate and clearing `__pycache__`; the
harness asserts the mutation text matched **exactly once**, that the source
changed, that the build succeeded, and counts pytest's `N error` apart from
`N failed`:

| mutation | reddened |
|---|---|
| whole fix reverted (HEAD `filters.rs`) | 16 |
| `Bool(true)` arm → `"True"` | 7 (incl. `[True-true]`, **not** `[False-false]`) |
| `Bool(false)` arm → `"False"` | 4 (incl. `[False-false]`, **not** `[True-true]`) |
| `None` arm → `"None"` | 6 |
| `Float` arm deleted | 7 (all three non-finite **and** `1e16` / `1e-05`) |

No survivors, and each of the four arms is independently reachable — a fix
handling only the truthy `bool` fails a test.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/ python/tests/ python/djust/tests/ -n auto` → **16963 passed,
  338 skipped, 0 failed**
- `cargo test -p djust_templates --lib --release` → 485 passed
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p djust_templates --all-targets`, `ruff
  check`, `ruff format --check`, `scripts/check-changelog-test-counts.py` — all
  clean

Refs #2413, #2405, #2339, #2270, #2241, #1079.

author: junixlabs
body:
`agent_sessions.failure_reason` held `job_failed` for every agent-side death — 1,787 live rows saying nothing — and, from a second writer, free text: 55 rows holding a classifier sentence where `queue_timeout` holds a token, 9 of them the agent's own prompt stored as its reason for failing. `VISION: state-never-lies`.

## What it turned out to be

Not a missing subsystem. The job lane already classified correctly; `jobs/agent-session-link.ts` threw the diagnosis away one column over and wrote a literal, and `agent-sessions/session-failure.ts` wrote a sentence into the token column. Two lines.

## The taxonomy

33 causes, each line naming its live count or its writer. The first two come from the eight transcripts ISS-871 burned 15h27m on and closed as "Not diagnosed" — seven `provider_spend_cap`, one `provider_refused_request` — read before the enum was designed, which was the mandated order.

Validated over 90 days of live failures rather than against the fixture: 10,904 failed jobs, **99.93% land on a named cause**. Getting there found the largest signature by re-measuring, not by re-reading — 1,231 rows of `Agent completed with errors`, which is `[NO_RESULT_*]` in the runner's older wording, and 88 rows carrying the classifier's *own* verdict string, which nothing fed back to a rule. The residue is 8 rows that genuinely say nothing, and they stay `unclassified` on purpose.

## Two axes, two columns

`failure_reason` is the cause token, bound to the taxonomy on the Drizzle column so free text is a build error; `failure_detail` (migration 0192, additive and nullable) is the sentence. No CHECK — migration 0180 measured what one costs on this table family — and no backfill: `job_failed` resolves to `unclassified` at read time, which is honestly what it was.

## `unclassified` is counted, never hidden

`forge_metrics.session_failures` returns it as a row like any other, plus the rate. A failed session that recorded *nothing* is counted too — the first query could not see it, because asking for a reason before counting a failure improves the rate by dropping the worst rows. Sessions that are not failed yet carry a reason come back under `nonFailedWithFailureReason` rather than silently.

## One list, two files

Core cannot value-import `@forge/contracts` (absent from the prod image; ISS-510 took the API down that way) and web-v2 cannot import core, so the list lives twice, the shape `NOTIFICATION_TYPES` already uses. `failure-causes-parity.test.ts` holds the copies identical — falsified in both directions.

## Evidence

`pnpm verify` 17/17 · core 5,010 · web-v2 519 · `pnpm build` 4/4 forced · `test:integration` 571 passed / 6 skipped against real Postgres. Every new guard was falsified: the defect planted, the right test watched going red naming its own rule, the file restored.

Reviewed independently twice — first round requested changes on four findings, second approved with four minor ones, all fixed rather than carried.

author: ravinald
body:
## Summary
The server called `RealIPMiddleware(nil)` unconditionally and `requestScheme` called `defaultTrustedNets()` directly, so the trusted set stayed at the hardcoded RFC1918 + loopback default with no way to narrow it. On a network with other tenants bodega believes every peer, and `admin_permit_cidr` defaults to loopback, so `X-Real-IP: 127.0.0.1` reaches the mutation API with no token. Adds tri-state `trusted_proxies` (absent = default, `[]` = trust none, list = trust those) and `tls_min_version` (1.2 or 1.3, default 1.3, refusing 1.0/1.1 by name). Closes #112, and gives #113 the safe proxy path that lets bodega hold a 1.3 floor. Verified: `TestSpoofedRealIPAgainstMutationGate` drives the full chain and separates 404 (gate passed) from 403 (gate refused) across four trusted-set states, with `go test ./...` and `golangci-lint run ./...` clean.

## Fix
`trusted_proxies` carries no `omitempty` so the tri-state survives a `Save`, and the resolved set rides the request context into `requestScheme` rather than falling back to a wider default. The default stays wide on purpose: tightening it to loopback would break any install whose proxy is a separate host, so that is a separate change.

## What was done

**Calendar publishes its read Api (no write Api — per the chantier mandate, IT-06 is read-only):**
- `Api\EventSummary` gains a `?string $description` field (filled in both construction sites of `CalendarService`).
- New `Api\SelectableCalendar` value object (`id`, `label`, `isSection`) and `Api\CalendarDirectoryInterface::selectableCalendars()`, implemented by `CalendarService` — the typed replacement for consumers reaching into `listSelectableCalendars()` arrays.
- New `Api\IcsFeedBuilderInterface::buildVirtualCalendar(string $calendarName, array $virtualEvents): string`, implemented by `IcsBuilder` (delegates to the existing `build()` with no module event rows) — renders a standalone VCALENDAR from §7.6 virtual events alone.

**Consumers move off the calendar's internals:**
- `Modules\Finance\Service\AiCategorizationService` now takes `?CalendarEventLookupInterface` (was two calendar repositories). `findNearbyCalendarEvents()` uses `findEventsInWindow()` over a ±21-day window. The scheduler path gets the capability through `TaskCapabilities` in `RunCategorizationRulesHandler` (completing the deferral noted in IT-04).
- `Modules\Rental\Controller\RentalManagementController` consumes `?CalendarDirectoryInterface`; `RentalRequestController` consumes `?IcsFeedBuilderInterface` for the renter's ICS feed. Both degrade to their previous "calendar disabled" behavior when null.

**Gallery: `GalleryException` moves to `Modules\Gallery\Api\GalleryException`** (git mv + namespace change, 26 files' references rewritten), following the `LlmException` precedent — consumers catching it no longer import from `Service\`.

## Decisions taken alone

- **`Role::SUPERADMIN` as the system caller for calendar hints**: `AiCategorizationService` reads the unit's own calendar to hint its own categorization model — this is the application acting for the installation, not a person; documented in an in-code comment. Event titles feed an LLM prompt that already receives the transaction wording itself; no personal data beyond what the feature already carried.
- **Window semantics**: `findEventsInWindow()` matches events whose *effective end* falls in range and includes supplementary calendars, where the old repository query matched start dates on section calendars only. For AI categorization hints this widening is benign (more context, same trust level), so I did not add a narrower Api method for it.
- **PHPStan baseline counts** for `calendarRepo`/`calendarEventRepo` in the finance wiring were reduced (2→1, 4→3) — downward only, never up.
- **`$calendarServiceForOthers` reuse** in `public/index.php` for the finance AI wiring, instead of introducing a new "might not be defined" variable that would have grown the baseline.

## Leak-edge tracker after IT-06

Remaining non-Api edges: `calendar→retro` Repository write (IT-08), `sos_staff→calendar` Service and `sos_staff→trombinoscope` Repository (IT-07). All other edges from the review matrix are emptied.

## Test state

- `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse`: OK
- `vendor/bin/phpunit`: 12,204 tests, 38,889 assertions, OK
- `npm run e2e:full`: **61 passed (11.2m)** — confidence tier + the 20-module boot matrix, run as `e2e:full` because composition-root wiring changed.

New/updated tests: `CalendarServiceTest` (SelectableCalendar parity with the legacy list), `IcsBuilderTest` (virtual-calendar feed), `AiCategorizationServiceTest` (rebuilt over a real `CalendarService`), `FinanceSeeder` fixture updated to the new constructor.

author: wkjarosz
body:
The layer nobody had hunted. Hunts [#187](https://github.com/wkjarosz/hdrview/pull/187) and
[#191](https://github.com/wkjarosz/hdrview/pull/191) hunt what a decoder does with bytes,
[#193](https://github.com/wkjarosz/hdrview/pull/193) what a writer emits, and
[#194](https://github.com/wkjarosz/hdrview/pull/194) what the GPU shows. This is the machinery around all
of them: which files get decoded, when, on what thread, whose lifetime they share, and what happens when
the disk changes underneath. `BackgroundImageLoader` and the `app-file-io.cpp` plumbing had been touched
only at their edges — #187 reordered the loader *table*, never the async part.

Five bugs, each verified by reverting its fix individually and watching a specific assertion fail.

## Watching

**"Add watched folder…" was cancelled by closing any image.** Its documented purpose is watching a folder
you have *not* opened — *"Do not load the selected folder, but monitor it for new files and load those as
they are created."* So no loaded image ever lives in it, and `close_image()` prunes with "drop every
directory that is not the parent of some loaded image", which is always true of one. Point HDRView at a
folder renders are being written to, close an unrelated image, and the watch is silently gone. Closing all
images took it too. Nothing in the loader recorded *how* a directory came to be watched, so nothing could
tell the two apart.

An explicit watch is now removed only by the X button beside it in the watched-folders table. Keeping the
directory in `m_directories` rather than tracking survivors separately is load-bearing: the same pruning
trims `m_existing_files` to files under a still-watched directory, and that set is what stops the watcher
treating already-known files as new — a directory kept without its file list would re-load everything in
it on the next 250 ms poll.

## Reloading

**A reload could duplicate an image, or bring back one you had closed.** An arrival is matched to its slot
by pointer identity, and identity goes stale two ways.

Two reloads in flight at once: the watch loop schedules one on every timestamp change and polls four times
a second, so a file being written repeatedly outruns the load — and "Reload all images" pressed twice does
it too. The first arrival replaces the image, so the second cannot find what it was told to replace and
lands as a second copy. The list then holds an outdated *and* a current version of one path, and every
later reload of either adds another. Queued replacements are now re-pointed at whatever took their
target's place.

The same missing target with the opposite right answer: an image closed while its reload was in flight has
no slot to fill, and appending puts back what was just closed. Those are dropped — which is only safe
because exactly one arrival per load now claims the slot, so a later part of a multi-part file can never
be mistaken for an arrival whose slot has gone.

`get_loaded_images()` also stops running callbacks from inside a `remove_if` over the list it is pruning.

## Zip archives

**Entries were allocated from their declared uncompressed size, unvalidated**, at all three extraction
sites — reachable from opening a `.zip`, dropping one on the window, and scanning one for a session
manifest. #187 closed this for image headers; the zip layer one level out was never covered.
`std::vector<char> buffer(n)` value-initializes, so the pages are really touched: overcommit does not
soften this into reserved address space.

Two bounds, because neither catches the other's case. Deflate cannot expand data by more than 1032:1, so a
larger ratio is a claim the archive's own stored bytes cannot back — sound, in that it never rejects a real
entry, and the same reasoning #187 used to bound the raw loader by pixels per byte. That leaves the honest
bomb, whose ratio is achievable and whose data really is there, so an absolute cap covers what the ratio
cannot.

## Buffers and paths

**An empty buffer was indistinguishable from no buffer.** `background_load()` decided where to read from by
asking whether the buffer was empty, so a zero-byte zip entry fell through to "open this path" — against a
name assembled for display (`archive.zip/inside.png`) that no filesystem has. The complaint was that a file
did not exist, about a file that was never meant to. It is a `std::optional` now.

**The Emscripten download progress could not report a percentage, and could divide by zero doing it.**
`(total_bytes - bytes_loaded) / total_bytes` is integer division, so every partial fraction came out zero
and the bar — drawn only while the value is above zero — vanished as soon as the first bytes arrived. When
the total is zero, which a server sending no content length reports and which the callback can also see
before the headers land, it divided by it. Nothing reset the value on success either; that was hidden only
by the division already forcing it to zero.

**A folder entered Open Recent whether or not it opened anything** — before anything in it had been read,
and even when the directory could not be listed at all, whose `error_code` was passed in and never
examined. Every other path is careful about this: a file is dropped from the list and only put back once a
load succeeds, and a zip is added only if an entry was scheduled.

## Verification

152/152 `ctest`, 48 GUI tests. Every fix was confirmed to fail its test when reverted on its own, which
mattered more than usual here:

- The first zip test was a **tautology** — an archive lying about a size fails to extract either way, just
  with the allocation and a decompression first, so the returned value is identical. Only the resource use
  differs. It now captures the log through a scoped sink, which distinguishes "refused up front" from
  "tried and failed"; unwiring any of the three call sites fails it, while the value-only form passed.
- A multipart test **claimed a regression it could not catch**. Instrumenting the loader showed why: an
  initial multi-part load yields ten images with no replacement, but a reload yields exactly one, since it
  carries the part's own channel selector. The multi-image-plus-replacement case never arises. The split is
  kept — it is what makes the drop rule safe — but described as the contract it is rather than a fix for an
  unreachable bug.

The download arithmetic moved with its test. It took no `this` and touched no member state, and sat on
`HDRViewApp` only so the test could reach it — which is what made it public. It is a free function in
`common.h` now, where `shorten_names()` went for this same reason and where `next_matching_index()`, which
the very same test file exercises, already lived. `tests/test_index_helpers.cpp` drops `app.h` entirely as a
result: that call was the only thing pulling the whole app header into a test of arithmetic.

Tests fold into their existing homes: the zip bounds into `tests/test_loader_limits.cpp`, which #187
created for exactly this class; the download arithmetic into `tests/test_index_helpers.cpp` alongside the
other small pure helpers, checked across every total up to 64 rather than at sampled points; the multi-part
reload case into `tests/gui/test_gui_multipart.cpp`. Only the watching and archive behaviour needed a new
file. Each test is broader than its bug — the watch one also proves an *implicitly* watched folder is still
dropped when its last image closes, so the fix cannot degrade into pinning everything.

The Emscripten toolchain earned its keep: it caught `hdrview_loadfile()` in `platform_utils.cpp`, the
browser drag-and-drop entry point, which the native build never compiles.

## Swept and clean

Recorded because it bounds where the remaining risk is not: the pending-session interaction (already
hardened by #189/#191, and undisturbed by the `get_loaded_images()` restructure — nothing reads
`num_pending_images()` from inside a callback); Open Recent's indexing, consistent across the File menu and
the command palette

author: deekaph
body:
Closes #1.

Some extractors (e.g. spankbang) return `title == id` — a URL slug like `7riba` — which `_clean_title()` can't repair from the URL path, so the slug lands in the filename (`[SpankBang] 7riba [7riba].mp4`).

## Change (app/downloader.py)
- New `_title_from_page(url, cookies_file)` helper: fetches the page via the existing cookie-aware `_fetch_page` (target sites 403 a plain GET), reads `og:title`, falls back to `<title>` minus a trailing `" - Site"` / `" | Site"` suffix, HTML-unescapes. Returns `None` on any error.
- In the main yt-dlp download block: when the title is **degenerate** (equals `id`/`display_id`, generic, or empty) *and* `_clean_title` left it unchanged, recover from the page. The existing sanitize+rename block does the rest.

## Safety

author: brady-aiello
body:
`@DeepPrint` on a class that isn't a `data class` produced a **0-byte file and nothing else**. No error, no warning. The first sign was `unresolved reference: deepPrint` at the call site, with nothing connecting it back to the annotation that silently did nothing.

```
e: [ksp] Classes.kt:6: DeepPrint: cannot generate deepPrint() for NotADataClass because
it is a class rather than a data class, and deepPrint() prints a call to a primary
constructor.

e: [ksp] Classes.kt:12: DeepPrint: cannot generate deepPrint() for Hidden because it is
private, and the generated extension is a separate file in the same package, which
cannot reach it.
```

The rules were already written down in `isEligible()` — the no-annotation mode filters on them. They just never reported anything where the annotation was written by hand. Each now carries the reason it exists, reported against the symbol so it arrives with a file and a line.

## The version I got wrong

My first pass treated `@DeepPrint` + `@NoDeepPrint` as contradictory. The `tostring` project stopped compiling, which is how I learned it's a **supported combination**: generate `deepPrint()`, but tell the compiler plugin to leave `toString()` alone. [ToStringTest.kt:57](test-project-tostring/src/test/kotlin/com/bradyaiello/deepprint/tostring/ToStringTest.kt:57) asserts precisely that, and my rule would have broken it.

`isEligible()` keeps the `@NoDeepPrint` rule for the no-annotation mode, where nobody asked for the class in the first place. It is not a reason generation is *impossible*, so it isn't reported.

## What the new tests actually prove

Less than they look like they do, and that's written into the test rather than left implied. The no-annotation project now holds an interface, a plain class and an enum beside its data classes — but **removing the mode guard doesn't fail them**, because `symbolsToProcess` filters ineligible classes out before the report is reached. Both would have to break together.

I found that by mutating the guard and watching nothing happen, so the comment says so instead of claiming coverage it doesn't have.

## Also

Stops creating the output file before knowing there's anything to put in it — the source of the 0-byte files.

Full suite, both multiplatform projects, JS, both `toString` projects, detekt and the ABI check.

author: juliusolsson05
body:
Talking to an NPC failed with `TypeError: Failed to fetch`.

## The problem

Three bugs stacked, only the first of which was visible:

1. **CORS.** TrueForge serves no `access-control-*` headers. The browser blocked the cross-origin call from `:5173` to `:8790` before sending it, which is why it surfaced as an opaque `TypeError` rather than an HTTP status. Confirmed with a preflight against the running harness.
2. **Missing required field.** `AgentSpec` requires `model`; the client never sent one. This would have been the next failure the moment CORS was fixed.
3. **No model configured.** The harness has zero providers, so there was no name to send even if the field had been there.

## The fix

Proxy `/api/v1` through the Vite dev server, making the call same-origin. This also matches the intended production shape, where a backend of ours fronts the harness rather than exposing it to the browser.

For the model, the client asks the harness which providers are configured and takes the first, rather than hardcoding a catalog id. The game then works with whichever provider is set up, and when none is, the NPC reports that specific cause instead of a generic failure.

## Verification

- Preflight and header inspection against `localhost:8790` confirmed no CORS headers — the root cause, not a guess.
- `GET /api/v1/models` through the proxy returns `{"data":[]}` from the harness, where it previously returned the game HTML. Proxy confirmed working.
- Request shapes checked against the harness OpenAPI spec rather than the docs prose; `model` being required was found there.
- `tsc --noEmit && vite build` passes.

## Known limitation

Item 3 is not fixed by this PR and cannot be — a model provider API key has to be added at `localhost:8790` by a human. Until then the intended behavior is the NPC saying so. That message path is reasoned about but not visually confirmed in-game.

body:
Two things.

## 1. Equipment correction → the 4×4 gets more faithful, not less

Kandy has **no stairs** to use, and does have a **treadmill** and a **road bike**. `DEFAULTS.kit` was wrong: stairs out, treadmill in.

So the Norwegian 4×4's stairs session becomes a treadmill session — which makes it the *faithful* one, since Helgerud's subjects ran. The guide now says the treadmill day is their protocol as written and the **bike** days are the adaptation, rather than the other way round. The descent warning is replaced with a treadmill one (find the stop button; don't hold the rails to survive an interval). Still 9 blocks, still 2280 s.

## 2. Progression for PPL, Upper/Lower, Full Body, Knee-Friendly

That's the four Strength-tagged programs that lacked it. The five Mobility and Conditioning plans are left alone — nothing in them holds a weight.

**How each number is reached, marked per entry in the code:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **BAR** | computed = the lift's ratio to its Setup lift × Epley inverted at **this program's own rep target** + 2 reps in reserve: `w = 1RM × (37 − (reps + 2)) / 36` |
| **DB** | taken verbatim from `SA_WEIGHT` for the same movement — those are shipped working weights, already rep-adjusted, so running Epley over them again would discount them twice |
| **start: 10** | isolation with no shipped equivalent; progression finds it. Guessing a lateral-raise ratio would be false precision |

Because the rep target comes from each program's own data, bench is `.750` in PPL (written for 8) and `.833` in Upper/Lower (written for 5) — 70 lb vs 75 lb off an 85 lb Setup entry. The lift ratios (a row at .90 of a bench, front squat at .85 of a back squat, good morning at .45 of a deadlift) are estimates, labelled as such, that the reps-hit rule corrects.

**77 entries.** Bodyweight movements are absent and progress by reps as before.

**Checked first, because it decides the design:** within any one program every loaded key has exactly one rep target, so one `saWeights` slot per key is sound. The only conflict is pull-ups in Upper/Lower (6/8) — and pull-ups carry no load.

**Two deliberate departures in Knee-Friendly**, the program whose whole point is starting under: B-stance RDL takes half `dbrdl`'s .30 (that value put it at the dumbbell ceiling, and the movement is near single-leg), and the shallow split squat sits under `stepup`'s .15. 50→30 and 20→15 lb/hand.

## Verification

- the four programs resolve **160 / 126 / 170 / 140** weights
- bench differs by program exactly as the rep targets predict: `ppl 70 · upper-lower 75 · full-body 75 · knee-friendly 75`
- hitting every rep raises **every** lift, missing holds **every** lift, in all four
- 36 `saWeights` slots written, **all namespaced**; the shared key `syn_romanian_deadlift` resolves to six different weights across the six programs (110 / 90 / 105 / 90 / 100 bar, 10 hand)
- Elite tier leaves loaded rep targets untouched in all four
- the five mobility plans and the 4×4 report **zero** hints
- sa2 / sa4 / sahyb / dumbbell / fpfocus still resolve on bare slots — no saved progress orphaned
- 24 programs render, no page errors

author: rotprods
body:
## Problem
`cwp-materialize-next` is triggered by any `NEXT.json` change, but the workflow previously failed whenever no `cwp_materialization_request` was active. That created a false-red main workflow after a legitimate phase transition out of CWP materialization.

## Change
- add deterministic `NO_ACTIVE_CWP_REQUEST` report semantics to `swiss_os.cwp_materialize`
- preserve strict `materialize_from_next()` failure semantics if a caller explicitly invokes materialization without a request
- make the workflow safety assertions accept either a fully materialized packet or an invariant-preserving no-op report
- add unit coverage for the inactive state

## Safety
The no-op report is explicitly `authority_advanced=false`, `h_id_allocations=0`, `OUTBOUND=CLOSED`, `send_allowed=0`. It never invents a stale CWP request, never touches candidate lineage, and never creates a packet when none is requested.

## Summary

Adopt `@robosystems/client` 1.13.0. It fixes every SSE-backed flow (operation monitoring, streaming queries, and the console's operator queries) going dead once a tab has lived past the session's first JWT refresh (~25 min): the SDK's `clients` singleton captured the JWT at construction, the backend revokes the previous JWT on every refresh, and the stream endpoint authenticates the JWT from the URL — so REST calls kept working through core's interceptor while every stream attach 401'd. Confirmed in RoboSystems prod API logs on 2026-08-29.

In 1.13.0 the SSE-backed clients resolve the credential on every connect through the `tokenProvider` core already registers via `setSDKClientConfig`, and `OperatorClient` follows a queued run over `/v1/operations/{id}/status` when the stream cannot open, so the result is never lost. Nothing in this app changes — the fix lives in the package (RoboFinSystems/robosystems-typescript-client#206).

## Changes

- `package.json` — `@robosystems/client` `^1.12.2` → `^1.13.0`.
- `package-lock.json` — resolves to 1.13.0.

## Deploy Notes

None — no env vars, no CloudFormation, no API version requirement (the API was already correct; this is the client catching up). The fix reaches users with the next app release; until then a tab open longer than ~25 minutes still fails its first stream-backed action and a page refresh remains the workaround.

author: farnalabs
body:
## What

QA-lens pass over the test suite surfaced a genuinely vacuous assertion and a gap in the architecture test-quality lens that let it through.

### 1. Fixed vacuous unicode-normalisation test
backend/tests/unit/test_trigger_engine_pre_guardrail.py::test_unicode_escapes_normalised

The old assertion compared canonical_payload_hash({"name": "caf\\u00e9"}) == canonical_payload_hash({"name": "café"}). In Python source, "caf\\u00e9" is decoded to café at parse time, so both operands were literally the same string — the test compared the hash with itself and could never fail, no matter how broken hashing was.

Reworked the left operand to simulate a raw webhook body: json.loads('{"name": "caf\\u00e9"}'), so the assertion now exercises real escape-vs-literal encoding normalisation.

### 2. Widened the self-comparison tautology lens
backend/tests/architecture/test_test_suite_quality.py — the _self_comparison_tautologies lens deliberately skipped Call operands (legitimate purity checks like f(a) == f(a)). That is exactly why the vacuous test above slipped through CI.

Added a narrow carve-out: identical calls to a bare-name callee fed only constant literals (fn(1) == fn(1), digest({'a': 1}) == digest({'a': 1})) are now flagged as dead code. Variable-arg calls (f(x) == f(x)), stateful method receivers (obj.method(a) == obj.method(a)) and ordering ops on calls (get_time() < get_time()) remain unflagged.

## Verification

- Full-tree scan of all 1062 backend test files against the widened lens: 0 violations after the fix.
- All 20 synthetic positive/negative control fixtures in test_self_comparison_lens_flags_tautologies behave as expected (10 flag / 10 pass).
- ruff check . and ruff format --check pass on the whole backend.
- The reworked assertion itself holds under direct evaluation (json.loads decodes the escape to the identical dict).

author: fury03
body:
## 1. Linked Issue
Closes #202

## 2. Problem Statement
Onboarding a new developer means manually creating sample users, courses, books and spaces before anything works locally, and a mistake leaves inconsistent fixtures that silently break flows. This is structural rather than a one-line feature: it needs a repeatable CLI surface, multiple dataset sizes, and a safe reset path. A stray helper or script hidden in one contributor's checkout cannot improve everyone's workflow, so the seeding and cleanup belong in the repo as first-class scripts.

## 3. Solution Comparison and Decision
- **Option A — Only a minimal insert script:** Handles onboarding but gives testers no representative, high-cardinality data, so analytics/list/search work remains painful. Rejected.
- **Option B — A separate CLI tool on npm:** Adds a dependency and a second toolchain for what is a repo-internal concern. Rejected.
- **Option C — Do it from a single script in src/scripts:** Places database schema seeding in the same folder as production scripts, but the issue explicitly asks for `/mongo/seeds/`, and the prior single-purpose `seedDatabase.js` script is a different concern. Rejected.
- **Option D (chosen) — `/mongo/seeds/` directory with a small runner plus one module per entity:** A self-contained, dependency-light set of ES-module scripts run through `npm run db:seed`, with `--minimal`/`--full`/`--reset`/`--clean`. This matches the requested layout, keeps each entity's fixtures readable, and gives devs both a starter set and a comprehensive set.

## 4. The Change
A per-entity seed module plus a runner that owns connect, mode selection, reset and summary:
```js
// mongo/seeds/index.js (abridged)
const users   = await seedUsers({ User, full });
const contentOwner =
  users.find(u => u.role === "mentor" && u.verifiedEducator) || users[0];
await seedCourses({ Course, full, createdBy: contentOwner._id });
await seedBooks({ Book, full, author: contentOwner._id });
await seedSpaces({ Space, full, host: contentOwner._id });
```
npm scripts vs. behavior:

| npm script | CLI flags | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `db:seed` / `db:seed:minimal` | `--minimal` | 3 users / 3 courses / 3 books / 3 spaces |
| `db:seed:full` | `--full` | 10 of each, users include multiple mentors/students |
| `db:seed:reset` | `--reset` | wipe the four collections, then seed (minimal) |
| `db:seed:clean` | `--clean` | wipe collections only (cleanup) |

Seeded accounts share password `DeenBridge#2024` (bcrypt-hashed, never stored in plaintext). Some books carry audiobook fields so the player flow works out of the box. Content is owned by a seeded verified educator so authorization guards behave realistically.

## 5. Compatibility Note (INTERFACE_VERSION)
No interface change. This adds new scripts and npm entry points only; no production route, model or response shape is altered, so this is safe to land without a version bump.

## 6. Incidental Fixes
- Content fixtures reference a verified-educator owner, so newly seeded content passes `requireVerifiedEducator` guards immediately.
- Seed user passwords are bcrypt-hashed with a documented, consistent password for easy local login across all accounts.

## 7. Testing
`test/seedScripts.test.js` runs the real `mongo/seeds/index.js` as a subprocess against an in-memory Mongo server and asserts on actual collections:
- `seeds the minimal dataset via npm run db:seed`
- `seeds the comprehensive dataset with --full --reset`
- `hashes seeded user passwords`
- `wires content to a seeded verified educator`
- `cleans the database with --clean (npm run db:seed:clean)`

Result: `Tests: 6 passed` before/after. No pre-existing failures were touched.

## 8. Additional Notes / Scope
One commit adding `/mongo/seeds/`, `package.json` scripts and a test. No production code, models, routes or services are modified.

author: pmurphinc
body:
### Motivation

- The in-world `RIVAL RIFT` canvas label remained static during the portal's staged victory/destruction sequence and should visually participate in the freeze → pull → collapse → blast progression.
- The goal is visual polish only: make the text feel attached to the Rift without changing gameplay, timers, audio, networking, or camera behaviour.
- Implement a small deterministic helper so per-character fragments animate cheaply and predictably during the existing victory phases.

### Description

- Added `app/rift-label-fx.ts` which exposes `drawRiftLabel(...)`, `riftLabelCharacterTransform(...)`, and the `RIFT_LABEL` constant to compute and draw per-character transforms driven by `VictoryVisualState`.
- Integrated the helper into the existing HUD canvas pass by replacing the single `ctx.fillText("RIVAL RIFT", ...)` call with `drawRiftLabel(...)`, reusing the same camera-derived `portalX/portalY` and `victoryVisualState(...)` timing so no independent timer is introduced. (`app/game.tsx`).
- Character blast motion is deterministic (no per-frame `Math.random()`): trajectories, rotation directions, speeds and variations are derived from stable math seeded by character index and fixed salts so motion is repeatable across frames and runs.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`: the reduced-motion path disables aggressive rotation and limits blast travel, while still collapsing/fading the label through the existing phases; Rift Run/Survival, multiplayer, scoring, and audio logic were not changed.

### Testing

- Ran focused unit tests `tests/rift-label-fx.test.mjs` and `tests/victory-sequence.test.mjs` via the repository test runner, and both suites passed (all assertions in those tests succeeded).
- Ran broader suites via the installed test runner; most gameplay, Rift Run and Survival tests passed (the bulk of the suite passed) while browser-dependent tests were skipped where appropriate, and one unrelated flaky private-code assertion surfaced in a separate run (external to the label change).
- Ran `npm run lint` and verified `git diff --check` (no file-check errors); a full `npm run build` could not be completed in this environment because the available Node runtime is older than the repo's `engines` requirement, so the vinext-based build step was blocked by Node version mismatch.
- Tests confirm: normal label renders pre-destruction, transforms derive from `victoryVisualState(...)`, no independent timer was introduced, freeze/pull/collapse behave as intended, blast emits deterministic per-character fragment transforms with fading opacity, and reduced-motion path avoids large flying-letter movement.

author: syymbba
body: ## Summary Follow-up to #4 (already merged), addressing three issues found after that merge. ### 1. Footer "Platform" links were opening the main app dashboard The footer's "Platform" column (Live Stream Feed, Creator Studio, Game Store & Vault, Short-Form Reels, Esports Tournaments) called `onEnterApp`/`onNavigateTab`, which rendered the actual authenticated app dashboard (Navbar + live/creator/store/reels/esports tabs) directly from the public marketing footer - letting a visitor bypass the landing page entirely without signing in. These links now smooth-scroll to the matching showcase section that already exists further up the same landing page (`#live-streams`, `#creative-tools`, `#features`, `#creators`), reusing the same `scrollToSection` helper the top nav bar already uses. A guest browsing the footer now only ever sees landing-page marketing content, never the app dashboard. ### 2. Privacy Policy <-> Terms of Service cross-links removed Each standalone legal page no longer links to the other. Also added an optional `onBackToApp` affordance: a signed-in user reaching `/privacy` or `/terms` from inside the app (e.g. Settings > Support & Legal) now sees a "Back to App" control that returns via client-side navigation, instead of only a "Visor Stream" home link that fully reloads the app. Guests still see the plain home link, unchanged. ### 3. Fixed `404: NOT_FOUND` instead of Privacy/Terms content Two compounding bugs caused this: 1. `AboutPolicyView`'s links to `/terms`/`/privacy` were plain `` tags with no click handler, so clicking them triggered a full browser navigation instead of the SPA's client-side routing. Added an `onNavigateLegal` callback (wired from `App.tsx`) that intercepts the click and routes through the app's own navigation, while keeping a real `href` so the links stay valid/crawlable. 2. This is a single-page app with no server-side route for every client path (`/privacy`, `/terms`, `/live`, `/settings`, ...) - only `server.ts`'s catch-all knows to always serve `index.html` for any of them. On static hosts like Vercel, without an explicit rewrite, a direct request to one of these paths (typing the URL, refreshing, or - as in bug 1 - a real full-page link) returns the host's own 404 instead of ever reaching the SPA. Added `vercel.json` with a rewrite that falls back to `index.html` for every path except `/api/*`, so deep-linking or refreshing on `/privacy`, `/terms`, or any other in-app route works correctly there too. I don't have access to the live Vercel project/domain from this environment, so I couldn't reproduce the exact reported 404 against production, but the `vercel.json` rewrite plus the click-handler fix address both concrete causes I could identify for that symptom in this codebase. ## Testing - `npm run lint` (tsc) and `npm run build` pass. - Manual browser walkthrough (via an automated computer-use agent) as a guest: - All 5 footer "Platform" links stay on the landing page (URL never changes) and smooth-scroll to existing sections; none ever show app dashboard UI (Navbar, tabs, wallet balance, Go Live button, etc.). - `/privacy` no longer links to Terms of Service; `/terms` no longer links to Privacy Policy. Guests see a "Visor Stream" home link (not "Back to App"). - From `/about`'s tab bar, clicking "Terms of Service"/"Privacy Policy" now uses client-side navigation (no full page reload) and correctly updates the URL and content.

body:
## Summary

`AUDIT-REPRO-1` (Fase 0, `docs/external-audit-2026-08.md`) construyó el journey
de Playwright (`tests/pilot/journeys/actions/recommendation-actions.spec.ts`)
que clasifica las seis acciones de Recomendaciones como `real` / `invisible` /
`entorno` — pero, a diferencia de `scan` y `write`, nunca se le dio un workflow
que lo pudiera disparar contra un preview real. Sin eso, el journey existe
pero nadie lo ha ejecutado, y Fase 4 (`ACTIONS-OBSERVABLE-1`) no se puede
acotar de verdad: el propio plan dice "el reparto exacto sale de la
clasificación", y esa clasificación no existe todavía.

Este PR añade únicamente `.github/workflows/ux-pilot-actions.yml`, calcado de
`ux-pilot-write.yml` (mismo proyecto reservado vía `PILOT_WRITE_PROJECT_ID`,
mismo arreglo de `pr_number` como string, mismo patrón de rama de evidencia),
con `--journeys actions` en vez de `write`. **No toca ningún fichero de
producto.**

Recordatorio importante, ya documentado en el propio journey y en `CLAUDE.md`
("Pilot write scope", tercera excepción aprobada): una de las seis acciones
(«Marcar como hecho») es **destructiva y sin deshacer hoy** — consume una
recomendación real del proyecto de escritura reservado. Dispararlo tiene ese
coste aceptado por el fundador el 2026-08-27.

## Agentic Handoff

- Phase: `ACTIONS-OBSERVABLE-1a` (medición previa a Fase 4, `docs/external-audit-2026-08.md`)
- Implementing agent: director
- QA agent: qa
- Human Gate required: sí

## Changed Files

- `.github/workflows/ux-pilot-actions.yml` — nuevo. `workflow_dispatch` únicamente, sin trigger de `deployment_status`, sin secreto propio.

## Untouched Areas

Cero cambios de producto: ni `recommendations-client.tsx`, ni ninguna server
action, ni el journey de Playwright en sí (`AUDIT-REPRO-1` ya lo dejó
terminado), ni `scripts/pilot.mjs` (ya soporta `--journeys actions` desde
Fase 0). Este PR es exclusivamente el mecanismo de disparo que faltaba.

## Validation

- [x] `pnpm run validate` — build + typecheck + lint en verde.
- [x] `pnpm test` — 220/220 ficheros, 3.035/3.035 tests (incluye
      `tests/pilot/support/selfcheck-checks.test.ts`, que cubre
      `checkActionsLockout` — sigue confirmando que el set de lectura por
      defecto no alcanza el journey `actions`).
- [x] `git diff --check` limpio.
- [ ] `pnpm pilot:selfcheck` real (necesita Playwright + red) — no se ha
      podido ejecutar en este entorno; lo corre CI sobre este PR.

No aplica la pasada estándar de `ux-pilot` de este mismo PR contra el propio
cambio: no hay pantalla nueva que pilotar, es un workflow. La pasada que
importa es la que este workflow habilita — el dispatch manual de
`--journeys actions` que hará falta para acotar Fase 4b.

## Scope Guard

- [x] No schema/RLS/migration changes, or explicitly approved
- [x] No secrets exposed — ningún secreto nuevo; reutiliza los ya existentes de `ux-pilot-write.yml`
- [x] No out-of-scope provider/pipeline changes
- [x] No generated/local files committed

## Self-Check

- [x] The PR matches the issue scope only.
- [x] Forbidden files were not modified.
- [x] Allowed files were respected.
- [x] Validation was run or the limitation was explained.
- [x] The PR is ready for QA review.

## QA Status

- [x] Ready for Claude QA
- [ ] Claude QA accepted
- [ ] Human Gate approved

## Risks

- Al mergear, para clasificar de verdad hace falta que **tú** dispares el
  workflow manualmente desde la pestaña Actions (`Agentic User Pilot
  (actions)` → `Run workflow`), pasando el número de un PR con preview activo
  — igual que ya haces con `ux-pilot-scan.yml`. Nadie más debería pulsarlo sin
  avisarte antes, por el coste destructivo de «Marcar como hecho».
- Este PR en sí **no dispara build de Vercel** (sólo toca
  `.github/workflows/`, fuera de la excepción de `ux-pilot.yml` en
  `scripts/vercel-should-build.sh`), así que no hay preview propio que pilotar
  ni gasta presupuesto de build.

## Screenshots

No aplica — no hay UI nueva, es un workflow de CI.

## Human Review Notes

Con esto mergeado, el siguiente paso real es que dispares
`ux-pilot-actions.yml` a mano contra algún PR con preview vivo para obtener el
veredicto real de las seis acciones. Con ese veredicto en mano, vuelvo con el
Task Intake de `ACTIONS-OBSERVABLE-1b` con alcance ya concreto (hoy sólo puedo
estimarlo, no fijarlo).

Expose the pool light scheduling that the Hayward app offers but the integration did not. Controllers can run the light on their own schedule, and until now the only thing Home Assistant could do was switch it on and off.

Four entities, all gated on the controller actually reporting the fields, so setups without light scheduling are unaffected:

- The frequency select maps its options to raw second values (86400 / 604800) rather than to option indices like the existing selects. Rather than a separate entity class, the select entity description gained an optional `value_map`, and the shared entity handles both mappings.

author: kristianwind
body:
Two pieces of plumbing, both found by taking Kristian's question seriously: *"hvordan deler vi versioner mellem hosted og open source?"*

## The beacon's default is the application's, not the package's

`URL()` now falls back to `b.DefaultURL`, a field only `cmd/mimir` sets. A `Beacon` built by the package alone reports **nowhere**.

The direction of that default is the whole point:

- Forget it in `main` → the beacon stays quiet. Visible, harmless, fixable.
- Bake it into the package → every test that ticks without an explicit address sends a real ping to production.

The second is not hypothetical. **Two rows arrived in the live `beacon_pings` table tonight** and both were mine:

```
752fd1ee…  dev      18:56:56    ← a local instance started to take a screenshot
a7080a46…  v1.2.3   18:54:35    ← the literal version string from beacon_test.go
```

Kristian deleted both by hand from the production database. Fixing the one test that leaked would have left the trap armed for the next one; this removes the trap.

## `:latest` means a release

The panel pulls `:latest`, and `:latest` was set by `{{is_default_branch}}`. So the hosted instance ran a build stamped `dev` that no self-hoster could install, while the newest release sat a week behind it. **The two were never the same image.**

That makes "the hosted instance runs this code" true of the repository and false of the artefact — an uncomfortable gap on the day the repository goes public and the site starts linking to it.

Now a version tag publishes `:latest` (and multi-arch, as it already did), and main publishes `:edge`. A merge no longer deploys by itself; a tag does, which is the release model the process already described.

Next: `v0.4.0`, which will be the first release to carry today's work — and the first where mimir.guide and a self-hosted install run the same bytes.

author: saltypatron
body:
## Root cause

`MatchRunner.PlayOneCore` already carried the exact played UCI token into the live ply callback, but the parallel `MatchRunner.Play` path discarded it and called `ChessLiveGameHost.RecordPlyAsync` with `"?"`. `ChessLiveGameHost` correctly validates a witnessed move against its pre-move board, so substrate-lift jobs failed immediately with `live move '?' does not resolve from its pre-move board`.

## Substrate-lift fix

- forward the exact UCI token into the live recorder
- retain board-based validation
- allow transition-only legacy callers to recover the unique legal move from exact pre/post board surfaces rather than recording `?`
- add a DB-gated MatchRunner/live-host regression

## Live Play recording that also landed here

The shared live recorder and browser Play path were extended before this PR merged:

- source-observed game metadata model (event/site/date/time control/class/termination/start position/external id/ratings)
- players retained on the Play session and emitted on completion
- resumed Play histories are recorded from their first supplied ply instead of only recording moves made after reconnect
- SAN is preserved from the exact pre-move board for replay/analysis
- per-ply search/recognition evidence can retain score/depth/nodes/PV/motifs and clock observations
- completed live games run the normal `ChessAnalyze` derivation for opening/motif/position projection/analysis markers
- actual searched position evaluations are deposited; absent evaluations are not invented
- external source occurrence ids may distinguish otherwise identical live playings while routing GUIDs remain outside identity

Lichess provider metadata wiring is completed separately in PR #1337 because this branch was merged while that follow-up edit was in progress.

author: dschmidt
body:
`ParseRecord.depth` is incremented for every composite parser a parse passes through. With `AutoDetectParser` wrapping `DefaultParser` that is two per document level, and the depth check compared that counter with `maxDepth + 1`, so `maxDepth=2` parsed depth 1 only, `maxDepth=3` reached depth 2, and so on. `maxDepth=0` and `1` happened to work, which is what the existing tests cover.

`ParseRecord` now has an embedding depth that `ParsingEmbeddedDocumentExtractor` and `UnpackExtractor` raise around the child's parse, and the limit is checked against that: with `maxDepth=N`, documents at depth N are parsed and their children are not, as the `EmbeddedLimits` javadoc describes. The composite counter stays as it is for its other uses (top-level detection, handler decoration).

The new test nests a parser five levels deep behind two composite layers and fails on main for maxDepth 2, 3 and 5.

author: min-hinthar
body:
## What & why

Second tranche of the backlog sweep. The #240 back-sweep **filed** six rows of Codex findings that had landed after a merge and were never answered; this PR works them.

The headline is not the fixes. **Two sub-items were already fixed by later work, and one does not reproduce against current source at all.** Acting on the filed text without re-reading the code would have produced changes for problems that no longer exist — which is the whole reason this repo's rule says to verify every finding against source before acting on it.

## M146 — `data-fx="off"` still moved the room, and the CSS alone would not have fixed it ✅

The `off` block nulled `animation` on the two ambient planes **and nothing else**. On a fine pointer `AmbientMotion` kept writing `--pa-px`/`--pa-py` every frame, so both full-viewport planes kept translating — with `--fx-promote: auto` having just removed their layer promotion, so "off" was doing *unpromoted* compositing work. `.pa-pause` is `display: none` there and never renders on a fine pointer anyway, so **that diner had motion and no stop control** (WCAG 2.2.2), while the checked-in comment claimed the opposite.

Fixed on both halves, because either alone is incomplete:

- The `off` rule now mirrors the reduced-motion block exactly — `animation` · `translate` · `transition` · `will-change` on both planes, `transform` reset on each.
- `AmbientMotion` reads the dial: `motionOk = !rm.matches && root.dataset.fx !== "off"`, so the listener is never attached.
- A **`MutationObserver` on `data-fx`** re-runs that decision, because `FxDial.tsx` *writes* the attribute at runtime. Reading it once at mount would leave a diner who turns effects off mid-session with the listener still attached — the same class of bug one level up.

Codex's tell was the right one: the reduced-motion block three rules down already killed all four properties, which is what makes the narrow shape an oversight rather than a decision.

## M147 — a `localStorage` throw took the device-tier fallback with it ✅

The boot script read storage and derived the hardware tier inside **one** `try`, so a browser that throws on storage access (Safari private mode, cookies blocked, a partitioned iframe) skipped the tier derivation too. The browser most likely to throw is a locked-down mobile one — exactly the low-end device `lite` exists for, and the one getting the full effect budget.

Now two `try` blocks, and pinned by **`apps/qr/lib/fx-boot.test.ts` (8 assertions) which reads `layout.tsx` and evaluates the shipped literal** rather than re-typing it, so a test cannot stay green while the real script rots.

**Two bugs in my own guard, both worth recording:**

1. Its first draft anchored the extraction regex on the post-fix `var f=null;` prefix — so reverting M147 made the script *unfindable*, the module threw at import, and vitest reported **"no tests"** instead of a red assertion. A guard that disappears on the regression it exists to catch is worse than no guard, because "no tests" reads like nothing was wrong. Now anchored on the storage key.
2. Its helper defaulted `opts.cores ?? 8`, which silently rewrote an *explicit* `undefined` to 8 cores — so the "a UA that doesn't report `hardwareConcurrency`" assertion tested nothing. Caught only because the expectation disagreed.

Red-first: the single-`try` shape → `AssertionError: expected undefined to be 'lite'`.

## M150 — one fixed, two already fixed, one unreproducible ⚑

- **(b) FIXED** — `.pa-mid` was `inset: 0` while translating by `--pa-parallax-mid` (**13px**, measured at `tokens.css:277`, not transcribed), so at full deflection its trailing edge pulled into frame and exposed a hairline of bare `--pg`. Now `inset: -16px`; `.paper-ambient` is `overflow: hidden`, so the overscan never paints outside the room.
- **(c) ALREADY FIXED** — `lastDefiningMigration()` reads the migration directory in apply order, not final identity, and its docblock already credits this exact Codex round: *"only the filenames prove the chain is COMPLETE."*
- **(d) ALREADY FIXED** — the M17 header's truth table already shows **two** KNOWN and **two** AMBIGUOUS quadrants and names `grocery_food` as the falsifier of the three-derivable draft.
- **(a) DOES NOT REPRODUCE** — the finding describes "the reward shimmer's light band … reusing `--print-head`", but the only consumer of that token in source is `.receipt-printhead::before`, measured at 4.6028 on `--t3`/`--cd` and documented as deliberately not `--sheen`. **No reward-shimmer consumer exists.** Left open with what I checked; a token invented for a call site that isn't there would be worse than the gap.

## M148 — two doc claims corrected, two left open honestly ⚑

- **(a) FIXED** — `HANDOFF.md` said *"All nine RPCs the app calls"*. Measured: **57** distinct literal `.rpc()` names. The wording made a narrow post-apply verification read as an exhaustive schema-drift check — the kind of claim the next reader stops looking behind. Reworded to "the nine RPCs M22 · M70 · M72a touch", with the 57 stated beside it.
- **(c) FIXED** — `HANDOFF.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` still carried *"`--include-all` … would force a replay … genuinely destructive"*, which was the **second unverified inference in a row** about a command nobody here has run (there's no DB connection string in the agent environment, so `--dry-run` was never executed against prod). Both now carry CLAUDE.md's measured-vs-unmeasured split. **The claim is removed rather than replaced with a third guess** — the conclusion never depended on the mechanism.
- **(b) and (d) still open** — they need the original Codex comments re-read first, and I'd rather leave them accurate than guess.

## QA checklist

- [ ] Server-authoritative pricing — untouched
- [ ] Supabase RLS — untouched
- [ ] Stripe webhook — untouched
- [x] Accessibility — M146 restores a real stop for `off` on fine pointers: nothing moves, so the absent pause control is now correct rather than a WCAG 2.2.2 gap
- [x] No secrets committed
- [x] `pnpm turbo lint typecheck build test --force` green locally (8/8)

## Docs / progress updated

- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` · `docs/HANDOFF.md` · `README.md` (measured counts 1094 → **1102**)
- [x] `docs/OPEN-ITEMS.md` — **M146 closed · M147 closed**; M150 and M148 updated to record precisely which sub-items were fixed, which were already fixed, and which does not reproduce

## Gates

`turbo lint typecheck build test --force` **8/8** · `check:docs` clean (96 files, **1102**+133 tests, 228 mutants).

⚠️ `apps/qr/app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts` carries prettier drift **inherited from `main`** (left by #240). It is fixed in #241 and deliberately not duplicated here to avoid a conflict; this branch's CI does not run `format:check` yet because that step is #241's.

author: rodacato
body:
## Why

The reported symptom was the old mark still showing on the installed app. The cause was not the artwork — production serves the correct manifest and the correct icons. It was the service worker.

`config/environments/production.rb` stamps everything in `public/` with a one-year `max-age`, on the premise stated in its own comment that it is all digest stamped. The service worker and the manifest are not. Cloudflare cached `/service-worker.js` accordingly and, at the time of diagnosis, was answering with the file from six days before the brand bump:

```
/service-worker.js        cf-cache-status: HIT   age: 508345   last-modified: 23 Aug
                          CACHE_VERSION = "v4"   PRECACHE_URLS = [ …?v=2 ]
```

That worker pins `?v=2` asset URLs into `stockerly-static-v4`, and `?v=2` is a separate edge cache key that still returns the old focal-frame mark today:

```
/apple-touch-icon.png?v=3 → 785cdc3a…  (new mark, = repo)
/apple-touch-icon.png?v=2 → 8ef73d16…  (focal-frame, retired 27 Aug)
```

So the new worker never installed, and every future brand bump had the same fate waiting.

## What this changes

**The cause.** `manifest.json` and `service-worker.js` render from `app/views/pwa/` behind `PwaController`, which sets `must-revalidate`. The cache-bust lives in `BrandAssets::VERSION` instead of a literal repeated across three files — the spec that existed to catch that drift is now structural rather than textual. The dead Rails scaffold at `app/views/pwa/service-worker.js`, which no route referenced, is gone.

**Icons.** The only maskable icon was an SVG, and Android mints the home-screen icon from a raster source — the entry was silently falling back to the plain icon inside a white circle, which is the non-native look. Maskable now ships as PNG at 192 and 512, plus a monochrome one for Android 13+ themed icons. Two SVGs nothing rendered are deleted.

**Launch and chrome.** `viewport-fit=cover`, without which every `env(safe-area-inset-*)` resolves to `0` — the bottom nav has been padding itself with one that never had a value. iOS startup images for eight device sizes in both schemes, so launch is not a blank screen. The status bar tracks `bg-surface` and follows the manual theme toggle, which `prefers-color-scheme` cannot see; the manifest keeps `#5B6CFF` for the splash and the task switcher, where the brand does belong. `orientation: portrait` is dropped — it blocked rotation on tablets and is ignored on desktop.

**Updates.** A deployed worker parks in `waiting` until the page sends `SKIP_WAITING`, instead of activating under a live tab. `pwa-update` is what asks.

**Web Push.** A third channel beside the digest and the urgent email, on the same terms: a fired rule interrupts, a dated notice rides the digest. The switch owns worker, permission and subscription together, so it cannot read "on" while the browser has revoked the permission. The unread count also rides the app icon.

## This reverses D16 — read before merging

`design/DECISIONS.md` closed push on 2026-08-25 (*"push is not revived, and the column is gone"*) and set a condition for any revival: *"needs its own 4-filter card, and the card has to answer the iOS limitation first — Web Push reaches a PWA only once it is installed to the home screen, so on a mobile-first product it can fail silently on the primary device."*

The iOS condition is answered rather than waived: a missing `PushManager` reads as *"agrégala a la pantalla de inicio"* when the page is not standalone, and as *"este navegador no la admite"* when it is. The predicted silent failure is the one case that now speaks.

**The card and the trigger are still owed.** Neither was written before the code. D16 records that. Whether this warrants an ADR — new dependency, new permission asked of the user, a reversed decision — is a call for the reviewer, not this PR.

## Deploying this

1. **Purge the Cloudflare cache** for `/service-worker.js` and the `?v=2` URLs. The edge holds them with a one-year TTL and the new headers do not evict the old entries. Without this the fix does not take effect.
2. `.kamal/secrets` needs three lines, or Kamal aborts with `Missing secret`:
   ```
   VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY=$VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY
   VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY=$VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY
   VAPID_SUBJECT=$VAPID_SUBJECT
   ```
   `config/deploy.yml` and the deploy workflow are wired here; the GitHub Environment values are not. With no keys the push switch simply does not render — see `WebPushDelivery.configured?`.
3. `bin/rails stockerly:vapid_keys` prints a pair. Generated once and kept: replacing it invalidates every recorded subscription.
4. On iOS the home-screen icon is pinned at install time — remove and re-add the app.

## Verification

2975 examples, 0 failures · rubocop 843 files clean · brakeman 0 · bundler-audit 0 · importmap audit 0 · i18n-tasks health clean.

`bin/quality`: every application file rates A. The D/F rows are `db/schema.rb` (generated, pre-existing) and four spec files whose flog score is long assertion strings — idiom noise, staying.

Not covered by tests: the three Stimulus controllers. A headless browser cannot drive a push subscription or a waiting worker; the Ruby side of both is covered, and `pwa_update_spec` proves the prompt stays hidden.

author: jakeoborn
body:
218 acts, **Oct 16–17, Mana Wynwood, Miami**. Gated (`available: false`) because the schedule does not exist yet.

## What is real

**The lineup.** Parsed from the 218 `<li>` rows of the single `ul.lineup__list` on [iiipoints.com/lineup-2026/](https://www.iiipoints.com/lineup-2026/) — 218 unique, 80 B2B, billing preserved verbatim because that is how the set is sold and how the schedule will print it.

**The venue.** `venue.footprint` is **T1** — OSM way `435880991` "Mana Wynwood Convention Center", all 23 surveyed vertices verbatim, 13,255 m². (A Douglas-Peucker pass to 17 was measured first — 0.13% area delta, no self-intersection — and thrown away; at 23 points it buys nothing.) `gps` is the OSM centroid, **not** the Nominatim address geocode; the two differ by 80 m.

## What is not published — verified, not assumed

Three ways: the lineup page is **one flat alphabetical list**, no stage headings and no Fri/Sat tabs; **`/experience/stages/` 404s** (still linked from the site's own popup config); and the guide FAQ says maps and set times publish *"prior to the event"* / *"during the days leading up to the festival."*

So **no stages, no day split, no set times, no gpsAnchors, no map art** — and no guesses.

> ⛔ **That site's JSON-LD is five years stale** — it still serves `"III Points Music Festival 2021"`, `startDate 2021-10-22`, location `"DMANA WYNWOOD"`. Everything here is sourced from the human-readable guide page. Flagged in the module header.

## The map

With no published layout there is nothing to draw in the SVG ground-plate style every other festival uses — and drawing one anyway is the poster-space-as-world-space defect #36 just removed from EDC LV.

New **`mapMode: "real"`**: opens on the real basemap, centred on the surveyed venue, live blue dot, no stage pins. It is also just the better map here — Wynwood is a street grid, so the streets are how you find the door; at EDC the poster *is* the wayfinding artifact.

Three deliberate consequences:
- the More-menu "Real map (BETA)" row is not rendered (nothing to toggle to);
- RealMap's fatal fallback no longer switches to an empty plate, and its error surface shows the **venue address + RETRY** instead of a "USE FESTIVAL MAP" button that leads nowhere;
- the **outside-mask is skipped** — dimming the streets around an urban venue removes the only wayfinding this screen currently has.

`festivalFootprint()` now prefers a surveyed `venue.footprint` ring over the hand-drawn `festivalBounds` box, which improves any festival that later gains one.

## One day bucket for a two-day festival

Measured, not assumed. With `day: null` on every act the lineup renders **empty**, because 48 sites across six files filter `a.day === activeDay`. Putting each act on both days would claim it plays twice. One bucket labelled **TBA** makes all 218 browsable and saveable now and states exactly what is unknown. Reverses cleanly at the flip.

## Three latent bugs found by actually booting it

None are new. All three surfaced only because this is the first festival with an empty stage list.

| # | Bug | Blast radius |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `data.jsx` `_WAVE1_IDS` is an **allow-list, not a scan** — the module loaded, registered, and **parsed green in the verify gate while never appearing in the app**. It booted straight back to EDC, silently, no warning. | any future module |
| 2 | `home.jsx:204` hardcoded `sunTimes[2]`/`sunTimes[3]` → *"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'rise')"*, whole Today screen to the error boundary, for **any** festival with <3 days | **4 of 13** festivals (three 2027 scaffolds + this) |
| 3 | `data.jsx` `mk()` did `STAGES.find(...).color` unguarded — throws at eval time on an empty stage list, killing the data layer before render. Every wave-1 `mk()` already had `\|\| STAGES[0]`. | any 0-stage festival |

Plus three unguarded `STAGES[0].id` dereferences in map.jsx's share/presence path (1141/1153 were guarded; 1955/1972/1999 were not).

**#1 is the one worth internalising:** the gate's module count going 5 → 6 proved the file *parses*, not that the festival *exists*. Only booting it caught that. Comment added at the allow-list.

## Verification

Booted with III Points force-activated (reverted before commit):

```
festival iii-points-2026 · artists 218 · stages 0 · days [1]
root children 1 · error boundary: no · console errors: none
```

Map render checked visually against Wynwood satellite imagery — the footprint sits on the actual building. Full verify gate green; v239 across `index.html` + `sw.js` + `app.jsx`.
