body:
| | |
|:---|:---|
|**_Related Issue(s)_**|  N/A |
|**_Has Unit Tests (y/n)_**| Y |
|**_Documentation Included (y/n)_**| Y|
|**_Generative AI was used in this contribution (y/n)_**| Y |

Change Description

Adds an optional per-channel receive directory to Svc::Ccsds::CfdpManager so that destination paths carried in incoming CFDP Metadata PDUs are confined to a configured directory, bringing CfdpManager in line with the Os::SandboxedFile confinement already used by Svc::FileUplink, Svc::FileDownlink, and Svc::PrmDb.

- New parameter ChannelConfig[n].rx_dir (Types/Types.fpp, Parameters.fppi). Default "" = unrestricted, preserving current behavior.
- Single validation point in Engine::recvMd() (Engine.cpp), the only place the PDU-supplied destination enters the transaction. New Engine::validateRxDestPath() resolves rx_dir from CWD, resolves the received path against rx_dir with Os::FilePathUtils::resolvePath (relative paths land inside the directory; ./.. collapsed), and enforces Os::FilePathUtils::checkContainment. The canonical path is what gets stored, so every downstream consumer (open in rInit, moveFile on late metadata, removeFile on cleanup) only ever sees a validated path.
- Rejection handling. recvMd() now returns bool. On rejection it emits the new RxDestPathRejected (WARNING_HI) event, increments faultFileOpen, and clears dst_filename so no later file operation consumes the rejected string.
  - Metadata-first / Class 1 (Engine.cpp): the transaction never enters R1/R2 and is finished from INIT with no file opened.
  - Late metadata on an R2 transaction with a temp file already open (TransactionRx.cpp): dst_filename reverts to the temp path and the transaction is failed with FILESTORE_REJECTION; the temp file is never renamed onto the rejected path.
- Docs. CfdpManager SDD: Assumption 7 corrected (temp-directory staging only occurs when File Data precedes Metadata in Class 2; all other cases open the Metadata destination directly), the destination-path discussion rewritten around rx_dir, parameter table updated. FileHandlingCfdp subtopology SDD note now points operators at rx_dir.

Transaction::m_fd intentionally remains Os::File rather than Os::SandboxedFile: it is shared with the TX path, which reads command-supplied source files that must not be confined, and SandboxedFile would not cover the Os::FileSystem::moveFile/removeFile calls anyway.

Rationale

CfdpManager currently opens, moves, and deletes files at whatever path the Metadata PDU names, with only a length check. A mistyped or     expected destination from the sending entity can thenywhere the process can write, or overwrite an existingfile. The sibling file-handling components already confine their file access to a configured directory; CfdpManager was the one uplink fileiter without that option. The SDD also described temapplied generally, when it only applies to one Class 2ordering. author: scala-steward
kannandreams
body:
Bumps the formula to `glyf-core` 0.4.0, and fixes the bump workflow that produced it.

## Formula

`url` and `sha256` point at the 0.4.0 sdist; the checksum matches what PyPI serves. Homebrew derives the version from the URL, and the formula's `pip install glyf-core==#{version}` follows it.

Installed size drops with the release's dependency removal: **276.1 MB, down from 538.7 MB** on 0.3.0.

## Workflow fix

`bump.yml` rewrote the formula *before* `Homebrew/actions/setup-homebrew`. That action symlinks the checkout in as the tap and then fetches it, resetting the working tree to the remote — so the edit was discarded and the first 0.4.0 run built and tested 0.3.0. Only the closing `test "$(glyf --version)" = "glyf 0.4.0"` assertion caught it, which is why no wrong-version PR was opened.

The rewrite now runs after that step, and fails loudly instead of silently writing the file back unchanged:

- a substitution that matches anything other than exactly one `url` and one `sha256` line is an error (`re.sub` previously returned the text unmodified and the step still printed "bumped to …");
- a version whose sdist is not listed on PyPI yet gets a clear "retry in a few minutes" message rather than a bare `StopIteration`.

## Verification

Run [33280235003](https://github.com/glyf-data/homebrew-glyf/actions/runs/33280235003) on macOS ran `brew style`, `brew audit --strict`, `brew install`, `brew test` and the version assertion against this exact change — all passed, installing `Cellar/glyf/0.4.0`.

That run could not open this pull request itself: **Settings → Actions → General → "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests"** is off for this repository, so `create-pull-request` failed with *"GitHub Actions is not permitted to create or approve pull requests"* after pushing the branch. Enabling that setting would let future bumps open their own PR; until then, the branch is pushed and the PR is opened by hand.

author: 9atatimer
body:
## Summary

Implements a two-layer content gate for this public repository to prevent accidental leaks of obscene language and work/IP markers. The system uses an allowlist (skills must be listed in `PUBLIC_SKILLS.txt` to publish) and a denylist (LDNOOBW community obscenity list plus internal markers), enforced via husky hooks at commit and push time, plus CI validation.

## Key Changes

- **`scripts/publicity-guard.mjs`**: Core gate logic with three modes:
  - `--staged`: scans index before commit (husky pre-commit hook)
  - `--push`: scans outgoing commits before push (husky pre-push hook)
  - `--all`: full-tree scan for CI
  - Checks both file paths and content; respects word boundaries; matches multi-word terms across spaces/dashes/underscores
  - Zero dependencies; exports pure functions for testing

- **`scripts/publicity-guard-words.txt`**: LDNOOBW community obscenity denylist (408 terms, CC-BY-4.0 licensed from Shutterstock)

- **`PUBLIC_SKILLS.txt`**: Allowlist of 29 publishable skill directories; adding a skill requires listing it here in the same commit

- **`.husky/` hooks**: Pre-commit and pre-push guards; `install.mjs` bootstraps husky safely (no-op in CI/publish contexts where husky is absent)

- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**: CI job runs full-tree publicity guard to prevent bypasses

- **`test/publicity-guard.test.mjs`**: Behavioral tests for parsing, term matching, word boundaries, multi-word phrases, path scanning, and skill allowlist enforcement

- **`package.json`**: Added `prepare` script, `guard` npm command, and husky dev dependency

- **Documentation updates**: `skills/gates/SKILL.md` expanded with self-adversarial review section; `skills/sdlc/SKILL.md` clarified skill layer definitions

- **`.gitignore`**: Reorganized to reflect new agent provisioning structure

## Implementation Details

- **Regex-based matching**: Terms are escaped and anchored with word boundaries (`\b`); spaces in multi-word terms match `[\s_-]+` to catch variants
- **Allowlist enforcement**: `ALLOW_TERMS` set (currently empty) can be widened by repo owner only, with required comments
- **Manifest consistency**: Skill allowlist is read from the same git snapshot being scanned, so adding a skill and listing it in one commit passes
- **Binary safety**: Binary files are path-scanned but content-skipped
- **Excluded paths**: The guard code and denylist itself are not content-scanned to avoid self-flagging

author: mukilan-rajasekar
body:
`prisma migrate dev` has proposed these two changes on every run for weeks.
Anyone generating a migration has had to notice them and strip them by hand —
`20260829013428_add_clubs` carries a header explaining why it did, and one
earlier run nearly shipped the column drop inside an unrelated migration.

```sql
ALTER TABLE "players" DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS "stats_profile_url";
ALTER INDEX "connections_user_a_user_b_key" RENAME TO "connections_user_a_id_user_b_id_key";
```

**The column is dead, and I checked before writing this.** `stats_url`
replaced it, the Prisma schema never carried it, nothing in the codebase
mentions it, and on production **0 of 11 players have a value in it** — so
there is nothing to migrate across first. The second is a rename only: same
columns, same uniqueness, the name Prisma expects.

## Written to be safe to re-run

Both statements no-op on a database that has already been fixed —
`DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS`, and the rename guarded by a `pg_class` lookup.
A failed `prisma migrate deploy` takes the production build down with it
(`scripts/vercel-build.sh`), and the live schema's exact shape is the one
thing a migration cannot ask about beforehand. Preview deploys share the
production database and skip migrations, so this one first runs on the merge.

## Verification

- Applied to a local Postgres: column gone, index renamed.
- `prisma migrate diff` afterwards returns **"This is an empty migration"** —
  the drift is actually gone, not just papered over.
- `prisma migrate status`: up to date.
- **Re-ran the same SQL against the fixed database**: clean no-op, one
  `NOTICE ... skipping` and a `DO` that does nothing.
- `bun test` (86), `tsc`, `lint`, `build` clean.

author: tvanhens
body:
Mechanical, behavior-preserving deduplication inside `internal/authorization/` and `worker/authorized-replication.ts` (~300 net lines removed; 243 insertions / 542 deletions). Every change replaces multiple spellings of one algorithm with a single shared definition — no validation semantics, error messages, or wire behavior change.

## What changed

- **Shared `plain.ts` module**: `clonePlain` (was defined in 5 files), `freezePlain` (6 files), `freezeBound`, `encodedJson` (4 files), `compareText` (2 files), and the rule-id remap helpers (`remapRuleIds`/`remapDecision`, byte-identical in `bind.ts` and `authoring/compile.ts`) now have one definition each.
- **`decode.ts`**: the four near-identical `*DescriptorCollisions` functions (entity/trait/field/operation) collapse into one `descriptorCollisions` helper parameterized by label and encoders; error strings are preserved verbatim via the label.
- **`catalog-unit.ts`**: the five per-table encoders, presence checks, and canonical-order comparisons are driven off one `CATALOG_TABLE_KEYS` list and row-encoder table instead of being spelled five times each.
- **`worker/authorized-replication.ts`**: one `requireSameVersion` helper replaces nine inline partition-change guards; a `reset()` closure replaces five identical 7-line `resetFrames` spreads; both 409 terminal responses share one `terminalErrorResponse` builder.
- **`operations-runtime.ts`**: `admissionFault` replaces seven hand-expanded admission `OperationRuntimeFault` throws; `isOperationSurfaceError` replaces the two identical rethrow ladders.
- **`bind.ts` / `validation/catalog.ts`**: `bind.ts` now imports `invalid`/`mismatch`/`isBlank`/`requireNonBlank` from `validation/common.ts` instead of redefining them verbatim, and the byte-identical 49-line `validateTarget` both files carried moves to `validation/common.ts` as `validateCatalogTarget` — removing one of two independent validators of the same document.

## Deliberately not included (follow-ups)

- Rewriting `invocation-receipts.ts`'s hand-rolled guards as Effect Schema unions: those validators carry semantic checks (duplicate-key detection in read sets, path uniqueness in consumed refs) a schema union doesn't replicate mechanically, and it's a replay-security fence — worth its own reviewed change.
- Deleting the legacy catalog-unit v1 decode path (~85 lines whose only effect is a friendlier migration error) — needs a product decision that no v1 units remain in the field.
- Merging `bind.ts`'s `indexCatalog` onto `prepareAuthorizationCatalog`: the remaining duplication differs in diagnostics (e.g. `catalogOfIdentity` message prefixes), so it isn't purely mechanical.

## Validation

- `bun run typecheck` clean (effect-tsgo diagnostics on)
- `bun run test:unit`: 1094 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run test:local`: 87 pass, 0 fail (real Worker/DO/R2 topology — exercises the replication changes)
- `bun run test:doubles`: clean

author: kos2001
body:
The question was whether a second standard cell library matters for RAG and training data. **It does — and the reason is sharper than "more data": the pipeline could not record it at all.**

## What was blind

`surrogate.featurize()` used `DIE_AREA` and `SYNTH_STRATEGY`. All 40 recorded samples were `sky130_fd_sc_hd`, and the library was not a field.

Measured on counter4:

| axis | area spread |
|---|---|
| all 11 design-knob samples | **4.3%** |
| switching library alone | **53.1%** |

The model was being asked to predict area from knobs that barely move it, with the one that does left out. A large part of why win-rate sat at **0.67** for both targets.

## Worse — collecting it would have destroyed it

`load_dataset` deduplicates by `(design, overrides)`, and the library is a `--scl` flag rather than an override (correctly: `STD_CELL_LIBRARY` as an override is accepted and ignored).

So two real runs differing only by technology **collapse to one sample and the later silently replaces the earlier.** Verified directly: counter4 at hd (290.3 µm²) and hs (444.4 µm²) recorded → **one sample survived.**

Fixed before collecting anything: `run_candidate` takes and records `scl`, the dedup key includes it, `featurize` carries it as a categorical feature.

## What the sweep found

`counter4`, `cdc_twoclock` and `spm` on `sky130_fd_sc_hs` all reach **step 74 of 78** and all fail the same rule — `licon.11`, diffusion contact to gate < 0.055 µm.

| design | cells | Magic DRC | KLayout DRC | route DRC | per cell |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| counter4 | 35 | 21 | 0 | 0 | 0.60 |
| cdc_twoclock | 93 | 48 | 0 | 0 | 0.52 |
| spm | 493 | 282 | 0 | 0 | 0.57 |

Violations scale with instance count across three unrelated designs, so this is **inside the cells** — not the placement, not the routing. And the two DRC engines flatly disagree.

On counter4, hd vs hs also differ by **+53% area, +59% power, +1.4% setup slack** — a "high speed" library buying almost nothing at 6 ns of slack.

## Why that matters for retrieval specifically

`tool_retrieval` had **no transferable guidance**: every entry came from `sram_wrapper`, so leave-one-out left `sram_wrapper` with nothing.

This is the first signature sourced from somewhere else. A new design hitting `sky130_fd_sc_hs` now retrieves counter4's finding **and survives leave-one-out**.

## An existing test caught a regression

Defaulting the SCL feature in `featurize` made every pair of configs share a feature, so `distance()` returned `0.0` instead of `None` for two rows with nothing in common — **every point equidistant, the exact failure its own docstring warns about**. Caught by `test_surrogate`, not by anything new.

The value is stored raw; the default is applied only when comparing a row that declares the library against one recorded before the field existed.

447 tests pass.

author: sxnnywu
body: Closes part of [BUI-575](https://linear.app/buildingoro/issue/BUI-575/design-system-a-needs-attention-pattern-warning-role-badge-callout). **PR 2 of 3.** > **Stacked on #37** (the `warning` role) — review that one first; this PR's diff is against it, not `main`. ## Why The badge is the only part of the needs-attention pattern that is **visible from outside the screen that owns the problem**. A user who never opens `/Account` never learns their phone is unlinked; the callout can only explain once they arrive. The ticket's spec: one component at two sizes, a bare dot and a pill with a count, same colour for both, count aggregating upward. ## Design decisions worth a look **Size follows from `count`, it isn't its own axis.** `count` omitted → dot; present → capsule. An explicit size prop would let a caller ship a dot for a two-item state, which is the "two severities" failure the ticket rules out. One prop, one signal. **The count text is the one genuine tier-3 divergence, and this is why it exists.** The fill is plain `warning` in both modes, no divergence there. The text can't be: white clears the light fill at 5.88:1, but on dark — where `warning` is base gold — white measures **2.17:1** and fails outright, so on plum it takes the `surface` colour instead (6.16:1). `components.ts` says that tier is for real divergences; this is one. There's a test pinning it in both modes. **`label` is required**, matching Button's `iconOnly` rule: a mark carrying meaning purely visually is invisible to a screen reader, and the dot has no text to fall back on. **A count of 0 still draws the dot** rather than vanishing. Whether the badge exists at all is the consumer's condition to evaluate — the ticket is explicit that badge, callout and row mark are renderings of one boolean — and a component that silently renders nothing would let a caller believe it had signalled something. **`TabBarItem` gains `badgeCount`.** This was the open question from planning and I went with including it: rule 3 says the badge propagates to every entry point, but `TabBarItem` was `{ key, icon, label }`, so without a slot a consumer physically could not render the pattern where it matters most. The badge is absolutely positioned so it can't shift the icon or the selection mark, and **the tab folds the count into its own accessible name** (`"you, 2 need attention"`) while hiding the badge from assistive tech — so it's announced once as part of the destination rather than as a second element to associate. There's a play function asserting that, because a bare `"you"` would mean a screen-reader user never learns anything is waiting. ## How it renders The two sizes, which are one signal: the bare dot, a count, an aggregate, and the 99+ cap. ## The two-marks question, answered on a render A selected tab now carries two marks: the 4px gold selection dot under the icon, and the warning capsule over it. I flagged this as needing a look rather than a ruling. It reads fine — they differ in size, depth and position: Both tones, showing the count-text flip that earns the tier-3 token: ## Verified `lint` · `build` · `-r typecheck` · `assert-inert` (55 shipped colours unchanged) · `test:unit` (88 pass, +2) · `build-storybook` · `test:interactions` (47 pass, +4) · `test:visual` **in the pinned Playwright container** (47 pass). Baselines regenerated in that image: **only the four new Badge stories were added and no existing baseline moved**, which is the evidence that wrapping TabBar's icon didn't shift the bar's layout. ## Out of scope Adopting the badge in Oro-Mobile-Refresh (BUI-574 and siblings), and the aggregation logic deciding what the count counts, which the ticket puts on the consumer. `Callout` is PR 3. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01UedceLPwgTZpS8BqG5J84m

author: mchacher
body:
## #764: the Release was published without a manifest arm64 could pull

`docker-arm64` is `continue-on-error`, so an arm64 failure skips `promote-manifest` by its own gate. The `release` job declared `promote-manifest` in `needs` but its condition only checked `docker`, so it created the GitHub Release anyway. `version-checker.ts` polls `/releases/latest`, not the GHCR manifest, so every Raspberry Pi would have been told an update was available and every `docker pull` would then have failed. The run stayed green, and the comment above the job described the opposite behaviour.

It was worse than the issue states. The amd64 job also pushed **`:latest`**, and `docker-compose.yml` pins `:latest` (spec 104's update helper rewrites compose back to it). So an arm64 failure did not merely show a phantom update: it repointed `:latest` at an amd64-only manifest, and the next `docker compose pull` on every Pi would have failed outright.

Three changes:

- the `release` condition now requires `promote-manifest` to have succeeded
- `:latest` moves out of the amd64 job into `promote-manifest`, pointed at the already-merged `:<version>`. Pushing it from a single-arch job left the tag amd64-only between the two steps, which is a real window on **every** healthy release, not only a failing one
- the two comments that documented behaviour the workflow did not have are corrected

## Two holes the review found on top of that

**A dispatched tag would publish a Release for a version with no images.** GitHub's "Run workflow" dropdown accepts a tag as its ref. On that path every "Resolve version" step takes the `workflow_dispatch` branch, so only `:<test_tag>` images are built, yet `startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')` still held and `gh release create` ran with `github.ref_name`. Pre-existing, and the recovery advice this branch first added ("re-run the workflow on the same tag") pointed an operator straight at it. The condition now requires a push, and the guidance says **Re-run all jobs**.

**A withheld release was silent.** With `continue-on-error` retained, an arm64 failure produced a green run in which `release` was merely grey, and GitHub notifies on red runs, not on skipped jobs: tag v1.58.0, see green, move on, and nobody ever receives it. The new `arm64-required` job fails the run when the release was withheld. `continue-on-error` stays so the amd64 image still reaches GHCR and is pullable by digest while the arm64 build is repaired.

## Behaviour change, deliberate

An arm64 failure now withholds `:latest` and the GitHub Release entirely rather than shipping an amd64-only update to half the fleet, and turns the run red. `:<version>` is still pushed for anyone pulling by tag or digest.

## #638: workflow token and interpolation hardening

`ci.yml` already carried `permissions: contents: read` on main, so what remained:

- `${{ inputs.test_tag }}` was expanded straight into three `run:` bodies. It goes through `env:` now, as does the one remaining `${{ github.event_name }}` in a run block, which makes "no workflow expression reaches a shell script" a property of the whole file rather than a habit
- routing through `env:` stops the shell re-evaluating the value but not a **newline** (which injects a second `GITHUB_OUTPUT` key; the dispatch REST API accepts multi-line input values even though the UI field is single-line) nor a **space** (which word-splits into extra `imagetools` arguments). Each "Resolve version" step now refuses a version that is not a valid image tag, and the `imagetools` arguments are quoted
- the amd64 `docker` job drops `contents: write`; it pushes packages and writes nothing to the repo

## Tests

A workflow file has no type checker and no test runner of its own, which is how a missing condition survived for months. `src/core/release-workflow.test.ts` asserts ten invariants against the workflow text, beside `version-checker.ts` because the updater's contract is what the ordering protects. **Seven fail against the workflow as it stands on main**, one per defect.

The `run:` scanner is hand-rolled, so it is pinned twice: its block count is compared against the count of `run:` keys in the file, and it is run against a fixture carrying all five YAML shapes (compact one-liner, compact block, indent indicator, chomping, folded). The first version of it anchored on `^\s*run:` and was already silently skipping `- run: npm ci`.

## Docs

The release-pipeline section of `architecture.{md,fr.md}` now lists all seven jobs and states why the ordering is a correctness requirement. The French page was separately drifted: it claimed the build was amd64-only and described a `release.sh` that bumps versions and commits, neither of which is true. Both were flagged in the 2026-08-29 documentation audit. The `sowel-release` skill gains the arm64-failure troubleshooting line.

Closes #764
Closes #638

author: shulmeister
body:
## The bug

Click a track → UI fully commits to "playing" (pause icon, correct title/art, `/api/play-events` POSTs) but **audio never starts**. Progress frozen at 0:00. **No console error, nothing in `shmearify.log` or `shmearify-error.log`.**

## Root cause

`serveOriginal()` parsed Range with `/bytes=(\d+)-(\d*)/`. A **suffix range** — `bytes=-1024`, "the last 1024 bytes", perfectly valid under RFC 7233 — has no digits before the dash and fails that match. The `!match` branch then did this:

```js
res.set("Content-Length", String(size));   // promises the whole file
return res.status(200).end();               // …sends zero bytes
```

The browser did exactly what it was told: waited for 12,740,047 bytes that were never coming.

| observed in the live `<audio>` element | |
|---|---|
| `readyState` | `0` (HAVE_NOTHING — no bytes ever arrived) |
| `networkState` | `2` (NETWORK_LOADING — still waiting) |
| `play()` promise | never resolved **or** rejected |

Because it never rejected, the `.catch()` wrapping every `audio.play()` had nothing to catch. Silent by construction on both ends.

**Why it looked un-reproducible:** `fetch()` and `curl` don't send suffix ranges, so every manual test of the same URL returned instantly. Only Chrome's media pipeline sends them, to read trailing ID3v1 metadata before decoding. That's also why it wasn't Grateful-Dead-specific — it reproduced on Widespread Panic and would hit any track.

## Fix

- Handle suffix ranges → serve the last N bytes as a proper `206` with correct `Content-Range`.
- Make the unparseable-Range fallback **actually send the body it promises**, per RFC 7233 ("ignore the Range, serve the full representation").
- Multi-ranges now take that same safe path instead of being answered with one range's bytes under a `206`.

## Verification — against the running service

| Range | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `bytes=-1024` | 200, CL 12,740,047, **sent 0** | 206, CL 1024, sent 1024 ✅ |
| `bytes=-500` | 200, CL 12,740,047, **sent 0** | 206, CL 500, sent 500 ✅ |
| `bytes=abc` | 200, CL 12,740,047, **sent 0** | 200, CL 12,740,047, sent 12,740,047 ✅ |
| `bytes=0-1023` | 206, 1024 | 206, 1024 ✅ (no regression) |
| `bytes=0-` | 206, full | 206, full ✅ |
| `bytes=0-100,200-300` | 206, 101 bytes | 200, full body ✅ |

`Content-Length` now equals bytes actually sent in all six cases. Confirmed through `shmearify.coloradocareassist.com` as well, not just localhost.

## Follow-ups NOT in this PR

- **Both 404 paths in `/stream/:id` are silent** (`server.js` unknown-id and file-missing) — worth a `console.warn` so this class of bug stops being invisible.
- **98% of Grateful Dead show-dates (1,938 of 1,977) have duplicate surviving directories** — `dedupeGdShows()` isn't collapsing them. Separate bug; all copies play.
- ⚠️ **Do not "fix" this with `/api/rescan`.** The dedup winner is chosen by raw `mtime` and flips between scans (two real scans: 334,021 vs 291,450 kept tracks), which would silently orphan durable track ids.
- `CLAUDE.md` still documents `MUSIC_PATH=/Volumes/Shulmeister HD/iTunes/Music`; live is `TSE - MASTER MUSIC - 5TB`.

author: morozsm
body:
Step 0 of the profile-driven command-bytes programme (MOR-2000): make the Yaesu
reference implementation actually exemplary. Two `YaesuCatRadio` methods held
their command text in code instead of resolving it from the profile — the same
defect class the programme removes on the Icom side, living inside its
reference. Ticket: MOR-2011.

## The measured finding that reshaped the ticket

A read-only bench probe of the live FTX-1 (2026-08-29) showed the old
`get_if_status` parsed a frame layout the radio does not emit. Against the
measured answer `IF00000014228000+000000200003;` it produced freq=142 Hz for a
14.228 MHz dial, and the `tx`/`split` fields it extracted (plus the `scan`
offset it skipped) do not exist in the real answer — `tx`'s offset holds RX CLAR,
`scan`'s the VFO/memory select, `split`'s the tone mode. Its writes to `state.ptt` and `state.split` were therefore garbage
writes, masked because the poller overwrites both shortly after via the
dedicated `TX;`/`ST;` reads. The CAT manual FTX-1_CAT_OM_ENG_2508-C confirms
the measured layout field-for-field. The ticket's original "same values before
and after" arrival test was replaced (recorded on MOR-2011) by: the parse
matches the bench frame and the manual, and the phantom fields are gone.

## Changes

- `rigs/ftx1.toml` — `get_if_status` gains a `parse` template matching the
  measured frame, with per-entry provenance (manual 2508-C + bench 2026-08-29;
  the undocumented observed P10=`3` is recorded).
- `parser.py` — three new placeholder names (`chan` 5-char alphanumeric,
  `tone`, `shift`), data rows in the existing per-command extension pattern
  (as `main`/`sub` were added for RM, `delay` for SD).
- `radio.py` — `_query` accepts optional params formatted into the read
  template via the existing `format_command`; `_read_meter` routes through the
  profile's complete `get_meter` entry; `get_if_status` routes through
  `_query` and maps the real P1–P10 fields, no longer touching `state.ptt` /
  `state.split` and no longer returning `tx`/`split` keys. No command literal
  remains in executable code.
- Tests — measured-frame pins for the parser (incl. alphanumeric channel

body:
Records four scope decisions taken on 30 August 2026, in the one place somebody would otherwise not see them.

Every command in `coilbox-zerok-protocol` is generated, so a message coilbox does nothing with looks identical whether it is a gap waiting to be filled or a decision already taken. Most are gaps, which is what the `lobby-protocol-gap` label tracks. Steam authentication and Planet Wars are not, and without saying so the next person to read the message list files both under that label and closes them.

The other two are about reach rather than messages. Zero-K's engine mirror, content service and image host are run by that project for its own client, so coilbox takes Zero-K content down rapid like anything else and a battle naming something rapid does not carry stays unjoinable. And there is now a second Zero-K server: `FIGHTORDER/ZkInfraNeo`, whose own planning document says it is not obliged to preserve the legacy protocol, so it is not a server these generated types describe.

The common thread is that coilbox is a lobby client on the model of skylobby against Beyond All Reason. It connects, logs in, browses, and plays, and it leaves alone the parts of the service the project running it owns.

Docs only, no behaviour change. Issues #1988, #1989, #1990, #1991, #1992, #1976, #1977 and #1980 are closed as not planned and carry the reasoning. Milestone 34's description says the same. #2087 covers the one user-visible cost, which is telling somebody with a Steam-only Zero-K account why coilbox cannot sign them in.

author: mattwilkinsonn
body:
## What

Recover MCP tools from a successful-but-empty `tools/list` during a gateway's cold-start warmup, instead of caching the empty set as authoritative for the rest of the session (and every later session). Adds `/mcp refresh` for manual recovery.

## Why

When MCP discovery ran during an aggregating gateway's warmup window (roughly the 15-20s after the gateway restarts), a `tools/list` could return a successful `200` with `{"tools":[]}`. That empty toolset was trusted as authoritative and cached for 30 days, so the session — and every later session reading the poisoned cache — came up with zero MCP tools until the config hash changed.

Three changes close it: an empty toolset is never persisted; an already-cached empty entry now reads as a cache miss (which self-heals a previously poisoned entry on the next read); and a connected server that lists no tools is re-listed on a bounded backoff so the session self-heals once the server populates. `/mcp refresh` re-fetches tools from already-connected servers without tearing the connections down, for a session that connected while the gateway was still advertising empty.

I reviewed the full diff; this stops an early empty `tools/list` from permanently hiding an MCP server's tools when the gateway is just slow to warm up, and lets a session that already hit the empty window recover without a restart.

## Testing

Red/green on the two regression files (`bun test`):

- With the fix: `test/mcp-empty-toolset-retry.test.ts` + `test/mcp-tool-cache-empty.test.ts` — 5 pass, 0 fail.
- Reverting the fix to confirm the tests catch the bug (removing both empty-toolset guards from `tool-cache.ts`) turns exactly two cases red, each naming the bug: `set() does not persist an empty toolset` and `get() treats an already-cached empty toolset as a miss`.

Rebased onto current `main` and re-run before submitting.

---

- [x] Tested locally
- [x] CHANGELOG updated (if user-facing)

author: iceteasa
body: Opened at your invitation on #3. Two commits, separable — take either alone. ## 1. `fix(vault)`: envelope selection by decision, not by variant order — closes residual 3 of #3 `CredentialGetResponse` was `#[serde(untagged)]` with `Direct` declared before `Wrapped`. Untagged enums are tried in declaration order, so a frame carrying **both** a wrapped `result.error` and top-level success fields decoded as a SUCCESS and discarded the error — `fetch()` would return a `CredentialToken` built from the stray bytes and hand it to a provider call. `result` now wins whenever present. The unwrapped form stays accepted, as a documented fallback rather than a coincidence of ordering. Scope, stated honestly: **claustrum cannot emit that frame today.** Their `GetOutcome` is an enum whose variants cannot coexist, confirmed from their types, so this is a latent hazard rather than a live bug. What made it worth fixing is the direction it fails in — toward serving a credential — and that the envelope choice rested on declaration order rather than on a decision. Also pins the missing-`code` frame. It was already rejected, but only because `code` is non-`Option` — an accident of the type rather than an intention. Adding `#[serde(default)]` later now reddens a test instead of silently widening what synapse accepts from the vault. Three tests: the defect, the fallback, and the missing-`code` frame. ## 2. `feat(manifest)`: declare provenance facts instead of blanket-`None` `provenance: None` carried a comment about release scripts not stamping `CK_BUILD_*` yet. That reasoning holds for the build facts and not for the other two: - `wire_crate_version` is a compile-time constant of the linked `subc-protocol` crate. - The newest migration this binary carries is a fact a daemon can compare against a store's actual version to spot a stale binary directly. Uses the SDK helper, which stamps `wire_crate_version` from the linked crate and maps an absent build fact to field omission rather than to a sentinel string. Build facts stay absent. `newest_schema_version()` derives from the migration list rather than restating it — a literal keeps reporting the old number the first time a migration is appended, which is the drift this field exists to catch. It uses `max` rather than `last` so it does not rest on the list happening to stay sorted. The test **deliberately does not restate the schema number.** Asserting a derived value against the same derivation would make the test agree with the code by construction and pass whatever the migration list said. ## Mutation proof Each test was verified capable of failing, with a positive control asserting the mutation target existed exactly once **before** editing — a substitution that silently matches nothing is indistinguishable from a test that catches nothing. | mutation | result | |---|---| | envelope precedence reverted to `Direct`-before-`Wrapped` | `FAIL wrapped_error_wins_over_stray_top_level_success_fields` — *stray top-level success fields must not outrank a wrapped error*; the other four vault tests stayed green | | `provenance` reverted to `None` | `FAIL manifest_provenance_declares_only_facts_this_binary_knows` — *an SDK module always has at least one honest provenance fact* | | schema fact dropped (`build_provenance(None, None, None)`) | `FAIL` — *a module with a migration list can state its newest migration* | | `wire_crate_version` set to synapse's own crate version | `FAIL` — `left: Some("0.0.0")`, `right: Some("0.14.0")` | The vault mutation left the other four tests green, so that test **discriminates** rather than merely triggering. Every mutation was reverted and the file confirmed byte-identical to its pre-mutation copy. One control fired for real: a second mutation stacked on an unreverted first was **refused** by its own positive control (`target not found exactly once (count=0)`) instead of running and reporting a meaningless pass. ## Gate Run at the pushed sha `adfa363` — a gate result is a claim about a tree, not about a diff — inside a network namespace with egress dead by DNS name and raw IP, loopback positive control live before and after: ``` 577 tests run: 577 passed, 3 skipped skip census: 15 (unchanged — no new silent skipping) clippy --all-targets: clean cargo fmt --all --check: clean Cargo.lock: untouched ``` Scope caveat: 4 crates (`synapse-core`, `synapse-engine-ort`, `synapse-module`, `owned-decode-worker`). CI runs 6 — `synapse-worker-llama` pulls a llama.cpp C++ build and `synapse-worker-decode` is macOS-gated, neither reachable here. Build note for reviewers: `master` now requires `subc-protocol` 0.14.0 for `self_signals`. This was built against an isolated sibling checkout at that version rather than by moving the shared fleet tree; `Cargo.lock` is untouched, which is the check that the sibling set was right rather than silently downgrading. ## Not included `_ => PauseJob` is unchanged — contract-backed per the resolution on #3, and claustrum has since published the widening rule that makes it correct. Residuals 1 and 2 of #3 are untouched. They are judgement calls about your error vocabulary rather than mechanical fixes. Residual 1 did stop being hypothetical, though: claustrum deployed `706e257` today, so `credential.get` on a signing-key handle now returns `kind_not_gettable` — a vault-side wrong-verb condition that synapse still reports to consumers as `credential_config_invalid`. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes vault credential envelope selection so a wrapped error can't be misread as a credential success, and declares the provenance facts synapse actually knows instead of blanket-None. **Bug Fixes** - Selects the envelope by the `result` key's presence rather than untagged variant order; claustrum can't emit the mixed frame today, but the old code failed toward serving a credential. - Pins a missing `code` on a credential error as malformed; it was rejected by the type, not by intent. **New Features** - Declares `wire_crate_version` from the linked `subc-protocol` crate and the newest migration version; build facts stay absent. - `newest_schema_version()` derives from the migration list via `max` so appending a migration can't stale the reported number. Written for commit adfa3632d54d36c7344cba3b104f20ec4bfd712d. Summary will update on new commits.

author: gregkliewer
body:
The Associates hero was the only one on the site not plotted from a real figure — a generic centre node with four spokes and four open dots. This swaps it for Auriga, the Charioteer, drawn to the same conventions as the Taurus, Ophiuchus, Hercules and Lyra heroes.

## Why Auriga

- Capella, the anchor star, is one point of light to the eye and four stars when resolved — one accountable executive, four associates.
- Auriga's pentagon does not close on its own. Its lower corner is Elnath, which the 1930 IAU boundaries assigned to Taurus, the home page figure. The figure is complete only by borrowing a star from the practice's own constellation.
- The charioteer drives the team himself, rather than sitting behind a bench.

## The plot

Star positions are the real J2000 RA/Dec of the five pentagon stars, projected `x = -RA° · cos(37.99°)` (the compression at the figure's mean declination) and `y = -Dec`, so east is to the left and north is up. Fitted to a 300px vertical span with 50px top and bottom padding, centred horizontally. No rotation — the natural bounding box is 0.71:1, close enough to square that the figure is letterboxed the way Lyra is. Radii track visual magnitude, so Capella reads as the brightest.

| Star | Bayer | Mag | cx | cy | r |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Capella | α Aur | 0.08 | 239.7 | 50.0 | 9 |
| Menkalinan | β Aur | 1.90 | 94.0 | 68.1 | 6.5 |
| Mahasim | θ Aur | 2.62 | 93.4 | 201.6 | 5.5 |
| Elnath | β Tau | 1.65 | 207.0 | 350.0 | 8 (open) |
| Hassaleh | ι Aur | 2.69 | 306.6 | 271.4 | 5.5 |

Elnath is the lone open node, drawn as an `r="8"` ring at `stroke-width="3"` with an `r="6.5"` `#F7F9FA` knockout — identical to the Gamma Lyrae treatment on `publications.html`.

The projection was re-derived independently before applying: every coordinate reproduces exactly, with mean declination 37.99° and a bounding-box ratio of 0.7107.

## Deliberately omitted

- The Haedi (ε, ζ, η Aurigae) are absent. Five nodes is one per person on the page.
- No animation, hover states, or `<title>` element — the graphic is `aria-hidden` and the other four heroes are static.

## Verification

- Screenshot-verified at desktop 1440px and mobile 390px. No horizontal page scroll at either width.
- No layout shift: same `viewBox="0 0 400 400"` in the same container, measured 468×468 before and after.
- The hero visual is hidden at 390px by the pre-existing `.hero-visual { display: none }` rule in the `max-width: 900px` block — that applies to all five heroes and predates this change.
- The one console error at both widths is the Google Fonts stylesheet failing against the sandbox proxy; the untouched `publications.html` fails identically, so it is environmental.

## Scope

Touches exactly one file and one contiguous hunk (`associates.html`, lines 74–96). `styles.css` is untouched, so no `styles.css?v=NN` bump on any page.

One thing worth a reviewer's eye: the comment block sits above the `<svg>`, whereas Lyra on `publications.html` places its comment inside the `<svg>`. Happy to move it if matching Lyra exactly is preferred.

author: davnika17g
body:
> ⚠ **EN BORRADOR A PROPÓSITO — no mergear todavía.** Hoy empieza el conteo diario
> y cualquier merge a `main` despliega. Pasar a "Ready for review" cuando cierre esa
> ventana.

Cierra #140.

## Qué cambia

Seis `<iframe>` del hub tenían el `src` hardcodeado en el HTML estático. Un iframe en
`display:none` **igual carga su `src`**, así que `deudas`, `pedidos`, `remitos`,
`inventario`, `ordenes` y `pagos` se descargaban y booteaban en **cada apertura del
hub**, los abriera alguien o no.

Pasan a `src="about:blank"`, que es lo que ya hacen los otros seis (`sueldos`,
`retiros`, `supervision`, `alertas`, `insumos`, `reportes`) y funciona. Son 6
atributos y un comentario.

## Medición

Localhost, abriendo el hub **sin loguearse**, sumando las líneas de tiempo de recursos
del hub y de cada iframe. El Service Worker se desregistró antes de medir.

| | `main` | esta rama |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Recursos | 116 | **9** |
| Requests a Supabase | 45 | **3** |
| Lecturas de `config` | 23 | **3** |

Desglose del control, para ver de dónde salía cada cosa:

| Origen | Recursos | Supabase | `config` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| hub | 15 | 3 | 3 |
| `deudas-iframe` | 11 | 4 | 2 |
| `pedidos-iframe` | 41 | 20 | 6 |
| `remitos-iframe` | 16 | 8 | 3 |
| `inventario-iframe` | 14 | 6 | 5 |
| `ordenes-iframe` | 10 | 2 | 2 |
| `pagos-iframe` | 9 | 2 | 2 |

Es coherente con `pg_stat_statements`, donde `config.valor` lleva **513.858 llamadas**
y `set_config` **817.373**, en una app que usa un puñado de personas. Y con el
incidente del 28-ago: seis módulos arrancando por apertura es parte de por qué una
base de 34 MB satura una instancia de 1 GB.

Ojo con una lectura fácil: **este PR no baja el costo de usar los módulos**, baja el
de *no* usarlos. Quien abra Pedidos va a pagar sus 20 requests igual.

## Cómo se verificó

No hay CI ni tests en este repo, así que:

1. **Control negativo primero.** Con el `index.html` de `main` se midieron los seis
   módulos descargados; con la rama, cero. Sin ese control la medición no probaría
   nada.
2. **Sintaxis** de los 3 bloques `<script>` inline con `vm.Script` de Node, con su
   propio control negativo (un error puesto a propósito que el checker detecta).
3. **Los seis módulos abren desde `about:blank`**: se llamó a `deudasOpen`,
   `pedidosOpen`, `remitosOpen`, `inventarioOpen`, `ordenesOpen` y `pagosOpen` uno por
   uno y los seis cargaron su documento.
4. **El contexto sigue llegando por `postMessage`**: tras `ordenesOpen()` el módulo
   pinta "Thames · Palermo", la fecha, el efectivo disponible y el último cierre — o
   sea que recibió `local`/`rol` y consultó Supabase con ellos.
5. **UTF-8 y CRLF** intactos (4.388 líneas CRLF, 0 LF sueltos, 0 mojibake).

## Trampa que evitó un reemplazo masivo

`deudasOpen()` reasigna con query params:

```js
iframe.src = 'deudas.html?local=' + (state.local || '') + '&rol=' + (state.rol || '');
```

Un grep de `src = 'deudas.html'` **no lo encuentra** y daría un falso negativo. Por eso
los seis se revisaron uno por uno, y el comentario que agrega el diff lo deja anotado
para el próximo que pase.

## Qué se rompe si sale mal

Un módulo que dependiera en silencio de estar precargado no aparecería al abrirlo desde
su card. Lo descarta el punto 3 de la verificación, que abre los seis. El rollback es
revertir un commit de 16 líneas.

## Relación con otros issues

- #139 (retirar `remitos.html`) se solapaba en la línea del iframe de remitos: ese
  punto queda resuelto acá.
- El costo que #139 le atribuía al módulo (3.797 llamadas, 374 s de CPU) **lo causaba
  este `src`**, no el módulo. Retirarlo sigue valiendo la pena como limpieza, pero ya
  no como optimización.

author: benjaminematton
body:
**Draft on purpose — this is the plan gate, not an implementation.** One file, no code. Opened as a PR so the gate can be sat with inline comments.

Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-29-spec-registration-seam.md`

## Three things need a ruling before Task 1 is dispatched

### G-1 — `strategies` does not exist, and §3.1 *and* §3.2 both read it

This is the one that matters. The fence says `strategies` stays out; the canonical contract for half two of this lane requires it in three places:

| Where | What it requires |
|---|---|
| §3.1 | "INSERTs spec **+ `strategies` row in state `SPEC`**" |
| §3.2 step 1 | "spec exists and **`strategies.state ∈ {SPEC, BACKTEST}`**" |
| §3.2 step 7 | "INSERT trial row; **UPSERT `strategies.state → BACKTEST`**" |

§3.2's own implementation note puts it beyond doubt: *"State check (step 1's `strategies.state` clause) **lives in the MCP handler**."*

Verified by enumerating `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` in `state/schema.sql` — 14 tables, `strategies` not among them — rather than grepping for the name.

**Recommendation: sequence, don't proxy.** Ship registration + the binding now; hold `run_backtest` exposure until `strategies` lands. Deriving state from `trial_registry` presence would manufacture exactly what §2 warns against (*"should **replace** the selector rather than add a second one"*), and it has a failure the real column doesn't: a `budget_exhausted` rejection **logs a trial row** (§3.2 step 3), which would flip a derived state to `BACKTEST` with no backtest having run.

**This is the plan's honest coverage gap:** three of the five Phase 5 acceptance criteria live in §3.2 and are therefore not delivered. Named in the plan's self-review rather than papered over.

### G-2 — no seat can call `submit_strategy_spec`

`SEAT_CAPS` grants caps to six seats and none has a registration cap; there is no `quant` seat. Recommendation: grant it to `analyst`. Adding a seat is a `run_day.SEATS` change with a wall-clock consequence — #169 established the 4-turn ceiling (5 × 240s > 1080s) — so it's a scheduling decision, not a tool-surface one.

### G-3 — the seam ships callable but undriven

Nothing in `orchestrator/` or `scripts/` assigns a turn that calls it. Per invariant 6 the orchestrator assigns every workflow-critical turn, so the queue stays empty and G1 still never runs on a real spec. Same shape as #182's own "not urgent today." Recommendation: ship it, file the driver as a child of #49, and don't claim "G1 live end to end" on a seam nothing drives.

## One defect found while writing the plan

**F-1: `StrategySpec` does not forbid extra fields.** §3.1 mandates `extra="forbid"`; `state/models.py` sets no `model_config`, so it runs on pydantic's default `extra="ignore"`. Demonstrated, not inferred — an extra `sharpe_target=2.0` is accepted and silently dropped.

The consequence is sharper than a lax schema. That model's own docstring says *"these fields ARE the hash input."* An ignored field never reaches `model_dump()`, so two semantically different specs collide on one `spec_id` and the second is discarded by `INSERT OR IGNORE` **with no error** — a spec the researcher believes was registered, wasn't. Task 2 Step 3 fixes it; it cannot change any existing id, because ignored fields were never in the hash.

author: lattymoy
body:
Both faults in the screenshot — the sail hanging in mid-air, and the tower standing across a path — are **one root cause**.

**Collada is right-handed; Unity is left-handed.** Every number the mod carries — the prefab's hub offset, the WorldData placements — is written in *Unity's* space, because that is where Kamer authored them. The DAE's vertices are not: Unity's importer negates X on the way in, and WM2a shipped without doing the same.

- **The sail.** The hub offset is x **+3.96**; the body's cap sits at x **−3.95**, its mirror. The sail turned about a point a cap's width away, in empty air. Its Y was right all along (6.01 against a cap spanning 4.06–10.84), which is why it read as a near miss rather than nonsense.
- **The tower.** Mirroring a body whose bounds are *not* symmetric about its origin (−12.06…3.89) swings its mass eight units across the anchor. That is what put it on the path.

The bake negates X now, with normals mirrored and winding reversed (a mirror turns every triangle inside out and the renderer culls back faces). After it: the cap's centre is **3.94** against a hub of **3.96**, and the hub stands 1.53 beyond the cap's face along +Z — the windshaft. The sail is flat in Z. It mounts.

`ROTOR_SIGN` flips with it, and that is not a disagreement: a mirror reverses the sense of a rotation about an axis in its plane (`M R(t) M⁻¹ = R(−t)`), so his −13°/s and our +13 turn the sails the same way. Flip one without the other and the mill runs backwards.

## Why every pin passed through it

The arc had eleven pins on the rotor and **not one asked whether the rotor meets the mill** — only whether it was flat, centred on its own origin, spinning, and standing on the ground. All true, and the sail in mid-air.

Now the hub must land within 3 units of some piece of mill (it was 5.54), **and** share the cap's centre across the shaft while standing clear of it along the shaft — because "near the mill" alone would pass a hub at the wrong corner. 3 mutants, 3 killed, the first being the bug itself.

## And his climate skins, which the .rar had all along

Seventeen `41600_*` variant prefabs, and only **two** of the body's five texture groups ever differ across them — the walls and the roof. Plank and Windmill are `067_1` and the Door `332_0` in every one.

Carried verbatim in `variants.json` rather than derived, because they are not quite a climate rebase: his walls follow ClimateSwaps' law (364 → 064/164/464, +1 for winter) but his roofs do not — 369_3 temperate, 069_1 desert, 369_0 mountain, 369_1 swamp, one snow roof 103_1 for every winter. **The desert mill never winters** — his prefabs and `ClimateSwaps.cs` stating the same rule independently.

Applied by uploading the mill's own mesh *per climate*, not through the location's `texRemap`: that map is keyed `archive_record` over the whole scene, and the mill's walls are `364_2` — a key other buildings carry, so remapping it would have re-skinned them too.

Suite 4613/476 — **4416 pass, 0 fail**. eslint clean, `npm run build` passes. Merged through MW-D9e.

author: marcusrbrown
body:
Renovate's grouped GitHub Actions update has been failing during branch construction (`Error updating branch: update failure`) while the job still reports success — so it fails silently and no PR ever appears.

## Cause

`fro-bot/agent` is both a GitHub Action and the publishing home for `@fro.bot/harness` binaries. Harness releases tagged before today use SemVer build metadata:

```
1.18.21+harness.22dee0ee
```

Build metadata is ignored for SemVer precedence, so that tag parses as a stable `1.18.21`. The `github-actions` manager resolves `uses:` pins from the `github-tags` datasource — candidates come from git tags — so it ranks `1.18.21` above the real `v0.106.0` action line and tries to update the workflows to a harness binary release.

## Fix

A `packageRule` in the shared preset capping the action to `<1.0.0`. It lives in `default.json` rather than this repo's `renovate.json5` because every consumer extending the preset sees the same tags.

Upstream, fro-bot/agent#1492 switches new harness tags to a prerelease identifier (`1.18.21-harness.<sha>`), which `ignoreUnstable` excludes by specification. That fixes it going forward, but the 18 existing build-metadata tags stay stable-shaped permanently — deleting them would 404 the asset URLs that already-shipped action versions construct from their own bundled code. So this cap is the durable consumer-side guard, not a temporary workaround.

Validated with `renovate-config-validator` (exit 0).

author: peter3605
body:
## Dark mode already worked. The choice is what was missing.

The palette is built from semantic system colours
(`secondarySystemGroupedBackground` and friends), no `UIUserInterfaceStyle` is
set in the bundle, and the only fixed colour in the app is `accentGreen`. A
device in dark mode already got a dark app.

What the app had no way to do was *differ* from the device. The web client has
had a three-state control since it shipped — light / dark / system, persisted
under `cf-theme` (`web/src/lib/theme.tsx`) — and the app had nothing.

`ThemeStore` mirrors it down to the storage key, so the two clients cannot
drift in behaviour even though the storage is separate. The override is applied
once at the root as `.preferredColorScheme` rather than per screen.

**`system` is the default and is deliberately not the same as `light`.** It
maps to a `nil` `ColorScheme`, which is how SwiftUI spells "do not override".
So anyone who never opens the new section sees exactly the behaviour they had
before, and a user flipping iOS into dark mode still gets a dark app.

Settings gains an **Appearance** section with a segmented picker.

## Tests

`ThemeStoreTests` injects `UserDefaults` so each case runs against its own
suite. It covers the default, persistence across a relaunch, that an
unrecognised stored value falls back to `system` rather than sticking (this is
read on every cold launch), and that only explicit choices override the device.

## Deploy

iOS-only, so nothing here reaches the server — `deploy.yml` ignores `ios/**`
and `ios.yml` is what checks this.

author: damienbattistella
body: Revue du Carnet de consultation TDAH sur mobile, à partir des captures d'écran signalées. ## 1. L'échelle annoncée au médecin est fausse (le plus grave) Le rapport titre « Moyennes par dimension (échelle 1-5) », mais les relevés sont saisis sur une échelle **0-10** : - `packages/validators/src/symptom.ts` : `ratingScale = z.number().int().min(0).max(10)` - `apps/web/src/components/symptoms/symptom-form.tsx` : ``, affiché « `{valeur}/10` » D'où le « Humeur 8.0 » sous un en-tête « 1-5 » visible sur la capture. C'est un document remis à un pédopsychiatre, donc le chiffre doit être lisible sans ambiguïté. Corrigé aux trois endroits : l'aperçu web, le PDF (`renderSymptomTable`) et la pièce jointe HTML envoyée par email. ## 2. Les sparklines ne s'affichaient pas `Sparkline` normalisait sur `min = 1, max = 5` alors que les valeurs vont de 0 à 10. Le tracé sortait donc du `viewBox` de 20 px : | Dimension | Moyenne | y (avant) | Rendu | |---|---|---|---| | Humeur | 8.0 | **−15.0** | hors cadre — aucune ligne | | Concentration | 5.0 | 0.0 | collée au bord supérieur | | Agitation | 3.0 | 10.0 | correct | Ce qui correspond exactement à la capture : la ligne « Humeur » est absente et les dimensions à 5.0 sont plaquées en haut. Passage à `[0, 10]`, plus un bornage `Math.min/max` pour qu'une valeur hors plage ne puisse plus sortir du cadre. ## 3. Divers - La cellule d'une série trop courte pour être tracée affichait une virgule isolée (`, `) — remplacée par un tiret cadratin, comme la colonne Moyenne. - Libellé « Vos questions au médecin » : `Label` est un conteneur flex, donc la mention entre parenthèses devenait une seconde colonne et les deux textes se coupaient en deux lignes chacun. La mention passe sur sa propre ligne. - En-tête de l'application vide sur `/report` et `/admin-analytics` : ces deux routes ne déclaraient pas de `crumb`, la barre supérieure n'affichait donc que le sélecteur de thème. ## Point signalé, non corrigé Les moyennes filtrent les relevés avec `typeof v === "number" && v > 0`, aux trois mêmes endroits (`report/index.tsx`, `report.ts:414`, `report.ts:797`). Or le curseur part de 5 et descend jusqu'à 0 : un 0 correspond donc à une saisie délibérée (la pire journée possible), pas à une absence de saisie. Ces relevés sont aujourd'hui exclus de la moyenne **et** du compte « Relevés », ce qui biaise le rapport vers le haut en écartant précisément les journées que le médecin doit voir. La convention est cohérente aux trois endroits, donc probablement délibérée — et la changer modifie des chiffres à visée clinique. Je ne l'ai pas touchée. Dites-moi si vous voulez que 0 soit compté comme une valeur valide. ## Vérification - `pnpm typecheck` ✅ · `pnpm test` ✅ - Géométrie des sparklines revérifiée après correction : les cinq dimensions se tracent dans le cadre, et une valeur hors plage est bornée. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_012iLaHMzX6wyeMaP1t5uQTV)_

author: thejefflarson
body:
## Summary

Step 4 of 6 in the herdr manifest engine (ADR-009 decision 4): given a terminal's PTY, resolve the foreground process and map it to a manifest `id`, or fall back to `nil` (generic detection tier) on any failure.

**Scope note:** this is identification only, standalone and tested. It is **not** wired into `driveAgentActivity` and `AgentActivityDetector` is untouched — that integration is JEF-902.

## Identification flow

1. `ForegroundAgentIdentifier.identify(childfd:shellPid:manifests:)` — `tcgetpgrp(childfd)` → foreground pgid. macOS nuance: the pgid *is* the group-leader's pid, so `proc_name(pgid)` names the leader directly, no extra indirection needed.
2. The resolved process name is passed to `AgentIdentifier.resolveManifestID(processName:manifests:aliasTable:)` — a **pure function**: checks a manifest's own `id`, then its `aliases` (vendored from herdr), then a local `aliasTable` for binary-name mismatches. Case-insensitive throughout. Returns the manifest `id` or `nil`.
3. `ForegroundAgentIdentifier.identify(termView:manifests:)` is the thin convenience for the real call site (JEF-902): reads `termView.process.{childfd,shellPid}` and delegates to (1).

## Guards (all degrade to `nil` — generic tier, never a crash or misidentification)

- `process` IUO nil (SwiftTerm's `LocalProcess!`)
- `childfd == -1` (PTY not open / already torn down)
- `shellPid == 0` (shell never spawned)
- `tcgetpgrp` failure (`<= 0`) → falls back to naming `shellPid` itself
- `tcgetpgrp` returning the shell's own pgid (no foreground child running) → same fallback; naming the shell binary correctly matches no manifest

## The empirical unknown (ADR-009 risk 2)

**DECISION NEEDED for JEF-902's live dogfood:** nobody has confirmed Claude Code's actual foreground process name yet. `AgentIdentifier.localAliasTable` assumes it reports as `node` (its distribution is a Node.js CLI) rather than `claude`, and maps `node` → `claude`. If a live dogfood terminal shows a different name, correcting this table is a one-line fix — that separation from herdr's own vendored `aliases` is the whole point of keeping a local table. Worst case for a wrong guess: a misidentified terminal degrades to today's generic tier, nothing worse.

## Retention discipline (f7fecc5)

Both `AgentIdentifier` and `ForegroundAgentIdentifier` are stateless enums — every method takes plain values (or reads `termView.process` once, without storing it) and returns a plain `String?`. Nothing here retains a terminal, so wiring this into the ~1 Hz drive path (JEF-902) needs no additional weak-capture discipline beyond what that call site already applies to its own terminal reference.

## Testing

`Tests/AgentIdentificationTests.swift` — the syscall path (`tcgetpgrp`/`proc_name`) is injected via `ForegroundAgentIdentifier.Environment`, so every guard/fallback path is exercised without a real PTY:
- known manifest id, known manifest alias, case-insensitive match
- local alias-table entry (`node` → `claude`), and alias-table target absent from loaded manifests → nil
- unknown/empty process name → nil
- `childfd == -1`, `shellPid == 0`, `tcgetpgrp` failure, `tcgetpgrp` returning the shell's own pgid, libproc failure, unidentifiable name → all nil

## Checks

- `xcodebuild build -scheme Mosaic` → **BUILD SUCCEEDED**, no warnings
- `xcodebuild build-for-testing -scheme MosaicTests` → **TEST BUILD SUCCEEDED**, no warnings
- `xcodebuild test` hangs in-sandbox per CLAUDE.md; deferred to CI
- Manual security self-review (no injection/secrets/network surface — local libproc syscalls + pure string matching only); `/simplify` pass applied (unified the id/alias match into one case-insensitive loop)

Closes JEF-901

author: jimy-r
body:
benchmark-sweep's arXiv lane already fetches the right papers; this adds the second readout: which of them are worth an independent reproduction study. One fetch, two readouts (benchmark demand + repro-worthiness) — no new module, no duplicate machinery.

## What changes

- **Repro annotations, arXiv lane only** — each paper candidate gains `code_link` (detected from link elements, then `arxiv:comment`, then the abstract; host-exact or parent-domain match on github/gitlab/huggingface so lookalike domains fail; stored as untrusted data, never fetched), `repro_tier` (deterministic named signals: code-link +2, eval-claim +1, survey −2; ≥3 high / ≥1 med / else low; ranks, never drops), and `repro_signals` (the audit trail for why a paper sits where it does). GitHub-lane candidates carry none — a thread is not a reproducible claim.
- **`mark-studied`** — records a finished reproduction study in an inward ledger (`state/studied_papers.jsonl`); matching is scheme- and version-insensitive so a v2 revision never resurfaces a published study. Studied exclusion runs before the seen-store so the permanent reason owns the drop counter and `studied-excluded` reports truthfully.
- **Digest** — new `repro` section (`code_linked`, `by_tier`, `studied_excluded`) and a repro summary line; every existing field keeps its exact shape. Sort gains repro tier as the tie-breaker inside a fit tier.
- **NoOutbound guard sharpened, not weakened** — the `append_ledger` token ban was a proxy for "no posting history"; replaced by a structural assertion that the only ledger entry shape (`date, url, property, study_url, note`) cannot express a recipient, body, or venue. All other banned tokens unchanged. No posting path exists; the module stays discovery-only.

## Verification

- benchmark-sweep suite 87 → 127, all suites green via `modules/run_tests.py`; ruff check + format clean.
- Link/comment field shapes confirmed against a live arXiv API response (one request, 3s courtesy delay); the probe's no-code paper became the realistic negative fixture.
